summary: Write the ten-section knowledge-base page for each feature (part 2): purpose, user experience, current implementation, required behaviour, implementation map, data flow, access rules, states, verification, gaps

aliases: AI and saved data in published apps
features.summary: A published HTML or React app can call AI and save small text values through helpers the page provides (agi.complete, agi.storage). The app never holds a provider key. Calls go through our servers for a signed-in viewer, who is billed. AI is off unless a server switch is set. Web only.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a published app two helpers: agi.complete(prompt) for an AI answer and agi.storage get/set/delete/list for small text values, private to each viewer or shared by all viewers. The frame relays each call to the web page, which sends it to our servers (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:255-326, 353-370; apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:272-304).
purpose.why_it_exists: So an app made in chat can be interactive and remember things without the author putting a provider key or a database into the page. The page text says the helpers work once the app is published and opened by a signed-in viewer (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:240-241).
purpose.who_uses_it: App authors (the model writes script that calls the helpers) and viewers of the published app. The viewer must be signed in (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/artifactRuntimeClient.ts:57).
problems_solved: Apps need AI without exposing a key in page source.
Apps need to keep small state between visits.

The cost of AI calls is attributed to the signed-in viewer and counted against that viewer's plan, not the publisher (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/complete/__tests__/route.test.ts:407 title: bills the signed-in viewer for a published app and never its publisher).
use_cases: A published quiz app asks agi.complete to grade a free-text answer.
A published checklist app saves each viewer's ticks with agi.storage.set(name, JSON.stringify(value)).
A shared scoreboard app uses agi.storage.set(name, value, true) so every viewer sees the same value.
The owner tries AI inside the app in their own chat before publishing (apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/useLiveArtifactRuntime.ts:1-40).

where_to_find_it: Web only: the published page at /shared-artifact/<token> (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:73-95).

Web owner preview in a chat: AI works there, but saved data says 'Saved data works once this app is published. Publish it to use storage.' (apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/useLiveArtifactRuntime.ts:21).

Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not available. A published app opens in the browser or system browser (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:402-410). The Chrome side panel answers every runtime request with 'AI and saved data are available once this app is published and opened by a signed-in viewer.' (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts:849-855; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:3359).
prerequisites: The app kind is html or react (apps/web/db/neon/0395_published_artifact_audience_revocation.sql:72-83).
The app is published and the viewer is allowed to open it: public, the owner, a workspace member, or an invited viewer (apps/web/db/neon/0395_published_artifact_audience_revocation.sql:72-108).

The viewer is signed in. Signed out, the page shows 'Create an account or sign in to use this app's AI and saved data.' with buttons 'Create an account' and 'Sign in' (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:267-289).
For AI: the server switch AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is on (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-8).
screens_and_controls: Published page with the app inside a sandboxed frame (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:321-330).
A permission panel labelled 'AI permission' with buttons 'Allow' and "Don't allow" (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx:57,133,140).
After the viewer allows a connected-app set: 'Refresh data' and 'Connected apps' buttons (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:298-318).
journey: 1. The author publishes an html or react artifact whose script calls agi.complete or agi.storage (see F028-10).
2. A viewer opens the link and signs in if asked.

3. The app calls a helper. The frame checks that the page enabled the runtime and that fewer than 8 requests are pending, then posts a request to the web page (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:353-370).

4. For AI, the page asks the viewer once to allow it; the answer is remembered per user, link and exact code (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:42-80,148-153,316-323).

5. The page posts to our servers with a CSRF token; the server checks the switch, the viewer's plan and limits, picks a model route, and returns text (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:112-310).
6. The helper's promise resolves with the text, or rejects with a plain message.
feedback_and_outputs: agi.complete resolves to a string; storage.get resolves to the value or null; set resolves to the saved entry; list resolves to keys (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:77-143).
Failures reject with an error named AgiRuntimeError and a readable message, such as 'Too many requests are waiting. Wait for one to finish first.' (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:249-253,360-364).
If AI is off: 'AI in apps is not available yet.' (apps/web/lib/artifact-ai.ts:3).
settings: Server switch AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED (name and purpose only) (apps/web/.env.example:1009-1012).
No viewer-facing storage or AI setting was found in the code.

working: The frame installs a frozen agi object with complete and storage helpers, and rejects when the runtime is not enabled or 8 requests are pending (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:255-326,353-370).

The web page validates each request and relays it to a host; without a host it answers that AI and saved data need a published app (apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:123-163; apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:272-304).

Storage route supports get, set, delete, list, personal or shared, with CSRF, account-active check, rate limit 'artifact-storage' (120 per minute) and size limits (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:51-143; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:439-443).
Storage writes use a transaction with an advisory lock so concurrent writes cannot pass the 20 MiB per scope cap (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:215-258).

Completion runs workspace policy, plan access, content moderation, content-safety preference, secret handling, route choice, model policy and egress gates, a concurrency slot, a usage reservation and a final usage record (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:136-310; apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:629-765).
The viewer, not the publisher, is billed (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/complete/__tests__/route.test.ts:407).
incomplete: Per-app AI call and spend caps are written in migration 0391, whose header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0391_artifact_runtime_usage_cap.sql:1-5), yet the service calls reserve_artifact_runtime_usage_microusd (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:804). Whether it is applied in production is unknown.

The database allows a value up to 5 MiB (apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:3-18) while the API refuses values above 4 MiB (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:10; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:85-91). The API limit is the tighter one.
disconnected_or_disabled: agi.complete is refused with 403 artifact_ai_off unless AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is 1, true, yes or on; the page also refuses before calling (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:3-8; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:116-118; apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:309). The .env.example says it stays off until a security review passes (apps/web/.env.example:1009-1012).

Connected apps from inside an app are refused with 'Connectors are coming soon.' because the release state is coming_soon (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14,46-48; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:121-123). Storage has no such switch (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:51-143).
not_available: Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome do not run published apps (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:402-410; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts:849-855).
Local mode and own-key mode: no path found. An owner preview requires the app to come from a Cloud chat (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:59-68).

established.statement: An app can call AI through a brokered product API instead of embedding keys (brief S28.22, web done; desktop, mobile, chrome missing).
An app can be given persistent storage (brief S28.23, web done; desktop, mobile, chrome missing).
Storage values are at most 4 MiB each and 20 MiB per scope; keys have no spaces, slashes or quotes and are 1 to 200 characters.
Shared storage is refused for an app that uses connectors when the viewer is not the owner.
Published apps are rendered only on the web page; other surfaces open the browser.

acceptance_criteria: With the switch off, agi.complete rejects with 'AI in apps is not available yet.' and no model is called.
With the switch on and a signed-in viewer on an eligible plan, agi.complete resolves to text and the viewer's usage rises, not the publisher's.
A signed-out viewer calling any helper sees the sign-in banner and the call rejects with a sign-in message.
storage.set then storage.get of the same key returns the same text for the same viewer; with shared=true a second viewer reads it; with shared=false the second viewer gets null.
A value over 4 MiB is refused with 'A saved value can be up to 4 MB.'; a key with a space or slash is refused as invalid.
A ninth concurrent helper call rejects with 'Too many requests are waiting. Wait for one to finish first.'
Unpublishing the app removes its saved values (table comment) and the link stops running.
inferred: Because the viewer is billed, a free-plan viewer may be refused; the exact plan list is unknown [inferred from evaluateManagedComputeAccess and acquireManagedTurnSlot plan-excluded, apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:87-92,150-160].
Local and own-key users cannot use AI inside published apps because the only model route is the managed one [inferred from apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:299-330].
proposed: [proposed] Align the database value check with the 4 MiB API limit so one number is owned in one place.
[proposed] Record in the repository whether migration 0391 is applied and drop the 'NOT YET APPLIED' header if so.
[proposed] Show the viewer a meter of their saved data against the 20 MiB cap.

steps.what_happens: The app script calls agi.complete or agi.storage; the frame builds a request and posts it to the parent page.
The parent checks the frame origin and source window, parses the request, and hands it to the runtime host.
The host requires a signed-in viewer, asks for AI consent if needed, then posts to our servers with a CSRF token and an idempotency key.
The server checks CSRF, account active, rate limit and request shape, then loads the runnable app by token under row-level security.
For AI: switch, connector gates, workspace policy, plan access, moderation, secret handling, route and policy gates, concurrency slot, usage reservation, model call.
The model call goes to the chosen provider's adapter and the answer text returns.
For storage: the server reads, upserts under a lock, deletes or lists rows in published_artifact_storage.
The response returns to the frame, which resolves or rejects the helper's promise.

data.what: Saved key-value text, personal (owner_user_id set) or shared (null)
data.synced: Server-held; every viewer who can run the app sees shared rows; personal rows only their owner
data.retained_or_deleted: Kept until the app deletes the key; deleted when the app is unpublished (table comment, apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql) or the profile is deleted (cascade, same file lines 3-18)

data.what: AI consent answer and allowed tools
data.retained_or_deleted: Kept until declined or storage cleared; a code change asks again (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:42-115)

data.what: Usage reservation and final record for each AI call
data.where_stored: managed usage tables, tagged with the app (published:<id>) per the 0391 header

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model route is chosen on the server from the viewer's plan and task type by the managed route admission, not by the app, and the provider key stays on our servers (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:299-330; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:211-244). When a run can reach Google user data, only routes that keep inputs out of training are allowed (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:205-210).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in viewer required; signed-out calls get a sign-in message (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/artifactRuntimeClient.ts:57; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/complete/__tests__/route.test.ts:449).
access_and_usage.permissions: Who may run an app: public, owner, workspace member or invited viewer, enforced by row-level security (apps/web/db/neon/0395_published_artifact_audience_revocation.sql:72-108). Shared storage is blocked for connector apps for non-owners (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:94-104). The workspace privacy-mode policy is checked for AI (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:136-148).
access_and_usage.subscription: AI is checked against the viewer's managed-compute access and plan turn limits (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:150-160,79-99). Connector use needs a plan with the artifact_connectors capability; which plans have it: unknown (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-connector-gate.ts:22-31). No plan check found for storage.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Prompt up to 100,000 characters, up to 10 connectors (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:3-4). AI route limit 30 per minute per user (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:359-363); storage 120 per minute (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:439-443). Output capped at 4,096 tokens (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:100). Each call reserves and records usage on the viewer (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:629-765). Per-app caps depend on migration 0391, applied state unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED (off unless set) (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-8). Connector release state coming_soon (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: The app cannot choose a model. Connector runs require a route with function calling (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:299-310).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Route and egress gates apply per provider (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:226-244). Named providers: none found in these files.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not available. Local and own-key sessions have no path into published-app AI; the owner preview refuses an app not made in a Cloud chat with 'Only an app made in a Managed Cloud chat can use AI and your connected apps.' (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:59-68). Free local inference does not apply here.

scenarios.name: AI switch off
steps: Leave AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED unset on a test environment.
Open a published html app whose button calls agi.complete('hi') while signed in.
Press the button.
scenarios.expected: The call rejects with 'AI in apps is not available yet.' and no usage is recorded.

scenarios.name: Viewer is billed
steps: Turn the switch on.
Publisher publishes an AI app; a different signed-in viewer opens it and allows AI.
Trigger one completion.
scenarios.expected: Text returns; the viewer's usage rises and the publisher's does not.

scenarios.name: Private versus shared storage
steps: Viewer A calls agi.storage.set('k','1') and set('s','2',true).
Viewer B opens the same link and reads both with get.
scenarios.expected: B gets null for k and '2' for s.

scenarios.name: Size and key limits
steps: Call storage.set with a value just over 4 MiB.
Call storage.set with a key containing a space.
scenarios.expected: First is refused as too large (413); second is refused as invalid (400).

scenarios.name: Signed out
steps: Open the link in a private window.
Trigger a helper.
scenarios.expected: The sign-in banner appears and the call rejects with a sign-in message.

scenarios.name: Chrome side panel
steps: In the Chrome extension, have a chat produce an html artifact that calls agi.complete.
Open it in the side panel preview.
scenarios.expected: The call rejects with the 'available once this app is published' message.

diagnostics: Error codes in JSON responses: artifact_ai_off, artifact_not_found, invalid_prompt, connectors_coming_soon, connectors_not_declared, shared_storage_with_connectors, storage_value_too_large, storage_limit_reached, concurrent_turn_limit_reached, concurrency_limiter_unavailable, model_unavailable (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts).
Log line '[artifact-runtime] content safety unread' and '[artifact-runtime] refresh not recorded' (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:187,294).
Table published_artifact_storage for saved rows; managed usage tables for AI usage.

gaps.gap: Desktop, mobile and Chrome cannot run AI or storage in a published app; they open the browser or refuse.
gaps.work_needed: Decide whether native surfaces host published apps or keep opening the web page; if they host, add a runtime host per surface.

gaps.gap: AI inside apps is off by default and tied to a security review.
gaps.work_needed: Finish the review, then set the switch; record the decision.

gaps.gap: Per-app cap migration 0391 is marked not applied in its own header while code calls it.
gaps.work_needed: Verify applied state with the migration status command and fix the header.

gaps.gap: No Local or own-key route for app AI; no user control for network destinations or secrets (brief S28.20, S28.21 missing).
gaps.work_needed: Product decision on whether app AI may use local models or the user's own key; add an explicit fork with consent if so.

gaps.gap: Draft line numbers for the frame (index.html:255-326, 353-370) are right, but the draft's 'viewer must be signed in' also depends on the page switch; the 5 MiB database check differs from the 4 MiB API limit.
gaps.work_needed: Pick one limit owner.

unknowns: Whether migration 0391 is applied in production.
Which plans carry the artifact_connectors capability and which plans may use AI in apps.
Whether the fallback frame (no sandbox origin configured) exposes the agi helpers.
Retention period of usage records for app AI calls.
Whether the AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED switch is on in production.

features.summary: Save an artifact's source as a file, or on web download every artifact in the panel as one zip. Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and the Chrome side panel can save a single artifact; only web builds a zip. CSV-style content is made spreadsheet-safe before saving.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person take generated code or documents out of AGI as a file on their own device. On web it also bundles all artifacts of the open panel into artifacts.zip (apps/web/features/chat/utils/downloadArtifacts.ts:104-131,157-164).
purpose.why_it_exists: To keep work portable and let it continue in other tools; the brief says the user can download the source and export a project archive (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/028-code-canvas-and-application-preview.md S28.24-S28.25).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who generated an artifact and wants the file; engineers who want the files in a folder.
problems_solved: Getting code out of a chat without copy and paste.
Getting several artifacts at once.
Spreadsheet formula injection when a model-chosen file is opened in a spreadsheet (apps/web/features/chat/utils/downloadArtifacts.ts:117).
use_cases: Web: open an HTML artifact and choose 'Download as HTML'.
Web: press 'Download all' to get artifacts.zip.
Mobile: open the artifact full screen and press Download to share the .html or .tsx file.
CLI: agi artifacts show <id> --out ./app.html.

where_to_find_it: Web: artifact preview download menu with items 'Download as HTML', 'Download source (.<language>)', 'Download as Markdown', plus 'Download as CSV', 'Download as SVG', 'Download as PDF', 'Download as Word (.docx)' where they apply (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2386-2412).

Web zip: artifacts panel button 'Download all' (aria-label 'Download all artifacts as zip'), shown only when the panel holds more than one artifact (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:732-749).

Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it uses the web controls (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). The internal Tauri build has 'Save a copy to the artifacts folder' (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/useDesktopArtifactActions.ts, id save-copy).
Mobile: full-screen artifact view button with accessibility label 'Download artifact' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1337-1339).
CLI: agi artifacts show <id> --out <path> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1371-1387).
VS Code: Artifacts list row actions 'Copy the content' and 'Save into the workspace' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/index.ts:97-107).

Chrome: side panel artifact toolbar copy and download buttons, label 'Download $FILE$' (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts:500-506; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:1370-1372).
prerequisites: An artifact exists in the chat or account.

CLI and VS Code need a signed-in Cloud account: the CLI refuses a non-managed session (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-373); VS Code shows a sign-in item when signed out (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactsTree.ts:100-105).
Zip: more than one artifact in the panel.
screens_and_controls: Web download menu items and 'Download all' button.
Mobile export sheet when more than one format exists (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:686-700).
CLI flags --out, --open, --copy, --json (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1371-1387).
VS Code save dialog titled 'Save "<title>" into the workspace' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts:192-195).
journey: 1. Open the artifact.
2. Choose the download or save control for your app.
3. On web, the file is built in the browser and the browser saves it; for zip a toast says 'Preparing artifact download…' then 'Artifact download ready' (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:737-741).
4. On mobile the file is made and the system share sheet opens (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:686-722).
5. In the CLI the path of the written file is printed.
6. In VS Code a save dialog opens, the file is written and shown in the editor.
feedback_and_outputs: Web zip: toast error 'Could not download artifacts' on failure (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:741).
Mobile: haptic on success; alert 'Download failed' on error (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:723-727).
CLI: prints the path, or JSON with id, path, opened (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3954-3969).

features.summary: Take generated code into a real coding tool. VS Code can save an artifact into a folder with a save dialog. The CLI can write an artifact to a file and open it in the computer's default app. Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome have no hand-off to a coding workspace.

purpose.what_it_does: VS Code reads an artifact from the account and writes it into a folder the user chooses, then opens it (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts:163-208). The CLI writes it to a path, optionally opening it with the default app (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3910-3969).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants generated code to be openable in a real coding workspace to keep developing it (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/028-code-canvas-and-application-preview.md S28.26).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who start an app in chat and finish it in an editor or terminal.
problems_solved: Moving generated code from chat into a project folder without copy and paste.
use_cases: In VS Code, press the save icon on an artifact and place it in the repo.
In a terminal, run agi artifacts show <id> --out ./src/ then edit it.

where_to_find_it: VS Code: Artifacts list in the AGI Code sidebar; row action 'Save into the workspace'; command title 'Code: Save Artifact into Workspace' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/index.ts:103-107; apps/extension-vscode/package.json command list). The command is hidden from the palette.
CLI: agi artifacts show <id> --out <path> [--open]; agi artifacts open <id> opens a browser page (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1371-1397).

Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome: none found. The web preview has 'Duplicate' (a copy inside AGI) and 'Start Work', whose target was not established (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2503-2530).
prerequisites: Signed-in Cloud account (VS Code sign-in item when signed out: apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactsTree.ts:100-105; CLI: apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-380).

2. Choose Save into the workspace, or run show --out.
3. Pick or confirm the target path.
4. The file is written; VS Code opens it in an editor; the CLI prints the path and can open the default app.

features.summary: Publish an artifact to a shareable link, change who can open it (anyone, only invited people, only the workspace) and take it down. Works on web, mobile and CLI for Cloud artifacts; the internal Tauri desktop only saves a local file. VS Code and Chrome cannot publish. There is no separate production version.

purpose.what_it_does: Copies an artifact's content to our servers under a random link at /shared-artifact/<token>, records a version, lets the owner set the audience and unpublish (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:42-127; apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:421-500).
purpose.why_it_exists: So an app, page or document made in chat can be shared or run by other people. The brief says the user can publish the app to a shareable preview link (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/028-code-canvas-and-application-preview.md S28.27).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners of Cloud chats who want to share; viewers who open the link.
problems_solved: Sharing a working app or page without sending files.
Limiting access to a workspace or invited people.
Taking a link away again.
use_cases: Publish a landing page and send the link.
Limit an internal tool to the workspace.
Invite named people to view a draft.
Unpublish a link shared by mistake.

where_to_find_it: Web: preview toolbar button 'Publish' (aria-label 'Publish artifact to a public link'); after publishing a bar with 'Copy link' and a selector labelled 'Who can open this' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2915-2930,3020-3040).

Web unpublish and history: Settings, Shared links, section 'Published artifacts', buttons 'Unpublish' and 'History' with 'Put live' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx:442-451,615-617,645-700; SharedLinksSection.tsx:502). The panel has no unpublish control (no match in ArtifactPreview.tsx).

Mobile: full-screen artifact button 'Publish artifact to a public link' or 'Republish artifact link'; audience choices 'Anyone with the link' and 'Everyone in this workspace (N)'; button 'Unpublish artifact' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1319-1325; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/PublishedArtifactControls.tsx:94-100,216).
CLI: agi artifacts publish, published, audience, unpublish (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1399-1427).

Desktop: the public Desktop shows the web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5); the internal Tauri build only exports a local file and injects no cloud publisher (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts:1-17).

VS Code: lists published artifacts and opens a published page ('Open the published artifact'); no publish action (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/index.ts:109-114). Chrome: no publish control found (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts).
prerequisites: The artifact was made in a Cloud chat; Local and own-key artifacts are refused with 'This artifact was created in <mode> mode. Publishing uploads it to AGI managed cloud, so it is unavailable in this privacy mode. Download the artifact instead.' (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifacts.ts:256-276).
Signed in. Mobile also needs Cloud mode on: 'Switch to AGI Cloud to publish' (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:731-746).

screens_and_controls: Publish button, link bar, 'Copy link', audience selector and confirmation dialogs.

2. The page sends the content to the publish route; the new link is copied: 'Published · link copied to clipboard' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1240-1246).

steps.what_happens: The app checks the artifact came from a Cloud chat and a publisher exists; otherwise it returns a reason and copies the source.
The client posts artifact id, title, kind, language, content and chat id to the publish route.
The server checks CSRF and rate limit, validates, runs the sharing gate, moderation and outbound inspection.

Audience change goes through PATCH with workspace and connector checks.
A viewer opens the link; the server reads the artifact by token (public, workspace, invited) and renders the page.

features.summary: Step through earlier versions of an artifact, see what changed from the previous version, and restore an older one as a new latest version. Web and mobile do all three; the internal Tauri desktop restores only. Web Settings can also put an older published version live. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps each saved version of an artifact, lets the person view one, compare it with the version just before it, and restore it; the restored content is appended so the versions between it and the latest survive (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1008-1030; apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/store.ts:358-381).
purpose.why_it_exists: So an edit or a regenerate that went wrong can be undone without losing work. The brief wants version comparison and rollback (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/028-code-canvas-and-application-preview.md S28.29-S28.30).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone editing or regenerating artifacts; owners who published a link and want an older version live.
problems_solved: Undoing a bad edit.
Seeing what a new version changed.
Putting an earlier published version back on the live link.
use_cases: Web: open the version chip, view version 2, choose Restore.

CLI, VS Code, Chrome: none found.

features.summary: On web, a viewer can press 'Save a copy to my chats' on a shared app to get their own editable copy in a new chat. A viewer's own connected accounts can be used by a shared app after they allow it, but connectors are switched off today (coming soon). Other apps have neither.

Viewer connected apps: the app asks to use the viewer's own connected apps; the viewer allows tool by tool; calls run with the viewer's connections, not the publisher's (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/connectors/route.ts:55-84).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a viewer can keep working on someone else's creation, and so a shared app that reads connected apps reads the viewer's own accounts, never the publisher's (brief S28.31, S28.32).
purpose.who_uses_it: Viewers of a published app, signed in or not.
problems_solved: Starting from someone else's app without retyping it.
Letting a shared app act on the viewer's data only with the viewer's consent.
use_cases: Open a shared calculator and press 'Save a copy to my chats' to adapt it.
Open a shared inbox tool, allow it to read your connected mail (when connectors are released).

where_to_find_it: Web only: header of the published page at /shared-artifact/<token>: button 'Save a copy to my chats' (while working 'Copying…') (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:221-231).

prerequisites: Copy: sign in (signed out, the button sends you to sign in and back: PublishedArtifactView.tsx:147-150).

steps.what_happens: The viewer presses 'Save a copy to my chats'; the page checks sign-in and builds a request authority tied to the session.
The page posts to create a conversation, then posts one assistant message with the code fenced.
The page verifies the saved message equals what was sent, adds the artifact to the local store and opens the chat.
For connectors: the page lists the viewer's connections through the connectors route.
A completion that names connectors is refused while connectors are unreleased; otherwise it runs a tool loop with the viewer's connections.
Tool calls reach the viewer's connected services.

aliases: Spreadsheet output format (composer Output menu, label 'Spreadsheet')
features.summary: A workbook made by the assistant has named sheets, one tab each, with strict name rules. Web, desktop (hosted web), mobile and the Tauri build can show the tabs read-only. Title and author metadata are not written, and adding, renaming, copying or deleting sheets in the product is not built, by founder decision.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the assistant build an Excel (.xlsx) file with several named sheets, and lets the apps show those sheets as tabs when a workbook is opened in chat. A 'title' field is required by the tool but is not written into the file (managed-office-file-service.ts:154; managed-office-file-service.ts:766-789).
purpose.why_it_exists: People ask AI assistants for multi-sheet workbooks (for example Sales and Costs) and expect the file to open in Excel with the right tabs. The brief also lists in-app tab, title and sheet-management items (S29.01-S29.03) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/029-spreadsheet-and-data-analysis-workspace.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who asks the chat for a spreadsheet file, and anyone who opens a workbook the assistant made or a workbook they attached.
problems_solved: The file opens with the sheet names asked for instead of one default sheet (managed-workbook-builder.ts:203-206).
Bad or repeated sheet names are refused before a broken file is made (managed-office-file-service.ts:96-105,159-163).
A person can switch sheets inside the chat preview without leaving the app (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:35-70).
use_cases: Ask for 'a budget workbook with Income and Costs sheets' and download the .xlsx.
Open an attached workbook in the chat preview and click the tab of another sheet.
On the phone, open a workbook the assistant created and swipe between sheet tabs.

Web preview: sheet tab strip with accessible name 'Worksheets' (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:46-49).
CLI, VS Code: nothing found.

Tab strip over the grid, one tab per sheet; shown only when the workbook has more than one sheet (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:75; TabularGridView.tsx:93-95).
Mobile tab list labelled with the sheet count, for example '3 sheets in this workbook' (TabularGridView.tsx:97-101).

Describe the workbook and name the sheets.
The server forces the file tool for this turn when the model accepts forced tool choice (request-processor.ts:6649-6655).

A one or two sentence reply naming the file (chat-output-format.ts:chatOutputFormatInstruction, lines 23-30).

working: Named sheets: names are 1 to 31 characters, no \ / ? * [ ] :, unique ignoring case, 1 to 20 sheets, 1 to 20,000 rows of at most 200 cells (managed-office-file-service.ts:96-105,155-164,103).
Workbook writer writes one sheet part and one workbook.xml entry per sheet, in the given order (managed-workbook-builder.ts:197-209,240-241).
A second uniqueness check runs on the finished package, ignoring case and surrounding spaces (managed-office-preservation.ts:311-326,352-353).
Read-only sheet tabs in the web and desktop-hosted preview (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:35-70,73-88; ArtifactPreview.tsx:1836-1870).
Read-only sheet tabs on mobile (TabularGridView.tsx:93-134; WorkbookFileView.tsx:109-175).
The reader keeps at most 50 sheets (workbook-sheets.ts:13,302).
Editing an attached workbook by cell edits keeps the other parts untouched (managed-office-file-service.ts:165-184; managed-office-preservation.ts:1364).
incomplete: The tool's 'title' is required and validated but never reaches the file: generateXlsx passes only sheets to buildWorkbook (managed-office-file-service.ts:154,766-789; managed-workbook-builder.ts:167).
No author, description or document-properties part is written (managed-workbook-builder.ts:172-253 lists every part written).
disconnected_or_disabled: Tauri desktop code can write title, author, subject and company and several sheets (create_excel.rs:6-12,57-68), but the tool entry point uses create_simple, which writes one sheet and sets the title to the sheet name (create_excel.rs:161-191; document_tools.rs:229-272). Tauri is retained internal code (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Tauri workbook editing refuses every edit variant (edit_excel.rs:94-130, tests).
not_available: Add, rename, duplicate, delete a sheet in an open workbook on any app: no code found. Founder decision lists S29.01-S29.04 among features the leaders do not offer and that are not built (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:73,119-123).
CLI and VS Code: no xlsx creation or sheet view found; the CLI only reads spreadsheet text (apps/cli/src/documents.rs:569-584).
Chrome extension: no office or workbook code in apps/extension/src found by search.

A one-sheet workbook shows no tab strip.

features.summary: A read-only grid exists. Web and the hosted desktop show a keyboard-navigable table with a sticky header, single-cell select and copy; mobile shows a grid with a sticky header, tap select and copy. Typing into cells, a formula bar, range selection, a freeze command and column resizing do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows tabular data and workbook sheets as a grid in chat. A person can pick one cell and copy it, and sort by a column. Editing, formula bar, freeze choice and resize are not built.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to see and check the numbers an assistant produced without opening Excel. The brief also asks for editing items S29.04-S29.06, S29.11 and S29.12 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/029-spreadsheet-and-data-analysis-workspace.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who gets a table, CSV or workbook in a chat.
problems_solved: Numbers can be checked in place, with the header staying in view (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:227; TabularGridView.tsx:311).
Large tables do not freeze the page: only 500 rows are drawn (tabular.ts:78).
Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can move through cells (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:134-155; keyboard test).
use_cases: Open a CSV result and copy one cell value.
Move through a table with arrow keys and copy with Ctrl or Command C.

features.summary: The assistant can write real formulas into a workbook. The server then recalculates them in a sandbox and refuses to deliver a workbook with errors or no result. Formula explanations, named-range creation and in-app error flags are not built. The viewer shows 'not calculated' for formulas with no stored result.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns any cell text that starts with = into a real spreadsheet formula, recalculates the workbook so every formula has a result, and refuses files whose formulas fail.
purpose.why_it_exists: A file with live formulas is more useful than pasted numbers, but a formula with no stored result shows blank in many viewers. The server check makes sure the delivered file has results (managed-office-preservation.ts:328-362).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who ask for budgets, totals or models in a spreadsheet; reviewers of generated workbooks.
problems_solved: Formulas stay formulas, not text (managed-workbook-builder.ts:70-71).
Formula errors are caught before delivery (managed-office-preservation.ts:346-351).
Formulas that reach outside the workbook are refused (managed-office-preservation.ts:757-775).
use_cases: Ask for a sheet whose total column uses =SUM(B2:B5).
Edit one input cell in an attached workbook and have dependent formulas recalculate.
Open a workbook from another tool and see 'not calculated' where no result was stored.

settings: Office execution availability is server configuration; its name is not recorded here beyond the chat template setting AGI_E2B_CHAT_TEMPLATE (chat-template.ts:1).

working: A cell starting with = becomes <f> (managed-workbook-builder.ts:70-71).
If any worksheet contains <f, the server requires a sandbox executor and recalculates (managed-office-file-service.ts:1000-1013).

features.summary: Planned tools to total rows by a key (pivot or grouped summary), preview what a data-cleaning step would change, and profile a dataset for missing values, duplicate rows and column types. purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person see grouped totals, a before-change preview of cleaning steps, and a per-column profile (missing values, duplicates, inferred types) of a dataset. Today nothing in the code does this as a dedicated feature. [inferred from the brief and from searches that found no matching code]
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists these as parts of a spreadsheet and data-analysis workspace (docs/product/requirements.md names data analysis among the leaders' features) (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:183). A person should check data quality before trusting an answer.

acceptance_criteria: Given a dataset, a summary lists each column with its count of missing values and the counts match the data.

A cleaning step shows the exact rows it would change before any change; cancelling leaves the data unchanged.

Each of the above works on every app the brief lists, or the app is stated as not applicable.

features.summary: When asked to change an attached Excel workbook, the server edits only the explicit cells named, and each edit must match an expected current value or the whole edit fails. The person gets a new file with a preservation receipt. There is no preview of cell changes and no accept or reject per range on any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the assistant change specific cells of an attached .xlsx and return a new file, refusing edits when the cell is not what the assistant expected or the file changed (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-preservation.ts:1364-1487).
purpose.why_it_exists: Changing a person's workbook must not silently damage it. The brief also requires a preview and per-range accept or reject, which is not built (briefs S29.31, S29.32).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who attach a workbook and ask for a targeted fix, such as correcting a value or formula.
problems_solved: Rewriting a whole workbook risks losing formatting and unrelated parts.
The assistant may edit the wrong cell; the expected-value check stops that.
use_cases: Change B4 from 100 to 120 in the Budget sheet.
Replace a formula in one cell.
Fix several labelled cells in one request.

where_to_find_it: Web: no dedicated control. Attach an .xlsx and ask in chat; the Output menu row 'Output' offers Document, Presentation, Spreadsheet (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:190, 975-1000; labels at packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/skills.ts:22-26).
Desktop: same as Web via the hosted app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

Mobile: the 'Create file' row with Document, Presentation, Spreadsheet (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:1182-1215). Whether a mobile attachment can be edited: tool takes attachments of the turn, so likely yes; not confirmed [inferred].
Chrome: no office control found in the side panel code; the server can still infer creation from the wording (request-processor.ts:993-998).
Voice: the live-voice tool list offers the tool without attachments, so no workbook can be edited by voice (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts:399) [inferred].
CLI and VS Code: none found.
prerequisites: Cloud mode, signed in, a streaming request, and a model with tool support (request-processor.ts:5460-5493).
An attached .xlsx under the size limit with a name that is a plain file name (managed-office-file-service.ts:237-247).
Not a free-offering request (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/free-quota.ts:126).
screens_and_controls: Attach button, the Output or Create file choice, and chat. No preview screen and no accept or reject buttons.
journey: 1. Attach the workbook.
2. Ask for the change in chat (words like create, make, export plus excel or spreadsheet can switch Office creation on, request-processor.ts:914-916, 993-998).
3. The model calls create_office_file with format xlsx and a source that holds the file name, its digest and a list of edits (sheet, cell, expected, value).
4. The server checks the file, the sheet, the cell and the expected value, applies the edits, recalculates formulas, and stores the new file.
5. The person sees a file card in chat; the verification receipt records changed parts.
feedback_and_outputs: A new file with the requested name (original stays); a receipt with input hash, changed parts and unchanged part count (managed-office-preservation.ts:1489-1510). Whether the web UI displays the receipt: unknown.
On failure the model receives the error text and tells the person.
settings: Output format choice per message; none specific to edit safety.

working: Edit engine: finds the one attached workbook by file name and type, checks its digest, maps sheet names to parts, and edits only existing explicit cells (managed-office-preservation.ts:1364-1487).
Mismatch of expected value fails: 'A workbook cell differs from the expected value; refresh the source before editing.' (managed-office-preservation.ts:1456-1458).
Refuses shared, array and spill formula cells, a cell edited twice, and inserting a new cell (managed-office-preservation.ts:1409-1430, 1471-1474).
Recalculation of formulas needs a sandbox; without one the request fails rather than return stale values (managed-office-file-service.ts:1007-1014).
A preservation receipt requires only worksheet parts changed (managed-office-preservation.ts:1489-1510).
Tool offers each attached workbook's digest to the model (managed-office-file-service.ts:237-247, 283-287).
Result persisted as a chat file and emitted (tool-loop.ts:2569-2607).
incomplete: Draft said the cap is 'per schema description'; the schema allows 1000 edits per request (managed-office-file-service.ts edits max 1000).
Edits are one request, all or nothing; a person cannot take some and drop others.
disconnected_or_disabled: Voice offers the Office tool with no attachments, so editing is not reachable there (live-voice-tools.ts:399) [inferred].
not_available: Preview of changed cells (S29.31) and accept or reject each range (S29.32): all six apps. No diff-of-cells UI found; the VS Code proposed-change review is for code files only (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/permissions/proposedChangeReview.ts).

established.statement: Before the assistant changes a sheet, the product previews the proposed cell changes.
The user can accept or reject each proposed range change.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; an agent never destroys user data and keeps a checkpoint.
Artifacts keep versions with compare and restore.

acceptance_criteria: A requested edit with a wrong expected value fails and the original is unchanged.
A changed attachment (different digest) fails with the 'source workbook changed' message.
Editing a spill or array formula cell is refused.
Only the named cells differ between old and new files; other parts are byte-identical.
With preview built, every changed cell is listed before any file is produced.
With per-range accept built, rejecting a range leaves those cells as they were.
The original workbook is never overwritten.
inferred: A preview can be built from the same edit list the model already sends (sheet, cell, expected, value) [inferred].
Receipts should be shown to the person [inferred from AGENTS.md section 9].
proposed: [proposed] Show a cell diff card from the edit list and wait for approval before generating.
[proposed] Split the edit list into ranges so each can be accepted or rejected.

features.summary: Ask the assistant for a Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or CSV file and it is built on our servers and attached to the chat as a download. A spreadsheet or table in chat can also be downloaded as CSV on web, and on mobile. Built on web, desktop, mobile and Chrome; missing on CLI and VS Code.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates real files (docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf, csv) from chat content and lets the person download them; also exports tables and spreadsheet artifacts to CSV with spreadsheet-formula protection (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts:126-207; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/tabular.ts:380-480).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need analysis in a file they can send, open in Office or import elsewhere (briefs S29.34, S29.35, S29.38, S29.39).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone turning an analysis into a workbook, report, deck or CSV.
problems_solved: Copying chat text into Office is slow and loses structure.
CSV with commas or line breaks breaks without quoting.
A cell starting with = can run as a formula when opened (guarded in client exports).
use_cases: Ask for a quarterly workbook with a chart and formulas.
Ask for a Word report with a table.
Ask for a slide deck of key findings.
Download a table in chat as CSV.

where_to_find_it: Web: composer plus menu row 'Output' with Document, Presentation, Spreadsheet (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:190, 975-1000; labels packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/skills.ts:22-26). Spreadsheet artifact: Download button (aria-label 'Download artifact', title 'Download') then 'Download as CSV' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:3472-3487; also a menu entry at 2383). Generated files show 'Download file' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2370-2379).

Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so the same (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). The Tauri build has its own artifact adapter that uses the same CSV-safe export (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts).

Mobile: 'Create file' row in the add-to-chat sheet with Document, Presentation, Spreadsheet (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:1182-1215). Tables in messages have a download button labelled 'Download table as CSV' and 'Copy table' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx:331, 376).

Chrome side panel: file cards with open and download buttons using the localized labels spAnswerFileOpen and spAnswerFileDownload (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/generatedFiles.ts:280-310; artifactPanel.ts:970-995). No output-format picker found.
CLI and VS Code: missing (brief); the server does not infer Office creation differently for them but excludes implicit sandbox for them (request-processor.ts:928).
prerequisites: Cloud mode, signed in, streaming turn, tool-capable model (request-processor.ts:5460-5493).
Not a free-offering request (free-quota.ts:126).
For formulas in xlsx or render checks: sandbox execution available (managed-office-file-service.ts:1007-1014).
screens_and_controls: Output or Create file choice (Document, Presentation, Spreadsheet).
File card with Download.
Artifact download menu: 'Download as CSV', 'Download as HTML', 'Download as Markdown', source download (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2383-2395).

journey: 1. Choose an output type in the menu, or just write 'create a spreadsheet of ...'. The server also turns Office creation on from create-like verbs plus words like excel, spreadsheet, slide deck, pdf or csv (request-processor.ts:914-916, 993-998).
2. Send. The assistant calls create_office_file with fields for the chosen format.
3. The server validates, builds the file (and recalculates formulas if present), and stores it.
4. A file card appears in chat.
5. Tap or click Download (Chrome: the download button saves via the browser).
6. For a table already in chat: open the artifact Download menu on web, or tap 'Download table as CSV' on mobile.

established.statement: The user can export data or a sheet as a downloadable .xlsx workbook.
The user can download tabular data as a CSV file.
From an analysis, the user can get a formatted report document (docx or pdf).
From an analysis, the user can get a slide deck (pptx).
Generated documents, spreadsheets and presentations are versioned objects with preview, edit, export and reopen behaviour.

features.summary: In the Presentation workspace, a person asks the assistant to change one slide. Web has an 'Ask about slide' box, a 'Rewrite slide' button and a selection toolbar ('Edit with AI'). Mobile has the same ask and rewrite. Each sends a chat message that tells the assistant to change only that slide. Nothing checks the reply.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a request about one slide (or a selected passage) into a normal chat message that names the deck, the slide number and the slide text, and tells the assistant to leave every other slide as it is. The reply becomes a new version of the deck. (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/deck-request.ts:14-42)
purpose.why_it_exists: So people can improve one slide without regenerating the whole deck. The brief wants selection edits, single-slide rewrite, single-slide regenerate and whole-deck restructuring (S30.20-S30.23). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/030-presentation-workspace.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person who has a deck open in the artifact panel on web, or in the full-screen deck viewer on mobile, inside a chat.
problems_solved: Rewriting one weak slide without losing the others
Changing the tone or length of one passage
Not having to copy slide text into a new chat message by hand
use_cases: Open slide 3, click 'Ask about slide', type 'add a number', send.
Click 'Rewrite slide' to tighten the current slide.
Select a sentence on a slide and choose 'Make shorter' in the selection toolbar.
On mobile, tap 'Ask about slide 2', type a change and send.

established.statement: The user selects part of a slide and asks the AI to change only that part (S30.20).
The user asks the AI to rewrite one slide and only that slide changes (S30.21).
The user regenerates one slide while the rest of the deck is kept (S30.22).
The user can have the AI restructure a whole existing deck: reorder, merge, split sections (S30.23).
Presentations are versioned objects.

acceptance_criteria: On web, with an editable latest-version deck, 'Ask about slide' opens a box labelled 'What should change on slide N?' for the slide on screen.
Pressing 'Rewrite slide' sends a chat message that contains the slide text and the rewrite instruction, and the form closes.
The sent message names slide N of M and says to keep every other slide, title and order.
After a hand edit the message also carries the current deck (up to 24,000 characters).
When sending is refused, the toast 'The change request was not sent. Try again.' shows and the typed text is kept.
On an older, read-only version, no Ask button appears.
On mobile, 'Ask about slide N' sends the same request text and 'Rewrite slide' uses the shared instruction.
inferred: A reply that changes other slides should be detected or discouraged, because the brief says only that slide changes [inferred from S30.21].
Local and own-key chats should handle the request the same as Cloud, because it is an ordinary chat message [inferred from WebChatPage.tsx:6097-6101].
proposed: [proposed] After the reply, compare the new deck with the old one and show which slides changed; warn if slides other than N changed.
[proposed] Add a 'Restructure deck' action with its own request builder and a preview before saving.
[proposed] Add Ask about slide to desktop, Chrome and VS Code deck views or mark them out of scope.

features.summary: A deck is an artifact with versions: every save is a new version, older ones are read-only and can be restored. On web a deck can be saved as a template ('Save as template'), started from 'New from template', and published as a web page link with an audience choice. features.summary: A person attaches a PDF to a chat in the Web app (or the mobile app) and asks for a summary or an answer. Web sends the page text with [Page n] labels, page images for scans, and the raw PDF to models that accept PDFs. Mobile Local reads text on the device. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no path.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a chat model read a PDF the person attached. On Web the server turns the file into labelled page text and page images, and also marks the original PDF so a model that takes PDFs natively can get it whole (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts:680-752). Summaries and page answers are produced by the chat model itself; no separate summary code was found [inferred from reading the PDF path].
purpose.why_it_exists: Leading assistants let people ask questions about a PDF. The brief requires summary, question answering and page-specific questions (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/031-pdf-and-document-transformation-products.md S31.04-S31.06). A code comment says a route with no document channel would otherwise fail the turn (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:147-154).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who attaches a PDF in chat on Web, the Electron Desktop (which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5) or the Mobile app.
problems_solved: Reading a long report without opening it
Finding what one page says about a topic
Asking about a scanned file that has no text
Asking about a PDF on a model that cannot take PDF files natively
use_cases: Attach a contract and ask 'summarise this'
Attach a report and ask 'what does page 4 say about fees'
Attach a scanned letter and ask who sent it
On a phone in Local mode, attach a text-based PDF and ask for key points

features.summary: Annotating a PDF (notes, drawings, highlights, comments saved with the file) is not built on any AGI Workforce app. The apps can read PDFs for chat and show them in a viewer, and can create new text-only PDFs, but nothing marks up an existing PDF.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person draw notes on a PDF, highlight text and attach comments, and keep them in the file. Today it does nothing: no code for it was found (rg for annotation and highlight terms in apps and packages returned only unrelated hits such as a code editor's state annotation in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactCodeEditor.tsx:13,40).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S31.11 and S31.12 set it as a required capability so AGI Workforce can match PDF markup that leading assistants and PDF tools offer (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/031-pdf-and-document-transformation-products.md). The product contract also lists an 'Edit/annotate capability' per file viewer and 'Annotation/edit request into the conversation' (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:499,517).
purpose.who_uses_it: Would be used by students, lawyers, reviewers and managers who mark up a contract, paper or report. No one can use it today.
problems_solved: Keeping review notes inside the PDF instead of in a separate chat or file.
Sharing a marked-up PDF with someone who does not use AGI Workforce.
use_cases: Highlight a clause in a contract and add a comment for the other side.
Draw an arrow and a note on a floor-plan PDF on a phone.
Ask the assistant to highlight every mention of a term and comment on each.

prerequisites: None, because there is nothing to use. Reading a PDF in chat needs an attached file and a chat model (see F031 reading features, not covered here).
screens_and_controls: No annotation toolbar, highlight tool, comment box or save-annotated-PDF control exists on any app. Exact labels: none found in the code.

purpose.who_uses_it: Would be used by archivists, public bodies, schools and people using screen readers. No one can use it today.
problems_solved: Cannot search or copy text from a scan.
Screen readers cannot read a PDF without tags.
use_cases: Make a scanned contract searchable.
Create a tagged report PDF a screen reader can navigate.
Archive a stack of scans as searchable files.

The Docusign setup uses the app's integration key and secret, redirect URL https://agiworkforce.com/api/connectors/oauth/callback, and scope 'signature' (plus two more only if the accounts have those products).

steps.what_happens: Person opens the connectors list and chooses Docusign on web (or the hosted web app inside Desktop).
The server checks release state, email confirmation, plan and workspace policy; today the first check refuses.
The server starts OAuth using operator credentials and a provider descriptor, and sends the person to Docusign to sign in.
Docusign returns to the callback; the server exchanges the code and stores the grant.
In a chat turn the server offers the connector's tools to the model, calls Docusign's tool server at its address with the stored grant, and returns results.
Docusign creates the envelope and sends the signature request to the recipient.

features.summary: On the web app, a person turns on 'Request edits', clicks an element in an HTML design, types what to change, and the model gets a request about only that element. For a picked image, 'Replace this image' swaps the source with an uploaded picture. Direct text editing in the design is not found.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person select part of a rendered design, then send a selection-based change request to the model (buildArtifactEditRequest in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-edit-request.ts:17-40) or replace one image locally (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/design/design-edits.ts:27-58).
purpose.why_it_exists: So small changes do not need a long chat description and do not disturb the rest of the design. Items S32.05, S32.14, S32.18 require it; S32.06 requires direct text editing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web chat users with an HTML artifact open in the panel.
problems_solved: Describing which element to change in words.
Model rewriting parts that should stay.
Swapping a picture without asking the model.
use_cases: Click the hero heading and ask for a shorter line.
Pick a photo and replace it with an uploaded image.
Pick a button and ask for a different colour.

where_to_find_it: Web: artifact panel header button 'Request edits' (aria-label), and a 'Request edits' item in the more menu on narrow panels (ArtifactPreview.tsx:527,2273-2280,2845-2858).
Desktop: hosted web app shows the same [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5].
Chrome: the brief marks S32.06 'unverified'; the side panel has artifact code but no picker was found (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts).
Mobile, CLI, VS Code: no picker code found.
prerequisites: Panel variant, preview tab, latest version, no changes view, no open source draft, no render error, non-empty content, onRequestEdits present, and a configured sandbox origin (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2089-2099).
screens_and_controls: Bottom pill 'Select content and ask for changes' with 'Cancel'; after a pick, a field 'Describe the change...' with a button 'Send the change request'; for a picked img, a button 'Replace this image'; optionally 'Comment on this element' (ArtifactEditRequestLayer.tsx:12-17,139).
journey: Open an HTML artifact in the panel.
Press 'Request edits'.
Click an element in the preview; the layer reports the pick.
Type the change and press the check button, or press 'Replace this image' and choose a file.
For a text request the model replies with a full updated artifact; for an image the new version is stored at once.
feedback_and_outputs: Error toast 'The change request was not sent. Try again.' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2129).
Success toast 'Image replaced. The previous version is in the history.' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2146).
Error toast 'That image could not be found in the source. Ask for the change instead.' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2142).
Image errors: 'Choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image.', 'That image is too large to place. Try a smaller one.', SVG refused (image-embed.ts:6-12).
settings: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN must be set for the picker (artifact-sandbox.ts:158).

working: Picker mode is posted to the sandbox and a pick returns a selection (SandboxedIframe.tsx:260-267,345).
The change request text contains title, CSS path, text and markup and asks for a full updated artifact (artifact-edit-request.ts:17-40).
Instruction is trimmed and cut to 2000 characters (artifact-edit-request.ts:9-13).
Image replacement edits only the picked img src, drops srcset, stores a new version (design-edits.ts:27-58; ArtifactPreview.tsx:2134-2156).
Images are resized to at most 1600 px and 600000 characters, as a data URL (image-embed.ts:1-3,40-60).
incomplete: Direct text editing of design text on the canvas: not found. A separate document edit mode exists (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2158 startDocumentEdit) but it is not a design-element editor.
Replace image appears only when the artifact is HTML and source is editable (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3178).
disconnected_or_disabled: Whole feature is off when no sandbox origin is configured (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2099).
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code: no picker code found. Chrome: not found.

features.summary: Comments on an artifact in the Web chat side panel (also the public Desktop window, which shows the web app). A reader can comment on selected text, a slide, a picked element of an HTML design or the whole artifact, reply, resolve, delete, and send open comments to the assistant as an edit request. Element comments save but draw no pin.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a signed-in person leave notes on an artifact (document, deck or HTML design) in the Web side panel. A note can point at a quoted passage, a slide, a picked element of a rendered design, or the whole artifact. Notes form threads that can be replied to, resolved, reopened and deleted, and open threads can be handed to the assistant as one edit request. (comments/ArtifactCommentsPanel.tsx:228; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-comments.ts:9-29)
purpose.why_it_exists: Migration 0369 says artifacts had no way to leave a note on a passage, a slide or an element and come back to it, or to hand a batch of notes to the assistant as edit requests. (apps/web/db/neon/0369_artifact_comments.sql:4-7) The brief item S32.17 asks that the user can pin comments to a spot or element on the design. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/032-design-workspace.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: A person reviewing their own generated design, deck or document on Web or in the Desktop window that shows the hosted web app [inferred from ARCHITECTURE.md:51]. Comments belong to one account; row-level security keeps other accounts out, so this is a personal review tool, not multi-reviewer sharing. (apps/web/db/neon/0369_artifact_comments.sql:41-47)
problems_solved: Keeping review notes attached to the passage or element they are about instead of in chat text.
Turning a list of notes into one precise edit request to the model.
Coming back later to see which notes are still open.
use_cases: Select a sentence in a document, choose Comment, type a note, later press Resolve.
Pick a button in an HTML design with Request edits, choose Comment on this element, describe the issue.
Add three notes, press Ask AI to apply all 3 open comments and let the assistant revise the artifact.
Comment on slide 4 of a deck from the slide strip.

journey: Open an artifact in the side panel.
Select text and press Comment, or press Request edits, pick an element and press Comment on this element, or use the slide control, or open Comments and type into 'Comment on the whole artifact'.
The Comments panel opens with the anchor quoted and a composer 'Add a comment'.
Type the note and press Comment; it is saved to the account and appears as a thread.
Optionally Reply, Resolve, or Delete (a confirmation names what is lost).
Optionally press Ask AI to apply on one thread, or Ask AI to apply all N open comments; the panel sends an edit request to the chat and shows a toast.
feedback_and_outputs: Toast 'Sent the comment to the assistant' or 'Sent N comments to the assistant' (ArtifactCommentsPanel.tsx:271-284).
Toast 'The comment was not saved' on failure; 'The change request was not sent. Try again.' when the chat will not take the request (ArtifactCommentsPanel.tsx:263-286).
Open text anchors are highlighted in the rendered content (use-comment-highlights.ts:110-135).
Delete dialog 'Delete this comment?' naming the anchor and the number of replies (ArtifactCommentsPanel.tsx:396-400).
settings: No user setting found. Limits: 4000 characters per comment, 500 comments per artifact (artifact-comments.ts:3; artifact-comment-service.ts:10).

working: Create, list, reply, resolve, reopen and delete comments through three routes with CSRF check, rate limit and per-user row security. (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/[artifactId]/comments/route.ts:32-78; .../[commentId]/route.ts:34-76)
Four anchor kinds: text with surrounding context, slide, element (selector, text, x, y), whole artifact. (artifact-comments.ts:9-29)
Text anchors are located again with the surrounding text, so a repeated phrase picks the right occurrence, and are highlighted with the browser highlight API. (use-comment-highlights.ts:66-135)
Admission of a new comment takes a per-user-per-artifact lock and refuses past 500. (artifact-comment-service.ts:86-107)
Client keeps a cache and merges a slow read with comments saved meanwhile. (artifact-comments-client.ts:53-140)
Comments are in account export and in account erasure. (apps/web/app/api/user/export/route.ts:2269; apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:50)
incomplete: Element comments store selector, text and x/y but nothing draws a pin on the design; the highlight hook skips non-text anchors and scrollToAnchor returns false for them, so pressing the quote shows 'That passage is not on screen in this view.' (use-comment-highlights.ts:120,137-152; ArtifactPreview.tsx:3158-3162)
Slide anchors have no on-slide marker either (same files).

The schema allows author 'assistant' and the panel labels such rows Assistant, but the client create call never sends it and no producer was found. (artifact-comments.ts:36; artifact-comments-client.ts:166-170; ArtifactCommentsPanel.tsx:154)
Replies are saved with anchor artifact and attached to the root thread only. (artifact-comment-service.ts:109-127)
disconnected_or_disabled: Ask AI to apply is passed only when the chat supplies an edit-request handler and the shown version is the latest (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3151).
not_available: Mobile app, Chrome extension, VS Code extension, CLI and the retained Tauri desktop: no comment code found.
Sharing comments with other people: rows are per account (0369:41-47); published pages carry no comments in the code opened [unknown beyond the files read].

established.statement: The user can pin comments to a spot or element on the design (item S32.17). The brief marks web, desktop, mobile and chrome as missing, which the code contradicts for web.
A visual design workspace is a required suite capability that follows artifact retention rules for storage, share, publish and delete.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; a mutation fired straight from a click is a defect.
Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route Local content to managed cloud.

acceptance_criteria: Selecting text and pressing Comment saves a thread anchored to that text and highlights it.
A second identical phrase gets the comment on the occurrence that was selected.
Reply, Resolve and Reopen change the thread; Delete asks first and removes the replies too.
The 501st comment on one artifact is refused with a message.
Another account cannot read or change the comment.
A comment on an element shows a visible pin on the design [proposed requirement; not met today].
Ask AI to apply sends one request that quotes each open comment and its replies.
inferred: A comment should be refused or kept on the device when the artifact belongs to a Local or temporary chat, because comment text and a quote of the artifact go to our servers (route.ts:61-68) while the artifact push skips such chats (apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts:1059-1072). [inferred]
proposed: Draw numbered pins at the saved x/y of element comments and make pressing a thread scroll to them.
Add a slide marker for slide comments.
Show pins in the shared Desktop and Mobile surfaces only after the trust-boundary rule is settled.

steps.what_happens: Person selects text or picks an element; the page builds an anchor (quote with 200 characters of context on each side, or selector, text and x/y).
Client sends POST with CSRF header and cookies.
Route checks CSRF, rate limit, validates the body with the schema, resolves the user.
Service opens a transaction, takes an advisory lock, counts rows, resolves the parent thread, inserts the row.
Client updates its cache and the panel lists the thread; highlights are repainted.
Ask AI to apply builds a prompt from threads and hands it to the chat as an edit request; the model reply is a normal chat turn.
steps.evidence: comment-request.ts:22-34; ArtifactCommentsPanel.tsx:271-286. The chat send path is in SYS-chat-turn-pipeline [inferred].

features.summary: Web has a saved library of templates and brands (colours, two font choices, a voice note) that applies to decks and text documents only. Importing a design system, a component library, token mapping and conformance feedback for HTML designs are not built in any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Today the Web side panel keeps per-account templates and brand kits. A brand holds background, text and accent colours, heading and body font family (sans, serif, mono) and a voice note. A brand can theme a deck or rewrite a document in its voice. features.summary: Each artifact keeps its versions. Web and Mobile can open an earlier version, show what changed against the one just before it (lines or words added and removed), and restore an older version as a new latest. Web asks before restoring; Mobile does not. Only neighbouring versions are compared.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person step through an artifact's versions, see added and removed text between a version and its predecessor, and bring an older version back without losing the ones between. (ArtifactChangesView.tsx:65-130; artifacts-store.ts:976-989)
purpose.why_it_exists: Edits and model revisions replace content; people need to see what changed and undo it. The product contract says compare and restore are part of artifacts, and failed edits must keep the previous version. (docs/product/experience-contract.md:782; docs/product/requirements.md:1470,1489)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone revising a design, document or code artifact with the assistant, on Web, the Desktop window or Mobile.
problems_solved: Finding what the assistant changed.
Undoing a bad revision.
Choosing which suggested changes to keep (Review changes for text documents).
use_cases: Open version 2 and press Show changes to see the lines the assistant added.
Press Restore on version 1 to go back.
Use Review changes to undo one of several suggested edits.
Step Undo and Redo through edit versions.
