aliases: Publish artifact to a public link
features.summary: Turns a finished chat artifact (page, app, diagram, document or code) into a hosted page with a link. Works from web (and the Electron desktop, which shows the web app), mobile and the CLI. Only Cloud-mode artifacts can be published. Publishing again updates the same link. There is no publish on VS Code or Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Copies the content of a chat artifact to AGI Cloud storage as a published page and returns a share link. The page is stored in the published_artifacts table and each changed publish adds a version (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:421-498; :871-955).
purpose.why_it_exists: A chat can build a small site or app, but the result lives only in the conversation. Publishing gives it a link that can be opened without the chat. The platform package says the publish seam existed with no backing before this adapter (published-artifact-service.ts:15-21).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person who made an artifact in an AGI Cloud chat and wants to share it. Mostly web and mobile users; CLI users for scripted use.
problems_solved: No way to share a generated page outside the chat.
Sharing by copy and paste loses the running page.
Republishing after a fix should not change the link people already hold.
use_cases: Ask the assistant for a landing page, press Publish, send the link.
Fix a bug in a published HTML tool and publish again; the same link now shows the fix.
Publish a diagram or markdown document for a colleague.
Run agi artifacts publish <id> from a script to get a link.

where_to_find_it: Web: the artifact panel header button labelled Publish (aria-label 'Publish artifact to a public link'), and an item named Publish in the artifact's overflow menu on narrow screens (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2305-2311; :2917-2929).

Desktop (Electron): the public desktop shows the hosted web app, so the web control is what appears (AGENTS.md section 5; doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md). Tauri desktop code writes local files only (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts:1-17).

Mobile: a globe icon in the full-screen artifact header, labelled 'Publish artifact to a public link', or 'Republish artifact link' once published (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1319-1334).
CLI: agi artifacts publish <id> [--audience public|workspace] [--json] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1399-1408).
VS Code and Chrome: none found; founder decision says VS Code does not publish (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md lines 116-118).
prerequisites: Signed in to AGI Cloud on the app used.
Web: the artifact was created in Cloud (managed) mode; otherwise Publish returns unavailable with a message to download instead (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifacts.ts:256-275).
Mobile: app mode must be Cloud; signed-out users get 'Sign in to AGI Cloud to publish', Local mode gets 'Switch to AGI Cloud to publish' (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:731-745).
CLI: managed account mode and a stored sign-in token (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-379).
Artifact kind is one of html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text, code and has content (published-artifact-service.ts:61-69).
screens_and_controls: Web: Publish button/menu item; after success a link bar with the URL, a Copy link button, a 'Who can open this' selector (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3007-3062).
Mobile: confirm alert 'Publish to a public link?' with Cancel/Publish (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:285-296); alerts 'Artifact published', 'Publish not confirmed', 'Publish failed'.
CLI: prints "Published '<title>' at <url> (opens for <audience>)." (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4005-4016).
journey: Build an artifact in a Cloud chat.
Open it in the artifact panel (web) or full screen (mobile), or note its id (CLI).
Choose Publish (mobile asks to confirm that anyone with the link can open it).
The app sends the content to the server and waits.
The server checks policy, stores the page and returns the link.
The app shows or copies the link; the first publish is public unless the artifact uses connected apps.
feedback_and_outputs: Web toast 'Published · link copied to clipboard' or 'Published. Copy the link from the bar below.' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1243-1245); error toast with the server message or 'Failed to publish artifact' (:1265).
Mobile copies the link and shows an alert if the copy cannot be confirmed (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:773-780).
CLI prints the link, or JSON with --json.
The returned receipt carries token, shareUrl, version, kind, title, sandboxed flag, visibility and workspace member count (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:100-118).
settings: None found that change publishing. The audience can be changed afterwards (see the audience feature F033-03).

working: Web publish end to end: client publisher posts to /api/artifacts/publish and validates the receipt (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/publishArtifactClient.ts:74-130).

Server validates body (kind enum, content 1 to 1,000,000 characters, title up to 300), checks CSRF and rate limit, applies workspace sharing policy, moderation and secret redaction, then upserts and versions (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:33-60; apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-publication-policy.ts:55-85).

Per-person cap of 200 publications with a 409 conflict message 'Unpublish one before publishing another' (published-artifact-service.ts:59; :414-416). Republishing an existing artifact is exempt (:395-412 of the loop; admitPublishedArtifact returns the existing id).
Mobile publish with cloud-mode and sign-in guards and uncertain-outcome recovery (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:731-800; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/artifactPublishing.ts:60-100).
CLI publish with kind check, optional workspace audience and rollback of a fresh publication if narrowing fails (apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs:451-538).
Artifact created from connected apps is published as 'invited' on first publish (published-artifact-service.ts:436-441).
incomplete: Web only maps the artifact types html, react, svg, mermaid, code and document (markdown or text); other types such as images or PDFs throw 'cannot be published to a public page yet' (publishArtifactClient.ts:22-52).

The module comment in packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifacts.ts:66-72 says desktop and mobile inject no publisher, but mobile has its own publish function (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/artifactPublishing.ts:60); the comment is stale.
The brief lists CLI as n/a for S33.04 but the CLI has a publish command (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1399-1408).
disconnected_or_disabled: Tauri desktop adapter publishAdapter.ts writes files under the app data folder and injects no cloud publisher (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts:1-17); it is retained internal code per AGENTS.md section 5.
not_available: VS Code: no publish code found in apps/extension-vscode/src; founder decision confirms (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md).
Chrome: no publish code found in apps/extension.
Publishing Local or own-key (BYOK) artifacts: refused on web by the trust-boundary check (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifacts.ts:256-275).
No description field on a published page (published-artifact-service.ts:154-167; route.ts:33-40).

established.statement: Prompt-based creation then hosting must work: the user prompts, then hosts the result (brief S33.04).
Only kinds with a safe renderer can publish: html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text, code.
Content is capped at 1,000,000 characters and empty content is refused.
Title is capped at 300 characters on the route.
A person may hold at most 200 publications; over the cap returns a conflict telling them to unpublish one.
A Local or own-key artifact must never reach the managed-cloud publisher.
VS Code does not preview, export or publish artifacts (decision).

acceptance_criteria: Publishing an html artifact from a Cloud chat on web returns 201 with a 24-character token and a /shared-artifact/<token> link.
Publishing the same artifact again returns the same token and does not create a second row or, if content is unchanged, a new version.
Publishing an empty artifact, or one over 1,000,000 characters, is refused with a validation error and nothing is stored.
The 201st distinct publication returns a 409 whose text tells the person to unpublish one first.
On mobile in Local mode no request is sent and the alert 'Switch to AGI Cloud to publish' appears.
A web artifact made in Local or own-key mode shows an unavailable message and sends nothing.
Content with a detected secret is stored redacted or the publish is refused, per workspace policy.
inferred: Publish should be refused for a signed-out visitor on every app; the server uses getUserScopedDb and the route test says a 401 propagates (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.test.ts: 'propagates a 401'). [inferred]
The brief marks desktop built; for Electron this holds only because the desktop shows the web app. [inferred]

steps.what_happens: Person presses Publish; the web panel locks the view and calls the publish handler with the current content.
The platform publisher checks the artifact was created in managed mode and the requested mode matches; otherwise it returns unavailable without any network call.
The web client maps the artifact type to a kind and POSTs JSON with a CSRF header to /api/artifacts/publish.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit (5 per minute), parses the body, resolves the user-scoped database connection.
Server applies the workspace external-sharing policy, content moderation, and secret redaction or refusal.
In one transaction: confirm the conversation is the caller's, take an advisory lock, enforce the 200 cap, upsert the row, record a version if anything changed.
Server writes an audit event named share_link_updated and returns 201 with the receipt.
Client validates the receipt matches the artifact id, shows the link and copies it.
Mobile and CLI follow the same server path; the CLI first fetches the artifact's message text from the conversation, then posts.

access_and_usage.local_mode: Not allowed. Web refuses Local and own-key origin artifacts; mobile alerts to switch to AGI Cloud; CLI refuses any non-managed mode (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-373). Nothing is uploaded.

features.summary: Every publication gets a random 24-character token and a link at /shared-artifact/<token> on the web site. Anyone with the link can open a public page; the page renders the artifact, running scripted kinds in a sandbox. Bad, revoked or not-allowed links show an honest unavailable page. Mobile, CLI and desktop open the same link in a browser.

purpose.what_it_does: Serves a published artifact to visitors by token. The public page shows the title, the date, the rendered artifact, a 'Save a copy to my chats' button and a report link (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:68-97; PublishedArtifactView.tsx:228-230).
purpose.why_it_exists: A publish needs a place people can open it without the chat. An unguessable link is the access grant for public pages (published-artifact-service.ts:15-21).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners who share the link; visitors who open it, with or without an account.
problems_solved: Sharing a working page with someone who has no chat access.
Keeping visitors safe from untrusted scripts.
Giving visitors a clear message when a link no longer works.
use_cases: Send a public link to a client in an email.
Open your own page on a phone from the Sites list.
A recipient taps Save a copy to my chats to remix the page.
A visitor reports an abusive page from the footer link.

where_to_find_it: Web: the link bar under the artifact (Copy link button), the Sites page (Copy link to <name>, Open), and Settings published list (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:3007-3035; apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteCard.tsx:113).

Mobile: the artifact screen and Site screen offer Copy link, Share, and Open in Safari or Open in browser (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:1135-1153; apps/mobile/src/features/sites/SiteDetailScreen.tsx:275-300).
CLI: agi artifacts published lists links; agi artifacts open <id> opens the page in the browser (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1387-1398; cloud/artifacts.rs:692).
Desktop (Electron): the published page opens in the system browser (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md, Connected apps in artifacts section).
prerequisites: A publication exists (F033-01).
Public page: none for a visitor. Workspace or invited pages: the visitor must be signed in (page.tsx:29-46).
screens_and_controls: Public page: heading, 'Published <date>', a line for the audience ('Shared conversation', or 'Shared with you'), rendered artifact, 'Save a copy to my chats' button, report link (PublishedArtifactView.tsx:228-260).
Unavailable page: heading 'Shared artifact unavailable' and an 'Open chat' button (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/UnavailableArtifact.tsx).
Invite-only page: 'Sign in to open this' or 'You do not have access' (InviteOnlyArtifact.tsx).
journey: Owner copies the link after publishing.
Visitor opens the link in a browser.
The server validates the token shape and looks the page up.
A public page renders; scripted kinds run inside a sandboxed frame.
Visitor can save a copy to their chats (needs sign-in) or report the page.
feedback_and_outputs: Rendered page or the unavailable or invite-only page.
Browser tab title '<title> - AGI' for public pages, with search engines told not to index (page.tsx:48-57).
Mobile and web show 'Link copied' style confirmations (ArtifactPreview.tsx:3027-3031).
settings: Server switch AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED turns on the in-page AI feature of the public page (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-8); it does not affect whether the page opens.

working: Token is 18 random bytes encoded as 24 URL-safe characters; the link is the site address plus /shared-artifact/<token> (published-artifact-service.ts:289-295; :107).
Public read returns a row only when visibility is public and the owner's account may run unattended (published-artifact-service.ts:824-841; apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:53-66).

Scripted kinds html, react and mermaid render in a sandbox frame on a separate sandbox origin, with a fallback frame lacking same-origin rights (published-artifact-service.ts:92-105; apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:395-431).
svg renders as an image, markdown through the markdown renderer, text and code as text (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/publishedArtifactRender.ts:20-60; PublishedArtifactView.tsx:52-70).
Malformed token shows the unavailable page, and a revoked token looks the same on purpose (page.tsx:60-72).
Report link on the page footer (page.tsx:95).
incomplete: Page views are not counted or audited (published-artifact-service.ts:44-47).
disconnected_or_disabled: In-page AI calls are off unless AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is set (artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-8).
not_available: Mobile, CLI, desktop and extensions do not render published pages; the link opens in a browser (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md).
Custom domains, expiry (no TTL), analytics: none found.

established.statement: The published site is reachable at a public URL (brief S33.10) and can be shared as a preview link (S33.07).
Each publication has a random 24-character token and a link built from the site address.
The anonymous read returns only public rows of owners allowed to run.
Scripted kinds render in a sandbox.
A malformed token shows the unavailable page, not the global 404.

acceptance_criteria: Opening a valid public link signed out renders the artifact.
A token that is not 24 URL-safe characters shows 'Shared artifact unavailable'.
After unpublish the same link shows the unavailable page.
An html artifact with a script runs inside an iframe, not on the app origin.
A visitor for a workspace-only page who is not allowed does not see the content.
The page is not indexable (robots noindex).
The footer report link opens the report form for that path.

steps.what_happens: Visitor opens /shared-artifact/<token>; the page rejects a malformed token with the unavailable page.
Server reads the row where token matches, visibility is public and the owner may run.
If not public, server tries the visitor's signed-in scoped reads (workspace then invited); if none, checks whether the page is invite-only to pick the message.
Server returns the page; the browser builds the render for the kind and mounts the sandbox frame for html, react and mermaid.
Save a copy to my chats copies the artifact into the signed-in visitor's conversations through the web app.
Mobile and CLI only open or share the URL; rendering happens in the system browser.

features.summary: Sets who may open a published page: anyone with the link, members of the owner's workspace, or named people invited by email who must sign in. Web and mobile have the selector and an invited-people list. The CLI sets public or workspace only. Workspace sharing needs a plan with team features. No password option exists.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a visibility on each publication (public, organization or invited) and enforces it on reads. Workspace access uses a grant row; invited access uses an email list of up to 100 people (apps/web/lib/services/published-site-viewer-service.ts:13; migrations 0184, 0372).
purpose.why_it_exists: A link in the wrong hands is a leak. Owners need to narrow who can open work that is internal or private, and pages that use connected apps must never be public (published-artifact-service.ts:73-80).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners who publish for a team or a few people; admins of workspaces.
problems_solved: Public links leak.
Sharing with a team without sending emails.
Keeping connected-app pages away from the public.
use_cases: Share an internal dashboard page with the whole workspace.
Invite two contractors by email and nobody else.
Switch a page back to public for a launch.
Block public sharing of a page that reads connected apps.

Choosing 'Only people you invite' shows the invited people editor (3064-3072).

steps.what_happens: Owner picks an audience; the app shows a confirm that names who loses access.
Client sends PATCH with only the visibility; the receipt must echo the token and the new visibility or the client reports it as unconfirmed.
Server checks CSRF and rate limit, parses the body and locks the row.
For workspace: checks the plan capability and content.share permission. For public: refuses if connectors are used or workspace policy blocks external sharing.
Server adds or deletes the workspace grant, updates visibility, and re-reads grants to verify.
Visitor read: public by token; otherwise a signed-in scoped read decides by row-level security for workspace members or listed emails.
Adding an invited email inserts a row under an advisory lock and writes an audit event.

features.summary: Lets a person keep working on a copy of a generated app or file, and take its source out as a file. Web has Duplicate (a local copy) and a Download menu. Mobile exports through the share sheet. The CLI writes to a file. VS Code saves into the workspace. Chrome downloads from the side panel.

purpose.what_it_does: Two jobs. Duplicate makes a separate artifact that starts from what is on screen, so edits to the copy never touch the original (artifacts-store.ts:929). Download hands the person the artifact's source or a converted document as a real file on their own device (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2381-2418).
purpose.why_it_exists: Generated apps and documents are made in chat. People need to try a different version without losing the first, and to own the file outside the product. The brief lists both as owner needs (S33.25, S33.26).
purpose.who_uses_it: The owner of a generated artifact on web (and desktop, which shows the hosted web app), phone users, CLI users, VS Code users and Chrome side-panel users. A viewer of a shared page can also save a copy into their own chats.
problems_solved: Trying a risky change without overwriting the working version.
Getting the HTML, code, Markdown, PDF or Word file out of the product.
Moving a generated file into a local project (CLI file output, VS Code workspace save).
Spreadsheet formulas in exported CSV or TSV text being run by Excel: exports are made safe (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1405-1410).
use_cases: A person duplicates a landing page, asks for a new colour scheme on the copy, and keeps the original.
A person downloads a generated deck as PDF to send it by email.
A developer runs agi artifacts show <id> --out ./site.html to put a generated page in a repo.

steps.what_happens: Web Duplicate: the browser calls forkArtifact, which reads the artifact from the shared in-memory store, makes a new id and writes the copy back to the store.
Web Download: the page builds a Blob from the artifact content and clicks a temporary link.
Deck PDF, Word and PDF conversions run in the browser code (imports from presentation/deck-pdf and an export handler).

CLI show: resolves the artifact id against the cloud index, fetches the source message, re-derives the content, then writes the file locally.
VS Code save: pages through the conversation to find the source message, derives the artifact and writes it to a chosen path.
Viewer 'Save a copy to my chats': posts the shared page content to create a chat in the viewer's account.

aliases: AI calls from inside an app
features.summary: A published or owned web app (HTML or React) can ask the assistant a question from inside its page. The server checks a switch, the viewer's plan and a per-app ceiling, picks a model, and bills the signed-in viewer, never the publisher. The switch is off by default.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a generated app a safe route to the AI service. The page sends a prompt to the runtime endpoint; the server runs it as managed cloud usage with a per-app call and spend limit and returns text (artifact-completion.ts:280-318).
purpose.why_it_exists: A generated app such as a summarizer or quiz needs a model, but cannot hold an API key. A bridge through the product keeps keys, moderation and billing on the server (docs/security/security.md:1250-1271).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in viewer using a published app, and an owner using an app saved in their own managed chat.
problems_solved: Apps with working AI without exposing a key.
One looping app emptying a person's whole five-hour allowance (per-app ceilings, migration 0391 header).
Publisher being billed for strangers' use: calls bill the viewer (route.test.ts:407).
Connected-app data leaking through public pages (connectors refused on a public share).
use_cases: A viewer opens a shared 'explain this text' app, signs in and gets answers.
An owner tries the app they built in a chat before publishing.
A published app that reads connected apps asks the viewer to approve before it runs.

Desktop shows the hosted web app, but the shared desktop frame and the extension refuse runtime requests (docs/security/security.md:1256-1258).

The app kind is html or react (PublishedArtifactView.tsx:68).

steps.what_happens: The app inside the sandboxed frame posts a request to the page bridge; the page blocks it if the switch prop is off or the viewer is signed out.
The page sends the prompt to the complete endpoint with the session and CSRF token.
The server checks the switch, workspace policy, entitlement, moderation, content safety and secret handling.
The server picks a model route through managed cloud admission, applies the model policy and the egress gate.
A turn slot is taken, then usage is reserved with the app as subject; per-app ceilings apply here.
The model call (or a tool loop with connectors) runs with the platform key; output is capped at 4,096 tokens.
The reservation is finalized with the observed cost, or released on failure; the text is returned.

data.what: Usage reservation row with provider, model, estimated and actual cost, artifact_subject.
data.where_stored: table managed_usage_requests in the cloud database.
data.synced: Server only; it feeds the shared usage ledger.

data.what: App saved data written by the app.
data.where_stored: table published_artifact_storage, capped by ARTIFACT_STORAGE_SCOPE_LIMIT_BYTES per scope.
data.retained_or_deleted: Deleted with the publication (foreign key on delete cascade, 0325 line 5) or cleared by the owner (data route DELETE).
Stays until the viewer revokes or clears storage (usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:56-95).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The server chooses the model through the shared managed cloud route admission, not the app or the viewer; the route can need tool calling when connectors are present and must keep inputs out of training for Google user data (artifact-runtime-service.ts:299-333). Calls use the platform key (artifact-completion.ts:187-196). Model identifiers are resolved by the catalog and are not written here.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in account is required; signed-out gets 401 (route.test.ts:449) and the page shows a sign-in banner.
access_and_usage.permissions: CSRF token, active account and rate limit 'llm-completion' per user (route.ts:33-38). Published apps must be runnable; an owned app must be in the viewer's own chat and made in a managed cloud chat. Connector use on a published app needs the publisher to have bound connectors (route.ts:50-60). Workspace privacy policy can forbid managed AI (artifact-completion.ts:131-143).
access_and_usage.subscription: Entitlement is resolved per viewer (resolveEntitlementBundle) and managed compute access is evaluated; plans without AI responses in apps are refused (artifact-completion.ts:103-105, 153-168). Per-app call counts differ by plan in the billing catalog (billing-catalog.ts:568-719): free has a finite count, some tiers are unlimited, enterprise is 'custom'.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Per-app calls and spend per viewer in a rolling five-hour window; spend share is a fraction of the plan's five-hour budget; 4,096 output tokens per call; prompt length cap ARTIFACT_RUNTIME_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS; concurrency slot per plan; the plan's own five-hour and weekly limits still apply; app calls cannot use usage credits (managed-usage-request-service.ts:763-769).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED (server, default off). Connector release switch (connectorsReleased).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Server-chosen. With connectors, a model with function calling is required; for Google data a no-training route is required (artifact-runtime-service.ts:305-313).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Platform-key managed route only; no provider key from the viewer or publisher is used (artifact-completion.ts:187-196).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not available. The call runs on our servers; an owned app must come from a managed cloud chat (artifact-completion.ts:63-72). Local inference is not used by this path [inferred: no local route in the code read].

features.summary: A visitor on a shared page can follow 'Report infringement or impersonation' and file a notice that is recorded and emailed to operators. Only a platform operator can remove the page, through an audited takedown API. Publishing and restoring a version also check the title and content against the usage policy.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives people a way to report a public shared page, keeps a numbered record of each notice, and gives operators a separate, audited way to unpublish. It also stops content that fails the usage policy or the sharing gate from being published (published-artifact-publication-policy.ts:55-72).
purpose.why_it_exists: Public links can host infringing or impersonating material. An anonymous allegation must not be able to take down a stranger's page, so intake and removal are separate (takedown/route.ts:19-26).
purpose.who_uses_it: Visitors and rights holders (reporting), platform operators (takedown and dispositions), and publishers (affected by the policy check).
problems_solved: No way for a rights holder without an account to report content.
Abuse of reporting to remove other people's pages.
Publishing content that breaks the usage policy.
Operators lacking an audit trail of removals.
use_cases: A designer finds their logo used on a shared page and files a copyright notice.
A person finds a page impersonating their company and files an impersonation report.
An operator looks up a token, reads the notice, and unpublishes the page with a reason.
A publisher tries to publish text that the policy filter blocks and is told why.

screens_and_controls: Footer link carries the page path into the form as ?url= (ReportContentLink.tsx:3-5).

The form asks notice type (copyright, trademark, impersonation), reporter name and email, phone and address for copyright and trademark, rights holder, a description, a signature and three affirmations (copyright-notice/route.ts:43-66).
Only /share/ and /shared-artifact/ URLs are accepted as the reported URL (report/page.tsx:16-27).
journey: A visitor opens a shared page and scrolls to the footer.
They choose 'Report infringement or impersonation'.
The form opens with the page address filled in.
They complete it and submit; the server finds the page by token, records the notice, writes a security-audit event, and emails the operators.
The screen shows 'Notice recorded, reference <IP-...>' or 'Report recorded' for impersonation, and says whether the operator was notified (CopyrightNoticeForm.tsx:213-229).
An operator opens the email, looks up the token with GET /api/admin/takedown, and, if justified, POSTs the takedown with a reason.
An operator can set a notice's disposition (actioned, rejected, counter_notified) through POST /api/admin/copyright-notices.

Public intake validates, resolves the token, records the notice in copyright_notices, logs a security event and emails operators; it never unpublishes (copyright-notice/route.ts:207-262).
Takedown deletes the published_artifacts row (or the shared_sessions row), after a required audit write, and only for a platform operator (takedown/route.ts:61-121).
Operators can list and set dispositions through /api/admin/copyright-notices (route.ts:53-109).

Publish and version-restore call preparePublishedArtifactPublication: external-sharing gate, usage-policy moderation on title and content, and outbound content inspection (publish/route.ts:63; versions/[version]/route.ts:69).
Runtime AI prompts are moderated too (artifact-completion.ts:170-181).
incomplete: Removal is a hard delete of the published row with no owner notice found in the code read (takedown/route.ts:99-108).
Moderation is a text filter of five categories and does not read images; the acceptable-use test states what it screens (published-safety-claims.test.ts:48-56, 127).

not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no report control (brief marks them n/a).

steps.what_happens: The visitor's browser loads the shared page and the footer link, then the report form with the page path.
Form submit posts to the intake endpoint with CSRF and the 'waitlist' rate limit bucket.
The server normalizes the token, looks it up in shared_sessions and published_artifacts, records the notice and writes the audit event.
An email goes to the support fallback address through the email service, with the next-step takedown instruction.
An operator POSTs the takedown; the server writes a required audit event and deletes the row.
At publish and restore, title and content go through the sharing gate, the text filter and outbound inspection before saving.

features.summary: Find inside the open chat lets a person type some text and jump between the messages of the conversation they are reading that contain it. Web and Desktop show a search bar with match count, next/previous and highlighting. The CLI full-screen chat has /find, which lists matching lines but does not jump. Mobile, VS Code and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Searches only the messages of the conversation that is open. On Web and Desktop it finds messages whose visible (rendered) text contains the query, scrolls the chat to each one in turn and paints the matched words. In the CLI full-screen chat it prints a list of matching lines.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long chats are hard to scan. Claude and ChatGPT both let people find text in the chat they are in, and the repository's product rules say to follow them (doc: AGENTS.md section 10; doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading a long conversation: people reviewing an earlier answer, a code snippet or a decision inside one chat.
problems_solved: Scrolling a long transcript to find one earlier answer
Telling whether a word was ever said in this chat
Reaching a specific message quickly with the keyboard
use_cases: Web user presses Ctrl+F in a 200-message chat to find where a command was suggested
Desktop user searches for a file name mentioned earlier
CLI user types /find migration to list every line that mentions it

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: inside any open chat, press Cmd+F (Mac) or Ctrl+F; a bar slides in at the top of the message list (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:1539, :2092). Desktop is the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
CLI full-screen chat: type /find followed by the text; the command list describes it as 'Search this conversation's messages' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4524, :5620).
Mobile, VS Code, Chrome: not present (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/034-search-experiences.md S34.01).
prerequisites: An open conversation with messages (Web/Desktop: the chat page; CLI: the full-screen chat).

No sign-in, plan or network is needed for the search itself: matching runs on text already loaded in the page or terminal (apps/web/features/chat/lib/message-search.ts:9; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4680).
screens_and_controls: Search bar (role search, label 'Search messages') with a text box whose placeholder is 'Search messages...' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageSearch.tsx:79, :95).
Match label: '<n> of <total> matches' or 'No matches' once something is typed (MessageSearch.tsx:62).
Buttons 'Go to previous match' (Shift+Enter) and 'Go to next match' (Enter); both disabled when there are no matches (MessageSearch.tsx:112-132).
Button 'Close search' (Escape) (MessageSearch.tsx:136).
CLI: /find <text>; with no text it answers 'Usage: /find <text>' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4683).
journey: Web/Desktop: press Cmd+F or Ctrl+F; the browser's own find is cancelled and the bar opens with the text box focused and selected.
Type the text. The count updates and matching words are highlighted in the messages that are on screen.
Press Enter or click the down arrow for the next matching message; Shift+Enter or the up arrow for the previous one. The list scrolls so the match sits in the middle and wraps from last to first.
Press Escape or click Close. The bar closes and the query is cleared.
CLI: type /find text; a system message lists '<n> line(s) match ...' with '#<message number> <you|assistant|teammate> <first 120 characters of the line>'.
feedback_and_outputs: Count text, highlighted words, smooth scroll to the matching message.
'No matches' text and disabled arrows when nothing matches.
CLI: a list capped at 30 lines followed by '... N more'; or "Nothing in this conversation matches '<text>'." (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4702-4713).
settings: None found for find-in-chat itself. The shortcut is a fixed key check on the window, not a registry entry (ChatMessageList.tsx:1539) [inferred: no shortcut id was found for it].

working: Web: bar opens on Cmd/Ctrl+F, Escape closes and clears (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:1504, :1539-1551).

Web: matching ignores case, trims the query and compares against the Markdown-rendered text, so formatting marks and link addresses are not matched (apps/web/features/chat/lib/message-search.ts:9-40).
Web: next/previous wrap around using modulo and scroll the row to the centre (ChatMessageList.tsx:1518-1535).

Desktop shows the same code because the public desktop window shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
CLI full-screen chat: /find lists matching lines of user, assistant and teammate messages, skipping system, error, detail and tool messages (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4680-4713).
incomplete: The count is the number of message groups (rows) that match, not the number of occurrences: the total comes from matchingGroupIndexes, which returns one index per group (message-search.ts:9-31) [inferred].

Highlighting reaches only text currently mounted in the page; the transcript is a virtualised list with a small overscan (ChatMessageList.tsx:2110) [inferred: rows far away are not in the page until scrolled to].
CLI lists lines only; it does not jump or highlight (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4713).

established.statement: Inside an open conversation the user can type a query and jump between the messages that match it.

Matching is case-insensitive on the text as shown on screen; the list scrolls to the match, centres it and wraps from last to first; matched text is highlighted; with no matches the arrows are disabled; closing clears the query.
CLI /find lists matching lines as '#<message number> <who> <line>', shows at most FIND_RESULT_LIMIT with '... N more', and says nothing matches when empty; it does not jump.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, Ctrl+F in an open chat opens the bar with the text box focused; typing 'abc' shows '1 of N matches' when N messages contain 'abc' in any letter case.
Enter moves to the next matching message and the list scrolls so it is centred; on the last match Enter goes to the first.
Shift+Enter moves backwards and wraps from the first to the last.
A query that matches nothing shows 'No matches' and both arrow buttons are disabled.
Escape closes the bar and reopening it shows an empty query.
Text that only appears as Markdown syntax (for example the asterisks around bold text or a link address) is not matched.
CLI: /find with a word present in 40 lines lists 30 lines and '... 10 more'; with a word not present prints "Nothing in this conversation matches '<word>'."
inferred: The count label should say how many messages match rather than 'matches' if it counts rows [inferred from the code, not stated in any document].
Find should work offline, because no network call is made in the matching path [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show the number of occurrences, or label the count as 'messages', so the count matches what people expect.
[proposed] Make CLI /find jump the transcript view to the chosen line, like the web bar.
[proposed] Add in-chat find to Mobile, as the leaders do, with the same matching rules.

steps.what_happens: Web: a window key listener catches Cmd/Ctrl+F, cancels the browser find and opens the bar.
Each keystroke recomputes matching groups from the messages already loaded in the page, using cached rendered text.
Next/previous changes the current index (with wrap) and asks the virtual list to scroll that row to the centre.
The highlight hook walks the message elements in the page and paints matches.
CLI: /find scans the in-memory chat messages and returns a system message.

features.summary: One place to search past work. Web and Desktop open a Search dialog that finds chats by title and message text, plus projects, files, artifacts, code sessions and scheduled tasks, with filters and recent searches. Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome each search their own chat history only, with fewer filters.

purpose.what_it_does: Finds earlier chats (by title and by what was said) and, on Web and Desktop, also projects, library files, artifacts, code sessions, project sources and scheduled tasks. Each result shows a title, a snippet with the matched words and a type label, and opens when chosen.
purpose.why_it_exists: Leader products let people search their chat history; the project says to follow them (doc: AGENTS.md section 10).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone with more than a few chats; Desktop users also look for local code sessions.
problems_solved: Finding a chat when the title is forgotten
Finding an old project, file or artifact from one box
Repeating a search without retyping
use_cases: Web user types 'invoice' and filters to their own messages after a date
Mobile user searches the chats tab and sees chats, projects, files and artifacts in groups
CLI user runs agi --search 'rust' --output-format json to script over all matching sessions

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: the Search dialog opens from the sidebar or from the 'open-search' shortcut (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1711; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/shortcutRegistry.ts:47). The text-box label is 'Search your workspace'.
Mobile: the 'Search' box on the chats list; accessibility label 'Search chats, projects, files, library, and artifacts' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx:930-931).

CLI: '/sessions search <query>' in the line chat (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:968), '/sessions' then search in the full-screen chat (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5998), or 'agi --search <query>' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7848).

VS Code: the 'Search sessions' box in the sidebar and a session picker with a search box (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:3043; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/trees/sessionPickers.ts:70-110).
Chrome: 'Search recent chats' box in the side-panel Recents drawer (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:950).
prerequisites: Web and Desktop: signed in; a workspace whose data region can be confirmed (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:130-150).
Type at least 2 characters (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:297; VS Code picker MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH = 2).
Mobile Cloud search needs a signed-in Cloud account; Local mode searches the phone only (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatViewStore.ts:233-246).
Chrome: the box appears only when the drawer holds more than 10 chats (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:1131, :12821).
screens_and_controls: Web/Desktop category chips (group 'Search category'): All, Artifacts, Sessions, Code, Projects, Scheduled; Desktop adds 'Local Code' (apps/web/features/chat/lib/global-search-categories.ts:1-8; GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:119-121).

Filters (shown for All and Sessions only): 'Message Type' (All messages, My messages, AI responses, System messages), 'From Date', 'To Date' with a calendar, 'Include archived conversations', 'Clear Filters' (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:556-650).
Before typing: 'Recent Searches' chips with a 'Clear' button and 'Your frequent searches' chips with a count (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:672-730).
Clear confirmation titled 'Clear search history?' (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:190).

journey: Open Search (shortcut or sidebar). Before typing, recent and frequent searches are shown; click one to run it.
Pick a category chip and, for All or Sessions, optionally open filters.
Type 2 or more characters; after a short pause (300 ms) the search runs and a spinner 'Searching workspace' shows.

Read the results (title, snippet with the matched words marked, type label) and click one; the dialog closes and the chat, project, file, artifact or session opens. A message result opens its chat with the message highlighted.
Mobile: type in the chats search box; results appear in groups; tapping a recent search runs it; clearing recent searches asks first.
CLI: run agi --search 'text' and read the id, title, model, message count and matching snippets.
feedback_and_outputs: Spinner 'Searching workspace'.
Empty: 'No results found' and 'Try different keywords or clear filters' (Local Code: 'Try a different session title') (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:775-780).
Failure: 'Search could not be completed' with a Retry button (role alert) (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:757-770).
A crash of the dialog shows 'Search unavailable' (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:445-452).

working: Web/Desktop: GET /api/search returns session titles, message hits (up to 100), project rows, library file rows (All only), scheduled task names, and indexed documents, scoped to the user and workspace, skipping deleted and temporary chats and archived ones unless asked (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:299-480).
Web/Desktop: role, start date and end date filters are applied to rows; setting any of them turns off the indexed-document search (route.ts:398-411).
Search history: recorded unless track=false or the request is cross-site (route.ts:604-620); recent and popular lists read from SQL functions; DELETE clears (route.ts:262-283, :660-680).
Region guard: refuses with a clear message if the data region cannot be confirmed or is not served by this deployment (route.ts:130-150).
Web/Desktop dialog: debounce, abort of old requests, result labels, empty/failed states, confirm-before-clear (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:202-345).
Desktop adds a 'Local Code' category that searches code session titles through the desktop host on the device (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:119-121, :207-250).

Mobile: Cloud mode tries GET /api/search?q=&limit=50 first and falls back to on-device messages with searchFailed set; Local mode searches the phone only (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatViewStore.ts:233-345). Recent searches (5, per mode and per account) are kept in device storage (apps/mobile/src/features/search/recentSearches.ts:3-12).

CLI: search_sessions matches title or any message text, normalises text, also matches GitHub pull-request URLs and shorthand, and includes archived sessions; display limit 50 (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:919-950).

VS Code: sidebar and picker search through the local runtime per workspace folder, with a 250 ms debounce and a 2 character minimum (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/trees/conversationTreeProvider.ts:323-345; sessionPickers.ts:14-15).
Chrome: Recents drawer filter matches every typed word against the title and message text of saved chats (apps/extension/src/features/background/conversation-history.ts:1597-1618).
incomplete: Mobile has recent searches but no date filter and no frequent-search chips (apps/mobile/src/features/search/recentSearches.ts; ChatsListScreen.tsx:372-405).
CLI and VS Code search chats only: no projects, files or preview beyond snippets (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:919).
Mobile Cloud search sends no category or filters, so only default chats and projects from the server are used (chatViewStore.ts:251-266).
Message hits are capped at 100 rows before the overall limit (route.ts:466).

Found by searching apps and packages for 'suggestions' callers: only the route and its test.

established.statement: The user can search past conversations by title and message text and open a match; only conversations the user can see in history are returned.
The user can search Projects by name or description and open a match.
The user can limit a search to a date range and get only results inside it.
Before or while typing the user is offered suggested queries and can pick one.
Results show a preview (title, snippet or matched text) before opening.
Empty and unavailable searches show a clear state, not silence.
Only the user's own, non-deleted, non-temporary chats are searched; archived are excluded unless asked; search is blocked with a message when the data region cannot be confirmed.
Unsupported or incomplete capabilities are hidden or clearly unavailable, never presented as working.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, typing 1 character shows no search; 2 or more runs one after a short pause.
A chat that only matches in a message body appears as a message result with the matched words marked; a chat that only matches in its title appears with the label 'Title'.
Setting 'My messages' or a From date removes document-index results and filters message rows.

features.summary: A chat can look up current information on the internet and answer with cited sources. Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome use the Cloud service, which turns search on by itself when the model has a search route. The CLI and VS Code need the user's own search key outside Cloud. The API accepts allowed and denied sites.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the model a web_search tool (or the provider's own search). The service runs the search, returns up to five results with title, link, snippet and dates, and the answer cites them. Search can be required for a turn when the question asks for it or is time-bound.
purpose.why_it_exists: Models do not know recent facts. ChatGPT and Claude search automatically and the founders decided the same (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-15-01).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone asking about current events, prices, versions or facts; developers using the API who need to limit sites.
problems_solved: Answers from stale training data
Answers with no sources
Unwanted or unsafe sites as sources
use_cases: Ask 'who is the current president of India' and get a cited answer
CLI user runs /search to force a search for one question
API caller sends allow_domains=['nature.com'] so only that site is used

screens_and_controls: Composer: no search switch on Web; the tool toggles on its own (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1692-1698).

journey: Ask a question. Say 'search the web for ...' or use time words such as 'this year' to make search required for that turn.
The service runs up to three searches (ten for AGI Work), reads the results and writes the answer with citations.
Citations show site, title, snippet and the publication or retrieval date when known; open the source from the chip or card.
If search is unavailable the answer says so instead of inventing sources.
CLI: type /search question; if no key is saved it prints how to save one.
feedback_and_outputs: Cited answer with source cards.

working: Server tool: 5 results, 3 calls per normal turn, 10 per AGI Work turn, query cut at 400 characters, 15 second timeout, 1 retry after 400 ms on rate limit or server error (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-tool.ts:54-58, :39, :159-160).

Search service is configured from web-search-providers.json: one provider entry, api.perplexity.ai, key name PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, delivery 'indexed' (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-providers.json; web-search-tool.ts:37).
Results become canonical sources with publication, index and retrieval times (apps/web/lib/web-search/search-provider.ts:150-180).

Domain policy: workspace, agent and request rules are combined; rules are capped at 32; deny wins over allow; up to 20 allow rules (or deny rules as '-domain') go to the search service and every result is re-checked before the model sees it (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/research-sources.ts:19-60; web-search-tool.ts:144-155; request-processor.ts:5262-5290).
Required search: explicit mode, work mode, explicit words, freshness phrases and research tasks make search mandatory (apps/web/lib/web-search/required-search.ts:218-232).
Composer keeps search on whenever the model or Cloud has a search route; Free sends are blocked when the allowance is checking or exhausted (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1596-1698).

Budget: Free interactive turns draw on the 20 per 30 days allowance; paid plans and automated callers (api, cli, vscode, AGI Work, research, scheduled) are charged credits (apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:32-33, :54-100, :133-142).
Mobile sends web_search, web_fetch and search_requested to Cloud (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:3251-3262, :3388-3394).

Chrome: managed chat turns on web search and fetch when the routed model searches (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedChatHandler.ts:781-782); the side panel renders source cards with site, title, snippet and published date (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/sources.ts:36-45).
Deep Research plan card on Web lets the user choose 'Only this site' and 'Never this site'; they are sent as research_sources (ResearchActivity.tsx:198-203; apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4605).

established.statement: A chat can search the public web and answer from the results.
The user can restrict a web search to named sites; include and exclude domains are respected; allowed and denied sites up to 32 each; denied wins.
Results and sources show how fresh they are.
Free keeps 20 searches per 30 days; paid plans include no free searches and every search is charged in credits at provider cost, shown as 'Agentic search'.
Web search, page fetch and read run without asking in the default read-only mode.
If search is unavailable the answer must say so and not invent sources.
Web search and memory are provider-route or harness features, never described as intrinsic model abilities.

acceptance_criteria: Asking 'search the web for <topic>' on Web returns a cited answer with at most 5 sources per search and no more than 3 searches.
A question with 'this year' triggers a search without the words 'search the web'.
With a Free account that has used 20 searches in 30 days, an explicit search request cannot be sent and the composer shows the allowance message.
A request with deny_domains ['example.com'] never returns a result from example.com, even if the provider returns one.
A request with the same domain in allow and deny never reads that domain.
With no search route, the answer says search is unavailable and lists no invented sources.
CLI /search without a saved key prints the key instructions and sends nothing.
Mobile switch 'Web search' off sends web_search false.
inferred: Freshness dates should appear in CLI and VS Code too [inferred from S34.31 and Web behaviour].
Local privacy mode must never call a search service unless the user gave a key and consent [inferred from doc: AGENTS.md section 6].
proposed: [proposed] Offer a domain control for ordinary chats, not only Deep Research and the API.
[proposed] Add a rate-limit retry to the CLI search path to match the server.
[proposed] Show dates in CLI results.

steps.what_happens: Composer or app decides search is available and sets web_search on the request (Web: automatic; Mobile: switch; Chrome: managed handler).
The Cloud chat service classifies whether search is required, merges workspace, agent and request domain rules, and offers the search tool.
Before each search the budget is checked (Free window or credit reservation).
The service calls the search provider with the query and domain filter and retries once on 429 or 5xx.
Results are filtered by the domain policy, wrapped as untrusted web results and given to the model.
The model writes the answer; the app shows citations and cards.
CLI outside Cloud: the tool calls Brave Search or Tavily directly from the machine with the user's key.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Search runs through the platform's search provider (Perplexity search API per web-search-providers.json) or, for some models, the model provider's own search tool; four tool shapes are recognised (generic function, OpenAI hosted, Anthropic server, Google built-in) (required-search.ts:260-295). The model must accept tools; a model without tools gets single-turn handling (route.ts:792-794). CLI uses Brave Search or Tavily.

access_and_usage.account: Cloud search needs a signed-in account. CLI outside Cloud needs only a search key. VS Code needs a key for Local or own-key use.
access_and_usage.permissions: Capability canUseWebSearch decides access (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1599; ChatStateManager.ts:2358). Workspace policy can block sites. Tool approval default lets search run unasked (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-15-01).
access_and_usage.subscription: Free: 20 included calls per 30 days; paid: no included calls, charged in credits (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-15-16; search-budget.ts:66-68, :133-142). API, CLI, VS Code, AGI Work, research and scheduled runs are charged to credits even on Free.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 5 results per call; 3 calls per turn (10 for AGI Work); 400-character query; 15 second timeout; up to 32 domain rules, 20 forwarded to the provider.
access_and_usage.flags: generic_web_search billing flag (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1596); FEATURES.webSearch on Mobile (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:22); kill switch for capabilities.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs a model with native search, or tools plus the generic backend; Auto uses the generic backend flag (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1602-1616). Free plan on its own model is offered search only when required (required-search.ts:236-246).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Native search shapes depend on the model's provider route; the platform search needs PERPLEXITY_API_KEY configured (name only).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local mode on a phone or desktop does not use the Cloud search route; no on-device search was found. CLI Local needs the user's own Brave or Tavily key and sends the query to that service; whether Local privacy mode blocks it is unknown.

features.summary: Files added to a project become knowledge that every chat in that project can use. Short files are sent whole; long ones are searched and only matching passages are sent. steps.what_happens: The app uploads the file (checksum bound) and registers it; the server extracts text and summary and starts indexing.
The indexer splits text, optionally embeds it, and stores chunks; the file shows pending, indexing, indexed or failed.
On each chat turn the chat service loads the project, ranks files against the question, and for files over 16,000 characters queries the index for matching passages.
Whole files, passages, instructions and sibling chat excerpts are fitted into a character budget and sent to the model with citations.
Mobile Local: sources are read from the phone and added as a system message; no server involved.

features.summary: After a finished answer, the app can show up to three tappable next questions. When a short request is too vague, the assistant can show a choice card instead of guessing. Follow-ups run on Web, Desktop and Mobile (Cloud only). Choice cards run on Web, Mobile and Chrome. The CLI has a separate question tool.

purpose.what_it_does: Two helpers that keep a chat moving. Follow-up suggestions show up to three short questions under the last answer; one tap sends it as the next message. The clarify card shows one to four questions, each with two to four options plus a free-text 'Something else' box, so the person answers by tapping instead of typing.
purpose.why_it_exists: Leaders such as ChatGPT and Perplexity show related questions after a searched answer, and ask a quick choice question when a request has no usable default. The code comments say the same: a searched turn earns follow-ups, and an ambiguous request used to come back as prose asking the reader to describe the choice in words (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:1428; apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts:210).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone chatting on Web, the public Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile in Cloud mode, or the Chrome side panel. Developers on the CLI get the ask_user tool.
problems_solved: People do not know what to ask next after an answer.
A vague one-line request such as a trip with no destination leads to a guess or a wall of questions in prose.
Typing a reply on a phone is slow; a tap is faster.
use_cases: After a web-searched answer about a product, tap 'Is it repairable?'-style follow-up to dig deeper.
Type a bare 'plan my trip' and pick destination and budget from a card.
On Mobile in Cloud mode, tap a suggested question under the answer while the composer is empty.
In the CLI, the agent asks which of three options to take, and the person picks one in the terminal.

screens_and_controls: Follow-up chip: one tap sends its text as the next user message (apps/web/features/chat/components/FollowUpSuggestions.tsx:118).
'Hide' button: hides the group for that answer on Web (dismissed state, line 94) and Mobile.
Clarify card option buttons, a 'Something else…' text box per question, 'Send answers', and 'I'll just type it' (dismiss).
CLI option picker with a last row 'Type your own answer'.
journey: 1. Ask a question; the answer streams in. If it searched the web, Web marks the turn as searched.
2. When the reply finishes and is longer than 20 characters and did not fail, Web asks the server for three questions grounded in the answer and its source titles; chips appear when they arrive.
3. If the server gives nothing (temporary chat, refused, error), Web shows chips picked by a keyword matcher instead.
4. Tap a chip; its text is sent as the next message.
5. Separate path: send a short vague message. If the model decides it cannot go on, it calls the clarify tool and a card appears.
6. Tick options or type in 'Something else…', press 'Send answers'; the answers go back as the next turn and the model continues.
7. Or press 'I'll just type it' to decline and answer in your own words.
feedback_and_outputs: Chips fade in with a short stagger; they are hidden while the person is typing (Web) or while the composer has text (Mobile).
After answering, the clarify card turns read-only and shows each answer, 'Skipped' or 'No answer'.

A failed answer shows an error line: "Couldn't send that answer, the questions are still waiting for you." (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:1354).

established.statement: Follow-ups appear only if the user setting for follow-up suggestions is on, the last reply is longer than 20 characters, it is not generating or failed, and either follow-ups are enabled for the surface or the last turn searched the web.
established.source: S34.21 'Should' in the area brief, matches apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:1466-1474

established.statement: Follow-up generation is hidden in temporary chats, and any follow-up that asks for a web search is dropped when search was unavailable.
The clarify tool is offered only for short messages with no attachment, URL or code, and not for research runs; choices that are only about format, tone or length are rejected.

After a search-backed answer, the user is offered follow-up or refined queries and can send one with a tap (Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome per the area, with CLI, VS Code and Chrome marked missing).
When a query is ambiguous the product offers clarification choices the user can pick before answering.
Citation chip and sources disclosure and search and citations are named components of the experience contract; follow-ups and clarify are not named there.

acceptance_criteria: On Web with the setting on, after a web-searched answer longer than 20 characters finishes, one to three chips appear under it; tapping one sends that text as a new user message.
With the setting off, no chips appear on Web or Desktop.
In a temporary chat on Web, no server call is made for suggestions and the keyword-matched chips appear instead.
When the turn's web search was unavailable, no chip containing 'search ... web' or 'browse ... online' wording is shown on Web or Mobile.
On Mobile in Cloud mode, chips appear under the last clean answer only while the composer is empty, and 'Hide' removes them for that answer.
A bare 'plan my trip' on Web in Cloud mode can produce a clarify card; a message that starts with 'summarize', or holds a URL, code fence or attachment, does not offer the tool.
Pressing 'Send answers' on a clarify card sends the chosen labels back and the card becomes read-only.
A card whose options are only 'Short / Long / Bullets' is rejected and the model answers directly.

Because the Electron desktop shell reports the 'desktop' surface, the clarify tool should be allowed there if Desktop is meant to match Web. [inferred]

steps.what_happens: Web finishes an answer and decides whether chips may show (setting, length over 20, not failed, searched or enabled).
Web or Mobile posts to the follow-ups route for the answer's message id, once per answer.
Server loads the conversation and message, returns empty for a temporary chat, or the cached set if present.
Otherwise it admits a utility route, reserves usage, sends the answer (max 6,000 characters) and up to 8 source titles to a model, and sanitises the lines into at most three questions.
The model call goes to the chosen provider adapter.
The set is saved into the message metadata under followUpSuggestions unless one already exists; the client shows the chips, or the keyword matcher if the list is empty.
Tapping a chip sends its text through the normal send path.

For the clarify card: the client lists clarify.v1 in x_interactive_cards, the server adds the tool if the message passes the test, the model calls it, the server validates and stores a card, and the turn pauses.
The person's answers go to the respond endpoint, which records them on the card; the client then sends the answers as the next message.
CLI ask_user shows the question in the TUI or terminal, or asks the connected client, and returns 'User responded: ...' to the model.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The suggestion call uses a model chosen by the managed Auto route on the economy tier, not the model the user picked, and is dispatched through the server provider adapter (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/admission.ts:25-27; generate-follow-ups.ts:137-146). The clarify tool is called by whichever model answers the turn, and only if that model can use tools (request-processor.ts:5598). The keyword matcher uses no model.

access_and_usage.account: Follow-ups and clarify need a signed-in account because both go through account-scoped server routes (getUserScopedDb in route.ts:26; respond/route.ts:61). The keyword fallback on Web needs no account but is only shown after the server step settles.
access_and_usage.permissions: The route checks the conversation belongs to the user and organisation (route.ts:36-44). Workspace rules for providers apply through managed admission. No other permission found.
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan check in the follow-up code beyond the usage lease: the lease takes the entitled plan tier and refuses when the reservation fails, which returns no suggestions (generate-follow-ups.ts:151-176). Which plans may use it: unknown. The clarify tool has no plan check of its own; the chat route itself is gated by plan (apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:121).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: One model call per answer, 160 output tokens, three suggestions, lease of 60 seconds, usage recorded as follow_up_suggestions (generate-follow-ups.ts:24-33,155-170). The route uses the 'chat-message' rate limit (route.ts:31). Clarify limits: at most 4 questions, 4 options, labels 60 characters, questions 200 (clarify-tool-service.ts:14-19).
access_and_usage.flags: Setting followUpSuggestionsEnabled (default on). Prop enableFollowUpSuggestions (default off, not passed in app code). Request field x_interactive_cards.supported must list clarify.v1. No remote feature flag found.

features.summary: Shows where an answer came from. Web and Desktop show site-name citation chips with a hover card and a side panel listing 'Citations' and 'More' as cards. Mobile shows tappable [n] citations with a preview and a 'Sources' sheet. The Chrome side panel has hover cards and a Sources list. CLI prints a text footer. VS Code has a link list.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns the pages an answer used into visible, clickable sources: inline citation chips, a compact 'Sources' control, a full list, and links that open the original page.
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to check an answer. Claude and ChatGPT show cited sources next to answers; the experience contract lists 'Citation chip and sources disclosure' and 'Search and citations' as required parts (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:394,457).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who gets a web-searched or researched answer on any of the six apps.
problems_solved: Trust: the reader can see and open each source.
Context: a hover or tap preview shows title, site, date and a snippet without leaving the answer.
Clutter: many sources fold into one compact control.
use_cases: Hover a citation on Web to read a snippet, click to open the page in a new tab.
Open the sources panel to see which pages were cited and which were only searched.
On a phone, tap [2] in the text to see a preview, then 'Open page'.
In the CLI, read the numbered 'Sources' list under the answer.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): inline citation chips in the answer; a 'Sources' pill under the answer labelled 'View N sources' for screen readers; a globe button 'Open sources panel' (title 'Research sources') in the chat header menu; the side panel tab 'Sources' with headings 'Citations' and 'More' (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:306-318,351-352,429).

Mobile: a pill 'Sources' (or 'Sources so far' while a run waits or after a stop) under the answer opens a sheet with headings 'Citations' and 'More'; inline [n] citations are tappable (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CollapsibleSources.tsx:156-160,246-256).

prerequisites: The answer must have search results or citations in its metadata (web search ran, research, or native grounding).

CLI: the turn must have called web search (or the managed route sent search results); in own-key mode a Brave or Tavily key must be configured (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/web/mod.rs:431-435).
screens_and_controls: Citation chip (link): shows favicon or globe, site name, '+N' for grouped sources; hover or keyboard focus opens a card with title, site, published date, 'Retrieved <date>' and a 180-character snippet (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx:109-186; citationPublisher.ts:89-115).

4. Click the chip or choose 'Open page' to open the original page (new tab without referrer on Web and Chrome; in-app browser on Mobile).
5. Open the whole list: Web pill or globe button, Mobile pill, Chrome or VS Code details, CLI footer.
6. Click or tap a card to open its page.

established.statement: Sources behind an answer are shown as cards with at least title, site and link.
Hovering or tapping a citation shows a preview (title, site, snippet) without leaving the answer.
A compact source summary can be expanded to the full list of sources used and consulted.
From a citation or source card the user can open the original page or document.
Each card shows the site icon, title, site, date, snippet and an external-link mark (Web panel).
Links open in a new tab without referrer; only openable links are pressable on mobile; with no sources the panel says 'No sources yet'.
Citation chip and sources disclosure and search and citations are required transcript components.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, an answer with three searched pages shows a 'Sources · 3' style pill only after streaming ends.
Hovering or keyboard-focusing a citation chip shows title, site, published and retrieved dates and a snippet of at most 180 characters.
Clicking a chip opens the first source in a new tab; the link has rel noopener noreferrer.
The panel lists cited pages under 'Citations' numbered by citation order and the rest under 'More'; an empty panel says 'No sources yet'.
On Mobile, tapping [n] in the answer shows an alert with Cancel and 'Open page'; a source with an invalid URL is not pressable.
On Mobile, the 'Sources' pill reads 'Sources so far' when a run is waiting for approval or ended early.
In the CLI, a turn with web results prints 'Sources' and one numbered line per distinct URL; a turn with none prints nothing.
On Chrome, the 'N sources' details list has an accessible label and each item opens in a new tab.

Opening a source should never load a third-party favicon on Mobile without the person asking (CollapsibleSources.tsx:41-44). [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add an 'open source' action in the CLI TUI using the same list.
[proposed] Show snippet and date in the VS Code list.

steps.what_happens: A searching turn runs the web search tool on the server, which calls a search provider and returns up to 5 results (title, URL, snippet, date).
Results and citations are stored in the message metadata and sent to the client.
The client builds the source list, removes duplicates, links [n] markers, and splits cited from more.
Hover or tap shows the preview from data already on the device; no request is made for the preview.
The browser may fetch the site's icon from a public favicon service (Web and Chrome side panel use google favicons URL; Mobile does not).
Clicking opens the original page in a new tab, or in the in-app browser on Mobile.
CLI own-key: the device calls the Brave or Tavily search service directly with the user's saved key; in Managed mode the cloud runs the search and streams result events.
The CLI renders the footer after the turn ends.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model decides what to cite; the search itself runs on a search provider, not the chat model: the server uses Perplexity search with a key set in environment configuration named PERPLEXITY_API_KEY (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-providers.json), and some turns use native search of the answering model (message-sources.ts comments). The CLI own-key mode uses Brave or Tavily. Viewing sources uses no model.

access_and_usage.account: Sources are shown for any answer that has them. Producing them needs the managed chat service (account) or, on the CLI, a search key. Viewing them needs no extra account.
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace site rules can drop results: the CLI filters results the workspace administrator does not allow (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/web/mod.rs:462-471); the server applies allow and deny domain lists to results (web-search-tool.ts:458).
access_and_usage.subscription: No gate on viewing sources found. Searching is metered: each search is charged as Agentic search (apps/web/public/openapi.json:762). Plan limits on search: see apps/web/lib/web-search/search-allowance.ts (not read).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: At most 5 results per search and 3 searches per turn (10 in AGI Work) (web-search-tool.ts:54-56). Snippet clip 180 characters in hover cards and 300 in the CLI.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Display works for any model that returns citations or whose turn ran the search tool.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Search provider is fixed per route (Perplexity on the server; Brave or Tavily on CLI own-key).
access_and_usage.local_mode: No source cards come from local inference by itself. On Mobile Local mode no search tool was found in the paths read; unknown. On the CLI the web_search tool runs on the device but calls an outside search service, so it is not offline; whether Local mode blocks it is unknown.

features.summary: A list of search controls the product does not have: choosing source types, academic, news, video, image or social search, language and region filters, and adding, removing or saving a source on an answer. There is nothing to click in any app. The web search tool takes only query text. Nearby: allowed and blocked site lists and Search dialog chips.

purpose.what_it_does: Records what is missing so no one assumes it exists. It also names the closest things that are built, so a tester knows what not to expect.
purpose.why_it_exists: Perplexity, ChatGPT and Claude offer some of these (for example academic or news modes, or source filters). The brief lists them as requirements; the code has none, and four are marked not applicable.
purpose.who_uses_it: Product owners, engineers planning search work, and testers who must not report a missing control as a bug that was never built.
problems_solved: Stops false 'done' claims.
Shows where the nearest working controls are.
Gives each gap an owner and an evidence line.
use_cases: A tester is told to find an 'Academic' mode: this page says there is none.
An engineer plans a news-only search: starts from the single query field in the web search tool.

features.summary: Starting a Deep Research run: the person switches on Deep Research in the chat box (web, desktop through the hosted web app, mobile) or sends research true on a streaming chat request. The server checks plan, model and lockdown, then runs a bounded plan, search and write loop. Only the web plan card shows a credit estimate.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person ask a question as a Deep Research run instead of a normal chat reply. The server plans searches, runs them within fixed limits, then writes a cited report. The web plan card shows an estimated credit cost and the credits available [inferred from ResearchCostEstimate.tsx:32-57].
purpose.why_it_exists: Research costs many model calls and searches, so it is opt-in, paid-plan only and bounded, and the cost is shown before the person approves spending (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md W08 row, line 781).

problems_solved: A normal chat answer does not read many sources and cite them.
Unbounded agent loops could spend a person's budget without warning.
Models that cannot do research must not silently fail.

steps.what_happens: Composer decides research is allowed (plan, model capability) and sends research true with stream true.
The server parses the body, refuses Free plans and free trials, checks the capability gate and the research-capable model, applies the research prompt and turns web search on.
Lockdown check: refuse with lockdown_blocks_research.
The route starts a cloud agent run of kind research, scopes connectors, searches the person's files and starts the loop.
The loop makes tool-free planning, searches through the search backend, then a tool-free writing turn.
Each search is admitted and billed through the search budget before running.
The estimate on the plan card is computed in the browser from the catalog price and the usage summary.

features.summary: While a research run is active the person can Steer it with a note, Pause it to resume later, or Stop it. Web has all three plus Resume with optional guidance; mobile has Pause, Stop and Resume or Retry but no Steer; VS Code can steer and stop a cloud run; Chrome is unverified.

purpose.what_it_does: Steer queues a message the loop reads between rounds. Pause asks the loop to stop at the next round and save what it gathered. Stop cancels the run. Resume starts a new request that carries earlier sources and finished steps [research-loop.ts:3171-3172,2092-2105,2039-2060].
purpose.why_it_exists: Runs last minutes and cost money; people need to change direction or stop without losing what was gathered (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:781).
purpose.who_uses_it: People running Deep Research on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile, and VS Code users managing cloud tasks.
problems_solved: A run heads the wrong way.
The person must leave and come back.
A run must stop to protect spend.
use_cases: Steer: 'focus on EU rules'.
Pause now and resume tomorrow with a note.
Stop a run that is no longer needed.

Mobile: 'Pause' and 'Stop' buttons on the research card, and 'Resume' or 'Retry' after it ends [ResearchRunCard.tsx:651,660,679; chatExecutionStore.ts:5525].
VS Code: cloud task detail list items 'Steer' and 'Stop this task' [apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudRunDetail.ts:166-181].

Server stores a pause, steer or cancel flag on the cloud agent run row and writes an audit event for pause.

Loop saves an interrupted report and ends the stream with a stop event.
Resume sends a new request with the carried material.
