features.summary: When a run is stopped, paused, or cut off it is saved once as an interrupted report with the sources and steps gathered. Stopping or pausing stores no written text; only a cut-short writing turn keeps partial text. The reader shows a banner. Budget limits still produce a completed report that names what was not searched.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves the run's state in table research_reports exactly once with a status (completed, interrupted, failed), so the person can reopen it or resume [research-loop.ts:1984-2032].
purpose.why_it_exists: A stopped or failed run has cost money and gathered real sources; they should not vanish (migration comment 0094).

features.summary: The report reader shows one finished Deep Research report: title, source count, duration and credit cost, a contents list, the body with clickable [n] citations, tables, mermaid charts and a Sources list. Web and the public Desktop (which shows the web app) have a Report tab; mobile has a Reports screen. Supporting attachments are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Takes a saved research report (title, summary, key findings, planned questions, markdown body, citations) and presents it for reading. It builds a contents list from the headings, turns [n] markers into links to a numbered Sources list, and renders markdown tables and mermaid charts through the shared markdown renderer on web and a chart view on mobile.
purpose.why_it_exists: A research run produces a long, cited document. People need to read it comfortably, jump around it, and check where each claim came from, instead of reading raw model output in a chat bubble.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid-plan people who ran Deep Research (the server refuses research on plans without the capability, see D-2026-09-28-11), on web, public Desktop and mobile; testers and engineers checking citations.
problems_solved: Long reports are hard to navigate without a contents list.
A numbered claim cannot be checked if the number does not lead to a source.
Reports that cite sources the run never captured would otherwise look sourceless; the reader says so.
Figures in a comparison are easier to read as a table or chart.
use_cases: Open the Report tab after a run, click a heading in Contents to jump to a section.
Click [3] in a sentence to scroll to source 3 and open its link.
Open the full-screen reader to read a long report in a narrow column.
On the phone, open Reports from the drawer, open a report and tap a section.

where_to_find_it: Web (and public Desktop, which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): Research panel opened with the sources toggle (aria-label 'Open sources panel'), tab 'Report' shows the newest report of the open conversation (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx:418-431,214-313). Tab 'Library' opens any report in the same viewer (ResearchPanel.tsx:432-445).

established.statement: A finished report opens in a dedicated reader with title, summary, body and sources.
The reader shows an outline of sections the user can navigate.
Citations in the report link to their sources.
Reports can include tables and charts that render in the reader.
A report can carry supporting attachments the user can open or download. Status missing on every app.
Research is offered on paid plans and the server refuses a research request the capability document denies.

acceptance_criteria: With a report that has 3 or more headings, 'Contents' lists them and clicking one scrolls to it.
A [n] where source n exists is a link; a [n] with n above the source count stays plain text.
A report with no captured citations but [n] markers shows the 'run recorded no links' note, not a blank.
A markdown table in the body renders as a table; a mermaid xychart-beta or pie block renders as a chart on web and mobile.
Header shows source count, seconds and credits when the report has them (web).
Full-screen toggle opens a dialog, Escape closes it and focus returns to the toggle.
A stopped, paused or failed report shows its banner.
Attachments: a tester finds none (documented gap).
inferred: Mobile should show the same count, duration and cost as web, since the brief's Should line names them for the header (brief S35.20 lists title, summary, body, sources; the cost line is from the task draft) [inferred].
Reading mode should keep the report content identical and only change layout [inferred from ResearchReportView.tsx:327].
proposed: [proposed] Add source count, duration and cost to the mobile reader header.
[proposed] Add attachment storage for data files and source documents through the files and artifacts system.
[proposed] Show a visible contents list on shorter reports or a collapsed outline instead of hiding at fewer than 3 headings.

features.summary: Inline citation markers turn a marker such as [1] in an assistant answer into a small source chip at the claim it supports. Touching markers such as [1][2] become one grouped chip. Web, Desktop (hosted web) and the Chrome side panel draw site-name chips. Mobile draws teal [n] text. CLI and VS Code have no markers.

purpose.what_it_does: Places a clickable source marker at the end of the claim it backs, so the reader can see which source supports which sentence. The shared web renderer turns the text marker into a pill with the site name, an optional +N count and a hover card (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx:124-186). Mobile turns the marker into teal [n] text that opens a preview (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MarkdownInline.tsx:256).
purpose.why_it_exists: A reader cannot trust a sourced answer if sources sit only in a list at the bottom. The area brief says each claim carries a marker that identifies its source (S36.01) and sits at the claim it supports (S36.16) and that one claim can cite several sources (S36.17). docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:283 asks for each citation to connect to the correct source.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading a web-grounded or research answer in Web, Desktop, Mobile or the Chrome side panel. Engineers and testers use it as the reference for how markers become chips.
problems_solved: The reader cannot tell which source backs which sentence.
Raw [1] text is easy to miss and not clickable.
Several markers in a row clutter the line.
A marker that points to no delivered source could mislead, so it is left as plain text.
use_cases: A user asks a current-events question on Web and clicks the chip after a sentence to open the first source.
A user hovers a chip with +2 and reads all three sources in the card.
A mobile user taps [1, 2] and picks one of two sources from a list.
A Chrome side-panel user hovers a chip to read the source card.

where_to_find_it: Web: inside the answer text of any assistant message that has sources (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2035, 2887-2900).

Desktop: the public Desktop window shows the hosted web app, so it shows the same chips (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). The retained Tauri build renders its own shared message bubble with a citation pill list (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:846); whether Tauri also draws inline chips is unknown.
Mobile: inside the answer text as teal [n] markers (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MarkdownInline.tsx:256-280).
Chrome side panel: inside the answer bubble (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:402).
CLI and VS Code: not available.
prerequisites: The answer must come with a delivered source list and markers in its text (or provider positions that the app turns into markers, packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/citationMarkers.ts:138).
Markers are linked only after streaming ends on Web (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx:915-916).
Web search or research must have produced sources. The route that does this for each mode is not established here.
screens_and_controls: Web/Desktop chip: round pill with a favicon or globe, the site name and +N when more than one source (CitationChip.tsx:150-166). It is a link to the first source with target _blank and rel noopener noreferrer (CitationChip.tsx:147-151).
Web/Desktop hover card: lists every source for the claim (CitationChip.tsx:168-182).
Mobile marker: teal text [n] or [n, m], role link, label 'Citation n: title' (MarkdownInline.tsx:268-279).
Chrome chip: link showing the host, and a count label from locale key spCitationMore when grouped (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/sources.ts:42-56).
journey: Ask a question that triggers web search or research.

features.summary: Points a citation inside the user's own material. A project-file chip shows the file name and a page or heading trail and opens the project file at that place. A past-chat chip opens the earlier chat at the message used. Web, Desktop (hosted web) and Mobile have both; CLI, VS Code and Chrome do not.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows which project files and which earlier chats an answer used, with a place inside them, and links the reader to that place (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/ProjectFileCitationChip.tsx:111; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/CitationPastChats.tsx:21).
purpose.why_it_exists: Without it the reader cannot tell a remembered or file-based fact from an invented one (comment in CitationPastChats.tsx:15-19). The brief asks for page locators (S36.09) and message links (S36.14).
purpose.who_uses_it: Users who work with Projects and memory on Web, Desktop and Mobile.
problems_solved: No way to check which file page an answer came from.
No way to reach the chat a recalled fact came from.
Three passages on one page would show as three identical chips.
use_cases: Click 'report.pdf · p. 12' to open the project with the file at page 12.
Click a past-chat chip to open the earlier chat at the message.
On Mobile, tap a file chip, read the passage, then tap Open file.
See a heading trail such as 'Pricing › Refunds' for a document with headings.

where_to_find_it: Web: below an assistant answer, a row labelled (for screen readers) 'Project files used in this answer' and a nav 'Previous chats this answer used' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3577-3587).

CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not available.

working: The contract parses an untrusted list of project sources, keeps at most 8, clips names to 200 and passages to 160 characters (packages/contracts/types/src/project-file-citations.ts:29-35, 66-84).
An anchor is a page number, or a heading trail cut to the last 3 segments of up to 60 characters each; a valid page wins over a heading trail (project-file-citations.ts:44-60).
Anchor text is 'p. N' or the trail joined by ' › ' (project-file-citations.ts:86-93).
Two citations for the same file and place become one chip (project-file-citations.ts:95-113).
Href is /chat/projects/<projectId>?knowledgeFile=<fileId>&page=<n>; no project or file id gives no link (project-file-citations.ts:117-150).
A chip without a link is a note (ProjectFileCitationChip.tsx:56).
A chip whose location is named in the answer text comes first (project-file-citations.ts:152-165).
Past-chat link is /chat/<conversationId>?highlightMessage=<messageId> (CitationPastChats.tsx:11-14); the chat page scrolls and flashes that message (WebChatPage.tsx:5088-5112).

The server sends sources in a base64 JSON response header, capped at 6000 characters, dropping snippets if too long (apps/web/lib/chat-project-sources.ts:21-40; free-quota-turn.ts:1320 for the past-chat header).
The server builds page markers and heading anchors from file text (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-anchors.ts:34, 77).
Mobile has both chips and deep links to projects and chats (ProjectFileCitations.tsx; PastChatCitations.tsx; apps/mobile/app/(app)/projects/[id].tsx and chat/[id].tsx use the param names).

features.summary: Tells the reader when a cited source cannot be opened. Web and Desktop show a notice when a research report cites numbered sources the run never saved links for. Mobile disables a chip or card that has no openable link. No app marks a source as restricted or as stale. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have nothing.

purpose.what_it_does: Stops the product from showing a dead link for a source it cannot open. On Web and Desktop, a research report whose text cites [1], [2] and so on but whose saved source list is empty shows a Sources heading and a sentence saying the links were not recorded (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchReportView.tsx:618-640). On Mobile, a citation chip or search-result card whose URL is missing or not http/https is rendered disabled and announced as text, not a link (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CitationChip.tsx:71,86,94; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/WebSearchResultCard.tsx:36,41,42). Restricted-source and stale-source notices do not exist in the code (brief S36.20, S36.21: missing on all apps).
purpose.why_it_exists: A reader cannot tell whether a report has no sources or the product lost them. The code comment says hiding the section left numbered references pointing at nothing (apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchReportView.tsx:619-624). The brief also requires restricted and stale notices (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/036-sources-and-grounding-interface.md S36.20, S36.21).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading a Deep Research report or an answer with citations on Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app) or Mobile.
problems_solved: A numbered reference in a report that points at nothing, with no explanation.
A tappable chip on Mobile that does nothing when the source has no usable link.
Not knowing whether a source is out of date or off limits: NOT solved today.
use_cases: A user opens an older report on Web whose source list was never saved and sees the notice instead of an empty space.
A user on Mobile sees a search-result card for a source with a bad URL and cannot tap it.
A tester wants a stale or restricted notice: none exists, so this is a gap.

steps.what_happens: Person opens a saved report on Web or Desktop; the page fetches reports for the signed-in user.
Server reads the report row including its citations JSON array and returns it.
ResearchReportView counts citations and cited [n] numbers in the text; if citations are empty and numbers exist it renders the notice.
Source rows load favicons from a third-party favicon service by domain.
On Mobile, the same API is called, the mapper drops URL-less citations, and the appendix renders chips or cards, disabled when the URL is not http/https.
Tapping an openable Mobile chip shows a dialog, then opens the page in the in-app browser.

features.summary: A project (the brief calls it a notebook) is a named workspace in the AGI account that holds instructions, source files and chats. This feature lists the projects a person can open and creates new ones. Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile, CLI and VS Code have it; Chrome only reads the list for two pickers.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the projects the signed-in person owns or that are shared with them, lets them open one, and creates a new project that is stored in the account. The product UI says 'project'; the brief says 'notebook'. [inferred from labels: 'New project', 'Create project'] (apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx:247; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ProjectGallery.tsx:264)
purpose.why_it_exists: Chats need a home where instructions and source files are kept together, so answers can be grounded in the same material every time. The list is the way back into that home. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who wants a standing workspace: students, researchers, people who work with the same documents again and again.
problems_solved: Without it every chat starts with no memory of the user's documents and rules.
Without a shared list the same workspace would have to be rebuilt on each app.
Free accounts need a clear limit on how many workspaces they can make (5 on the free plan) (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:618).
use_cases: A student creates a project called 'Biology' on the web and later opens it on the phone.
A developer runs 'agi projects create Launch' in the terminal, then sees it in VS Code.
A team member opens a project a colleague shared with them (team workspace only).
A person archives an old project and restores it later from the Archived view.

where_to_find_it: Web: the Projects page at /chat/projects, titled 'Projects'; button 'New project'; sort menu 'Sort: Updated (newest) / Created (newest) / Name (A-Z) / Starred first'; link 'Archived (n)' (apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx:27-32, 247, 274, 292).

Desktop: the public Desktop window shows the hosted web app, so it is the same page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). The retained Tauri build has its own list in apps/desktop/src/features/v3/AgiWorkProjects.tsx:61 but it is not the public Desktop (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

Mobile: the Projects tab (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/projects.tsx). Controls: 'Search projects', 'Create new project', 'Sort projects', 'Filter projects' with All, Created by you, Shared with you, Archived (apps/mobile/src/features/projects/projectList.ts:24-29; projects.tsx:345, 445, 451).
CLI: 'agi projects list', 'agi projects create <name> [--description]', 'agi projects show', 'agi projects recent', 'agi projects link' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1287-1340).

VS Code: the Projects tree in the side bar, commands 'Code: Show Projects', 'Code: Refresh Projects', 'Code: Open Projects on Web' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:650-661; projectsTree.ts:87-121).
Chrome: no list screen found. The side panel fetches the project list only to fill the 'move chat to a project' picker and the @-mention list (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:12323, 14479).
prerequisites: An AGI account signed in on the app (web: signed-in session; CLI: signed in and Cloud privacy mode; VS Code: account token) (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368-381; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/projects/projectsClient.ts:77-83).
Creating needs the 'projects' workspace feature to be allowed by the workspace policy and a plan that allows projects (apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts:147-166).
Mobile: Cloud mode for account projects; Local mode shows projects kept only on the device (apps/mobile/src/features/projects/store.ts:390-436).
screens_and_controls: Web list: search box 'Search projects...', 'New project', cards with pin/star, archive, delete, share, 'Show more' / 'Loading projects' pagination (ProjectGallery.tsx:247-264; page.tsx:491).
Web create dialog 'Create project': 'Project name' field (required) and a description field (apps/web/features/chat/components/dialogs/CreateProjectDialog.tsx:135-190).
Mobile: project cards, pull to refresh, retry buttons, empty states 'No archived projects' and 'Nothing is shared with you yet.' (projects.tsx:52, 421-426).
VS Code: tree items; a notice item 'Sign in to see your projects' (projectsTree.ts:93), 'Projects could not be loaded' with Retry (107), 'No projects yet' that starts Create Project (118).
journey: Open the app's project list (web Projects page, mobile Projects tab, CLI 'agi projects list', VS Code Projects tree).
Read the list. It shows the person's own projects and, in a team workspace, projects shared with them.
To open one, select it (web card, mobile card, VS Code tree item).
To create one, choose 'New project' (web, mobile) or run 'agi projects create <name>' or the VS Code create command, type a name, optionally a description and instructions, then confirm.
The new project appears in the list and, because it is saved to the account, in the other apps after their next refresh.

established.statement: The user sees a list of their notebooks (knowledge workspaces) and can open one.
The user can create a new notebook that is saved to the account.
Signed-out VS Code users see a sign-in prompt, not an empty list.
Projects are shared across apps through the account (the CLI header says the list is shared with the web app and mobile).
One Subscription system governs project limits: a plan sets the number of projects and a 0 limit refuses creation.
Projects is a general-availability feature present on all surfaces per the matrix.

acceptance_criteria: Signed in on web, the Projects page lists every project created on another app within one refresh, and shows 'No projects yet.' only when none exist.
Creating a project with an empty name is refused; a valid name creates it and it appears in the list on a second app after refresh.
On the free plan, creating a sixth project is refused with a message naming the plan limit; the project count does not change.
In VS Code signed out, the tree shows 'Sign in to see your projects'; signed in with no projects it shows 'No projects yet'.
In the CLI with a signed-out account, 'agi projects list' fails with a sign-in error and does not print an empty list.
In a team workspace, a project shared with the user appears in the web list marked as shared and opens read-only unless they have edit access.
inferred: The mobile Local-mode project list is a separate device-only list; creating a project in Local mode must not appear on other apps [inferred from store.ts:421-436].
Shared projects should appear on every app that lists projects; today only web, mobile and VS Code request the full list [inferred from the sync route SQL and listAllManagedCloudProjects use].
proposed: [proposed] Show shared projects in the CLI list, or print a line saying shared projects are web-only.
[proposed] Give Chrome a read-only project list screen, or record in the matrix that Chrome only uses projects as a picker.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the list; the app calls GET /api/projects with the account session (CLI uses the sync route).
Server checks rate limit and workspace access, reads the caller's projects plus projects shared into the active team workspace, counts non-temporary conversations, and pages the result.

Person creates a project; server validates the body, checks the CSRF token, the 'projects' workspace feature and the plan limit, then inserts the row and a quota guard in one statement inside a transaction.
Server records a 'project_created' analytics event and returns 201 with the project.
Mobile in Local mode writes the project into the on-device store and never calls the server; in Cloud mode it writes the cloud store, marks it dirty and the sync engine pushes it.
Other apps pick the new project up on their next list or sync pull.

features.summary: Each project has a name, a description and instructions. The person can change them at any time on web, mobile, CLI and VS Code. Instructions and description are added to the model's context in every chat in that project, so the person does not repeat the rules in each chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a name (up to 200 characters), a description (up to 2000) and instructions (up to 10000) per project and sends them with every chat in the project (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/project-contract.json:3-5; apps/web/lib/services/project-context-service.ts:585-610).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want a workspace to behave the same way every time, for example 'answer in Spanish', without typing it again. It also lets a project be recognised by name. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Project owners; on a shared project, people granted edit access may change name, description, instructions and appearance (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:262-271).

Telling projects apart in a long list.
Keeping edits safe when two people or two apps change the project at once (If-Match version check).

steps.what_happens: Person edits a field in the app and saves; the app sends PUT /api/projects/[id] with the project version in If-Match.
Server verifies CSRF, rate limit and body, builds the update, and matches by owner and version; on a miss it checks if the caller is an editor.
Server returns the new project with a new ETag, or the latest copy with a precondition-failed answer.
On the next project chat turn the server loads the project row and renders name, description and instructions into prompt blocks.
In mobile Local mode the phone adds the instructions as a system message before sending to the on-device model.
Mobile Cloud mode edits the cloud store, marks the project dirty and the sync engine pushes it.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Whatever model the chat uses receives the project text as system context; the notebook feature does not pick a model. Project text is trimmed to a character budget and dropped by layer when the context is full (project-context-service.ts:554-568). In Local mode the on-device model gets the instructions; no provider is called by the edit itself.

access_and_usage.permissions: Owner may edit everything; an editor may edit name, description, instructions, appearance; a viewer cannot (route.ts:33-43, 257-279; ProjectSharingControls.tsx:40-48).

access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Instructions are plain text for any model; none found in the code that varies by model.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode: instructions live on the device and are sent only to the on-device model (chatExecutionStore.ts:2755-2775). Web, CLI, VS Code: no Local mode.

features.summary: A project owner in a team workspace can share a project with everyone in the workspace or only invited people, and give each person view or edit access. Members see instructions and files, but chats stay private. Separately, account projects sync across web, mobile and CLI through the same account routes.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets an owner or sharing manager share a project into a team workspace with an audience ('Everyone in the workspace can view' or 'Only people you invite') and per-member access (Can view, Can edit, No access). Also keeps one account's projects the same on every signed-in app (apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectShareDialog.tsx:56-143; apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectSharingControls.tsx:40-44, 105-106).
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams need shared source material and rules without sharing private chats; individuals need the same workspace on each device. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Team owners and admins, members with the content.share permission, and every person who uses more than one AGI app.
problems_solved: Sharing documents and instructions without copying them.
Controlling who can only read and who can change sources.
Seeing the same project on web, phone and terminal.
use_cases: An owner shares 'Launch' with the whole workspace as view-only.
An owner invites one colleague with Can edit so they can add sources.
A member opens 'Shared with you' on the phone and reads the files.
A user creates a project on the CLI and finds it on the web.

where_to_find_it: Web: project card or project page menu item 'Share' opens the dialog 'Share <project>' with description 'Choose who can open this project and what they can do.' (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:150-153; apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx:653, 1358).
Desktop: same hosted web page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

Mobile: Project settings screen, section for who can access (ProjectMembersSection mounted at ProjectSettingsScreen.tsx:193); Projects tab filter 'Shared with you' and screen 'Shared with you' (SharedWithYouScreen.tsx:267, 281); read-only 'Shared project' screen (SharedProjectScreen.tsx:99-171).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no sharing screen found.
prerequisites: A team workspace (the dialog says 'Only you can open this project. Switch to a team workspace to share it.' otherwise) (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:76-81).
Permission sharing.manage, or content.share on a project the person owns (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:91-118).
A plan whose shared-project limit is not 0 (org-sharing-service.ts:305-312).
Edit access can only go to members whose workspace role can edit; Viewers can only get Can view.
screens_and_controls: Share dialog: audience select, 'Share' button ('Sharing…' while saving), member list with an access select per person labelled 'Access for <name>', add-people picker, 'Stop sharing', 'Copy link' (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:99-141, 161-164; ProjectSharingControls.tsx:196-200).
Note text 'Instructions and files are shared. Each person's chats stay private.' (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:96-98).
Access labels: Can view, Can edit, No access; viewer note 'Viewers can only get Can view. Change their role to Member to let them edit.' (ProjectSharingControls.tsx:40-48).
Confirm dialog 'Stop sharing <project>?' with the consequence text (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:129-136).
Mobile members section: owner row, per-member 'Change access', share buttons, alert 'Stop sharing' (ProjectMembersSection.tsx:199-284).
journey: Owner opens Share on the project.
Chooses the audience and presses 'Share'.
Optionally adds people by name or email and picks Can edit or Can view.
Members open the project from their list (web) or 'Shared with you' (mobile); they see instructions and files.
To end it the owner presses 'Stop sharing' and confirms.
feedback_and_outputs: Toast 'Project link copied. It opens only for people who have access.' (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:41).

Errors: 'Sharing could not be loaded. Try again.', 'Your workspace role does not allow changing what is shared.', 'Health cannot be shared.', shared-project limit message (ProjectShareDialog.tsx:73; org-sharing-service.ts:77-79, 361-368).
Viewer edit refusal: 'This person's workspace role, such as Viewer, can open the project but not edit it. Change their role to Member to give them edit access.' (org-sharing-service.ts:408-414).
Mobile: 'Could not change their access. Try again.', 'Could not share this project.' (ProjectMembersSection.tsx:167, 274).

working: Web: share, change audience, per-member access, stop sharing, copy link, read-only view for non-editors, editor view with content controls (ProjectShareDialog.tsx; apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx:160, 1332-1338).

Server: shareProject inserts organization_shared_projects with a quota guard, setProjectMemberAccess writes organization_project_access and refuses write for roles that cannot edit (org-sharing-service.ts:305-436).
Server: shared projects appear in GET /api/projects with is_org_shared and a shared access of read or write (apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts:74-114; [id]/route.ts:106-143).
Mobile: sharing controls, shared-with-you list and read-only shared project screen exist (ProjectMembersSection.tsx; SharedWithYouSection.tsx:10-31; SharedProjectScreen.tsx).

Sync: mobile Cloud mode pulls and pushes projects (cloudSyncEngine.ts:723, 1035-1038); CLI reads and writes through the same sync route and project routes (apps/cli/src/cloud/projects.rs:1-3; cloud/mod.rs:417-559).

The 'Share' item is hidden for health-space projects on the web list (page.tsx:454).

established.statement: The user can share a notebook with others with a chosen access level.
A notebook and its sources and notes are available in every app the user signs into.
A Viewer cannot be given edit access; the UI tells the owner to change their role to Member.
Members see instructions and files, but each person's chats stay private.

acceptance_criteria: An owner in a team workspace shares a project as 'Only people you invite', adds one member with Can view; that member sees it and cannot edit the name.
Giving Can edit to a person whose workspace role is Viewer is refused with the Viewer message.
After 'Stop sharing', the member no longer sees the project or its files.
A member with Can edit can add a source on web; a member with Can view sees the Sources tab read-only.
A project created on web appears on mobile (Cloud mode) after sync and on the CLI list.
The Share dialog in a personal workspace shows the 'Switch to a team workspace' text and no share button.
inferred: A member's own chats in the shared project stay private to them [inferred from the dialog note and mobile copy].
Sharing is meant to hold for projects only, not for each conversation [inferred from the note].
proposed: [proposed] Add a CLI or VS Code read of 'shared with me' or state that sharing is web and mobile only.
[proposed] Add a live check of a shared member chat with the project's instructions and files.

steps.what_happens: Owner opens Share; the dialog reads the workspace sharing overview.
Owner presses Share; the app sends PUT to the shared-projects route; server checks sharing right, the plan's shared-project limit and the health-space rule, then upserts organization_shared_projects.
Owner sets a member's access; server refuses write for roles that cannot edit and upserts organization_project_access.
Member lists projects; the server adds the project ids readable by the member in the active workspace.
Member opens the project; the page sets read-only unless sharedAccess is write.
For sync, mobile (Cloud mode, signed in) pushes dirty projects and pulls changes since a cursor; the CLI does the same through the sync route.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider is called for sharing or sync. Members' chats use their own model choices; the shared part is instructions and files.

access_and_usage.account: Required; sharing needs membership in a team workspace (org-sharing-service.ts:120-125).
access_and_usage.permissions: requireProjectSharingRight: sharing.manage, or content.share for the owner of the project (org-sharing-service.ts:91-118). Roles: owner, admin, member, viewer (line 15). Edit grants need a role that can hold write (lines 405-415).
access_and_usage.subscription: sharedProjectLimit comes from the plan's projects limit; 0 refuses sharing and over-limit returns a conflict (org-entitlements.ts:128; org-sharing-service.ts:305-312, 361-368).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Shared-project count limit through assert_org_resource_limit('org_shared_projects') (org-sharing-service.ts:340-343). No model metering.
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile cloudChat true; mobile sync needs Cloud mode (cloudSyncEngine.ts:97-103). Health space cannot be shared (org-sharing-service.ts:370-372).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable; none found in the code.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Sharing is not available in Local mode: mobile Local-mode projects are device-only and have no share path found (store.ts:421-436).

Mobile has a Sources tab and a Notebook screen with search. Per-source checkboxes for choosing what grounds an answer do not exist.

purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using a project with sources; read-only members of shared projects.
problems_solved: Not knowing which files the assistant can read.
Finding one file among up to 40.
Seeing whether a file has been read yet or failed.

Type 'budget' in 'Search sources by name or summary' to find a spreadsheet.
On mobile search 'Search sources' in the Notebook screen.

steps.what_happens: Panel opens and calls the list route for the project; a 15 second timeout turns a slow load into an error.
Server checks read access, selects non-deleted, non-superseded files newest first, adds index states and the storage meter.
Browser filters, sorts and searches the loaded list in memory.
While any file is pending or indexing, the panel polls the list every 5 seconds, up to 60 times.
Retry indexing posts to the reindex route, which marks the document and dispatches an indexing workflow.
Mobile Local mode reads sources from the on-device store; Cloud mode lists from the server.

features.summary: A person adds files (PDF, Office, text, images) or a typed note to a project as sources. Each file is checked, stored, read for text and indexed so the project's chats can use it. Web, Desktop, Mobile and CLI can add; the limit is 40 files and the plan's size and storage limits.

established.statement: The user can add files (PDF, docs, text) to a notebook as sources and they are indexed for its chats.
The user can write or paste a note and add it to the notebook as a source.
A project holds at most 40 active files; replacing a file with the same name is allowed at the limit.
A file already in the project (same checksum) is refused with its name.
Files over the plan's size limit or beyond storage are refused.
Archived projects cannot receive sources.
Content that fails inspection is rejected and purged, and a moderation event is recorded.

acceptance_criteria: Uploading a PDF to a project adds a row that moves from indexing to indexed and the chat can quote it.
Uploading the same file twice is refused the second time with its name.
With 40 files, uploading a 41st with a new name is refused; uploading a file with an existing name replaces it.
On the free plan a file over the plan's size limit is refused with an upgrade message.
Text input with an empty body disables 'Add text'; with an empty title the source is named 'Text note'.
An archived project refuses an upload with the Unarchive message.
On mobile 'Add text' with a title 'Brief' creates 'Brief.txt'.
CLI add-file on a missing path fails with a read error and adds nothing.
inferred: Text notes are ordinary text files, so they show in the Sources list with a text icon and count toward the 40-file limit [inferred from SourcesPanel.tsx:298-304].
Replaced files keep older versions superseded, not shown (superseded_at) [inferred from SQL].
proposed: [proposed] Accept several files at once on web.
[proposed] Explain on the row that images are not read for text.
[proposed] Show the 40-file counter and storage meter in the add dialog.

steps.what_happens: App checks the file type and size against the shared attachment rules, and computes a SHA-256 checksum.
App asks POST /api/uploads/presign for an upload address (kind 'knowledge-file', project id, name, type, size, checksum).
App uploads the bytes directly to object storage using the address.
App registers the file with POST /api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files.
Server checks access, archive state, 40-file limit, duplicate checksum, plan size and storage.
Server reads the stored bytes, inspects content, extracts text (a scan may need a vision call, metered and billed to the plan), seals the object under a new key.
Server inserts the row as the next version of that file name, marks the older version superseded, records anchors and any outside-origin reference, deletes the upload key.
Server dispatches an indexing workflow; embeddings come from a managed provider route and are metered.
Mobile Local mode skips all server steps and stores the source (name, type, size, file URI) in the project on the device.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Text extraction is code, not a model, for most types. A scanned document with no text layer is read with a vision call that is metered to the plan and is withheld when the account opted out of training or the file came from Google data (project-knowledge-files.ts:316-326, 157-162). Indexing uses an embedding route from managed providers (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:215-220). Own-key mode: none found in the code. In mobile Local mode the on-device model later reads the source text (chatExecutionStore.ts:2755-2770).

access_and_usage.account: Required for account projects (web session, CLI Cloud mode, mobile Cloud mode). Mobile Local mode needs none.
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner or editor may add; viewers cannot; archived projects refuse (project-knowledge-files.ts:203-236).
access_and_usage.subscription: Per-file size limit by plan (attachmentSizeRefusal, project-knowledge-files.ts:266) and storage cap by plan: free 500 MiB, basic 4 GiB, pro 20 GiB, max 50 GiB, team 25 GiB (billing-catalog.ts:564, 619, 636, 655, 693).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 40 files per project; storage meter returned by the list route; scan transcription and embeddings are metered managed compute (project-knowledge-files.ts:319-326; retrieval-embedding-service.ts:225-234).
access_and_usage.flags: Connector release constant 'coming_soon' disables Google Drive only (connector-release.ts:14).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Image sources are stored without text; the model only gets the file name (project-knowledge-files.ts:164-169).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Embedding and scan reading use managed providers; the no-training filter applies for opted-out accounts (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:215-220).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode: sources stay on the phone and are read into the prompt by the on-device model, up to a character budget (services/attachmentContext.ts:68-90; chatExecutionStore.ts:2755-2770). No upload, no index. Other apps have no Local mode for sources.

features.summary: This area covers sources that come from somewhere other than a local file: a website, a video transcript, an audio file and a Google Drive document. Only Google Drive has code, and it is switched off by a release constant, so the web button reads 'Coming soon'. Website, video and audio have no code.

The user can add a video (for example a YouTube link) whose transcript becomes a source.
The user can add an audio file that is transcribed into a source.
The user can add a document from a connected service such as Google Drive as a source.
A source added from a live location can be refreshed to pick up changes.
Connectors are coming soon; the UI must not offer them as available.

acceptance_criteria: While released state is 'coming_soon', the web Drive tile is disabled and reads 'Coming soon'; POST to the Drive import route returns 403 'Connectors are coming soon.'
With release on and env set, picking two Drive files adds two rows with Drive origin and a refresh button.
If one of two files fails, the response is 201 with one 'added' and one 'failed' and the toast names the count.
Refreshing an unchanged Drive source shows 'already up to date'; a changed one creates a new version.
Refreshing a source that did not come from Drive is refused with 'Only sources added from Google Drive can be refreshed.'
No website, video or audio control appears anywhere until built.
inferred: Drive sources ride the same limits as uploads (40 files, plan size and storage) because they register through registerProjectKnowledgeFile [inferred from project-knowledge-files.ts:299-305 and the import route].
proposed: [proposed] Define website, video and audio requirements: fetch rules, size limits, transcription provider route, consent, and where each runs (device or our servers) before building.
[proposed] Decide whether audio transcription can run on the device in Local mode on mobile.
[proposed] Add a failing-link message set (unreachable URL, private video, no transcript).

steps.what_happens: Web checks connectorsReleased(); today it is false, so the Drive tile is disabled and nothing else runs.
(Released) The app asks GET /api/connectors/google-drive/picker; the server returns not-configured, not-connected, reconnect-required, or ready with an access token and the picker settings.
(Released) The browser loads the Google script and shows the Picker to choose files.
(Released) The app posts the chosen ids to the import route; the server fetches each file from Drive with the person's connector token and registers it like an upload.
(Released) Indexing runs as for any file; scan reading is withheld for Google user data.
(Released) Refresh calls the refresh route, which re-imports if the Drive version changed.

features.summary: A notebook (project) source row shows a one-line note under its name, and a Google Drive source has a refresh button that re-fetches it. A failed source offers Retry indexing. No automatic guide is generated: the note is only filled when a file cannot be read. Web and Desktop (hosted web) only; Mobile has only reindex.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a short note under each source in a notebook's Sources list, lets the person re-fetch a source that came from Google Drive, and lets them restart reading (indexing) of a source that failed or went stale. [inferred] The note is not an automatic guide of the content.
purpose.why_it_exists: The area brief wants each source to get an automatic guide and each live source to be refreshable (S37.12, S37.36) as NotebookLM-style notebooks do. What exists today covers the refresh need for Drive and the failed-index need; the guide need is not met.
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person who keeps files and Drive documents as sources in a notebook on Web, or on Desktop, which shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5).
problems_solved: A Drive document changed after it was added, and the notebook still answers from the old text.
A source failed to read and the person needs to retry without re-uploading.
A file with no readable text is flagged so the person knows only its name reaches the model.
use_cases: Edit a Google Doc, open the notebook Sources list, click the refresh icon on that source, and ask a new question.
See 'Not readable' under a scanned image file and replace it with a text version.
Click Retry indexing on a source whose reading failed.

established.statement: Each source gets an automatic guide or summary the user can read.
A source added from a live location can be refreshed to pick up changes.
Only Retry indexing exists in the brief's account; sources are uploaded copies. This is superseded by the Drive refresh found in code.

acceptance_criteria: A Drive-added source in a notebook shows a refresh control; an uploaded file does not.
Refreshing a changed Drive file replaces its text and the next notebook answer uses the new text.
Refreshing an unchanged file reports it is up to date and creates no new version.
A viewer with read-only share access sees no refresh, retry or remove control.
A failed source can be retried without re-uploading and its status returns to ready or failed again.
[proposed] Each indexed source shows a generated guide of at least a few sentences.
inferred: [inferred] The guide is a product gap, not a bug: the summary column exists and is read by search, the prompt manifest and the UI, so a generator could fill it.
[inferred] A guide generation step must respect the same model, plan and usage rules as chat turns.
proposed: [proposed] Generate a guide after indexing finishes using the notebook's chosen model, and store it in the summary column with a marker that separates it from a not-readable notice.
[proposed] Add Refresh for Mobile using the same origins and refresh routes.
[proposed] Extend origins beyond Drive as new source types are added.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the Sources tab; the browser lists files from the knowledge-files route.
The browser then asks the origins route which files came from where; Drive ones are marked refreshable.

Click refresh: browser sends POST with a CSRF header; the server checks the project, finds the source's Drive id and version, resolves the person's Drive access and imports the file again if the version changed.
The server fetches the file from Google Drive using the person's connector grant.
The new text is extracted and stored as a new version; the old row is marked superseded; reading (indexing) runs again.
The list reloads from the server.

features.summary: Chats filed under a notebook (project) get its instructions, source text and recent sibling chats added to the model's context, with caps. Answers can show citation chips naming a file and page; on Web and Mobile a chip opens that file at that page. A chat can be started inside a notebook or bound to one from the main chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Adds the notebook's instructions, source contents and related chats to each turn of a chat that belongs to the notebook, returns file citations with the answer, and opens the cited file when a chip is clicked.
purpose.why_it_exists: The area brief requires chats in a notebook to answer from its sources, citations to open the source, and the main chat to be able to use a notebook (S37.14, S37.19, S37.37).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person with a notebook, on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile, CLI and the Chrome extension; the VS Code extension manages projects but its chat link was not established.
problems_solved: Answers ignore the person's own documents.
The person cannot check where a claim came from.
A chat started outside the notebook cannot use its files.
use_cases: Ask a notebook chat to compare two uploaded reports and click the page chip to check one figure.
Start a chat from the main composer with a notebook selected so the instructions apply.
Run a CLI turn linked to a project and use its knowledge files.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: notebook page, Chats tab, composer; the first message is handed off through browser session storage to a new project chat (apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx:235-262; apps/web/features/projects/lib/project-chat-handoff.ts:126-129).

Mobile: project selector bar in chat and chip row under answers (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ProjectSelectorBar.tsx; ProjectFileCitations.tsx).
CLI: 'agi projects link' binds the working folder to an account project (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3840-3850), managed turns then use its instructions and knowledge files.
Chrome: side panel conversation carries a project id (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:9012-9022).
prerequisites: Signed in; the project exists, is not archived or deleted.
A source must be indexed or have extracted text to be quoted.

Mobile: Cloud mode for the notebook screen.

steps.what_happens: The composer sends the message with the project id; the web page stores a handoff and opens a new chat bound to the project.
The chat request reaches the completions route; the server reads the conversation, finds its project id.
The server loads the project (not archived or deleted), picks up to 40 files, ranks them by the question and selects passages inside a total budget, plus up to 15 related chats.
Blocks are fitted to a total cap and the citations list is kept in step.
If loading fails the turn is refused with 503, if the project is gone with 409.
The model call is made through the chosen provider with the project text in the system context; the file text is marked as untrusted reference data.
The answer and citations return; the client renders chips; a click navigates to the project page with the file and page parameters.

features.summary: Study mode turns one chat into a tutoring session. On web (and so the Electron desktop) and mobile Cloud mode, the person names a subject, picks Learn it, Practise it or Revise it, and picks a level. The server then adds teaching instructions to every model turn in that chat. CLI and VS Code only offer a prompt-only 'study' output style.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a conversation titled '<mode label>: <subject>', records a study_sessions row (topic, mode, level), and from then on the chat service adds a study instruction to the system prompt of each turn while the session is open (apps/web/features/study/components/StudyPage.tsx:103-126; apps/web/features/study/server/study-session-store.ts:86-101; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6562-6569). The person can leave and resume study mode, list past sessions and delete one (StudyPage.tsx:128-165).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a learner gets a tutor that teaches in small steps instead of a normal assistant that hands over finished answers. Study mode is a mode of a normal chat, not a separate engine: the conversation, messages, model and billing stay as they are (doc: apps/web/db/neon/0247_study_sessions.sql header).
purpose.who_uses_it: Students and self-learners on web, Electron desktop and mobile Cloud mode; developers who pick the study output style in CLI or VS Code.
problems_solved: Chats that answer instead of teach
Having to retype 'teach me step by step' each turn
Finding earlier study chats again (Your sessions list)
Turning tutoring off without losing the chat
use_cases: A student opens Study, types 'eigenvalues', picks Learn it and New to it, and is taught one idea at a time.
A learner picks Practise it for 'German dative case' and is quizzed one question at a time.
A user leaves study mode in a chat to ask a normal question, then turns it back on.
A CLI user sets output-style to study to get guided hints in the terminal.

where_to_find_it: Web: sidebar item 'Study' at /chat/study (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:143-148; apps/web/app/chat/study/page.tsx:1-18). The item is marked hideable (app-nav-items.ts:149).

Desktop (Electron): shows the hosted web app, so the same page [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5 (doc: AGENTS.md)]; the Electron window registry test treats /chat/study as a section, not a conversation (apps/desktop/electron/__tests__/windowRegistry.test.ts:42).

Mobile: in Cloud mode only, the Add-to-chat sheet row 'Study and learn' opens the screen titled 'Study and learn' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:1255-1262; apps/mobile/src/features/study/StudyScreen.tsx:207).
CLI: /output-style or config key output-style, value 'study' (apps/cli/src/output_styles.rs:55-60; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:182; apps/cli/src/config.rs:1543).
VS Code: output style 'Study' in the sidebar output-style picker (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/outputStyles.ts:21).
Chrome extension: nothing found (grep of apps/extension for 'study' returned no files).
prerequisites: Web: signed-in account; the session routes use a user-scoped database connection (apps/web/app/api/study/sessions/route.ts:54).
Mobile: Cloud mode; Local mode shows 'Study runs in AGI Cloud' with a 'Switch to Cloud mode' button (StudyScreen.tsx:175-202).

features.summary: On the web Study page, if the person has projects, a 'Course material' menu lets them start the study chat inside a project. The chat service then loads that project's context and knowledge files into the model turn, and the study instruction tells the tutor to teach from it. The page itself uploads nothing.

purpose.why_it_exists: So a student can teach from their own notes, syllabus or slides, kept in a project, instead of from the model's general knowledge.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web (and Electron desktop) learners who already have a project with files. Mobile has no such menu.
problems_solved: Tutor ignores the learner's own course
Re-attaching files each time

A teacher keeps a syllabus in a project and studies against it.

features.summary: A checkbox on the web Study page, 'Start with a personal study plan', puts a ready-written plan request into the chat's message box. The person sends it and the model writes the plan. There is no stored plan and no diagnostic quiz; the diagnostic has no code.

purpose.why_it_exists: A learner often wants an ordered plan before the first lesson, shaped by their level and weekly time.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Electron learners starting a session. Not on mobile.
problems_solved: Not knowing what order to study in
Plan that ignores weekly time
use_cases: Start 'Organic chemistry' with a plan, send the draft, get parts, timings and checks.
A learner with a syllabus in a project gets a plan that points to where the material covers each part.

features.summary: The tutor's behaviour is text added to the model's system prompt: a way of working (learn, practise, revise), a level, a rule not to give an answer before the learner tries, and teaching practices (outline, one hint at a time, worked examples, visuals, interactive explanations). It is a prompt, not a lesson engine. CLI and VS Code use a shorter style text.

purpose.what_it_does: composeStudyInstruction joins: the subject, a mode paragraph, a level paragraph, the no-answer-before-attempt rule and a block of teaching practices (apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts:19-79). The chat service adds it to every turn while the session is open.
purpose.why_it_exists: To make the tutor guide with questions, hints and examples instead of dumping answers, without building a separate lesson system.
purpose.who_uses_it: Learners in a web, desktop or mobile Cloud study chat; CLI and VS Code users who choose the study output style.
problems_solved: Answers given before the learner tries
Whole subject dumped at once
No hints
No visual or interactive explanation
use_cases: Learn it: one idea, one check question, then move on.
Practise it: one question at a time, says exactly where a wrong answer went wrong.
Revise it: asks what the learner remembers first.
Stuck learner gets hints, each more specific.

where_to_find_it: Web, Electron desktop, mobile Cloud: choose the way of working and level on the Study screen (F038-01); the style applies inside the chat.
CLI: output style 'study' (description 'Teaches step by step with questions instead of finished answers.') (output_styles.rs:55-60).
VS Code: output style 'Study' (outputStyles.ts:21).
Chrome: none.
prerequisites: An open study session (web, mobile) or a selected output style (CLI, VS Code).
screens_and_controls: Mode radio buttons and level menu on the start screen; the 'Leave study mode' control in chat stops the instruction (StudyModeIndicator.tsx).
journey: Start a session with a mode and level.
Chat: the tutor opens with a numbered outline and says which step it is on.
Answer questions in the message box; ask for a hint when stuck.
The tutor shows a worked example then gives a similar problem, may draw a diagram or build an HTML explanation, and may ask you to explain back in your words.
Leave study mode to get ordinary replies.
feedback_and_outputs: Chat replies in the taught style; quizzes and flashcards as artifacts (see F038-05, F038-06). The learner never sees the instruction text; the page keeps it off screen (test: StudyPage.test.tsx 'keeps the tutoring instruction off the screen').
settings: Mode and level per session; none for the strength of the style.

working: Mode text: learn is one idea at a time with a check question; practice asks one question at a time and says where a wrong answer went wrong; review starts from what the learner remembers (study-session.ts:19-26).
Level text for beginner, intermediate, expert (study-session.ts:28-33).
Rule: do not give the answer until the user has attempted it (study-session.ts:35-36).

Practices: numbered outline; one hint at a time, each more specific; worked example then similar problem; diagram or HTML interactive explanation; quiz and flashcards formats; teach from attached material; ask for explain-back typed or spoken with feedback; language exercises (study-session.ts:38-47).
The text reaches the model as a developer-layer block (request-processor.ts:2121-2127).

Study text is ranked so a current user request and account instructions are resolved by the shared precedence helper in tests; production path uses layers, not composeStudyPrompt (study-session.test.ts:75-125).
CLI and VS Code load study.md, a shorter text (study.md).
incomplete: No lesson list, step tracker or hint counter is stored; all behaviour depends on the model following text (study-session.ts; no table beyond study_sessions).
Spoken explanation is only 'typed or spoken with the microphone' in the instruction; capturing speech is Voice, not Study [inferred].
CLI and VS Code text lacks the hint-order, outline and quiz format rules (study.md).
disconnected_or_disabled: composeStudyPrompt (precedence-aware) is unused in production code (grep).
not_available: Chrome: none.

Mobile Local mode: not offered.

In Practise it the tutor asks one question and waits before judging.
Asking the answer straight away still gets an attempt request first.

features.summary: Study mode asks the model to write practice questions as an interactive quiz block. The quiz viewer on web and mobile shows one question at a time, grades the answer in code, shows an explanation, offers progressive hints, a score and a follow-up question to the tutor. The written feedback in chat comes from the model.

The viewer parses it (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/study-set.ts:100-112) and shows 'Question n of N', 'Check answer', 'Correct.' or 'Not quite. The answer is ...', and the explanation (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/study/QuizView.tsx:119-281).
purpose.why_it_exists: Practice with instant feedback is the core of studying; a viewer gives it without waiting for the model each time.
purpose.who_uses_it: Learners in study chats on web, Electron desktop and mobile Cloud; any chat where a quiz block appears.
problems_solved: Practice questions as plain text with no marking
Waiting for the model to grade each answer

features.summary: Flashcards turn a model answer into a set of cards the learner flips, marks 'Got it' or 'Still learning', shuffles and reviews again. Web (and the Electron desktop that shows web) can also edit and print a set. Mobile shows and flips it. The area brief calls every item missing; the code shows it built on web and mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: When the model writes a ~~~flashcards block of JSON (title, cards with front and back) inside a document artifact, the app shows an interactive deck instead of code: tap a card to flip it, mark it 'Got it' or 'Still learning', shuffle, and re-run only the cards still being learned (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/study/FlashcardsView.tsx:17-137). On web the set can also be edited and printed (StudyDocument.tsx:99-125).
purpose.why_it_exists: Memorising terms is a core study task and ChatGPT and Claude style study tools offer card decks [inferred from the product context and the brief's Should lines S38.22 to S38.26]. A plain list of terms in chat is hard to practise from.
purpose.who_uses_it: Students and self-learners using Study mode or a project's Studio, and anyone who asks the model for flashcards.
problems_solved: A list of terms in chat cannot be self-tested; the deck hides the back until the learner flips the card.
The learner can focus on weak cards with 'Review N still learning'.
A model-written set with a typo can be fixed by hand on web without asking the model again.
use_cases: A learner in Study mode asks for flashcards on the Krebs cycle, flips through them and marks which ones they know.
A learner opens a project with course notes, picks the Flashcards tile in Project Studio and gets twenty cards built from the sources (apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectStudio.tsx:87-93).
A teacher on web edits two wrong cards and prints the set as a two-column sheet.

where_to_find_it: Web: there is no Flashcards page. A deck appears in a chat answer or in the artifact panel when the answer holds a ~~~flashcards block (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1921-1930). Ways to ask for one: Study page 'Study' at /chat/study, whose mode text tells the model it may write flashcards (apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts:53), or the 'Flashcards' tile in Project Studio on a project page (ProjectStudio.tsx:87-93).

Desktop (Electron, the public desktop): shows the hosted web app, so the same as web (doc: AGENTS.md section 5; apps/desktop/electron/__tests__/windowRegistry.test.ts:42 lists /chat/study). The retained Tauri desktop source (apps/desktop/src) has no flashcard or study code found by search.

Mobile: deck shows inline in a chat answer or in the artifact viewer (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1447; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/ArtifactViewer.tsx:63-72). Ask via the Study screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/study.tsx) or a project notebook output (apps/mobile/src/features/notebook/ProjectNotebookScreen.tsx:7-9).
CLI, VS Code extension, Chrome extension: no flashcard viewer found; a ~~~flashcards block would not be drawn as a deck there [inferred: no match for the study-set module outside web and mobile].
prerequisites: Signed-in account and a chat turn that returns a ~~~flashcards block; the model must follow the prompt format. Nothing else is required to flip, mark or shuffle, which run in the browser or app (FlashcardsView.tsx:17-30).
To edit on web: the artifact must be a stored artifact, its latest version, in the panel view, and the set must be 'lossless' (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1041-1042; StudyDocument.tsx:57,101).
screens_and_controls: Web deck: header with the set title (or 'Flashcards') and 'Card N of M · K known'; a card button labelled 'Show the back' or 'Show the front'; 'Previous card' and 'Next card' arrow buttons; after a flip, 'Still learning' and 'Got it'; 'Shuffle cards'; 'Review N still learning' once some cards are known (FlashcardsView.tsx:55-135).
Web document controls under each set: 'Edit cards' (only when editable) and 'Print' (StudyDocument.tsx:99-125).
Web editor: 'Set title', 'Card N front', 'Card N back', 'Remove card N', 'Add card', 'Cancel', 'Save' (StudySetEditors.tsx:296-358, 25-36).

Mobile deck: same labels 'Previous card', 'Next card', 'Still learning', 'Got it', 'Shuffle cards', 'Review N still learning' and a progress line (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/study/StudyFlashcardsView.tsx:84-184). No edit or print on mobile.
journey: 1. The learner asks for flashcards (Study session, Project Studio tile, or a plain chat request).
2. The model replies with a document whose ~~~flashcards block holds JSON.
3. The app finds the block, parses it and draws the deck with the front face up.
4. The learner taps the card to see the back.
5. The learner taps 'Got it' or 'Still learning'; the app moves to the next card and shows the known count.
6. At any time the learner taps 'Shuffle cards', or 'Review N still learning' to loop only the unknown cards.
7. On web the learner may tap 'Edit cards', fix text, add or remove cards, and 'Save'; or tap 'Print'.
feedback_and_outputs: 'Card N of M · K known' counter (FlashcardsView.tsx:54-58).

If the JSON cannot be read: web shows 'This flashcard set could not be read.' (StudyDocument.tsx:50-56); mobile shows 'Writing the flashcard set' while streaming and 'This flashcard set could not be read.' after (StudyDocumentView.tsx:50-59).
If part of a set is beyond the limits: 'Part of this flashcard set is beyond what can be shown or edited here, so editing is off to keep the original intact.' (StudyDocument.tsx:93-98).
Print opens the browser print dialog with a two-column sheet (study-print.ts:48-71).
settings: None found in the code. The study mode, level and 'Course material' choices on the Study page change the prompt, not the deck (apps/web/features/study/components/StudyPage.tsx:201-268).

working: Web: parse, flip, Got it / Still learning, shuffle, review-still-learning (FlashcardsView.tsx:17-137), covered by a test (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/study/StudyDocument.test.tsx:128-141).
Web: edit and save back into the document, add card, card limit, text limit (StudySetEditors.tsx:280-358; StudyDocument.test.tsx:162-180, 332-358).
Web: print as a two-column table from a sandboxed frame (study-print.ts:48-71; StudyDocument.test.tsx:187-203).
Mobile: parse, flip, mark, shuffle, review (StudyFlashcardsView.tsx:32-186; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/__tests__/StudyDocumentView.test.tsx:277-317).
Generation by prompt: Study mode instruction (study-session.ts:53), Project Studio tile on web (ProjectStudio.tsx:87-93).

Parser accepts front/back, term/definition or question/answer keys; strips a model-written 'Card 1 of 5' counter from the title (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/study-set.ts:114-129; packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifact-derivation.ts:356-358).
Title and one-line summary of a set in the mobile artifacts list without showing answers (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/study/studyContent.ts:54-84).
incomplete: Known and still-learning marks live only in component state, so they reset when the view is remounted or the page reloads (FlashcardsView.tsx:22-24 uses useState only; no store or API call found).
Editing is web only, and only in the panel on a stored latest version (ArtifactPreview.tsx:1041-1042).
Print is web only (no print code found in apps/mobile).

Project Studio on mobile and in the shared contract asks for a one-card-at-a-time chat flow, not a ~~~flashcards block, so mobile gets a deck only if the model chooses the block (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/project-studio.ts:94-99 versus ProjectStudio.tsx:87-93).
Shuffle is not seeded or persisted and 'Shuffle cards' resets position to card 1 (FlashcardsView.tsx:108-116).

established.statement: The product generates flashcards on a topic or from material.
The user can edit flashcards.
Flashcards flip between front and back.
The learner marks cards as known or needing practice.
Cards or questions can be shuffled.
The model-generated set is capped at 300 cards and each text at 2,000 characters.

acceptance_criteria: A reply containing a valid ~~~flashcards block shows a deck with the first front face up and 'Card 1 of N · 0 known', and never shows the JSON.
Tapping the card shows the back; tapping again shows the front.
After a flip, 'Got it' raises the known count by one and moves to the next card; 'Still learning' leaves it unchanged.
'Shuffle cards' reorders cards, returns to card 1 and shows the front.
'Review N still learning' shows only unknown cards.
On web, 'Edit cards' then changing a back and 'Save' updates the stored artifact; Save is disabled while any card side is empty.
A set of 301 cards shows only 300 and turns editing off.
Print on web opens the print dialog with a title and a two-column table.
inferred: Marks should survive a re-render of the same chat message at least within a session [inferred: a progress counter that resets is surprising].
Because the same brief items are marked missing on all apps, the brief status is stale for web, desktop (via web) and mobile and should be refreshed [inferred from code present].
proposed: [proposed] Store known/still-learning marks per set so progress survives reload and can feed F038-08.
[proposed] Add edit and print on mobile, or an explicit decision that mobile is view only.
[proposed] Give CLI, VS Code and Chrome a plain-text fallback that lists cards.

features.summary: In Study mode the model is told to ask the learner to explain an idea back, typed or spoken, and to run language exercises. This is prompt text only. There is no study-specific microphone, speech scoring or pronunciation feedback in any app.

purpose.what_it_does: The study instruction tells the model to now and then ask the learner to explain an idea in their own words and give feedback, and for languages to run translation, fill-in-the-blank, form-choice and reply exercises (apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts:55-56).
purpose.why_it_exists: Explaining back and practising a language are common ways to learn; the brief lists them as S38.29 to S38.31.
purpose.who_uses_it: Learners in an open Study session, including language learners.
problems_solved: Passive reading does not test understanding.
Language learners need varied short exercises with corrections.
use_cases: A learner studying German dative case gets translation and fill-in-the-blank prompts.
A learner explains photosynthesis in their own words and gets feedback on what was missing.
A learner dictates the explanation with the general chat microphone [inferred: the prompt says spoken with the microphone; the mic belongs to general chat].

VS Code, Chrome: nothing found.

2. The model, following the instruction, offers short exercises.

features.summary: After the last question of a quiz, the results screen offers 'Explain what I missed' (or 'What should I study next?') which sends a message to the chat with the score and each missed question. This works on web (panel view) and mobile. It asks the model to use the source material; it does not retrieve sources itself.

purpose.what_it_does: On the results screen the learner can send a prepared follow-up: the quiz title, score, and each missed question with the answer given, asking the model to explain using 'the source material we have been working from' and say where each answer comes from (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/study-set.ts:329-355). A second button on a wrong short answer asks the model whether the wording also counts (study-set.ts:357-359).
purpose.why_it_exists: A score alone does not teach. The brief says the learner can follow up with questions grounded in the source (S38.35).
purpose.who_uses_it: Learners finishing a quiz, especially from a project with course notes.
problems_solved: The learner no longer has to retype missed questions.
Strict short-answer grading can wrongly mark a valid answer; the learner can ask the model.

After a perfect score tap 'What should I study next?'.
On a marked-wrong short answer tap 'Ask whether my wording also counts'.

Each question gets feedback on whether and why the answer was right.
Multiple-choice and short-answer questions are limited to 100 questions per quiz, 8 options and 2,000 characters per text.

acceptance_criteria: Finishing a quiz shows 'You scored N of M'.
With misses, 'Explain what I missed' sends a message listing each missed question and the answer given.
With no misses, 'What should I study next?' sends a message asking for next topics.
The sent message asks for source pointers.
A wrong short answer shows 'Ask whether my wording also counts' and sends the recheck question.
If the surface cannot send, no follow-up buttons appear.
In a project with notes, the reply cites those notes (model behaviour; tester judges).
inferred: Web inline quizzes should offer the same follow-up as the panel [inferred from mobile parity].
A true grounded follow-up needs source retrieval attached to the turn [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Attach the project's source snippets for the missed questions to the follow-up turn.
[proposed] Save quiz results so follow-ups and progress (F038-08) can use them.
[proposed] Show the follow-up inline on web as well.
