features.summary: Memory is a per-account switch, off by default, that decides whether AGI Workforce saves and uses facts about the person. A separate switch decides whether it may look up excerpts from other past chats. The server enforces both. No first-run introduction to Memory exists in any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person turn Memory on or off, and separately allow or forbid the assistant to search excerpts of their other chats. When Memory is off the server reads no saved facts into a turn, saves nothing automatically, and offers no memory tool (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1146; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1123-1146, 2392-2406).
purpose.why_it_exists: Requirements say memory must be explicit and controllable, with a disable switch and a separate reference-chat-history toggle (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 18). Competitors expose the same controls (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:313-316).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on Web, Desktop, Mobile (Cloud and Local), CLI and VS Code. Chrome has no switch of its own.
problems_solved: A person who does not want the assistant to remember anything can stop it with one switch.
Past-chat lookup can be turned off without losing saved facts, and the reverse.
A workspace owner can close memory for all members, and the person sees why the switches are disabled.
use_cases: A new user leaves Memory off (the default) and chats normally.
A user turns Memory on in Settings so later chats know their preferences, but keeps Search past chats off.
A CLI user runs agi memory off to stop memory on every surface.
A mobile user in Local mode turns Memory on so facts stay on the phone.

where_to_find_it: Web (and public Desktop, which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): Settings, Personalization, then the Memory heading. PersonalizationSection renders MemorySection (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PersonalizationSection.tsx:604). Privacy settings also show a Memory preferences row with a Manage link to Personalization (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:835-860).

Mobile: Profile, then the Memory row (apps/mobile/app/(app)/profile/index.tsx:199) opens the Memory screen titled Cloud Memory or Memory, with a MEMORY CONTROLS card (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/components/MemoryControlsCard.tsx:60; apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx:538,709).
CLI: agi memory on, agi memory off, agi memory status (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1477-1481, 4225-4235). The flag --no-memory runs one session without memory (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:888-890).
VS Code: command Code: Turn Memory On or Off, or the Code: Memory menu entry (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:479-486; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1949-1962, 2037).
Tauri desktop build (internal code, not the public Desktop): Settings Memory tab with Enable memories (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/Memory.tsx:185-191).
Chrome: no switch found in the memory sheet (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/memorySheet.ts, whole file searched).
prerequisites: Web and Cloud mobile need a signed-in account and a ready workspace; otherwise the web page says Cloud memory is unavailable until your account and workspace are ready (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:513).
Mobile Local mode needs no sign-in: the Local scope is created without an account (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/accountScopedUiState.ts:10-12).

The workspace must allow memory; otherwise switches are disabled and a notice appears (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:38, 140-150 via organizationMemoryAllowed in apps/web/features/settings/hooks/use-capabilities-preferences.ts:176-190).
screens_and_controls: Web switches: Persistent memory (MemorySection.tsx:320), Save memories from chats (398), Search past chats (411), Include sensitive topics in memory (422), Allow memory generation from tool-assisted chats (435).

Web: the three dependent switches are disabled while Persistent memory is off and show the hint Turn on persistent memory to change this (MemorySection.tsx:401,425,438 and the hint constant near line 59). Search past chats is disabled only when settings are not loaded or the workspace blocks memory, not when Memory is off (MemorySection.tsx:413).
Web contract text: When off, nothing is saved or read. Existing memories stay until you delete them. (MemorySection.tsx:61).

Mobile switches in the MEMORY CONTROLS card: Memory, Search and reference chats, Generate memory from chat history, Include sensitive topics in memory; the last two are disabled while Memory is off (MemoryControlsCard.tsx:64-96).
Mobile footnote says whether memories are on the account or on the device and that existing entries stay when Memory is off (MemoryControlsCard.tsx:128-140).
Mobile Memory screen shows Memory is off, so new memories can't be added or imported. with a Turn on button (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx:593-598).
CLI prints Memory is on... or Memory is off... (apps/cli/src/cloud/personalization.rs:297-301).
journey: Open the Memory settings on the app (see where to find it).
See the Memory switch, off by default (apps/web/features/settings/hooks/use-capabilities-preferences.ts:62).

Flip it on. The change is saved as the capabilities setting for the account; a failed save shows the message Your memory settings were not saved, so nothing changed. with a Try again button (MemorySection.tsx:32,290-296).
Optionally flip Search past chats or Save memories from chats.
Start a chat. The server reads the switches on each turn and decides whether to load facts, past-chat excerpts and the memory tool (request-processor.ts:4126-4160).
feedback_and_outputs: Web: switch state changes at once (optimistic) and reverts to the last saved value if the save fails (use-capabilities-preferences.ts:296-313).
Web: a saved-count line, Cloud memories are not loaded. when sync is not ready (MemorySection.tsx:338).
Mobile: deletion-warning card, only for reset (MemoryControlsCard.tsx:30).
VS Code: information message Memory turned on in your user settings, saved facts are included with your turns. or the off variant (commandSetup.ts:2037-2054).
settings: Account settings namespace capabilities: keys memory, generateFromHistory, searchPastChats, includeSensitiveTopics, allowToolAssistedGeneration (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:258-281).
Per-chat request field memory_enabled and personalization (request-processor.ts:712, 3523); the web chat sends memory_enabled false when the chat opted out (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:835).
VS Code settings agiWorkforce.memory.enabled (default true) and agiWorkforce.optOut.memory (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1332-1346).
Workspace policy allowMemory (managed-memory-context-service.ts:85-125).

working: Server reads the account switches on every turn: memory is on only if capabilities.memory is exactly true; generateFromHistory defaults to true once memory is on; searchPastChats is separate (managed-memory-context-service.ts:258-281).

Memory off: loadManagedMemoryContext returns no facts (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1146-1149); auto-saving is skipped (request-processor.ts:2392-2406); the memory tool is not offered (request-processor.ts:1123-1146); a write is refused with reason user_memory_disabled (managed-memory-context-service.ts:619-625).

Past-chat lookup depends on searchPastChats, the surface not being api, the chat not being temporary and memory_enabled not being false; it does not depend on the Memory switch (apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:128-131).
Web switches, disabled states, workspace-off notice and save retry (MemorySection.tsx:285-440).

Mobile Cloud writes memory, searchPastChats and generateFromHistory to the account settings (apps/mobile/services/cloudSettingsMapping.ts:166-168) and reads the account value back (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:600-603). Mobile Local uses a separate local settings store (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2789-2799).
CLI agi memory on/off/status writes the same account switch (apps/cli/src/cloud/personalization.rs:273-296).
VS Code switch and per-folder opt-out exist and gate whether facts are sent (apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/config.ts:255-261; src/memory/memoryStore.ts:54).
incomplete: No onboarding or first-run introduction to Memory in any app: nothing found in the code searched (brief S39.01 marks every app missing; doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/039-memory-product.md). A founder decision says no memory step at sign-up (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:130), which conflicts with the brief's Should line.

VS Code switch is a local VS Code user setting, not the account switch: it stops facts being sent from that editor only (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1336; commandSetup.ts:2037-2054). Its menu label says Turn account memory off (commandSetup.ts:1955), which overstates what it does.
CLI and VS Code have no past-chat switch (brief S39.03; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1435-1486 lists no such subcommand).
The Tauri desktop Memory tab shows no past-chat switch (no match for past or reference in apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/Memory.tsx).
disconnected_or_disabled: The tool-assisted-generation and sensitive-topics switches only matter when Memory and Save memories from chats are on (MemorySection.tsx:401-438).
not_available: Chrome extension: no Memory switch and no past-chat switch found (memorySheet.ts, memoryClient.ts).
First-run Memory introduction on all six apps.

established.statement: A visible switch turns Memory on or off, and when off the assistant neither reads nor saves memories.
A control separate from the Memory switch decides whether the assistant may look up excerpts from other past chats.
A first-run flow introduces Memory: what it stores, that it is off by default, and how to turn it on or manage it.
Memory must be explicit and controllable: disable memory and a reference-chat-history toggle are required.
Temporary chats must not update or reference memory unless the user explicitly changes that behaviour.

acceptance_criteria: With Memory off, a chat that mentions a personal fact creates no row in the memory list afterwards.
With Memory off and a fact already saved, a reply does not use the fact.
Turning Search past chats on or off does not change the Memory switch, and the reverse.
If saving a switch fails, the switch returns to its saved value and a Try again action is shown.
A workspace with memory closed shows the notice and all switches disabled.
A new account starts with Memory off.
inferred: The past-chat switch staying enabled while Memory is off is deliberate because the server computes the two independently [inferred from turn-context-service.ts:128-131].
The server, not the client, is the authority; client toggles only change stored settings [inferred from managed-memory-context-service.ts:258-281].
proposed: [proposed] Decide with the founder whether a one-time Memory explanation (what is stored, off by default, where to manage) should be added, since the brief requires it and a recorded decision removes a sign-up step.
[proposed] Rename the VS Code menu item so it says it controls this editor only, or make it write the account switch like the CLI does.
[proposed] Add a past-chat switch to CLI and VS Code, or record the decision not to.

steps.what_happens: Person flips a switch; the web hook updates the screen at once and queues a save of the capabilities namespace with a version check, retrying once on a version conflict.
Save error: the switch returns to the last acknowledged value and an alert with Try again shows.
On each chat turn the server reads the workspace policy and the account capabilities, in parallel with attachment work. A temporary chat gets the disabled policy without reading.
If memory is on and the chat is not temporary, account facts are loaded, ranked and added as a system message; past-chat excerpts are added only if searchPastChats is on.
Mobile Local: facts come from the device store when Memory is on and the chat is not temporary; Cloud mode leaves assembly to the server.
CLI agi memory on posts a patch {memory: true} to the account preferences route, then reads it back.

features.summary: After a completed chat turn, the server finds durable facts in what the person said and saves up to five as memories marked as learned. It runs only when Memory and Save memories from chats are on, never in temporary chats, and a failure never breaks the chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Learns lasting facts and preferences from ordinary chats without being asked, and stores them in the account memory (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:145-215; managed-memory-context-service.ts:1343-1439).
purpose.why_it_exists: Founders decided automatic extraction must be on because both leaders extract automatically (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:53-62). The brief requires facts saved after ordinary conversations when allowed (S39.12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with Memory on, on Web, Desktop, Chrome, CLI and VS Code Cloud turns, and on Mobile in Cloud (server) or Local (on device).
problems_solved: People do not have to repeat preferences in every chat.
Facts are saved without asking, yet can be stopped with a switch.

User mentions where they live; the fact appears in the Saved Memory list as learned.
Mobile Local user chats on the phone; a fact is saved only on the phone.

The fact appears in the list; the list item shows its origin and the chat title when known (MemoryEditor.tsx FactOrigin; apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:58-70).

Environment AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION: model-based extraction is on unless set to 0, false, off or no (apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:79-82).

working: Gate for learning: policy enabled, generateFromHistory, not temporary, memory_enabled not false, surface not api (request-processor.ts:2392-2406).
Pattern extractor yields at most five candidate facts (request-processor.ts:2408-2418; MAX_AUTO_MEMORIES_PER_TURN 5 at managed-memory-context-service.ts:72).
Explicit remember or forget sentences are removed from passive learning so they are not saved twice (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:214-226; apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:51-58).
Only a completed turn saves; failed or cancelled returns early (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:149).

A tool-assisted turn is skipped unless allowToolAssistedGeneration is on; research and AGI Work turns are treated as tool-assisted (request-processor.ts:2420-2423, 6451-6455; managed-auto-memory-service.ts:150-155).
A turn that carried Google user data saves nothing (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:101-110).
The project of the conversation scopes the new fact (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:111-130).
Failures are logged and the chat still succeeds (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:138-142).

Model extraction runs after the response through the framework's after hook, on a managed utility route with a metered usage reservation, and falls back to pattern facts on any refusal or failure (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:55-68, 163-215; apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:117-170).
Each learned fact passes the eligibility gate, never-remember list, credential refusal and duplicate or conflict merging (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1381-1437, 742-870).
Mobile Local consolidates facts on the device after a completed local turn (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/consolidation.ts:66-80, 176-215; chatExecutionStore.ts:2830-2846).
CLI also builds local memory files from session summaries, separate from account memory (apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:1-20).
incomplete: VS Code and CLI auto-save to the account runs through the shared server path for managed turns; I did not open the CLI or VS Code runtime to confirm [inferred from surface list in apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:10-12 and request-processor.ts:2392-2406].
Chrome auto-save is likewise inferred from the server path, not from Chrome code.
disconnected_or_disabled: Model extraction is skipped when the turn text was withheld, zero-data-retention is on, or the extraction prompt cannot be built (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:41-52).
The shadow worth-extracting probe records data only and changes no gate (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:195-213).
not_available: API surface: never learns (request-processor.ts:2402-2404).

Own-key and Local turns never save to server memory: the eligibility gate refuses non-managed trust modes (managed-memory-context-service.ts:646-660). Whether own-key turns reach this path at all is unknown.

established.statement: After ordinary conversations the assistant automatically saves new durable facts to memory (when allowed).
Model-assisted extraction is on, runs on the cheapest reliable utility model, is metered, fails safe, and excludes temporary chats, Memory-off sessions, API and zero-data-retention traffic.
Temporary chats must not update or reference memory.
Do not save secrets, tentative guesses or transient tool output.
Mobile Local and Cloud memory stay separate; one is never copied into the other.

acceptance_criteria: With Memory and Save memories from chats on, a completed turn stating a personal preference adds a learned memory within a short time.
With Save memories from chats off, no learned memory is added but a Remember request still works.
A cancelled or failed turn adds nothing.
A temporary chat adds nothing.
One turn adds at most five facts.
A fact in a project chat is listed as project-only.
A turn that used tools adds nothing unless the tool-assisted switch is on.
inferred: The learned fact ranks below user-written facts, so it cannot override them [inferred from memoryWriteRank, managed-memory-context-service.ts:687-690].
Automatic saving gives the person no immediate in-chat confirmation [inferred from no notice found].
proposed: [proposed] Show a small, dismissible note when a chat saved a learned fact, with an undo, as the leaders do.
[proposed] Record in the list which chat turn produced each fact (the source turn id is already stored).

steps.what_happens: Chat turn arrives. The server reads the memory policy, and builds pattern facts from the person's message only if learning is allowed.
Tool-assisted turns clear the facts unless the tool-assisted switch is on.
After the answer is complete the recorder runs; non-completed outcomes stop here.
Without model extraction: persist pattern facts at once. With it: after the response, call a managed utility route under a usage reservation; on refusal use pattern facts.
Model call goes to an outside provider chosen by the managed routing layer, not the person's model.
Google-data check, project lookup, then persist: exclusions, dedupe, up to five writes, each through the eligibility gate.
Mobile Local: the same idea on the phone using local rules and SQLite.

See SYS-model-catalog-and-routing and SYS-inference-providers. Pattern extraction needs no model.

features.summary: A person adds a fact to memory by typing it into the Memory list, or by asking the assistant to remember it. The server checks the never-remember list and refuses credentials. A repeated fact is merged. A newer same-topic fact replaces an older one unless a higher-ranked one holds the topic.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person direct control over what is saved: a typed fact through the list, or a Remember request in chat answered with a clear outcome (apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:85-160; apps/web/app/api/memory/commands/route.ts:20-95).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires typed facts and an explicit remember action with confirmation (S39.10, S39.11). Inspectable, user-controlled memory is a stated product requirement (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with Memory on, on all six apps.
problems_solved: Important facts are saved at once instead of waiting for automatic learning.
The person knows whether the save worked.
Secrets and never-remember terms stay out.

Say in chat: Remember that my team uses pnpm.
CLI: agi memory add I use tabs not spaces.
VS Code: select text and run Code: Remember This.

Credentials and special-category facts are always refused (managed-memory-context-service.ts:570-580).

Web chat posts explicit commands to /api/memory/commands; the server runs remember or forget and returns a status (apps/web/app/api/memory/commands/route.ts; apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:232-262).

The brief maps CLI remember to registry.rs:1490 and tui_app.rs:3792, which open instruction files, not account memory (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1933-2040). Behaviour for CLI chat Remember is unverified.
Mobile Local mode has no never-remember list: the row appears only in Cloud (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx:569).

Mobile Cloud adds are accepted locally first; how a server refusal during sync is shown was not established (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/store.ts:176-200; apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:160-215).
disconnected_or_disabled: Memory tool is not offered unless the message matches a remember or recall pattern (request-processor.ts:1116-1121,1145).
not_available: The Remember command is not offered through the memory tool on cli, vscode or api surfaces (AMBIENT_TOOL_SURFACES, request-processor.ts:1111-1114).

established.statement: The user can type a new fact and save it to their memory, where later chats can use it.
From inside a conversation the user can explicitly ask the assistant to remember something and gets confirmation it was saved.
The user can stop sensitive information being remembered and credentials are refused automatically.
Add, edit and delete memory are required features.
Memory must never silently absorb Local-only sensitive data into synced or global memory.

acceptance_criteria: Typing a new fact in the web list adds it and the list shows it.
Typing the same fact twice leaves one memory.
Typing a fact containing a never-remember term shows the Not saved message and adds nothing.
Saying Remember that I use pnpm in a chat saves it and the reply states the outcome.
Saying a Remember sentence in a temporary chat saves nothing.
An empty or whitespace-only fact is refused with Content is required.
A text with a password or key is refused on every app.
inferred: Edits to a fact do not trigger merge or supersede, only admission checks [inferred from apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/route.ts:100-135 vs writeConsolidatedMemory use in route.ts:151].
Pinned facts win topic conflicts, so a typed fact may be kept out with the overruled outcome [inferred from managed-memory-context-service.ts:687-690, 813].
proposed: [proposed] Make CLI and VS Code chat Remember sentences call /api/memory/commands so the answer is the same on every app.
[proposed] Add a never-remember list to mobile Local mode.
[proposed] Show the server refusal reason when a mobile Cloud add is refused during sync.

steps.what_happens: Person submits a fact in the list.
Client shows the fact as pending, fetches a CSRF token, posts to /api/memory.
Server checks rate limit and CSRF, reads the body with the shared contract, resolves the project, runs the never-remember check.
Admission: credentials refused; temporary chat refused; workspace and user switches checked; trust mode must be managed.
One SQL statement merges a duplicate, finds same-topic rivals, inserts, and supersedes lower-ranked rivals.
Chat command path: client posts the message to /api/memory/commands; server parses, applies the same gates and answers; the next chat turn carries a note so the reply states the outcome.
Mobile Local add writes SQLite on the device after refusing credentials.

access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Typed adds are model independent. Tool-based remember needs tool support and a streaming turn (request-processor.ts:1131-1142).

access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local adds stay on the device with credential refusal only (localMemoryWriter.ts:25-75). Server memory never accepts Local or own-key content (managed-memory-context-service.ts:646-660).

steps.what_happens: The editor mounts and asks the store to hydrate from the server.
Store fetches pages of /api/memory until hasMore is false.
Server runs one query joining projects and chats under row-level user scope and returns the page.

CLI refreshes its cache from /api/memory/sync before printing.

features.summary: The person can change the text of a memory, delete one, delete all of them after a confirmation, or reset memory without touching chats. Deleting a memory keeps an empty row so other devices learn of it. Deleting chats does not touch memory.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person correct or remove saved facts, individually or all at once, separately from chat history (apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/route.ts:78-170; apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:168-205).
purpose.why_it_exists: Add, edit and delete memory are required features, and correction and deletion must propagate to future sessions (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 18; doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:317).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who wants to fix or erase what the assistant knows.
problems_solved: Wrong facts keep being used.
The person wants a clean start without losing chats.
Removed facts must disappear from other devices.
use_cases: Change I live in Paris to I live in Rome.
Delete one outdated preference.
Press Clear all memories before sharing the account.
Say Forget my address in chat and confirm.

working: Edit: PUT /api/memory/[id] trims text, rejects never-remember terms and ineligible text, updates the row and updated_at; only live, unexpired rows in the person's workspace (apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/route.ts:78-135).

Delete one: DELETE /api/memory/[id] soft-deletes by blanking text, category and import key (route [id]:138-165; managed-memory-context-service.ts:391-392); a database trigger also blanks text on any deleted row (apps/web/db/neon/0355_user_memories_purge_deleted_text.sql:1-30).
Delete all: DELETE /api/memory marks every live memory in the current workspace deleted, including project-only ones, and returns the count (apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:168-205).
Web store removes optimistically and restores the fact if the server call fails (memoryStore.ts:364-383).

Chat forget: matching memories (at least 3 characters, at most 25 matches) are shown for confirmation before deletion; ids only are logged (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:60-64; commands/route.ts:76-90).
Mobile edit, delete and reset for Cloud and Local; Cloud reset calls DELETE /api/memory (store.ts:251-340).
CLI edit and forget by id or exact text (lib.rs:4173-4223,4332-4345).
VS Code edit, delete, clear all with confirmation (commandSetup.ts:1998-2026,2101-2160).
Chrome edit and delete with confirmation (memorySheet.ts:111-190).

Deleting chats does not run any memory deletion: no chat deletion code references user_memories in apps/web/app or lib outside memory, export, erasure and workspace files (search of app and lib). Account deletion does include user_memories (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:93).
incomplete: DELETE /api/memory/[id] does not check that a row matched; it always answers success (route [id]:150-170).
Edit does not re-run merge or conflict handling, so editing a fact into a duplicate of another is not merged [inferred from route [id]:100-135].
Whether the interface tells the person that deleting chats leaves memory in place: not found; the dialog only says chats are not deleted by clearing memory.
Edited text on mobile Cloud reaches the server through sync; refusal at sync is not shown in code I opened.
not_available: CLI: no delete-all or reset subcommand (lib.rs:1435-1486).
Chrome: no delete-all or reset (memorySheet.ts).

established.statement: The user can change the text of a saved memory and the corrected text is what later chats use.
The user can delete one saved memory so the assistant stops using it.
One action deletes every saved memory, after a confirmation, and afterwards none remain.
The user can reset all memory without deleting chats, and deleting chats does not silently wipe (or silently keep) memory.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.
Propagate corrections and removals through retrieval and future sessions.

acceptance_criteria: After editing a fact, the list and the next chat use the new text.
After deleting one fact, it is gone from the list and from a second device after sync.
Clear all memories asks first, shows the count and says chats are not deleted.
After Clear all, the list is empty and the saved-count reads zero.
Deleting a chat leaves memories in place and the learned fact stays in the list.
Reset on mobile Local deletes only on-device facts; Cloud reset deletes only account facts.
A failed delete shows an error and the fact is still listed.
inferred: Deleted rows are kept as empty tombstones so sync clients delete their copy [inferred from the comment on DELETED_MEMORY_ASSIGNMENTS, managed-memory-context-service.ts:388-391].
Whether keeping memory after chat deletion is intended or a gap depends on the Should line, which asks that it is not silent [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Tell the person when they delete a chat that learned facts remain, with a link to Memory.
[proposed] Add agi memory reset with confirmation to the CLI and a reset action to Chrome.
[proposed] Make delete-one return 404 when nothing matched.

features.summary: A person can pin a memory so it ranks first and wins topic clashes. When a newer fact about the same topic (name, home, employer, role, origin) is saved, the older one is replaced but kept. A list of replaced memories lets the person restore one.

purpose.what_it_does: Pinned facts rank highest in the list, in what the assistant reads and in conflicts. A new same-topic fact replaces an older one, which stays as history, and the person can swap them back (managed-memory-context-service.ts:687-690, 760-870; apps/web/app/api/memory/conflicts/route.ts:15-60; apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/restore/route.ts:20-70).
purpose.why_it_exists: Explicit current instructions should override stale memory and conflicts should be recorded, not silently kept (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:316). The brief requires pin, stale correction and a visible, settleable conflict (S39.16, S39.19, S39.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone whose situation changes, or who wants a fact kept first.
problems_solved: Old facts such as a previous city keep being used.
Important facts get crowded out.
A wrong automatic replacement can be undone.
use_cases: Pin Reply in short sentences so it is always used.
Move house and say I live in Berlin now; the Paris fact is replaced.
Open Replaced memories and restore the old employer.
See why a typed fact was not kept because a pinned one outranks it.

established.statement: The user can mark a memory as important (pin) so it is kept and preferred over others.
When the user states a newer fact that contradicts a stored memory, the outdated memory stops being used without a manual edit.
When two memories disagree, a stated rule decides which one is used, and the user can see or settle the conflict.
Explicit current instructions override stale memories; record conflicts rather than silently preserving obsolete preferences.

acceptance_criteria: Pinning a fact moves it to the top of the list and keeps it after reload.
With I live in Paris saved, saving I live in Berlin leaves only Berlin active.
The Paris fact appears under Replaced memories next to Using: I live in Berlin.
Pressing Use the replaced one instead makes Paris active and Berlin replaced.
With a pinned I live in Paris, typing I live in Berlin is not kept and the person is told why.
A replaced or restored memory never appears twice in the active list.
The conflicts list shows at most 50 entries.
inferred: The rule is: pinned beats user-written beats learned; among equals the newer wins [inferred from memoryWriteRank and rivals.rank > incoming.rank, managed-memory-context-service.ts:687-690, 813].
Restore swaps rather than adds, so there is never an ambiguous double winner [inferred from restore route:48-68].
proposed: [proposed] Broaden conflict topics beyond five, or let the model judge contradictions, then show them in the same Replaced memories list.
[proposed] Add pin to VS Code and Chrome and a replaced-memories entry to CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
[proposed] Connect or remove the unused consolidation sweep.

steps.what_happens: Pin: client flips the flag locally, then sends PUT with pinned.
New fact write: one SQL statement checks duplicates, finds same-topic rivals, chooses a keeper by rank, inserts and marks superseded rows.

Review: client fetches /api/memory/conflicts.
Restore: POST swaps the two rows after the exclusion check.
Mobile Local does the same on SQLite.

features.summary: Three views of what AGI has learned. Web Settings, Memory has a model-written card, "What AGI knows about you", with About you and Your preferences. Reflect (web, mobile) lists "Work in progress", built from chat history, not memories. Mobile "Memory summary" only groups saved facts. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a signed-in person read a short account of what AGI knows about them. The web card gives lines about who they are and how they like answers. Reflect gives a list of chats that look like ongoing work. The mobile Memory summary screen groups the saved facts as Pinned, Learned from chats and Added by you.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief (S39.07, S39.08, S39.09) requires the person to be able to read what the assistant learned about them, their preferences and their ongoing work, so memory is inspectable and not a black box. docs/product/experience-contract.md:28 asks for inspectable memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people who have memory turned on and want to check or correct what AGI remembers. Support staff and testers use it to see the effect of saved memories.
problems_solved: The person cannot tell, from a long list of single facts, what the assistant believes about them.
The person cannot see which chats AGI treats as continuing work.
A wrong or stale fact is easier to spot in a short summary and then fix in the list below it.
use_cases: On web, open Settings, Memory, press Summarise my memories and check the About you and Your preferences lines.
On web or mobile, open Reflect and read Work in progress to see which chats ran over several days or had several follow-ups.
On mobile, open Memory, then Memory summary to see pinned facts, facts learned from chats and facts typed by hand, on the device.
After deleting a memory, reload the summary and see that the old line is gone only once the summary is written again.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Memory section, card titled "What AGI knows about you" (apps/web/features/settings/components/MemorySummaryCard.tsx:153; hosted at apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:493).

Web: Settings, Reflect section, heading "Work in progress" (apps/web/features/settings/sections/ReflectSection.tsx:296; the section is registered in apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx:298).

The Electron desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5), so it gets the web screens [inferred].
CLI, VS Code and Chrome: not present (no code found).
prerequisites: Signed in to an AGI account for the web card and for Reflect.
Memory switched on. Reflect also needs the generate-from-history setting not switched off (apps/web/lib/services/reflect-service.ts:65).
For the web card, at least one saved memory in the current workspace; otherwise the card says nothing is saved (apps/web/features/settings/components/MemorySummaryCard.tsx:173).
Mobile Reflect is reached through the Cloud settings route only (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:838-843).
screens_and_controls: Web card: buttons "Summarise my memories" (first time) or "Update summary", "Try again" after a load error, lists headed "About you" and "Your preferences", and an "Updated <date>" label (MemorySummaryCard.tsx:179,199).

Web Reflect: range dropdown labelled "Reflect range" (30 days, 3 months, 6 months, year), button labelled "Refresh recap" (ReflectSection.tsx:114), and a link to Personalization settings when memory is off (ReflectSection.tsx:137).
Mobile Reflect: range selector, "Retry loading Reflect" button and "Open memory settings" button (reflect.tsx:269-305).
Mobile Memory summary: read-only sections Pinned, Learned from chats, Added by you, and a footer line naming the memory count and date (consolidation.ts:113; memory-summary.tsx:44).
journey: 1. Open Settings, then Memory (web) or Memory, then Memory summary (mobile).
2. Web: the card loads the last stored summary for the current memories (GET /api/memory/summary).
3. Press Summarise my memories (or Update summary) to ask our servers to write a new one.
4. Read the About you and Your preferences lines; the footer shows the date it was written.
5. To change a line, edit or delete memories in the list below; the card reloads, and the summary shows as not written until you update it.
6. For ongoing work: open Reflect, pick a range, read Work in progress; each row shows the project, the days active, the number of follow-ups and the last active date.
feedback_and_outputs: Spinner with label "Loading your memory summary" while loading.
"Nothing is saved yet, so there is nothing to summarise." when there are no memories.
"AGI has not summarised your saved memories yet." before the first write; "Your memories do not say enough yet to summarise." when the model found nothing.
Error text with "Try again"; write failure text "The summary could not be written right now. Try again in a few minutes."
Reflect: "Building your recap..." while loading; "Memory is off" panel with a settings link; "Reflect could not load" with a retry control.
settings: Memory on/off and Save memories from chats (the generate-from-history flag) decide whether Reflect is allowed (reflect-service.ts:65).
No setting turns the web summary card off separately [inferred from the absence of one in MemorySection.tsx].

working: Web profile and preference summary exists: POST /api/memory/summary writes About and Preferences lines (up to 6 lines of 240 characters each) from up to 200 memories, and GET returns the cached one (apps/web/app/api/memory/summary/route.ts:29,69; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/memory-summary.ts:5).

The summary is cached for 30 days under a fingerprint of memory ids and update times plus the workspace, so any edit makes the stored summary stale (apps/web/lib/services/memory-summary-service.ts:35; fingerprint function in the same file).
Summary generation is metered: it reserves usage under the feature name memory_summary and is rate-limited to 10 per hour (memory-summary-service.ts:28,200; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:287).

Web Reflect builds Work in progress from conversations that span more than one day or have at least 3 user messages, newest first, at most 6 (reflect-service.ts:19,104; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversations.ts:308).
Reflect excludes temporary chats and chats that contain a cloud agent run, and only reads the signed-in owner's chats in the active workspace (reflect-service.ts:327,335).
Reflect refuses with code memory_required (HTTP 409) when memory is off (apps/web/app/api/reflect/route.ts:37).
Mobile Reflect shows Work in progress and a Memory is off state (reflect.tsx:251,498), fetching /api/reflect (apps/mobile/src/features/reflect/service.ts:39).

Mobile Memory summary groups local or cloud memories on the device with no network call (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory-summary.tsx:40; apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/consolidation.ts:113).
incomplete: Ongoing work is built from conversations, not from memories as the brief's Should line says (reflect-service.ts:104,277). Memory only acts as a switch.

Mobile Memory summary is a grouping of stored facts, not a written profile or preference summary; the page footer says "Generated from N memories" although no model is used (memory-summary.tsx:40; consolidation.ts:113).
Desktop (Tauri) Reflect tab fetches the recap but shows no ongoing-work list (CloudReflectSection.tsx; grep for ongoingWork found nothing).
disconnected_or_disabled: The summary cache is skipped when no key-value store is configured; the GET then returns an empty summary even after a write (memory-summary-service.ts, readCachedMemorySummary returns null without a store). Whether production has the store is unknown.
not_available: Profile summary and preference summary on mobile as model-written text: not built, and a decision says it will not be (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:294).
Any of the three summaries in CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no code found.
The brief and decision D-2026-09-28-17 say web and desktop show no profile summary; the web card exists in code (git commit 997be012c4), so those documents are out of date.

established.statement: The user can read a summary of what the assistant learned about them as a person.
The user can read a summary of the preferences the assistant learned from memory.
The user can read a summary of the ongoing work or projects the assistant knows they pursue.
Memory is inspectable, scoped, and every entry exposes provenance, last update, edit, exclusion, export and deletion.
Mobile does not add a generated profile summary because the leaders show none (S39.07 mobile).

acceptance_criteria: On web with at least one memory, Settings, Memory shows the card "What AGI knows about you"; pressing Summarise my memories shows About you and Your preferences lines, each at most 6.
With zero memories the card says nothing is saved and pressing nothing calls a model (route.ts:79 gate is skipped when no memories).
After editing or deleting a memory the card reloads and the old summary is no longer returned until the person updates it.
In a personal workspace the summary uses only personal memories; in a workspace it uses only that workspace's memories.
Reflect with memory on lists at most 6 Work in progress rows, each from a non-temporary chat that spans more than one day or has at least 3 user messages.
Reflect with memory off returns 409 memory_required and shows the Memory is off panel on web and mobile.
The mobile Memory summary lists Pinned, Learned from chats and Added by you facts and works offline in Local mode.
If the model call fails the card keeps working and shows the retry message.
inferred: The brief's "built from memories" wording for Work in progress should be read as "allowed by the memory setting" because the code reads chats [inferred from reflect-service.ts:277-345].
Electron desktop gets the web card because it shows the hosted web app [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5].
proposed: [proposed] Add the summary card to the desktop Tauri Memory tab and to the mobile Memory screen in Cloud mode, reusing /api/memory/summary.
[proposed] Change the mobile footer from "Generated from" to "Grouped from" so it matches what the screen does.
[proposed] Update the brief and D-2026-09-28-17 to say the web card exists.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Summarise my memories; the card sends POST /api/memory/summary with a CSRF token.
Server reads up to 200 active memories of the current workspace, pinned first.
If memories exist, the workspace policy check decides whether managed compute is allowed.
Server picks a utility route, reserves usage under memory_summary, and asks the model provider to write About and Preferences lines (low randomness, 600 output tokens, 30 second limit).
Reply is cleaned, deduplicated, capped at 6 lines per section and cached for 30 days under a fingerprint of the memories.
Reflect: the server reads user-owned chat rows for the range and computes counts, topics and the ongoing-work list in code, then returns it with no-store caching.
Mobile Memory summary groups the facts already held in the app's memory store.

data.what: Memory summary text and generation time
data.where_stored: Server key-value store, key prefix agi:memory-summary:, per user and fingerprint
data.synced: Read by every web session of the account; not copied to other apps
data.retained_or_deleted: Expires after 30 days; a changed memory set gives a new fingerprint so the old entry is no longer read (memory-summary-service.ts:35)

data.where_stored: Computed in memory from the app's memory store

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The web summary uses a managed utility route chosen on the server (admitManagedCloudRoute, kind utility); the person cannot choose the model and no model name is fixed in this feature's code (memory-summary-service.ts:180). access_and_usage.account: Web card, web and mobile Reflect need a signed-in account (getUserScopedDb in both routes). Mobile Memory summary has no account requirement in Local mode (it reads the device store).

aliases: Use memories from outside this project
features.summary: A memory can be tied to one project so only that project's chats use it, and a project can refuse account memories. Done on web, mobile and CLI (with limits); the desktop Tauri build keeps separate device folder notes. Memory kept by a custom agent apart from personal memory does not exist in any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person save facts that apply only inside one project, and choose whether that project also draws on account-wide memory. Memories show an Only in <project> label in the list so they are not mistaken for global facts.
purpose.why_it_exists: Project work has its own facts (a market, a stack, a client). Mixing them into every chat is wrong, and mixing personal facts into a client project is a privacy risk. Brief S39.24 and docs/product/requirements.md:760 require a project memory boundary.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who use Projects on web or mobile, and CLI users who link a folder to an account project.
problems_solved: Facts for one client leaking into unrelated chats.
A project that must stay clean of the person's other memories.
Not knowing whether a listed fact is global or project-only.
use_cases: Open Project settings on web, add 'This project targets the EU market' under project memory, and see it used only in that project's chats.
Turn off 'Use memories from outside this project' so a client project uses only its own memories.
On mobile, open a project's settings and add a memory under PROJECT MEMORIES.
In the CLI, run agi memory add --project after linking the folder, so only that project's chats draw on it.

aliases: Work and personal memory kept apart
features.summary: Memories belong either to a person or to a workspace. Every read, write, import, export and chat lookup filters on the active workspace, so work facts never show in personal chats and the reverse. Web, mobile, CLI and VS Code say which scope is active; desktop Tauri and Chrome show no label.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps memories saved in a workspace (an organization) apart from personal memories. The server stamps each memory with the workspace and filters by it on every query. A workspace owner or admin can turn memory off for all members.
purpose.why_it_exists: Work facts must not leak into personal chats or the reverse, and a company must be able to control memory for its members. Brief S39.26 and docs/product/experience-contract.md:28 require separately scoped memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who belong to a workspace and also use AGI personally; workspace owners and admins who set policy.
problems_solved: A client name saved at work appearing in a personal chat.
A member's personal facts being read in a company chat.
A company wanting memory off until it has reviewed it.
use_cases: Switch to a workspace on web, save a memory, switch back to personal and see it is not listed.
An admin opens Workspace, Policy and turns Allow memory off; members see a notice in Settings, Memory.
In the CLI run agi memory list and read which workspace the memories belong to.
In VS Code open the memory tree and see 'Personal memory' or '<workspace> memory'.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Memory; description 'Facts saved in your selected Cloud workspace.' and a scope explanation list (Account, Workspace, Project) (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:41); notice when workspace memory is off (MemorySection.tsx:38).
Web admin: Workspace policy section, Memory group, switch 'Allow memory' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:484).

Mobile: Settings, Memory screen shows a scope line, for example '<name> workspace memories, never used in personal chats.' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx:72). It is a line of text, not a tab.
CLI: agi memory list prints '<N> memories in <workspace>' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4114).
VS Code: memory tree header 'Personal memory' or '<workspace> memory' with the text that work and personal memory are kept apart (apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/memoryTreeProvider.ts:103).

Desktop Tauri Memory tab and Chrome memory sheet: no workspace or personal label found (grep of apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/Memory.tsx, apps/desktop/src/api/cloudMemory.ts and apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/memorySheet.ts returned zero matches). Electron desktop shows the web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5) [inferred].

features.summary: People can bring memories in from another assistant or a file and download theirs. Web has a paste-or-upload dialog with a preview; mobile has a similar screen. Desktop Tauri imports and exports device JSON. CLI imports and exports from the terminal, but its import shows no preview. VS Code and Chrome have neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Import turns a pasted reply or an uploaded text or JSON file into candidate memories, shows them for review, drops duplicates and saves the chosen ones. Export writes the person's saved memories into a file they can keep.
purpose.why_it_exists: People moving from another assistant should not start from zero, and they should be able to take their data out. docs/product/requirements.md:1513-1522 asks for an import with a prompt for the other provider, paste or upload, parsed candidates, dedupe, edit before saving and approve.
purpose.who_uses_it: People switching from another assistant; people backing up or auditing their memories; support staff.
problems_solved: Rebuilding memory by hand.
No copy of what AGI holds about the person.
Duplicate or unsafe facts entering memory in bulk.
use_cases: On web, copy the prompt, send it to another assistant, paste its list, preview, tick the items to keep and import.
On web, press Export memories to download a dated JSON file.
In the CLI run agi memory import notes.md --source ChatGPT.
On the desktop Tauri build, export Markdown for reading and JSON for backup, then import the JSON on another device.

features.summary: Only the CLI shows a memory limit. Its /memories overlay shows 'N of M stored' and lets the person pick a cap (100 to 2000 facts) that the on-disk memory file is trimmed to, newest kept. It does not list which facts fall outside. Web, desktop, mobile, VS Code and Chrome show no capacity.

purpose.what_it_does: In the terminal app, the Memory Settings view shows auto-memory on or off, a decay period in days, and a maximum number of facts with the number currently stored. When memory is merged, older lines beyond the maximum are dropped.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S39.23 says that where memory has a limit, the person should see how much is used and which memories fall outside it. The CLI stores memory in plain files on disk, so a cap keeps them bounded.
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users who keep learned memory on their machine.
problems_solved: Memory files growing without bound.

Web, desktop, mobile, VS Code, Chrome: not present. Web Settings, Memory shows only a count line '<N> saved memories' with no limit (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx, line with counts.savedMemories).

Keys: up and down move, Enter toggles or cycles, S saves, Esc closes without saving (memories_settings.rs:122,133).
journey: 1. Type /memories in the terminal UI.
2. Read the stored count against the cap on the Max facts row.
3. Press Enter on a row to change it.
4. Press S to save; Esc discards.
5. The next memory merge (hourly cooldown) trims each memory file to the cap.

features.summary: Rules for what memory may hold and use. People list terms to never remember; credentials and other prohibited facts are refused for every source; sensitive topics need opt-in for automatic saves. Temporary chats neither read nor save memory. Web and mobile show which memories a reply used. The server applies one memory context to every model.

purpose.what_it_does: Enforces privacy rules on memory: a never-remember list of terms, automatic refusal of credential-like and other prohibited facts, an opt-in for sensitive topics, temporary chats that skip memory completely, a 'Memory · N' indication on replies that used memory, and the same memory for every model and every signed-in client.
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to stop sensitive information being remembered and see when memory shaped a reply. Brief S39.27 to S39.32 and docs/product/requirements.md:765 require temporary chats to neither update nor reference memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who uses memory; privacy-minded people; workspace admins relying on policy; testers.
problems_solved: Passwords, payment details or identifiers ending up in memory.
Private topics being remembered without consent.
Not knowing whether an answer came from memory.
Memory working on one model or app and not another.
use_cases: Add 'home address' to Never remember; a later attempt to save a fact containing it is refused with a message naming the term.
Start a temporary chat and tell the assistant a fact; it is not saved and no memory is read.
Open a reply's 'Memory · 3' control to see which saved facts were used.
Save a fact in the CLI and see it on web and in VS Code.

5. In a normal chat, if memory shaped a reply, open Memory · N to see which facts.

Typed saves, edits, sync pushes, imports, explicit remember commands and automatic saves all check the list; a read failure refuses the write (apps/web/lib/services/memory-write-service.ts:39,44; apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:148; apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:170; apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:107; apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:114; managed-memory-context-service.ts:1372).

Sensitive topics (health, ethnic origin, religion, politics, sexual orientation, gender identity, union membership) are refused for automatic saves unless the person opts in or explicitly asks (memory-content-policy.ts:13-21; managed-memory-context-service.ts:603-640).

Memory is loaded by user, workspace, project and source filters only, with no model input, so every model gets the same context (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1128). Local-model turns on web and desktop prefetch the same account context (apps/web/app/api/memory/local-context/route.ts; apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4479).

Mobile temporary chat 'Personalized' option sets personalization true or false; the server turns memory off when personalization is false (request-processor.ts:3523), and what 'Personalized' adds in a temporary chat beyond instructions is not traced.
disconnected_or_disabled: Model-based extraction of automatic memories is switched by the environment setting AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION and only runs when the turn text was kept (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:36-58; docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:53-58).

established.statement: The user can stop sensitive information being remembered (never-remember terms or categories) and sensitive facts such as credentials are refused automatically.
In a temporary chat nothing is read from or saved to memory, and the chat is never used later as past-chat context.
When saved memory or past chats shaped a reply, the reply shows it and which memories.
Saved memory and personalization apply the same way whichever model the user picks.
A memory saved on one client appears and is used on every other client signed in to the same account.
Temporary chats must not update or reference memory unless the user explicitly changes that behavior.
Mobile keeps Local and Cloud memory separate; one is never copied into the other.
Temporary chats, Memory-off sessions, API and zero-data-retention traffic stay excluded from automatic extraction.
Sensitive categories require explicit controls.

acceptance_criteria: Adding 'home address' to Never remember then saving 'my home address is X' by typing, import, remember command and auto-save all refuse with the term named.
A fact that looks like a password or card number is refused in every app that writes memory.

A normal reply that used memory shows 'Memory · N' listing the facts on web and mobile.

A fact added in the CLI shows in web Settings, Memory and in VS Code after sync.
Exclusion terms shorter than 3 characters are rejected with a message.

The Chrome temporary chat probably excludes memory through the server's temporary conversation check [inferred].

steps.what_happens: Person adds a term; the client saves it in the account's memory settings namespace.
Any memory write reaches the server, which loads the list (failing closed on error), then runs the content and policy gate.
For a chat turn the server checks if the conversation is temporary; if so it uses a disabled memory policy and loads no memory or past chats.
Otherwise it loads memories filtered by user, workspace, project and suppressed sources, ranks them against the question, takes up to 30, and places them in the prompt fenced as untrusted data.
The model provider receives the prompt; the reply stream carries memory citations back to the app.
The app shows 'Memory · N' from the citations.
After the turn, automatic saving extracts facts, applies the exclusions and the eligibility gate and writes rows.
Other clients pull the new rows by delta sync.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Memory is added by the server for every model and provider and no model identifier enters the query (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1128). Auto-extraction may use a utility model route when the environment flag is on and the turn is not zero-data-retention (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:36-58). On Local-model turns on web and desktop the device asks for account memory and injects it itself (useChatStream.ts:4479); in own-key and Local modes content outside Managed storage is never saved to user_memories (trust_mode_outside_managed_storage, managed-memory-context-service.ts:540,654).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 50 terms of 3 to 100 characters; 30 memories and 8,000 characters per prompt; at most 5 automatic memories per turn (managed-memory-context-service.ts:67,71,72 MAX_AUTO_MEMORIES_PER_TURN); mobile reads 5 facts per local turn (chatExecutionStore.ts retrieveMemoryContext(content, 5)).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION for model-based auto extraction; user switches memory, generateFromHistory, searchPastChats, includeSensitiveTopics, allowToolAssistedGeneration (readUserMemoryCapabilities, managed-memory-context-service.ts:258).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Same for every model; no capability check was found. Tool-assisted memory generation has its own switch.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Memory is not saved from turns in own-key or Local trust modes (managed-memory-context-service.ts:654). Content tied to Google user data is excluded from memory reads (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1170 memoryFreeOfGoogleUserDataSql).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode keeps memory on the device, refuses credentials and sensitive topics, skips memory in temporary chats, and has no never-remember term check (localMemoryWriter.ts:25-35). CLI Local sessions do not receive account memory; only Managed sessions do (apps/cli/src/cloud/memory.rs header).

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person tell AGI what to call them, what their work is and a free-text background note. The text is saved to the account and added to Cloud chat requests as a user-preference block, never as system authority. Web (and the Electron Desktop that shows it), Mobile, CLI and VS Code can set it.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a preferred name (60 characters), a work description (120 characters) and an about-you note (1500 characters) on the account, and folds them into a <user_profile> block that is added to the model prompt for Managed Cloud chats (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:160-210). The block says it is user preference, not system authority, and asks the model to use the name sparingly and never to open a reply (user-identity.ts:182-190).
purpose.why_it_exists: So replies fit the person without them repeating who they are in every chat. [inferred] The product aim in docs/product/definition.md lists profile instructions and personalization as canonical account state.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on Web, Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app), Mobile, CLI (Managed mode) and VS Code. Chrome has no editing screen; it only receives the effect through Managed Cloud turns [inferred].
problems_solved: The assistant does not know the person's name or job.
The person has to restate background in each new chat.
A name typed in capitals is not shouted back (the name is title-cased by normalizeDisplayName, tested in apps/web/lib/server/__tests__/personalization-reaches-model.test.ts:80-130).
use_cases: A teacher types 'Ada' as name and 'Education' as work so examples are about classrooms.
A founder writes 'I run a small bakery and I am learning to code in the evenings' in More about you.
A CLI user runs /personalize set name Ada to change the name from the terminal.
A person clears the name so the assistant never uses a name (an empty name is treated as an explicit opt out, apps/web/lib/server/__tests__/user-identity.test.ts:104-142).

features.summary: In the CLI, a person defines a named agent as a Markdown file with front matter and a body that is its system prompt. Running with --agent or choosing it applies its instructions, model, tool limits and spend cap to the session. No other app has it.

purpose.what_it_does: Loads agent files from project and user folders, and when one is chosen, injects its body as a system message wrapped in <agent_system_prompt agent="name"> and applies its overrides (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:1-12,111-152).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a developer can keep reusable roles with fixed instructions and limits, for example a reviewer that cannot edit files.
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI developers.
problems_solved: Re-typing role instructions.
Limiting tools or spend for a role.
Sharing agents in a repository.
use_cases: Create a 'reviewer' agent restricted to read tools.
Run agi --agent reviewer for one session.
Describe an agent in words and have the model draft the file.
Set a budget cap for an agent.

features.summary: Lets a person pick a response style for one chat only, without changing their saved defaults. Web and Desktop store a per-chat style and length choice; Mobile stores a per-chat style; the CLI has a session-only switch. VS Code and Chrome have no per-chat choice.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person choose a response style (and, on Web and Desktop, a response length) that applies only to the open conversation. The saved defaults in Settings stay as they are. The choice is looked up again when the person returns to that chat.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief item S40.19 says: 'For one conversation the user can override their standing style/instructions without changing their defaults.' People want a formal answer in one chat and a short answer in another without editing Settings each time. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone chatting on Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile or the CLI. [inferred from (doc: AGENTS.md section 5) and the brief status]
problems_solved: Avoids editing global personalization for a one-off need.
Keeps a style choice attached to the chat it was made for, so a later chat starts clean.
A choice made before the first message is carried onto the new chat once it gets an id.
use_cases: Ask for a Concise style in one research chat while Settings stay at Default.
Pick Formal for a chat that drafts a letter.
In the CLI, run /output-style concise --session to try a style without changing the saved default.

Mobile: five rows (Normal, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal), no length control (StyleSelector.tsx:17-24).

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a pasted writing sample inside a custom style. When that style is used, a bounded, fenced copy of the sample is added to the instruction so the model can copy tone, vocabulary and sentence shape.

purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop people who write emails, posts or documents and want drafts in their own voice.
problems_solved: Replies sound generic and not like the user.
Describing a voice in words is hard; a sample shows it.
Pasted samples are treated as data so text inside them cannot give the model orders.
use_cases: Paste three paragraphs of a newsletter and ask for a draft in the same voice.
Keep two styles: one from formal client emails, one from casual posts.
Edit the sample later and see replies change.

features.summary: Lets a person start a chat that AGI does not keep in history, either for one chat or as the default for all new chats. Built on web, desktop (Cloud chip, Local header button, Electron menu), mobile and the Chrome extension. Missing on CLI and VS Code.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks a chat as temporary when it is created, so its messages are never written to the saved history. A person can arm it for the next chat from the composer, or turn on a default so every new chat outside a project starts temporary (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:60; apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:640-650).
purpose.why_it_exists: The leading assistants offer a private chat. People want to ask something sensitive or throwaway without it landing in history, search or memory. The decision record says the flag existed on the wire, the create route and the purge job, but no control could turn it on, so a control was wired (doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md, row 'Desktop temporary chats').
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on web, desktop, mobile or the Chrome extension who wants a conversation that is not kept.
problems_solved: A chat leaves a record in history and search that the person did not want.
A person has to remember to switch privacy on for each chat, so a default is offered.
Marking a chat temporary after the first message races the first save, so the flag is sent at creation (apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:640-646).
use_cases: On web, click + in the composer and choose Use incognito, then ask a private question.
On web, open Settings, Privacy and turn on Start new chats as temporary so every new non-project chat is temporary.
On mobile, tap the eye-off pill on the Chat tab, confirm Turn on, and chat without leaving history.
On Electron desktop, choose File, New Temporary Chat.

Temporary/private chats are clearly marked if supported.
The default is off unless the setting is on; a project chat cannot be temporary.
Turning temporary on is sent at creation, not applied afterwards.
The flag is read at creation, so toggling it later cannot change an existing chat's retention (desktop chip).

acceptance_criteria: On web with the default off, a new chat started from + menu Use incognito is created with isTemporary true and its messages never appear in history or search.
On web with Start new chats as temporary on, a new chat outside a project is temporary; the same in a project is saved to the project and shows the project notice.
Creating or patching a chat with a project and isTemporary true is refused with the project refusal text.
If the PATCH that changes the flag fails, the menu row does not show a mode the database does not hold, and the composer notice appears.
On mobile, after an app restart the pill is off.
On mobile, turning on shows 'Turn on temporary chat?' and Cancel leaves it off.
On Electron desktop, File, New Temporary Chat opens a new chat that is temporary even if a project was active.

steps.what_happens: Person arms temporary (menu row, default switch, File menu, pill, chip).
On first send the client decides temporary from the pending choice, the default and the project, and sends isTemporary true in the conversation create request.
The server validates (project plus temporary refused) and inserts the web_conversations row with is_temporary.
Each turn re-reads is_temporary from the conversation row; a temporary conversation's messages are not persisted and memory, past chats, file search, schedules and plugin drafts are not offered.
The turn is answered by the chosen model through the chat route; for a device model on web the chat is forced temporary and answered on the device.
A nightly job deletes temporary conversations older than 30 days (see F041-05).
Desktop Tauri Local: the chat id -1 is used for the native runtime, nothing is written to SQLite.

features.summary: In a temporary chat memory is never read and never saved. A Personalized switch decides whether profile, custom instructions and response style apply to the turn. Web and mobile Cloud have the switch; Chrome excludes memory but has no switch; CLI and VS Code have no temporary chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps temporary chats out of memory in both directions and lets the person choose whether their profile, instructions and style are used for the turn.
purpose.why_it_exists: Product rule: temporary chats neither read nor write memory (doc: docs/product/definition.md:173; docs/product/requirements.md:765). Without the rule a private chat could leak into or be shaped by saved memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: People using a temporary chat who want a clean answer, or want a private chat that still sounds like them.
problems_solved: Private questions becoming remembered facts.
Old memories steering a throwaway chat.
Custom instructions that do not fit a one-off chat.
use_cases: Ask a sensitive question without it entering memory.
Flip to Unpersonalized to get a plain answer without instructions and style.
Say 'remember that...' in a temporary chat and see nothing saved.

features.summary: Turns a temporary chat into a normal saved one. On web the person sees a Save this chat? question that counts the messages and mentions files; one database transaction keeps the messages and files. On mobile it is reached only through Share link. Chrome and Tauri desktop have no save path.

purpose.what_it_does: Writes the messages of a temporary chat into history, flips the chat to saved and keeps its files, after the person confirms (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:4969-5012; apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/keep/route.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: A temporary chat holds no messages on the server, so switching it off without a save would lose the conversation. The person can change their mind about a chat worth keeping, and sharing needs a saved chat (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:6-7).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who started temporary and later wants the chat kept or shared.
problems_solved: Losing a useful chat because it began as temporary.
Sharing a temporary chat (refused until saved).
use_cases: Web: turn off Use incognito mid-chat, confirm Save chat.
Mobile: Share link on a temporary Cloud chat, then Save chat.
Share a temporary chat after saving.

where_to_find_it: Web: + menu row 'Exit incognito', or the same control reached from the header flow (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1822-1838).
Web dialog titled 'Save this chat?' with confirm 'Save chat' (WebChatPage.tsx:4987-4991).
Mobile: open a Cloud temporary chat, chat menu, 'Share link' (cloud only), alert 'Save this chat to share it?' with Cancel and 'Save chat' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:2136-2160, 2186-2196).
Share dialog on web shows 'A temporary chat cannot be shared. Turn off temporary chat to keep it, then share it.' (apps/web/features/chat/components/share/ShareConversationDialog.tsx:396).

Choose Save chat. The page posts messages to the keep endpoint.
Server flips the chat, writes messages in order, sets the active leaf and flips the files in one transaction.
Toast 'Chat saved to your history.' and the row becomes a normal chat.
Choose Cancel: the chat stays temporary and nothing changes.
If there are no keepable messages the flag is simply patched with no question.

aliases: Private browser session that keeps no cookies or history
features.summary: Not built on any app. The brief wants searches that are not saved to history and an agent browser session that keeps no cookies or history. No control, setting or code for either was found. Only the word 'incognito' exists, as a label on Temporary chat in Web. Chrome extension refuses incognito windows.

purpose.what_it_does: Planned: (1) a mode where a search is not added to the person's search history; (2) a private browser session for the agent that discards cookies and history when it ends. Today neither exists. What does exist is a saved search history on Web and Mobile and a persistent browser profile for agent browsing in the internal Tauri desktop code (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/automation/browser/playwright_bridge.rs:331).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists it as something the product should offer (brief S41.12 and S41.13). The product experience contract also names a 'Temporary/incognito' notice for Cloud Chat, so the idea is expected in the product (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: A privacy-minded person on any app who does not want a search remembered, or who wants the agent to browse sites without leaving logins or history behind. [inferred]
problems_solved: Recent searches on Web and Mobile are kept until cleared, with no way to run one search unrecorded.
Agent browsing on desktop reuses a dedicated profile on disk, so cookies from one agent run can stay for the next.
use_cases: Look up a sensitive topic without it showing in recent searches.
Let the agent open a site where it must sign in, and leave nothing behind.
Run a research task that should not train the history list.

where_to_find_it: No app has a control for it. Web: none. Desktop: none. Mobile: none. CLI: none. VS Code: none. Chrome: none (brief S41.12, S41.13 status missing on all six).

Nearest things: Web shows 'Use incognito' and 'Exit incognito' labels for Temporary chat (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:3). Web Global Search has a 'Clear search history?' action (apps/web/features/chat/components/dialogs/GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:190). Mobile chat list shows 'Recent searches' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx:109).
prerequisites: None, because nothing exists to use.
screens_and_controls: Nothing to tap, type or click for this feature.
Related but different: Web Temporary chat switch 'Start new chats as temporary' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:717).
journey: A person looks for a private-search switch in the search box or in Settings and finds none.
Their searches are recorded as normal (Web and Mobile recent searches).
To remove them they must use 'Clear search history' on Web, or clear recent searches on Mobile.
feedback_and_outputs: No output for this feature. Web confirms a history clear with a toast such as 'Cleared {{count}} search from history' (apps/web/features/chat/components/dialogs/GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:177).
settings: None for this feature. Web 'Start new chats as temporary' keeps chats out of history and search, but it does not change how a web search or agent browser runs (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:33).

working: Web keeps a recent-searches list on the server and can clear it (apps/web/features/chat/services/global-search-service.ts:318, apps/web/features/chat/services/global-search-service.ts:368). This is the thing incognito search would bypass.

Mobile keeps up to five recent searches per mode in the device key-value store and can clear them (apps/mobile/src/features/search/recentSearches.ts:3, apps/mobile/src/features/search/recentSearches.ts:60).

Chrome extension is installed with incognito not allowed and the agent tab list skips incognito tabs (apps/extension/manifest.json:9, apps/extension/src/background.ts:4668). This is a refusal, not a private mode.
incomplete: Web Temporary chat is called 'incognito' in two labels but only affects chat saving, not search or browsing (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:3).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found in the code
not_available: Incognito search: missing on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome (brief S41.12).
Private browser session: missing on all six apps (brief S41.13).

Internal Tauri desktop agent browser uses a fixed on-disk profile folder named 'automation' under the app data folder, so it keeps cookies between runs (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/automation/browser/playwright_bridge.rs:331). Whether the public Electron desktop has a comparable browser profile is unknown.

established.statement: The user can run searches that are not saved to their history.
The agent can browse in a private session that keeps no cookies or history afterward.
Cloud Chat should show a Temporary/incognito notice; memory entries need an incognito exclusion.

acceptance_criteria: With private search on, a search run on Web does not appear in the recent-searches list after reload.
With private search on, a search on Mobile does not add an entry to recent searches in either mode.
A private agent browser session starts with no cookies from earlier runs.
After the private session ends, no cookie or history file from it remains on the device.
The mode is visibly marked while on and off by default.
A private search does not weaken the Temporary chat promise and does not change where the query is processed (still disclosed).
inferred: A private browser session should use a throwaway profile folder that is deleted on exit, because the current automation profile is fixed and persistent. [inferred]
Private search should be separate from Temporary chat because the two keep different data (chat text vs. search queries). [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add a 'Private search' switch beside the search box on Web and Mobile that skips recording of the query.
[proposed] Give agent browsing a 'Private session' option backed by a temporary profile that is deleted at the end of the run.
[proposed] Decide whether Chrome should ever allow incognito, since the current manifest test says local storage is shared across profiles.
