features.summary: Chats and files that stay on the device. Mobile Local Mode keeps chats and files in on-device storage; a copy to AGI Cloud needs a separate, reviewed action. CLI Local sessions run on local models and need an explicit handoff to leave. VS Code and Chrome are partial. Web and Desktop have no Local mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person keep conversations, and files used in them, on their own device so they are not uploaded to the AGI account. Each app does it differently: Mobile Local Mode runs on-device models; CLI Local privacy mode only allows local model providers; VS Code runs local models and saves developer sessions on the computer; Chrome has a switch that stops copying Managed Cloud chats to the account.
purpose.why_it_exists: The product has three separate trust boundaries (Local, own key, Cloud). Local must stay on the device and any move to another boundary must be explicit (doc: AGENTS.md section 6; doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 7.1 and 7.4).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who want AI help without sending chats or files to a server, and developers working on private code.
problems_solved: Chats are not silently uploaded.
Moving to Cloud or a provider key needs a visible step with a preview.
Works without an AGI account on Mobile.
use_cases: Chat on a phone with a downloaded on-device model while offline.
Ask the CLI about a private repo using a local model and attach files that stay on the machine.
Keep Chrome side-panel chats in the browser only by turning the mirror off.
Later copy selected local chats to AGI Cloud on purpose.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: model picker and mode switch ('Local Mode' / 'AGI Cloud'); Settings, Privacy (cloud privacy screen) shows the card 'Data privacy'; Settings, Privacy, Data use & access lists 'Chat in Local Mode'; Settings, Data Controls has 'Sync Local Chats to Cloud' and 'Delete all local chats'.
CLI: type /privacy-settings to see the mode; /privacy-mode shows or refuses changes; /files attaches files; /add-dir adds folders; /continue-with-byok and /continue-with-cloud draft a handoff.
VS Code: settings page, card 'Where your data goes', rows 'Local models' and 'Session history'.
Chrome: extension options page, section 'Privacy and data handling', switch 'Save Managed Cloud chats to my account'.
Web and Desktop: no Local mode; the Web privacy page says so ('Hosted Web and Desktop have neither mode').
prerequisites: Mobile: an on-device model must be installed; otherwise the chat shows a 'local model unavailable' error. No account needed for Local Mode (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/Common.tsx:179).
CLI: a local provider such as Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server on a local address with no key.
VS Code: Ollama or LM Studio running on the computer, per the settings text.
Chrome: signed in to Managed Cloud for the mirror to matter.
screens_and_controls: Mobile mode switch dialog: title like 'Switch to AGI Cloud?', body 'Sign in to use AGI Cloud; your local chat stays on this device.', button 'Continue' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ModeSwitchModal.tsx:102).
Mobile Data Controls alert 'Sync Local Chats to AGI Cloud?' with buttons 'Cancel' and 'Sync to Cloud' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:181).
CLI /privacy-settings lines: 'Local file access: explicit workspace roots only', 'Attached files: never included in BYOK handoff drafts automatically' (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:443).
Chrome toggle row with status text 'Managed Cloud chats stay in this browser only.' (apps/extension/src/features/privacy/dataHandling.ts:57).
journey: Mobile: pick a local model in the model picker; the app mode becomes Local; chat; messages are saved in the on-device database.
Mobile move to Cloud: pick a Cloud model on a new chat or confirm the mode switch; for old chats use Settings, Data Controls, 'Sync Local Chats to Cloud', read the counts, tap 'Sync to Cloud'.

CLI: start with a local provider so the session is Local; run /files <path> to attach files; run /continue-with-byok or /continue-with-cloud to get a reviewable draft; send the draft to complete the move.
Chrome: open options, find 'Privacy and data handling', switch off 'Save Managed Cloud chats to my account'; chats then show 'Saved on this device'.
feedback_and_outputs: Mobile local chat error when Cloud model chosen: 'This is a Local Mode chat. Start a separate AGI Cloud chat to use Cloud models.' (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2265).
CLI /files prints 'attached: <path>', 'already attached', 'truncated to budget' or 'failed' lines (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:389).
CLI handoff draft line 'Attached files excluded from this handoff: N' (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:572).
Chrome side panel label 'Saved on this device' with detail 'Account mirroring is off in AGI settings, so chats stay in this browser.' (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:598).
settings: Mobile app mode (persisted as 'chat-app-mode-store', default local) (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/appModeStore.ts:62).
CLI privacy_mode in config (project or account) (apps/cli/src/config.rs:140).

working: Mobile Local Mode: a Local chat uses the on-device runtime and refuses Cloud models; Cloud sync only runs in cloud mode with an account (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2262; apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:97).
Mobile explicit copy of local chats to Cloud with counts, caps and exclusions of temporary chats (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:181).

Mobile local-only chat files are removed by the wipe via removeAllLocalChatAttachments (apps/mobile/services/dsarExport.ts:467); Temporary Chat explainer in Local mode says attachments never leave the device (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:14).
CLI derives the privacy mode from the provider: local Ollama or keyless local OpenAI-compatible server is Local; ManagedCloud is Managed; everything else is own key (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:3070).
CLI refuses Cloud account calls unless the session is Managed (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368). Startup update check is skipped in Local (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:130).

CLI handoff is a reviewed draft: it records intent and does not flip the mode until the draft is sent; /privacy-mode refuses a Local-to-other change and points to the handoff command (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:225; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:470).
CLI file collection: /files attaches files, /add-dir adds folders, handoff drafts exclude attachments (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:389; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:572).
CLI sessions saved as files under the config folder in managed_sessions (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session_control.rs:18).

Chrome mirror switch gates conversation upload, history pull and account deletion sync (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/conversationSync.ts:304; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/conversationHistoryPull.ts:337).
VS Code settings text states local models stay on the computer and sessions are saved by the CLI on this computer (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/settingsWebviewContent.ts:1600).
incomplete: Chrome: the mirror is on by default and only controls storage of chats; the model call still goes through AGI Managed Cloud, so chats are not 'local-only' in processing (apps/extension/src/features/privacy/cloudMirroring.ts:3; apps/extension/src/features/privacy/dataHandling.ts:36).
VS Code: only a description in settings; the local-only behaviour comes from the CLI runtime, and the extension has no own switch. Memory text there says account memory (see F041-09).

Web privacy copy says 'Local Mode and BYOK belong to the CLI', while Mobile also has Local Mode; the two texts disagree on which apps have Local (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:495).
CLI /privacy-mode cannot select Local; the mode follows the provider, so the draft instruction 'use /privacy-mode local' does not set it (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:470).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found in the code
not_available: Web: no Local mode and no local-only file collection (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:495).
Desktop: no Local mode or local-only file collection in the public Electron app, which shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). Internal Tauri desktop code was not assessed.
Mobile: no local-only file collection screen; files live per chat only. Brief gives no Mobile status for S41.15.
VS Code and Chrome: no local-only file collection (brief S41.15).

established.statement: The user can keep conversations only on their device, never uploaded to the account (done on Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome).
The user can keep a collection of files on the device that chats can use without uploading them (done on CLI only).
Local mode: no account required, local storage, no hidden provider or cloud call, no sync unless the user signs in and moves selected content.
Crossing Local to BYOK or Cloud needs user action, context selection, secret scan, payload preview, label, consent and a new branch that keeps the Local original.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to BYOK or managed cloud.
Local files do not leave the device in Local mode.

steps.what_happens: Mobile: person picks a local model; the app mode is set to local and the turn runs on the on-device runtime.
Mobile: messages are saved to the on-device database; cloud sync is skipped because mode is not cloud.
Mobile: person chooses 'Sync to Cloud'; selected text is sent to AGI Cloud and acknowledged per chat.
CLI: provider decides the privacy mode; Local sessions run through a local model server on the machine, and Cloud calls are refused.
CLI: /files reads file text on the device into the session; a handoff draft redacts secrets and leaves out attached files.
CLI: after the reviewed draft is sent, the session moves to the destination provider (own key or Managed).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Mobile Local uses an on-device model only; no provider key can be stored on Mobile v1. CLI Local allows local providers such as Ollama or a keyless local OpenAI-compatible server (packages/ai/providers/ollama, packages/ai/providers/lmstudio hold the shared adapters). VS Code names Ollama and LM Studio. Chrome has no Local model: its model calls go to AGI Managed Cloud.

access_and_usage.account: Mobile Local Mode: none required. CLI Local: none needed for Local itself. VS Code local models: none stated. Chrome: needs a Managed Cloud sign-in for mirroring to be relevant.
access_and_usage.permissions: CLI file access is limited to explicit workspace roots; extra folders are opt-in with --add-dir or /add-dir (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:443). Mobile file pick uses the system picker (not opened).
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code. Local inference is free of any paid plan per product requirement; no plan gate was found on any Local path.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Mobile copy to Cloud is capped (conversation limit and last-N messages per chat, shown in the alert) (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:181). CLI handoff has a message cap and a payload byte cap (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:586).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Mobile Local needs an installed on-device model; with none, the send fails with a local-model-unavailable error. CLI Local needs a local model server.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Mobile v1 has no provider-key route. CLI Local refuses non-local providers inside a Local session.
access_and_usage.local_mode: This feature is the Local mode behaviour. Mobile: chats, files and memory stay on the device and Cloud models are refused in Local chats. CLI: Cloud account calls and update checks are not made.

features.summary: Memory kept only on the device. Mobile stores facts in a local table named memory_facts and shows 'On-device memory' in Local Mode. The CLI keeps memory as markdown files under its config folder, split by trust boundary, with the Local file raw_memories.md. Web, Desktop, VS Code and Chrome have no local-only memory.

purpose.what_it_does: Remembers facts and preferences for later chats without putting them in the AGI account. Mobile in Local Mode saves typed or learned facts in a device database. The CLI extracts a summary after each session and merges summaries into a memory file per trust boundary.
purpose.why_it_exists: Memory must never silently absorb Local-only data into synced memory (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 18 text on memory). Local, own key and Cloud memory stay separate.
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile Local Mode users and CLI developers who want continuity without cloud storage.
problems_solved: Personal facts are not uploaded to the account.
Local memory is not mixed into BYOK or Managed prompts in the CLI.
use_cases: Tell Mobile Local Mode your preferences and see them grouped under Memory summary.
CLI remembers project conventions across sessions without leaving the machine.
Review what is stored with /memory and /memories.
Turn memory off or reset it.

VS Code: settings card 'Where your data goes' says Memory lives in the AGI Cloud account; button 'Memory' opens the memory tree. This is not local-only.
Web, Desktop, Chrome: no local-only memory.

Mobile Cloud mode instead reads the cloud memory store and marks changes for sync, so the two are separate (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/store.ts:135).

CLI merges summaries per boundary: Local into raw_memories.md, own key into byok_memories.md, Managed into managed_memories.md; a BYOK or Managed prompt carries only its own file, a Local prompt carries all three (apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:40).

features.summary: One action that erases the app's data on this device. Built on Mobile only: Settings, Storage, Danger Zone, 'Delete everything', then two confirmations. It withdraws provider sharing, signs out all accounts, deletes local tables, settings, models and files, and returns to onboarding. The age-refusal screen reuses it. Other apps have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Wipes conversations, memory, custom instructions, settings, installed model records, downloaded model files, chat files and exports from the phone, signs the person out of every account on the device and restarts onboarding.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires one action that clears all data the app keeps on this device (brief S41.17). It also serves the under-age refusal flow, which must be able to erase device data.
purpose.who_uses_it: A Mobile user leaving the app or handing over the phone; a person refused by the age gate.
problems_solved: No need to delete each chat, memory and model separately.
Account sessions on the device end with the data.
use_cases: Sell or hand over the phone.
Start fresh after testing.
Erase after the age check refuses the account.

screens_and_controls: Alert 1 'Delete all local data?': 'This permanently deletes all conversations, memory, settings, and downloaded models from this device. This action cannot be undone.' Buttons Cancel, 'Delete Everything'.
Alert 2 'Are you absolutely sure?': 'All local data will be wiped. You will be signed out and returned to onboarding.' Buttons Cancel, 'Yes, delete everything'.

settings: Related: Storage 'Clear cache' (removes temp files only) and per-model delete in the same screen; Data Controls 'Delete all local chats' (chats only).

working: Two-step confirmation with named consequences (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/useEraseDeviceData.ts:11).

wipeAllLocalData: withdraw provider sharing for this device, sign out all accounts, delete rows from telemetry_queue, memory_facts, custom_instructions, installed_models, provider_keys (if present), settings, conversations and memory_vectors in one transaction, close the database, delete set-aside databases, clear the key-value store and set-aside stores, run a reset callback, delete model folders, the export folder, local chat attachments and file exports and viewer copies (apps/mobile/services/dsarExport.ts:425).
Reset callback empties in-memory stores, clears the biometric flag and device id, and sets the app mode back to local (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/localDataSnapshot.ts:182).
Failure shows 'Wipe failed' and clears the spinner (useEraseDeviceData.ts:34).
The same hook backs the age-refusal screen (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/AgeRefused.tsx:62).
incomplete: Cloud copies of chats and memory are not deleted by this action; only a local sign-out and local deletion run (apps/mobile/services/dsarExport.ts:425). The alert text says 'conversations' without saying Cloud copies stay [inferred from the code path].
Storage totals shown on the screen cover only models and cache, not all data (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/StorageScopeNotice.tsx:13).
Alert text omits custom instructions and provider sharing even though they are removed.
disconnected_or_disabled: none found in the code
not_available: Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome have no clear-all-local-data action (brief S41.17).

No 'move to Trash first' step: the wipe is permanent and deletes files directly, which differs from the user-data rule in AGENTS.md section 9 for agent actions (this is a user-initiated action, which is allowed to be permanent) [inferred].

established.statement: One action clears all data the app keeps on this device.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and the question names the consequence.
Permanent removal happens only from an explicit user action that names what is lost.

acceptance_criteria: Both alerts appear in order and Cancel in either stops the wipe.
After 'Yes, delete everything', every listed table is empty and the key-value store is cleared.
Provider sharing is withdrawn before accounts are signed out.
If provider-sharing withdrawal cannot be recorded, nothing is deleted.
All accounts are signed out and the app lands on onboarding.
A failure shows 'Wipe failed' and the app stays usable.
The age-refusal screen runs the same wipe.
Downloaded model folders and chat files are gone.
inferred: Cloud data should be named in the alert as staying in the account, to avoid a false 'everything' claim. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add the same action to Desktop and CLI under their own data stores.
[proposed] Add a success confirmation before onboarding.
[proposed] Offer export first, as the age-refusal screen does ('Export this device's data').

aliases: Where each feature processes your data
features.summary: Privacy pages and statements on every app that separate history, model training and retention, and say where each feature is processed: on this device, on AGI servers then the provider, or direct to the person's own provider. Web and Mobile also have switches. CLI, VS Code and Chrome are statements only.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows, in plain words, what is kept as history, whether chats are used to train models, how long data is retained, and where each feature runs. Web and Mobile add controls: model-improvement toggles (off by default), a provider no-training switch, telemetry and temporary-by-default.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires history, training and retention to each have a separate control or statement, and each feature to state where data is processed (brief S41.18, S41.20). The leaders explain privacy settings in context (doc: AGENTS.md section 10).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any person judging whether to trust the product with their data; reviewers and support.
problems_solved: Confusion between deleting history, opting out of training and retention.
Not knowing whether a feature leaves the device.
Hidden provider handling on the Free plan.
use_cases: Check that 'Use my chats' and 'Use my voice' are off.
Find out that web search queries go to a third-party search service.
See how long a deleted chat is kept.
Check the CLI privacy mode before pasting private code.

features.summary: A recurring scheduled agent run that writes a short start-of-day brief. Web, desktop and Chrome seed it from the Daily briefing template (weekdays 08:00). Mobile has a Daily brief switch in Notifications that creates a daily schedule. The CLI only creates cron schedules. A server sweep runs it; a notice announces the run.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a schedule whose prompt asks the agent to brief the person on calendar, email, recent chats, saved memory and web news, in under 250 words (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:843). The server runs it at the chosen time and timezone and stores the run result. The person is told through a notice and reads the text in run history.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists 'the user sets up a recurring daily briefing that is generated and delivered to them' as item S42.01 and delivery time and timezone as S42.04 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/042-proactive-assistance-briefings-and-reflection.md). Proactive start-of-day help is a way to compete with Claude and ChatGPT scheduled tasks.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in Cloud users on a plan that allows scheduled tasks (billing-catalog.ts:593-723). Local and own-key users cannot (see access_and_usage).
problems_solved: The person does not have to open the app and ask each morning for a plan of the day.
One prompt covers several sources, so the person does not check each one.
Time and timezone mean the brief arrives at local morning, not server time.
use_cases: A manager turns on Daily brief on the phone and gets a notice at 08:00 each day.
A web user picks the Daily briefing template, moves it to 07:00 and saves.
A developer runs 'agi schedules create' with a cron expression and a briefing prompt.

steps.what_happens: Person opens a template; the form is filled in on the device and nothing is saved until Save.
Save sends POST /api/schedules; the server checks login, rate limit, CSRF and the plan's scheduled-task limit, then stores the schedule.
Mobile Daily brief creates the schedule through the same API and saves its id in the account notification preferences under 'dailyBriefScheduleId'.
Every 15 minutes the cron endpoint claims due schedules and runs up to ten at a time.
The executor picks a model route for an unattended run, loads allowed context (project, memory, recent chats), builds the tool plan (web, connectors) and calls the model.
The model provider answers the prompt.
The run result is stored and a 'notifications.schedule-completed' job is queued; it records an in-app notice, sends push through Expo and queues email.
Push reaches the phone through the Expo push service.

features.summary: A person stops a schedule without deleting it and starts it again. Web, desktop and Chrome have a Pause or Resume control; mobile has a switch; the CLI has 'agi schedules pause' and 'resume'; VS Code has Pause and Resume commands. The server also pauses a schedule itself when a run needs approval or the credit cap is reached.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a schedule off or on. Off keeps the prompt and settings, clears the next run time and marks status 'paused'. On recomputes the next run.
purpose.why_it_exists: Item S42.15 in the area brief: the user can pause and resume briefings (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/042-proactive-assistance-briefings-and-reflection.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with a schedule, such as on holiday or when briefings are noisy.
problems_solved: Deleting loses the prompt and settings.
Unwanted runs consume usage.
A schedule stopped by the system needs a way back.
use_cases: Pause the Daily briefing for a week away.
Resume after approving a paused run.
Pause from the terminal in a script.

Desktop (Tauri build): 'Pause' or 'Resume' button, status 'Active' or 'Paused' (DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx:1186,1229).
Mobile: switch on the schedule card (apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleCard.tsx:297); Notifications > Daily brief switch off pauses the brief (dailyBrief.ts:204).

features.summary: Quiet hours is a saved schedule of days and times. When on, the server drops routine push notices inside the window and delays routine schedule emails until it ends. Failed runs and approval requests are exempt. If the saved hours cannot be read, push is queued for retry and email is retried. Set on web, desktop and mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Stops routine proactive notices, such as 'Scheduled task finished', from alerting the person at night or other chosen times.
purpose.why_it_exists: Item S42.16: during quiet hours the product holds proactive notifications and nudges (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/042-proactive-assistance-briefings-and-reflection.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who receives scheduled-run notices.
problems_solved: A 07:00 brief or a night run buzzes the phone at the wrong time.
Email arrives while asleep.
The person still needs urgent failures and approvals.
use_cases: Quiet weeknights 22:00 to 08:00.
Weekend quiet all day.
A failed run still alerts at night.

working: Preferences namespace 'time-focus' with quiet hours, saved from web, desktop and mobile (time-focus.ts:1; useTimeFocusSync.ts:67).
Server push: sendPushToUser checks account quiet hours and returns no delivery inside the window (push-notification-service.ts:281-292).

Exempt types never held: agent_failed, emergency_stop_triggered, agent_approval_needed, approval_pending_escalation (time-focus.ts:6-11). Schedule failures, timeouts and approvals map to exempt types (schedule-notification-service.ts:82-88); only a success notice is held.
Device-level check also applies each phone's own quietHours from its push preferences (push-notification-service.ts:92-113; mobile-push.ts:24).

steps.what_happens: Person saves quiet hours; the app writes the 'time-focus' preference namespace to the account.
A schedule run finishes and a completion job records an in-app notice, then asks to push and, if email is on, queues the email.
Push: the server reads quiet hours from user_settings. Inside the window and not exempt, it returns without sending.
Outside the window, each phone is also checked against its own quiet hours before the Expo request.
The Expo push service delivers to the phone.
Email: the job computes when the quiet window ends and queues the email job to run after it.
If hours are unreadable, push is queued for retry and email is retried; on the last attempt push is dropped and email is skipped.
On the phone, an in-app alert reminds the person the window is active.

features.summary: Tells a signed-in person when background work ends or needs them. The server records a feed notice and sends Expo push and email for scheduled runs (done, failed, needs approval), and push for agent, research and code-session events. Chrome shows local browser notices for browser tasks. The CLI only rings a terminal bell. VS Code has nothing.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends a short notice when a scheduled run succeeds, fails, times out or pauses for approval, and when a cloud agent run, research report or code session finishes, fails or needs input. Delivery goes to an in-app feed row, then Expo push to the phone app and email, depending on per-schedule switches and account switches (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-notification-service.ts:65-80,139-213; apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts:140-184).
purpose.why_it_exists: Scheduled and agent work runs while the person is away, so they need a signal to come back, approve a step or read the result. The brief's target is: the user is notified when background work completes (S42.17, doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/042-proactive-assistance-briefings-and-reflection.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person with scheduled tasks or cloud agent runs, on web, desktop, mobile, the browser extension and (as a bell only) the terminal.
problems_solved: The person does not have to watch a long or unattended run.
An approval request is not left waiting unseen (approval notices bypass quiet hours, see states).
Failures are surfaced even when the person had silenced routine notices (failure type is quiet-hours exempt) (packages/contracts/types/src/time-focus.ts:6-11).
use_cases: A daily briefing schedule finishes at 07:00 and the phone gets a push 'Scheduled task finished'.
A scheduled run needs approval for a tool call and the person gets a push and email naming the step.
A scheduled run times out and the person gets a failure email even during quiet hours.
A browser task in the Chrome extension finishes while the person is in another tab and Chrome shows a notification.

The public Desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5), so the web pane applies there [inferred].

journey: 1. Person creates a schedule on web; the five notice switches default to on (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:114-125).
2. A run ends (success, failed, timeout) or parks for approval; the server queues a notice job (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1822-1869).
3. The job reads the schedule switches and the account push/email preferences (schedule-notification-service.ts:20-80).
4. It writes the feed row, then sends push and, through a separate job, email (job-handlers.ts:98-154).
5. The phone shows the push; tapping a schedule notice opens the Schedules screen (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:587-590).
6. The person reads the run in the schedule's run history (see F042-11).

Per-schedule notice switches are in the web schedule form only; none found in mobile, desktop src, extension, CLI or VS Code schedule code (search for onSuccess/onApproval/DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS).
disconnected_or_disabled: Schedule notices do not go to browser push: web transport is passed as false (schedule-notification-service.ts:184), while agent notices include web (agent-notification-service.ts:176).
The comment in agent-notification-service.ts:16-24 says schedule consent is opt-in; the code is opt-out (schedule-notification-service.ts:76-77). Code wins.

established.statement: The user is notified when background work (a scheduled run or agent task) completes.
During quiet hours the product holds proactive notifications and nudges.
Vscode is left at Claude Code in VS Code's scope; S42.17 is open for vscode in the audit.
Features ChatGPT and Claude do not offer are not built.

acceptance_criteria: With default switches, a successful scheduled run produces one feed row titled 'Scheduled task finished' and one push to a registered phone.
Turning 'When completed' off for a schedule stops the success notice but a failed run still notifies.
A stored schedule notice setting that is not valid sends nothing and logs a warning.
Two deliveries of the same run id produce one feed row and one email (idempotency key).
A cancelled run sends nothing.
During quiet hours a success push is not delivered and a failure or approval push is delivered.
An approval-needed run notifies once per approval step.
With mobilePushScheduleDone set to false the phone gets no push but the feed row remains.
inferred: A skipped run (status cancelled) never notifies, because skipped runs are finalized as cancelled and cancelled runs are not announced [inferred from apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:2257-2278,1825].
Every surface that shows a notice should respect the same Time and focus quiet hours [inferred from S42.16].
proposed: [proposed] Give the CLI a real completion notice for cloud schedules, or mark S42.17 partial for CLI.
[proposed] Expose the five per-schedule notice switches on mobile and desktop.
[proposed] Decide whether success push during quiet hours should be deferred like email instead of dropped.

steps.what_happens: A run ends or parks; the schedule service queues a notifications.schedule-completed job with task, run id and status. Running and cancelled and parked-for-approval end states are not announced by announceScheduleRun; approvals use announceScheduleApproval.
The job reads account notification preferences, profile email and the schedule's notificationSettings in one query scoped to the user and workspace.
If the status switch is on, the job queues the email job (delayed to the end of quiet hours for non-urgent types), then records the feed row.
Push: quiet hours are checked, then Expo push is posted for registered phones.
Expo's push service delivers to the device.
The phone applies its own category and quiet-hours gate before showing the banner.
Email is sent by the mail provider through the email job, idempotent per run.
Chrome: the background worker decides locally and calls chrome.notifications.create.
CLI: after a long turn the TUI writes a bell to stdout.

features.summary: Reflect shows a signed-in person patterns in their own chats over 30 days, 3 months, 6 months or a year: topics, active days, peak start time, daily activity and ongoing work. It needs Memory on, is computed by the server on request with no model, and is not stored. No weekly or monthly recap is delivered.

purpose.what_it_does: Builds an on-demand recap from the person's cloud conversations: total conversations, active days, most active day, peak start hour, topic shares, daily activity, four short observations and ongoing work (apps/web/lib/services/reflect-service.ts:127-274).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants a reflection on how the user uses the product (S42.19) and a recap of their past year (S42.21). Periodic recap (S42.20) is not built because neither ChatGPT nor Claude delivers one (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:134-135).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person who has Memory and 'generate from history' on, on web, desktop (cloud settings) and mobile.
problems_solved: Shows what the person actually uses the product for.
Gives a year view without exporting data.
Points to features that fit the pattern (observations link to projects, skills, Time and focus) (reflect-service.ts:217-248).

Pick 'Past year' for the annual view.

steps.what_happens: The page picks range and time zone and calls GET /api/reflect.
The server checks auth, rate limit and the query.
It reads user_settings and stops with memory-disabled if Memory is off.
It reads conversations and message samples for the range from the database.
It counts days and hours in the person's time zone, classifies topics by keywords, builds observations and ongoing work, and validates against the schema.
The client validates the response with the same schema and renders it.

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person look back at past scheduled runs, including daily briefings, with status, output, error, cost and a late or skipped note. Web and the internal desktop show a 'Recent results' list across schedules; mobile has a 'Scheduled runs' screen and per-schedule history. There are no saved editions; history is the run list.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists runs of the person's scheduled tasks, newest first, each with status, output, error, credits used and timing note (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:244-262,740-760; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1418-1454).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants past briefings and proactive outputs kept as a browsable history (S42.25). A briefing today is a schedule (S42.01), so its history is the run list.
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person with scheduled tasks on a plan that allows them.
problems_solved: Reading a result after the notice is gone.
Seeing why a run failed or was skipped.
Approving a paused run from the history.
use_cases: Open 'Recent results' to read this morning's briefing output.
See that a run 'Ran late' after downtime.
Page back through older runs with 'Show more results'.
Check how many credits a run used.

features.summary: The person attaches one or more pictures, or a screenshot, to a chat message and asks about them. The picture is checked, prepared and sent with the question to a model that can read images. Mobile Local mode cannot show the model the picture; it sends the on-device recognised text instead.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person put one image, several images or a screenshot into a chat message so a vision-capable model can answer a question about them. A screenshot is just an image file, so the same path covers captured and pasted screenshots.
purpose.why_it_exists: Competing assistants answer questions about pictures, and the brief lists single-image questions, multi-image comparison and screenshot interpretation as required for every app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, items S43.01 to S43.03). The one-chat requirement says a user adds images to a normal chat rather than using a separate file chat (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, section 4.2).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in chat user on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and the Chrome extension, including developers who paste error screenshots into the CLI or VS Code.
problems_solved: Describing a picture in words is slow and loses detail.
Comparing two pictures by hand is hard.
Explaining a screenshot of an error or a screen to an assistant.
use_cases: Attach a screenshot of an error in VS Code and ask what is wrong.
Attach two photos on the web composer and ask what changed.
Take a photo on the phone and ask about it.
Run the CLI with a file option for a screenshot and ask for a summary.

working: Web upload path: file picked, uploaded through the presign and complete routes, then scanned for executable signatures, type confusion, credentials and, when configured, an external scanner; a rejected file is deleted (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:397-420; apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:342, 601; doc: docs/security/upload-scanning.md).

Web turn path: the stored image is re-encoded only when it is too large, too wide, animated or in an unreadable format, then handed to the model as a data URL (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts:654-676; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/model-image.ts:63-121).
Web refuses a turn whose model cannot read images, whose image detail value the model does not accept, or whose image count passes the model limit (request-processor.ts:5099-5147).
Mobile Cloud: images are uploaded after consent with up to two retries (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadAttachment.ts:15, 83) and sent as file references (chatExecutionStore.ts:2745-2752).

CLI: images are read from disk, resized to fit, base64 encoded and sent as image blocks; clipboard images and the full-size option also work (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8383-8400; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:836-885, 916-940).

VS Code: drop and paste become pending image attachments stored as data URLs and are sent through the CLI app-server host, which caps 8 images per turn and 10 MB each (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:2207-2214; apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:132-138, 7573).

Chrome extension: composer accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF by paste or picker, checks size and a per-model image limit, and sends images with the turn (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:10059, 10177, 10343, 9501).
incomplete: Web and Desktop have no recorded live check on production; the brief marks them partial pending a live check after deploy (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.01 Unfinished).
Mobile Local mode: the on-device text model never sees the picture; it gets recognised text only (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:1241-1262, 2731-2735).

The web composer was not seen to warn before send that the chosen paid model cannot read images; the refusal is on the server after send [inferred from request-processor.ts:5099 and no composer check found].
disconnected_or_disabled: The CLI ACP server advertises image prompt capability as false (apps/cli/src/app_server/acp.rs:401), so that entry route does not take images.

If the upload scanner is required in production and not configured, every upload is refused with an external_scanner or scan_unavailable finding (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:408-440; doc: docs/security/upload-scanning.md).
not_available: Region selection, crop or zoom, annotated answers and input-quality warnings are not available on any app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.09 to S43.11, S43.19).
Own-key and Local-mode image handling on web, desktop and CLI: not established.

established.statement: A user attaches one image and asks a question; the image reaches a vision-capable model with the question.
A user attaches two or more images to one message and the model receives all of them to compare.
A user shares a captured or pasted screenshot and the model explains what it shows.
AGI keeps one chat: files, images and references are added to a normal chat, not a separate file chat.
Ask for consent before sending files to a provider and show the provider and model before use.
Local, own-key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing silently routes a Local file to another mode.

acceptance_criteria: Attaching a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file on the web composer shows a chip and the question is answered from the picture by a vision model.
Attaching two images in one message sends both; the answer refers to both.
Selecting a model that cannot read images and sending a picture returns a clear refusal and no model request is made.
A file whose bytes do not match its image type is rejected and deleted, with no answer.
On mobile in Local mode the app says the model reads only the text in the photo, and the picture is not uploaded.
In the CLI, /attach on a non-vision model refuses with the switch-model message; on a vision model it shows a chip.
Sending more images than the model allows is refused with the model's image limit in the message.
inferred: A picture sent in Cloud mode should be visible to the person as the same picture the model read, including a note when it was shrunk or animated; web adds a note for an animated image (model-image.ts:77-79) [inferred].

Paid-plan attachment limits should be the single source for every app that uploads [inferred from apps/web/lib/server/attachment-allowance.ts:83-97 and apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts:24-47].
proposed: [proposed] Disable or badge the attach control on web when the selected paid model cannot read images, as the free text-only model already does.
[proposed] Record a production run for each app with the S43.01 scenario and store the result in the audit register.

steps.what_happens: Web and Desktop: the person picks, pastes or drops an image; the composer checks count, size and plan limits.
The browser uploads the file through the presign and complete routes into private storage.
The server inspects the bytes (signatures, type confusion, credentials, data policy) and posts them to the upload scanner; a failure deletes the object and refuses.
steps.evidence: apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:397-440; apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:418-460; doc: docs/security/upload-scanning.md says the scanner service is our own

steps.what_happens: At send time the chat endpoint loads the stored asset, re-encodes it only if needed and builds an image_url data URL part.
The server refuses if the resolved model cannot read images, rejects an unsupported detail value, and refuses over the image limit.
The request, with the picture, goes to the chosen model provider and the answer streams back.
steps.evidence: apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:5099 (route resolved before); provider name depends on the route, not fixed

steps.what_happens: CLI: the image file is read, resized (or kept with --full), base64 encoded, held as a pending block and sent with the next message.
VS Code: the webview reads the dropped or pasted file; the extension holds a data URL; the CLI host validates and passes it as an image block.
Mobile Cloud: after consent the app uploads the image and sends an asset reference; Mobile Local: the app runs on-device OCR and sends text.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Any model whose registry metadata says it reads images may be used; the server checks the capability on the resolved model, including a model Auto picked (request-processor.ts:5098-5113). Routing treats an image attachment as an image signal (request-processor.ts:4502-4510). Per-route and per-model image counts come from the model registry and harness data (media-input.ts:60-66). The provider is not fixed by this feature.

access_and_usage.account: Web upload routes need a signed-in user and a scoped database (apps/web/app/api/uploads/chat-attachment/complete/route.ts:19). A guest chat route exists (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest); its image handling was not read: unknown. CLI Local and own-key use without an account: not established.
access_and_usage.permissions: Mobile camera permission for the Camera row and scan screens (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1526-1540); the capability canUseCamera gates the camera screens (scan.tsx:43). Mobile Cloud asks consent before the first upload (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/cloudUploadConsent.ts).
access_and_usage.subscription: Reading images has no plan entitlement of its own that was found. Plan limits apply to attachments: bytes per file, files per message and daily uploads (apps/web/lib/server/attachment-allowance.ts:83-97, 179; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:757-785). Free text-only models cannot take attachments and a free model with image input has its own rules (apps/web/lib/server/free-quota-turn.ts:761-770). Plan values per plan not read; see SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Image up to 20,971,520 bytes with handshake, 12,582,912 without; 20 files per message (10 without handshake) (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/chat-attachment-policy.json:2-12). Model copy up to 5,000,000 base64 bytes and 8000 px (same file:60-64). CLI app-server: 8 images, 10 MB each, 20,000,000 combined (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:132-134). VS Code attachment 10,000,000 bytes (apps/extension-vscode/src/protocol/webviewMessages.ts:171). Token metering for image input: the free-trial estimator counts per-image tokens (apps/web/lib/services/free-trial-service.ts:197-209); the paid metering rule for image tokens was not read.
access_and_usage.flags: UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL, UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN and UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED control the malware scanner (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:408-440). Mobile feature flags for attachments: none found in the code read.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Only models with the vision capability; others get code model_no_vision, HTTP 400 (request-processor.ts:5099-5113). The CLI checks supports_vision from its model catalog (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:213, tui_app.rs:853). Detail values beyond auto, low, high may be refused per model (image-detail.ts:5-28).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Provider routes may take fewer images; the strictest route bounds the inline image size (chat-attachments.ts comment on CHAT_MODEL_IMAGE_ENVELOPE). Animated images show only the first frame (model-image.ts:77-79). Provider support for original detail: unknown beyond the model registry.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local: no upload, no subscription; on-device OCR text is added to the prompt, and the sheet says the model reads text not the picture (chatExecutionStore.ts:1241-1262; AddToChatSheet.tsx:130). Desktop, web and CLI Local image handling: unknown. The CLI app-server marks the ACP entry as image false (acp.rs:401).

aliases: Read a photo of a document
features.summary: The person attaches a photo or scan of a document, a chart, a diagram or handwriting and asks for a transcript or explanation. The product treats it as an ordinary image; the model does the reading. Scanned PDFs without a text layer are turned into page images. Mobile Local gives only recognised text.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person ask a vision model to read a photographed or scanned document, explain a chart or diagram, or transcribe handwriting, using the same image attachment path as any picture. For PDFs with no text layer the web server attaches the pages as images.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires document-image, chart, diagram and handwriting reading on every app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.04 to S43.07). Rivals offer this in chat.
purpose.who_uses_it: Students, office workers and developers who hold a paper document, a whiteboard, a chart screenshot or handwritten notes.
problems_solved: Typing out a paper document by hand.
Understanding a chart or diagram without the source data.
Reading messy handwriting.
use_cases: Photograph a receipt on the phone and ask for the total.
Attach a chart screenshot on web and ask for the trend.
Attach a whiteboard photo in the Chrome side panel and ask for a summary.
Attach a scanned PDF with no text layer on web and ask a question.

Mobile: add-to-chat sheet rows 'Camera', 'Photos', 'Paste image', 'File' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:697-722).
CLI: /attach <file> and /attach --full <image>, which the help describes as for fine detail (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5484-5485).
VS Code: drag, paste or the + button 'Attach or use tools' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:3356, 7720, 7730).
Chrome extension: side panel composer paste or picker (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:14584, 14688).

Mobile Cloud needs sign-in and upload consent; Local needs the on-device model downloaded [inferred].
A readable picture; the product has no quality check.
screens_and_controls: Attach controls as listed above; image previews on web and VS Code.
CLI /attach --full to keep full resolution at a higher input cost (tui_app.rs:6256).

journey: Take or choose the photo or scan of the document, chart, diagram or handwriting.
Attach it to a chat message in the app.
Type what you want: a transcript, a trend, a structure, a translation of the handwriting.
Send and read the answer.
If the details are lost, retry with a sharper or larger picture, or on the CLI use /attach --full.

A note '[name has no text layer; its N pages are attached as images]' appears in the model context for a scanned PDF (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts:738).
A note when an animated image shows only its first frame (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/model-image.ts:77-79).
No quality warning or confidence flag is shown (brief S43.19, S43.20).

working: Web: an attached PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP goes through upload, scan, hydration and the model-image envelope exactly as in a single-image question (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:397; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/chat-attachment-hydration.ts:654-676).

Web: a PDF with no text layer has its pages attached as images with a text note (chat-attachment-hydration.ts:701-738); text-layer PDFs go as extracted text or a native file part (hydration.ts:679-700).
CLI: images are resized to 2048 by 768 bounds (long edge by short edge, swapped for portrait) unless /attach --full keeps the original (crates/agiworkforce-utils-image/src/lib.rs:19-22, 82-100).
VS Code and Chrome: images go through the same attach paths as F043-01 (ChatStateManager.ts:2207; side_panel.ts:10343).
incomplete: No code path treats documents, charts, diagrams or handwriting differently; accuracy depends on the model and the picture [inferred from no separate branch found].

Shrinking can blur small print: web caps at 8000 px and 5,000,000 base64 bytes (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/chat-attachment-policy.json:60-64) and CLI default caps at 2048 by 768 (utils-image lib.rs:19-22) [inferred effect].
Web and Desktop have no recorded live check (brief S43.04 to S43.07 Unfinished).

established.statement: The user attaches a photo or scan of a document, including a scanned PDF, and the model reads and explains it.
The user attaches a chart image and the model interprets data and trends.
The user attaches a diagram image and the model explains its structure.
The user attaches handwritten notes and the model transcribes or answers about them.
Before answering, the product warns when an input image is too small, blurry or low quality to read reliably.
Answers about images flag uncertain readings.

acceptance_criteria: A photo of printed text attached on web is transcribed by a vision model.
A chart screenshot attached on any app gets an answer that names the trend.
A PDF with no text layer attached on web is answered from its page images and the context carries the no-text-layer note.
A handwriting photo attached in the CLI with /attach --full is sent at original size.
On mobile in Local mode the prompt carries the recognised text and the app says it cannot see the picture.
A very small or blurred image produces a warning before the answer (required, currently not met).
inferred: Document and handwriting use needs the highest practical resolution; the default shrink on CLI is a risk for dense pages [inferred].
The warning for S43.19 would need image size and sharpness checks on the device before send [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Offer the full-resolution option on web, mobile and VS Code as the CLI does.
[proposed] Add a pre-send check for tiny images and show a low-quality warning.
[proposed] Ask models to mark unreadable words and surface the mark in the answer.

steps.what_happens: The person attaches the photo or scan (picker, camera, paste or drag).
Web and mobile Cloud upload the file; our server checks bytes and scans them.
For an image, the server builds a data URL image part, re-encoding only if the file exceeds the envelope. For a PDF with no text layer it renders page images and adds a note.
The model provider reads the picture and writes the transcript or explanation.

features.summary: The person attaches one or two pictures and asks how many items there are, what is different between two scenes, or what is wrong in a photo of a device or an error. No special code exists; the question and pictures go to a vision model, which answers. Local mobile mode gives only text from the picture.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person ask counting, comparing and fault-finding questions about photos or screenshots, using the same attach-and-ask path as any image.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires counting, scene comparison and visual troubleshooting on every app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.12 to S43.14). These are common reasons people use a camera with an assistant.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyday users with a phone, and developers with error screenshots.
problems_solved: Counting many similar items by eye.
Spotting the difference between two photos.
Finding what is wrong with a device or a screen without describing it.
use_cases: Photograph a shelf and ask how many boxes are on it.
Attach before and after photos and ask what changed.
Photograph a router with blinking lights and ask what is wrong.
Paste a screenshot of an error dialog in the CLI and ask for fix steps.

features.summary: On a phone, the Scan Text screen captures a picture, reads the text on the device, shows where the text was found, lets the person copy it, and sends it with the photo to a chat. Other apps have no separate text-extraction step; they ask the model to read the picture.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads the text in a camera capture or a handed-over image using the phone's own recogniser, shows it over the picture, offers 'Copy text', prefills a question and sends the image and question to a new chat.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires users to extract the text in an image and copy or reuse it (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.08). On-device recognition also feeds Local mode, where the text model cannot see pixels.
purpose.who_uses_it: Phone users who want text from signs, paper, labels or screens, including those in Local mode with no upload.
problems_solved: Retyping text from paper or a screen.
Giving a text-only on-device model something to read from a photo.
use_cases: Scan a printed letter and ask for a summary.
Copy the text from a photo of a sign.
Hand a photo over from an iOS shortcut for a scan.
In Local mode, attach a photo of a page so the on-device model reads its recognised text.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: screen route /(app)/scan, titled 'Scan Text' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/scan.tsx:457). Entry points found: the app deep-link verb 'scan' (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:304-309) and the iOS intent titled 'Scan with AGI' (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/ScanIntent.swift:5). An in-app button entry was not found in apps/mobile/app, apps/mobile/src or apps/mobile/components searches; the file the brief names (apps/mobile/src/features/shell/capabilityShortcuts.ts) does not exist: unknown.
Mobile Local chat: attaching a photo runs the same recogniser inside the chat send (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2731-2735).
Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no separate text-extraction screen found.
prerequisites: Camera permission and the canUseCamera capability for live capture (scan.tsx:43-44). A supplied image needs no camera access (apps/mobile/__tests__/SuppliedImageNeedsNoCamera.test.tsx:67).
The native recogniser module linked in the build (ocr.ts:15-28).
To send: a model selected; Cloud mode also needs sign-in and upload consent.
screens_and_controls: Camera view with scan corners, switch camera, flash toggle and capture button labelled 'Capture and scan' (scan.tsx:508).

After capture: image with text-region overlay, a badge such as '2 text blocks' or 'No text detected', a Retake button, a 'Copy text' pill (shows 'Copied' for a moment), a prompt box with placeholder 'Ask about this text…' (max 2000 characters) and a send button labelled 'Send to AI' (scan.tsx:389-417).
journey: Open Scan Text.
Allow camera access if asked.
Point at the text and tap capture.
Wait while the phone reads the text; a success haptic plays if text was read (scan.tsx:110-112).
Check the overlay. Tap 'Copy text' to copy, or Retake.
Edit the prefilled question ('Summarize this:' plus the text, or 'What does this image say?' if none).
Send. The app creates a conversation named Scan, attaches the photo and opens the chat.
feedback_and_outputs: Overlay boxes over recognised regions and a text-block count.
Error text 'Text could not be read from this image. Retake the scan or type your question.' (scan.tsx:106).
Alert 'No text to send' when the prompt is empty (scan.tsx:185-186).
Alerts 'Send failed' with 'The scan could not be sent. Check your model and try again.' or '... Check your connection and try again.' (scan.tsx:216, 224).
Copied text on the clipboard.
settings: Haptic Feedback setting changes whether success haptics play (apps/mobile/__tests__/ScanSendFailure.test.tsx:77-96).
The model selected for new chats decides where the question goes (ScanSendFailure.test.tsx:120).

working: The scan screen calls the on-device recogniser, shows regions and text, offers copy, retake and send (apps/mobile/app/(app)/scan.tsx:83-112, 171-228, 389-417).

The recogniser bridge calls native module AGIVisionOCR: Apple Vision on iOS and a bundled Latin-script recogniser on Android, described in source as making no network calls (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIVisionOCR.swift:6-7; apps/mobile/native/android/AGIVisionOCR.kt:12; apps/mobile/src/features/image/services/ocr.ts:15-31).

Local-mode chat appends recognised text for each locally attached image and caches up to 64 results (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:1225-1262, 2731-2735); earlier-turn images are re-read the same way (chatExecutionStore.ts:2696).
The send step reuses the normal send path with the image attached as a JPEG named scan_<time>.jpg (scan.tsx:197-210).
incomplete: Sending is not on-device only: in Cloud mode the photo is uploaded, and the prefilled text is sent as the question (scan.tsx:209-215; chatExecutionStore.ts:2484-2500).
An in-app entry to the scan screen was not found; reach is through intents and links (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:304-309).
The brief marks Web and Desktop partial; no separate OCR step exists there (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md S43.08).
disconnected_or_disabled: If the native module is not linked the screen shows the 'could not be read' text and the thrown error is 'AGIVisionOCR native module not linked, rebuild the iOS app' or the Android variant (ocr.ts:21-26).
not_available: No OCR or copy-text control exists in the web, desktop, CLI, VS Code or Chrome chat code found.

The web server OCR module apps/web/lib/server/tools/scanned-page-reader.ts and apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts serve scanned documents and project knowledge files, not a chat 'copy text' control (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts imports it).

steps.what_happens: The person captures a photo or a supplied image URI arrives from an intent.
The app calls the native recogniser with the image URI and gets text and regions back.
The screen shows overlay and text, prefills a question, and copies text on request.
On Send the app creates a conversation called Scan and calls the normal send with the image attached.
In Cloud mode the image is uploaded after consent and the question goes to the Cloud model; in Local mode the text is added to the prompt for the on-device model.

features.summary: A developer sends an image part and a prompt to the OpenAI-style chat endpoint and asks for JSON. The server passes the image through and can check the reply against a JSON schema. There is no screen and no dedicated extraction step; CSV or rows come only from the model's text.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets an API caller turn a picture such as a receipt or form into structured fields by combining an image part with a JSON-object or JSON-schema response format. The server validates a schema reply.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists image-to-structured-data extraction as done for the API only (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.15). Developers need data, not prose.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers calling the public chat completions endpoint.
problems_solved: Manual data entry from receipts, forms and cards.
Getting a machine-readable reply from a vision model.
use_cases: POST a receipt image with response_format json_schema to get fields.
Ask for rows of a table in a photo and parse them.
Extract fields from a business card image.

where_to_find_it: API only: the chat completions endpoint under apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions, documented in apps/web/public/openapi.json (message content parts text, image_url, file; response_format text, json_object, json_schema).
prerequisites: An API credential for the endpoint (auth details are in SYS-authentication-and-identity; not read here).
A model that reads images and, for json_schema, supports structured output (request-processor.ts:5099, 5168-5175).
stream set to false for json_object and json_schema (request-processor.ts:867-876).
screens_and_controls: No screen. Request fields: messages[].content[] with type image_url and image_url.url (https URL or data URL) with optional detail auto, low, high or original; response_format with type and json_schema (request-processor.ts:601-616, 682-705).
journey: Build a request with a text part describing the fields and an image_url part.
Add response_format json_schema with the fields, and stream false.
Send to the endpoint.
Read the choices[0].message content as JSON.
If the reply fails the schema the call returns an error instead of text (response-builder.ts:325-340).
feedback_and_outputs: JSON text content in the reply.

Errors: 'image_url blocked by egress policy', 'invalid image_url', model_no_vision, image_detail_unsupported, too_many_images, model_no_structured_output (request-processor.ts:611-612, 5099-5147, 5168-5175).
The documented error for a streamed structured request (request-processor.ts:875).
settings: response_format type text, json_object or json_schema.
detail on each image part: auto, low, high, original (image-detail.ts:5).

working: The request schema accepts image_url parts with a url checked against the egress policy and a detail value from auto, low, high, original (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:601-616; image-detail.ts:5).
The server refuses an unsupported detail value for the model (image-detail.ts:18-28; request-processor.ts:5115-5128).

json_object mode adds a directive; json_schema mode needs a model that supports structured output, adds a schema directive and, after generation, settles the reply against the schema (request-processor.ts:5166-5190; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/json-schema-mode.ts:869; response-builder.ts:323-340).
The OpenAPI document describes image parts and response formats (apps/web/public/openapi.json:609, 726).
incomplete: Output as CSV or table rows is not validated; only JSON schema replies are settled. No CSV mode was found.
Whether an invalid reply is retried before failing was not read: unknown (json-schema-mode.ts not opened beyond the export).
not_available: No app screen for image extraction. S43.16 (image-to-table workflow) is not applicable on any app per the brief (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md S43.16).

established.statement: The user turns an image (receipt, form, card) into structured fields (JSON, CSV or rows) that can be reused.
The structured reply must be honest about what the route supports; web structured output is refused on models without it.
Provider capabilities are not intrinsic model abilities.

acceptance_criteria: A request with an image_url part and json_schema returns JSON that matches the schema.
A request with json_schema and stream true is refused with a message naming stream false.
A model without structured output is refused with code model_no_structured_output.
An image URL that points at an internal host is refused by the egress policy.
A detail value the model does not list is refused with image_detail_unsupported.
A reply that does not fit the schema returns an error, not partial text.
inferred: Reusing the data means the schema reply is the product's contract; CSV is a caller conversion [inferred].
Receipt and form accuracy depends on the model and image quality, as in F043-02 [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Provide a documented example in the OpenAPI document for image extraction.
[proposed] Add an extraction preset in the apps once the API behaviour has a live run.

steps.what_happens: The caller sends a chat completions request with an image_url part and a response_format.
The server validates the image URL against the egress policy and the detail value.
The server checks the model reads images, the image count, and structured output support, then adds the JSON directive.
The model provider reads the image and writes JSON.
For json_schema the server settles the reply against the schema and returns it or an error.

Returned to the caller; usage accounting per SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model must have vision and, for json_schema, the json capability in registry metadata (request-processor.ts:5099, 5168). The wire shape to each provider is translated by provider-protocol and provider packages (doc: brief S43.18 lists those files).

access_and_usage.subscription: Plan, quota and credit rules for API calls apply through SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage; an image-specific entitlement for reading images: none found in the code read. The quota label 'image' at request-processor.ts:5621 is for image generation, not reading.

Image input token estimate exists for the free trial (apps/web/lib/services/free-trial-service.ts:197-209); paid metering for image tokens: not established.

features.summary: A person picks an image already in their Library, an earlier output or an upload and uses it as input: ask about it in a new chat, or use it as the starting point for an image edit, variation or masked edit. Built on web, desktop and mobile; missing on the CLI and Chrome.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves an existing image into a new task without downloading and re-uploading it: from the Library into a new chat with the file attached, into the composer in image mode for a remix, or from the mobile add-to-chat sheet into a chat or an image edit.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires that users pick an existing image (upload, library item or earlier output) as the reference input for a generation or edit (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/043-image-and-visual-understanding.md, S43.17). Without it an image from an earlier session was a dead end (apps/web/features/library/lib/library-chat-handoff.ts:70-74).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, desktop and mobile Cloud users who made or saved images and want to reuse them.
problems_solved: Re-uploading a file already stored in the account.
Starting an edit or variation from an older image.
Asking a question about a saved file.
use_cases: From the Library, ask 'What is in this picture?' about a saved image.
Remix an earlier generated image with its original prompt.
On the phone, pick a Library image in the add-to-chat sheet and edit it.
On web, attach an image in image mode and choose Edit, Variation or Mask edit.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): Library page. The detail view has a box with the placeholder and label 'Ask about this file' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1346-1348), actions 'Add to chat' (LibraryView.tsx:685) and 'Remix' (LibraryView.tsx:701). Wiring in apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:207-232.
Web composer image mode: operations 'Edit', 'Variation' and 'Mask edit' for an attached image (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:277-285).

Mobile: add-to-chat sheet lists recent Library images and files in Cloud mode (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:399, 368-389) with rows 'Create image' and others (AddToChatSheet.tsx:927).
CLI and Chrome: none (brief S43.17 missing).
prerequisites: Signed in, Cloud mode, and for generation or editing the plan capability canUseImages and a usable edit-capable image model (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1056-1067, 1370-1374; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:249-258).
An adult-eligible account for the image generation route (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:32-39).
screens_and_controls: Library detail with question box, 'Add to chat', 'Remix', 'Download to view' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1321, 1346, 685, 701).

Composer image operation menu with hints: 'Change the attached image with your prompt', 'A new take on the attached image', 'Redraw only where the second image is masked' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:283-285).
Mobile sheet with Library pick rows and thumbnails.

Type a question and send ('Ask about this file') or choose 'Add to chat' or 'Remix'.
The app stages the file and opens a new chat; the file is attached and any draft is placed in the composer.
For Remix the composer opens in image mode with the saved prompt and model.
Choose Edit, Variation or Mask edit if needed, then send.
Read the answer or see the new image.

'This file is too large to add from the Library. Download it, then add it from your device.' for an over-limit file (apps/web/features/library/lib/library-chat-handoff.ts:20-21).

Operation: Edit, Variation, Mask edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1255).

established.statement: The user picks an existing image (upload, library item or earlier output) as the reference input for a generation or edit.
One chat: users add files, references and images to a normal chat.
Local, own-key and Cloud stay separate; a Local file is not silently moved to Cloud.

acceptance_criteria: From the Library, 'Ask about this file' opens a new chat with that image attached and the question in the composer.
'Remix' on a saved image opens the composer in image mode with the image attached and its prompt.

In the web composer, an attached image in image mode offers Edit, Variation and, with a second image, Mask edit.
On mobile Cloud, picking a Library image attaches it without a second upload.
On mobile Local, the sheet lists no image files and says on-device models read text, not pictures.
inferred: The CLI and Chrome should offer a way to use a Library image if parity is required [inferred from brief status missing].
Because Library items are Cloud data, using one in Local mode would cross a boundary and must stay blocked [inferred from AGENTS.md section 6].
proposed: [proposed] Add a Library picker command to the CLI that stages a Library image through the existing /attach path.
[proposed] Add a Library entry to the Chrome side panel attach menu.

steps.what_happens: The person picks a Library image and asks, adds to chat or remixes.
The web app downloads the stored bytes from the Library and turns them into a File; an over-limit file is refused with the Library message.
The File is parked in memory, the composer mode and draft are set, and the app navigates to a new chat which takes the staged file.

The edit or generation runs on a managed image model and the result returns.
