features.summary: Lets the model's image reading level be chosen: auto, low, high or original. Developers set it per image on the Cloud chat API, and the web server refuses a value the chosen model does not accept. In the CLI a person can attach an image at full size. Web, desktop, mobile and Chrome show no detail choice.

purpose.what_it_does: Carries an image detail value (auto, low, high, original) from the request to the model provider, and refuses a value the model does not accept before the call (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/image-detail.ts:5-41; request-processor.ts:5115-5124). Separately, the CLI can attach an image without scaling it down (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5485, 6251-6258).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S43.18 says images should be processed at a resolution suited to the task, with a high-detail versus reduced-detail choice honoured end to end. A higher level reads fine print better but costs more input; a lower level is cheaper and faster (the CLI message says full-size attach 'costs more input', tui_app.rs:6254-6256).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers calling AGI Cloud's OpenAI-style chat API (api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions) and CLI users attaching images. Not exposed to ordinary people in the Web, Desktop, Mobile or Chrome apps (no control found; see gaps).
problems_solved: A request that asks for a detail level the model cannot honour fails fast with a clear message listing accepted values, instead of a provider error (image-detail.ts:37-41).
Small text, dense charts and screenshots lose legibility when scaled down; the CLI 'full' attach keeps the original pixels (crates/agiworkforce-utils-image/src/lib.rs:103).
Developers can discover which detail values a model accepts from the models list (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/models/route.ts:101-117).
use_cases: A developer sends a chart image with detail 'high' to a vision model through the chat API.
A developer sends detail 'original' to a model whose registry entry lists it, for a dense screenshot.
A developer sends 'original' to a model that does not list it and receives a 400 with code image_detail_unsupported.
A CLI user types '/attach --full photo.png' to send an uncompressed photo of a circuit board.

where_to_find_it: API (Cloud): optional detail field on each image_url content part of the chat request (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:616; apps/web/public/openapi.json:609).
API: GET models list returns image_detail per model (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/models/route.ts:59,117; openapi.json:493-499).
CLI (terminal chat): slash command '/attach --full <image>' and plain '/attach <image>' (tui_app.rs:5485, 6251). The help line reads 'Attach it without scaling it down, for fine detail'.
Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome: no detail control found in the code read. Brief status: web, desktop, mobile, chrome missing; vscode n/a.
prerequisites: API: a Cloud API credential and a vision-capable model; a model that cannot read images gets 400 model_no_vision first (request-processor.ts:5100-5112).
CLI: a vision-capable selected model, otherwise attach is refused with 'does not accept images; switch to a vision model with /model first' (tui_app.rs:852-859).
The image file must be inside the workspace and a supported image type (tui_app.rs:842-851).
screens_and_controls: API: no screen; the detail enum is auto, low, high, original (request-processor.ts:616; image-detail.ts:5).
CLI: the composer shows a chip labelled with the path and size; a full-size attach adds ', full resolution' to the chip (tui_app.rs:871-874).
journey: API: build a message whose content is an array with a text part and an image_url part.
API: optionally set image_url.detail to auto, low, high or original.
API: send the request; the server checks image support, then the detail value, then the image count (request-processor.ts:5100-5135).
API: read the answer, or a 400 error naming the accepted values.
CLI: type '/attach --full <path>' (or '/attach <path>' for the scaled default).
CLI: see the confirmation 'Attached <chip>. It is sent without being scaled down, so it costs more input; /attach remove drops it.' (tui_app.rs:6254-6256).
CLI: type the question and send; '/attach remove' drops the staged image.
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal text: 'The selected model does not accept image detail "<value>". Use "a", "b" or "c".' with HTTP 400 and error code image_detail_unsupported (image-detail.ts:37-41; request-processor.ts:5120-5125).
CLI confirmation message and chip described above.
Models list shows image_detail only for models the registry records (models/route.ts:117).
settings: No user setting stores a detail preference in the code read [inferred from absence].
Per-model accepted values come from the generated model catalog field imageInput.detailValues (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:750-755; packages/contracts/types/src/models.json:1038).

working: Cloud API accepts detail per image part and validates the enum auto|low|high|original (request-processor.ts:616).
Refusal before the provider call for a value outside the model's accepted list; auto is always accepted; a model without a registry record accepts auto, low, high (image-detail.ts:10,25-31).

Detail is carried to providers: wire content is turned into an image block with detail when it is one of the four values (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/openai-wire-compat.ts:112-135) and OpenAI chat and responses translations write it back out (packages/ai/providers/openai/src/translate.ts:51-57; translate-responses.ts:54-60).
Models list publishes accepted values as image_detail (models/route.ts:101-117).

CLI full-size attach: Original mode skips the downscale (crates/agiworkforce-utils-image/src/lib.rs:103); default mode shrinks beyond 2048 by 768 bounds (lib.rs:20-22,34). Staging code at tui_app.rs:832-877; loader at apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8383-8395.

Protocol type ImageDetail (auto, low, high, original) with default High exists in the shared Rust protocol (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/models.rs:796-803) and is parsed from metadata (models.rs:1690-1696).

Chrome extension sets detail internally: 'high' for computer-use screenshots and 'auto' for cloud bridge attachments (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/agentLoop.ts:214; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:569).
incomplete: CLI: the image block carries only mime type and base64 data, with no detail field (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8364-8368). So the CLI 'full' choice changes pixels sent, not a detail value; whether the CLI provider layer adds a detail value is unknown.

Tauri desktop vision command accepts only low, high, auto and rejects 'original' (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/vision.rs:335-342), while the managed cloud provider maps its detail enum to low, high, auto only (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/llm/providers/managed_cloud_provider.rs:366-372). Desktop chat attachments are hard set to Auto (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/chat/attachments.rs:465). The Tauri build is retained internal code (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Web chat attachments hydrated on the server get no detail on the image part (chat-attachment-hydration.ts:671-676,704-705), so the provider default applies.
The Chrome extension cloud-bridge reader rejects any detail other than auto, low, high (freeTrialClient.ts:645).
disconnected_or_disabled: No provider code under packages/ai/providers/anthropic or google referenced a detail field in my search; whether those providers honour or drop the value is unknown.
not_available: No detail picker for people in Web, Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5), Mobile or Chrome (brief S43.18 status missing).
VS Code: not applicable per the brief.
No upload-time automatic choice of detail based on task [inferred from absence].

established.statement: Images are processed at a resolution suited to the task, with a high-detail versus reduced-detail choice honoured end to end.
A detail value a model does not accept is refused before the call, naming the accepted values; auto is always accepted.
Do not hardcode what the repository already models (model capabilities); accepted detail values come from the generated catalog.
Documentation of a model capability is kept separate from route availability; image capabilities depend on provider route or AGI harness.

acceptance_criteria: A chat API request with image detail 'original' on a model whose catalog lists it is accepted and the value reaches the provider request.
The same request on a model that does not list 'original' returns HTTP 400 with code image_detail_unsupported and a message listing the accepted values.
A request with detail 'auto' is never refused for detail.
A model with no catalog record accepts auto, low and high and refuses original.
GET models returns image_detail for models with a catalog record.
CLI '/attach --full <image>' on an image larger than the scaled bounds keeps the original width and height; '/attach <image>' scales it down.
CLI attach of an image while a non-vision model is selected is refused with a message naming /model.
inferred: Each app that lets a person attach an image should offer the same detail choice or a documented automatic choice [inferred from the parity requirement S43.18 listing web, desktop, mobile, chrome as missing].
The refusal for an unaccepted value should also apply on routes other than the Cloud chat API, such as own-key calls [inferred; not found in code read].
proposed: [proposed] Add a per-image or per-chat quality choice labelled in plain words in web chat, mobile and the extension, defaulting to Auto.
[proposed] Make the CLI send an explicit detail value when staging a full-size image.
[proposed] Let the desktop vision command and managed cloud provider accept 'original' where the model lists it.

steps.what_happens: A developer's request arrives with image parts; the schema accepts detail auto, low, high or original.
The server refuses a turn with images if the model cannot read images (model_no_vision).
The server looks up the model's accepted detail values in the catalog and refuses any other value except auto.
The server then checks the number of images against the model or harness limit.
Wire content is converted to provider-neutral image blocks, keeping a valid detail value.
The provider adapter writes detail into the provider request and the provider reads the image at that level.
CLI: the image is read from disk, optionally left unscaled, base64 encoded and queued for the next turn.
CLI: the queued block (mime and data only) is sent with the next message to the chosen provider.

aliases: Point at part of an image
features.summary: Planned abilities to point at part of an image, zoom or crop it, get an image back with boxes or arrows, or turn a pictured table into a spreadsheet. None are built in any app. The only related thing is the phone Scan screen drawing text boxes over a photo for display.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person limit a question to a region of an image, inspect detail by cropping or zooming, receive an answer drawn on the image, and convert a table in a picture into an editable table. Today none of this exists as a feature; only the mobile Scan screen overlays text-recognition boxes on a photo for display (apps/mobile/app/(app)/scan.tsx:346-371, 534).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S43.09 and S43.11 say a person should be able to select a region so a question applies to that area, and an answer should return the image with marks. S43.10 and S43.16 are marked not applicable on every app in the brief.
purpose.who_uses_it: Would be people asking about pictures: shoppers, students, field workers. Nobody uses it today.
problems_solved: Would let a person ask about one object in a crowded picture without describing where it is.
Would show which part of an image an answer refers to.
Would remove retyping a table seen in a picture [inferred from S43.16].
use_cases: Circle a part number on a photo of a machine and ask what it means (not built).
Receive a screenshot back with a box around the setting to change (not built).
Zoom into a small chart legend before asking (not built).
Turn a photographed price table into a sheet (not built).

features.summary: Image mode lets a signed-in person on a plan that includes image generation type a description in Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile or the CLI, choose an image model, and get a picture back. It runs only on AGI Cloud. The Chrome extension composer and VS Code have no image mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a text prompt into one or more generated images, shown in the conversation (Web, Desktop, Mobile) or saved to a file (CLI). The person also picks which image model draws it, from models this deployment can actually run. The server stores the image in the account Library and labels it as AI-generated. (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:26-113; apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:883-970)
purpose.why_it_exists: AGI Workforce competes with Claude and ChatGPT, and an image maker inside the chat is part of that product (doc: docs/product/definition.md:44). One server route does the work for every app so that plan checks, safety checks, billing and storage are the same everywhere (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:150-153).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on an eligible paid plan (Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium, Enterprise) (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:351-356). Eligible Free accounts may get a limited free image offer instead (doc: docs/product/definition.md:342-349).
problems_solved: Making a picture without leaving the chat or opening another tool.
Choosing a cheaper or better image model without a developer setting.
A slow image provider does not lose the work: each request becomes a durable job that can be polled, cancelled or retried (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:804-881).
Refused prompts and failed images are not charged (apps/web/__tests__/api/media-image-generate.test.ts:1048,2014).
use_cases: On Web, click Create image in the composer plus menu, type 'a red bicycle on a beach', press send, and see the image in the chat.
On Mobile, open Add to chat, pick Create image, choose an image model, send, and wait while the app polls the job.
In a terminal, run: agi image "a red bicycle" --model <id> and get a file in the current folder.
Pick a different image model after a failure and send the same prompt again.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (the Electron window shows the hosted web app): composer plus menu row 'Create image' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:160,820), shown only when the host owns an image callback (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.test.tsx:2860-2870). After it is chosen an 'Image' pill appears (aria-label 'Exit image generation mode') and a model button (aria-label 'Select image model') (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6254-6266,6763).

Mobile: Add to chat sheet row 'Create image' with hint 'Switches this chat to image generation', then an 'Image model' list (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:927-930,962-978). The Images screen also has a 'Create image' control (apps/mobile/src/features/image/ImagesScreen.tsx:488). A typed '/image <prompt>' also starts it (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:235,250). A default image model can be set in Settings > media (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/media/index.tsx:182).
CLI: command 'agi image "<prompt>"' with --model/-m, --out, --list-models (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1110-1172). A TUI slash form exists (apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:1369-1380 run_slash).
Chrome extension: not available. VS Code extension: not applicable (brief).
prerequisites: Signed in to an AGI account; Web/Desktop passes an adult-eligibility gate first (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:42-49); Mobile needs a Clerk sign-in (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:255).
A plan that includes image generation, or a limited free media offer (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:195-212; doc: docs/product/definition.md:342-349).

Cloud mode. Mobile Local mode is refused with 'Image generation uses AGI Cloud' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:114-117,252); CLI refuses Local and own-key sessions (apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:833-835).
Online connection (Mobile: 'Network connection required' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:137-140,256)).
At least one image model the deployment can run; otherwise 'This deployment is not ready for image generation.' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2605-2613).
screens_and_controls: Web composer in image mode: placeholder 'Describe the image you want' (or 'Describe or edit an image' when the model can edit) (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5883-5887), model menu titled 'Image model' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6772-6776), send button.

Web generating card: role=status, 'Generating image', 'Generating with <model name>', 'Waiting for the image provider · <time> elapsed' (apps/web/features/chat/components/ImageGenerationCard.tsx:221-235).
Mobile: 'Create image' row, 'Image model' list, then the chat bubble shows progress (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:927,962-978).
CLI: prints the saved file path(s) and a one-line summary 'AI-generated with <model> (<provider>): ...' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3520-3529; apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:236-246).
journey: 1. Open a chat (Web/Desktop/Mobile) or a terminal (CLI).
2. Turn on image mode: Web plus menu 'Create image'; Mobile Add to chat 'Create image'; or type /image on Mobile.
3. Optionally open the model menu and pick an image model. Web shows paid admitted models plus any free promotional model (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1322-1335).
4. Type the prompt (up to 4000 characters) (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:90).
5. Press send. Web clears the composer and calls onGenerateImage (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3762-3770).

6. The client posts /api/media/image/generate with an Idempotency-Key. Web waits on the open connection; Mobile sends async:true and polls status every 2 seconds up to 170 seconds (apps/web/lib/hooks/useMediaGeneration.ts:500-517; apps/mobile/src/features/image/services/imagegen.ts:33-34,59-62,82-95).
7. The image appears in the chat (Web, Mobile) or in a file (CLI), and is also saved in the Library.

established.statement: User enters an image mode, types a prompt, and gets a generated image back in the conversation.
User picks which image model generates the image, from models the deployment can run.
A paid-plan image feature is governed by the single AGI Subscription system; image generation is a plan capability.
Unknown availability preserves the draft and asks for retry, not Upgrade.
Advertised media models and options must produce real decodable media, and retry reuses the original idempotency identity.

acceptance_criteria: On Web with an eligible plan, Create image then a prompt returns an image card that shows 'Generating with <model name>' while waiting.
A request from a Free account with no free offer returns 403 plan_upgrade_required; an account with no subscription returns 403 subscription_required.
A model id that is not an image model returns 400 model_unavailable, and a provider/model mismatch returns 400 provider_model_mismatch.
A prompt the safety floor refuses returns 422 content_policy_violation and nothing is charged.
On Mobile in Local mode, sending in image mode shows 'Image generation uses AGI Cloud' and sends nothing.
On Mobile, a request with async:true returns 202 with a job id and the app polls until the image arrives or 170 seconds pass.
In the CLI, agi image with a prompt writes a file and prints its path; in a Local session it refuses before any prompt leaves the machine.
The image is saved in the Library and is labelled as AI-generated.
inferred: Every app that offers image mode should list the same image models for the same account, because they all read the catalog [inferred from apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts:27-46 and apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/mediaMode.ts:31-46].
Showing only the first of several images on Web and Mobile is not an intended limit [inferred: the request accepts n up to 4 (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:98)].
proposed: [proposed] Make Web, Desktop and Mobile render every image of a multi-image result, or send n=1 explicitly so the contract and the UI agree.
[proposed] Give the Tauri media_generate_image command an Idempotency-Key, or remove the dead path.
[proposed] Decide and record whether a local on-device image model should exist, given the requirement that local inference is free of subscriptions.

steps.what_happens: The person turns on image mode, picks a model and types a prompt. The client checks plan, capability, model availability and attachments before sending.
The client posts to /api/media/image/generate with a body that follows the shared schema and an Idempotency-Key naming the app surface.
The route checks CSRF, rate limit (10 per minute, fails closed), sign-in, adult eligibility, managed-compute gate, organization policy and the workspace spend cap.
The server resolves the entitlement bundle, requires a subscription, checks subscription access, plan capability image_generation and the canUseImages flag.
The body is validated; the prompt goes through the always-on safety floor (a refusal is a 422 before any charge or provider call).
The server picks the catalog model and provider (google or openai), applies the workspace model policy and the training opt-out rule, checks image count, aspect ratio and storage.
It reserves usage cost, creates a durable job row, and schedules a background drive. With async:true it returns 202 and runs the attempt after the response; otherwise it runs the attempt and waits.
The attempt calls the outside image provider, moderates the output, saves it to media storage and the Library with provenance, then settles the reservation (failure releases it).
The client shows the image from the /api/files/<id> URL. Mobile polls /api/media/image/status; the CLI downloads bytes and writes files with embedded provenance.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model list comes from the generated catalog entries with image generation (apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts:27-46). Only provider google and provider openai are executable; each catalog entry names an image API (gemini, imagen or openai) that decides ratios, count and edit support (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-generation-provider.ts:203-229,329-342). Server-held provider keys are used; no user key is used (image-generation-provider.ts:387-421).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in AGI account required on every app; Web and Desktop add an adult-eligibility gate (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:42-49).
access_and_usage.permissions: Organization policy, workspace model policy and workspace spend cap can refuse the request (route.ts:70-99; managed-image-generation.ts:395-401). A training opt-out can refuse models that may train on inputs (managed-image-generation.ts:419-439).
access_and_usage.subscription: Needs an active subscription and a plan with capability image_generation: Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium, Enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:351-356). No subscription gives 403 subscription_required; Free or Basic gives 403 plan_upgrade_required (managed-image-generation.ts:159-170,196-211; apps/web/__tests__/api/media-image-generate.test.ts:756,786). Eligible Free accounts may use a limited free offer of up to 10 images per UTC day (doc: docs/product/definition.md:342-347).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit 10 per minute per user, fail closed (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:384-388). Cost is estimated and reserved before the job and settled after (managed-image-generation.ts:703-756). Monthly image quota is null on every plan (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1292,1338,1389). Prompt max 4000 characters; a job has 3 attempts (apps/web/lib/server/image-generation-jobs.ts:84).
access_and_usage.flags: Server capability canUseImages (route.ts:100-111). Mobile FEATURES.imageGen (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:26), per-account features.imageGen, and granted capability canUseImages (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:331-336).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: A model must be an image model with image generation and a named image API, live and not deprecated (apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts:27-46). The Gemini-API entry needs a catalog output MIME type or the server returns 503 image_model_contract_unavailable (managed-image-generation.ts:463-481).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Only google and openai can run; stability is refused (image-generation-provider.ts:402-421; managed-image-generation.ts:791-802). If neither server key is set the route returns 500 no_providers (managed-image-generation.ts:374-387).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not available. Mobile blocks with requires_cloud (resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:252); CLI refuses Local and own-key sessions before any prompt leaves the machine (apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:833-835); the Tauri command fails closed without a managed-cloud boundary (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/media.rs:110-115). No on-device image model was found.

features.summary: Settings that shape an image before it is made: a style preset (Web only, added to the prompt text), aspect ratio (Web, Mobile, CLI), transparent background (Web, Mobile, CLI, only on editing-capable models), and size, quality and count (CLI only). Chrome has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person choose the shape and look of the output. Style presets append a phrase to the prompt. Aspect ratio, transparency, size, quality and count are sent as fields of the shared image request. (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6344-6350; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:92-109)
purpose.why_it_exists: Different uses need different shapes (a phone wallpaper, a logo on a clear background). The server validates the choices against what the chosen model can do, so each app only offers what works. (apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts:63-92; apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:483-504)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using image mode on a plan with image generation; CLI users get the widest set of options.
problems_solved: Getting a portrait or widescreen image instead of a square.
Getting a logo or sticker without a background.
Getting a consistent look without writing the style words each time.
Scripting several images at set quality from the terminal.
use_cases: On Web, open Style and pick 'Watercolor' to add 'soft watercolor painting on textured paper' to the prompt.
On Mobile, pick 'Aspect ratio' 9:16 in Add to chat, then send a prompt for a phone wallpaper.
In the CLI, run agi image "logo" --aspect 1:1 --transparent -n 2 --quality hd.
On Web with an editing-capable model, press 'Transparent' to return a clear background.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop, image mode only: 'Style' button (aria-label 'Add a style to the prompt', menu 'Image style') (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6324-6360); aspect button (aria-label 'Select aspect ratio', menu 'Image aspect ratio'), hidden when the selected model is a free promotional model (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6271-6320); 'Transparent' toggle (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6439-6453).

established.statement: User picks a style preset (photo, illustration, etc.) that changes the generated look.
User picks the aspect ratio from ratios the model supports.
User picks the output size or resolution.
User picks a quality level (standard or HD).
User picks how many images to generate and sees all of them.

acceptance_criteria: On Web in image mode, choosing a style preset appends its phrase to the message text and does not add a separate field.

features.summary: In image mode on Web, Desktop and Mobile, the first attached picture is the one edited and up to three more guide it. Web also offers Variation and Mask edit. Only models on the openai image API can edit. The CLI and Chrome extension cannot.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person attach a picture and describe a change, so the source pixels are edited, or attach extra pictures that guide a new image. The server accepts a source image, an optional mask and up to 3 reference images. (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:86,101-108)
purpose.why_it_exists: Many tasks start from an existing picture: remove a background, change a color, make another take. The same managed route serves edits so safety and billing rules are the same as for new images. (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:527-699)
purpose.who_uses_it: Eligible-plan users on Web, Desktop (hosted web app) and Mobile.
problems_solved: Changing part of a picture without starting over.
Keeping a subject consistent by showing guide pictures.
Blocking unsafe uploads before any provider sees them (managed-image-generation.ts:591-651).
use_cases: Attach a photo, type 'make the sky orange', send.
Attach a photo, choose 'Variation' for a new take.
Attach a photo, choose 'Select an area', paint over a region, and describe the change.
On Mobile, attach one photo to edit and two more as style guides.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: attach a picture in image mode (the composer attachments); the pill 'What to do with the attached image' (menu 'Attached image action') lists Edit, Variation, Mask edit and 'Select an area' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6364-6430; operations defined at 282-286). On a finished image card, the 'Revise this image' panel has a change box, 'Variation' and a mask control (apps/web/features/chat/components/ImageGenerationCard.tsx:603,738-752).

Mobile: Add to chat sheet; with Create image active the hint reads 'Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.' or 'This model uses text only. Pick an editing model to edit a photo.' (AddToChatSheet.tsx:983-994).
CLI and Chrome: not available.
prerequisites: Image mode and an image model that supports edits: the catalog image API must be openai (managed-media.ts:69-75); Web reads supports_edit from the availability endpoint (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1370-1372).
Attachments must be images; image mode takes images only (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2256).
Each image under about 9 MB (12,000,000 base64 characters) (managed-media.ts:77-79; mobile alert at resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:151-154).
screens_and_controls: Attachment preview with numbered thumbnails when the operation is Edit and more than one image is attached (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5786-5789).

Operation menu: 'Edit' (Change the attached image with your prompt), 'Variation' (A new take on the attached image), 'Mask edit' (Redraw only where the second image is masked) (ChatComposerNew.tsx:282-286).
'Select an area' opens ImageMaskDialog to paint a mask (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6411-6435).
Card panel 'Revise this image' with an edit box, Variation, aspect and Download.
journey: 1. Enter image mode and pick a model that can edit (otherwise the composer says 'This image model cannot edit an attached picture. Choose a model that supports editing, or remove the attachment.') (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3756-3760).
2. Attach the picture to edit. Optionally attach up to 3 more as guides (Edit) or choose 'Select an area' to paint a mask (Mask edit).
3. Type the change and send. The files are read after the composer clears; guides are shrunk to 1024 pixels on the long side (imageGenerationOptions.ts:217-243).
4. The request goes out with operation edit, inpaint or variation, source_image, optional mask_image and reference_images as base64 (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3790-3810).
5. The new image appears as a new version in the chat. On a card, the same can be done from 'Revise this image'.

established.statement: User attaches one or more reference images in dedicated slots that guide the generation.
User edits a generated or uploaded image by describing the change, and the source pixels are edited.
The schema allows up to 3 reference images and 4 output images; edits need a model whose image API supports them.
If a provider does not support vision or image input, the app must not accept image input for that route.

acceptance_criteria: On Web with an edit-capable model, attaching one image and sending sends operation edit with source_image and returns a changed image.
With a text-only model selected, attaching an image and sending shows the notice and sends nothing.
Attaching more than 4 images shows 'Attach up to 4 images...' and sends nothing.
POSTing reference_images with operation generate is rejected 400 by the schema.
POSTing an edit with a source that matches the hash denylist returns 422 content_policy_violation before any usage is reserved.
A malformed or polyglot image returns 422 invalid_source_image.
A mask whose size does not fit the source returns 422 invalid_mask_image.
On Mobile, attaching a non-image file to an image request shows 'Attach only images to edit'.
inferred: Edit support must come from catalog evidence, not a vendor name [inferred from managed-media.ts:56-75 comment and tests managed-media.image-edit.test.ts:83-94].
The brief's 'reference slots' are the second to fourth attachments; there is no separate slot UI on Web [inferred from ChatComposerNew.tsx:3777-3781].
proposed: [proposed] Add the same edit path to the CLI (--source, --mask, --reference) since the route already supports it.
[proposed] Persist edit retry inputs on the server or device so retries survive beyond 3 items.

steps.what_happens: The device checks that the model can edit, that attachments are images, within size and count limits.
The device reads the files as base64 (guides shrunk to 1024 pixels on Web) and sends them in the generate request.
The server validates the schema, runs the prompt safety floor, then resolves the images, hashes them against a denylist, checks structure and mask, all before reserving usage.
It refuses a model that cannot edit, then reserves usage and creates a job with only the hashes (and asset ids when the source is stored).
The attempt sends the images to the provider's edit endpoint, moderates the result and saves it.
The client shows the new image as the result of the turn; failures keep the typed change and mask on Web.

data.retained_or_deleted: The job can be re-driven only with the same bytes or stored asset ids (image-job-executor.ts:285-296)

features.summary: While an image is being made, the person sees a waiting state, can stop the request, and can try a failed request again. Each request is a saved job on our servers with up to three attempts. A Library list called Generations shows queued and running jobs. Partial preview images are not offered.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows that an image is in progress, lets the person stop it, and lets the person retry a failed or stopped image. Behind the screen, every Cloud image request becomes a durable job row with a reservation of the person's usage. The job survives a closed tab or a dead request. The product contract says cancellation, provider failure, storage failure and late callbacks must settle the transcript and usage consistently, and that refresh resumes the existing job instead of submitting another. established.statement: User stops an image generation in progress and the job is cancelled (not billed further).
After a failed or stopped generation the user retries it in place with the same prompt.
While generating, partial or preview images appear before the final one where the model supports it.
Cancellation, provider failure, storage failure and late callbacks settle the transcript and usage consistently; retry uses the original idempotency identity; refresh resumes the existing job.

acceptance_criteria: Pressing stop on Web before the provider call starts ends the turn with 'You stopped this image.' and the job closes as canceled with the reservation released.
Pressing stop while a provider call is in flight leaves no unexplained charge: either the job is canceled and released, or the person is told it will still finish (Mobile and CLI do say so).
After a retryable failure, 'Try again' (or --retry) reuses the same job and does not create a second reservation; after 3 attempts the server answers 409 image_job_not_retryable.
Closing the browser mid-generation still ends with the job completed, failed or canceled within the lease, with no stuck 'processing' row.
Library Generations shows a queued/running job within 5 seconds and offers Cancel; a failed generate job offers Try again.
A different account cannot cancel, retry or poll the job (403).
inferred: A cancelled job that already produced images should be reported as delivered and charged, not as 'not billed further'. [inferred from executor and complete query]
Partial previews depend on a provider streaming API the route does not use; supporting them needs new contract fields. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Make the executor check cancel_requested_at after the provider call and release instead of completing, or change the product promise to say an in-flight image still finishes and is charged.
[proposed] Make mobile chat Retry call the job retry endpoint so it reuses the reservation like Web and CLI.
[proposed] Show the Generations list in the chat surface, not only the Library.

steps.what_happens: Person sends an image prompt; the client builds an Idempotency-Key that names the surface and operation.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, auth, age gate, plan capability, organisation policy and spend limit.
Server moderates the prompt, reserves managed usage for one hour, inserts the job row and queues a drive 180 seconds later.
First attempt claims the job and calls the image provider (Web waits inline; Mobile and CLI-async use a detached attempt and poll status).
Stop: client aborts or stops waiting and posts cancel; server sets cancel_requested_at and, if no live claim, releases the reservation and closes the job as canceled.
Retry: server requeues a failed retryable job and runs a new attempt on the same reservation; status poll or drive handles abandoned attempts.
Client shows the image, the failure sentence or the stopped state and (CLI) writes the last-image memory file.

features.summary: Turn an existing image into new ones. Web and Mobile can make a variation or describe a change. Library Remix sends an image, its prompt, model and ratio back into the composer. The CLI can reuse the last prompt and settings. Sharing a prompt as a recipe and image-to-video are not offered.

purpose.what_it_does: Starts a new generation from an earlier one: a variation of the same picture, a described change, a reframed ratio, or a fresh request that reuses the old prompt and model.
purpose.why_it_exists: People rarely accept the first picture. Starting over loses the prompt and the picture the person liked. Product requirements list variation, reuse prompt and reuse settings as items of the image studio. (doc: area brief 044, S44.20, S44.24, S44.25)
purpose.who_uses_it: People who generate images on Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile and CLI and want to iterate.
problems_solved: Retyping a long prompt.
Losing the model and ratio that worked.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a photo the person owns into the source of an AI image edit, then applies a typed instruction. The request goes to the managed image route with operation edit or variation, a source image and optional guide images (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:3755-3815; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:96-110).

The product requirements list image generation and editing among the ChatGPT and Claude features to match (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:183).

steps.what_happens: Web composer reads the attached files as base64 (guide images shrunk) after clearing itself.
WebChatPage creates the conversation if needed, adds the prompt message and a generating card, and calls generateImage.
Browser POSTs JSON to the managed image route with an Idempotency-Key and a deadline.
Route checks CSRF, rate limit, age gate, managed-compute gate, organization policy and workspace spend limit before any credit is reserved.
Server checks subscription, plan tier and the canUseImages flag, validates the body, then screens the prompt and the uploaded bytes (hash denylist, file structure).
Server refuses a model that cannot edit, then reserves managed usage once for the whole job.
The job executor sends the source (and guides) to the provider's image edit endpoint and stores the returned image as a media asset.
Mobile resolves the request (cloud only), asks the provider-sharing question, reads the photo, then calls the same route with a 180 second timeout.

features.summary: Starts a new edit from an image made earlier. On web, the chat card button 'New version' opens the revision panel for this chat's images; the Library row action 'Remix' loads the saved image and its prompt into an image-mode composer. Mobile Library also has Remix, in AGI Cloud mode only. CLI and Chrome have nothing.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person pick up an earlier image and change it. In this chat the card opens the revision panel; for older chats the Library stages the saved file, its original prompt and its aspect ratio into the composer in image mode (apps/web/features/library/lib/library-chat-handoff.ts:75-92).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires that an image generated earlier, in this chat or an older one, opens into an editing state (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/045-image-editor.md S45.02). The code comment says an image from an earlier session used to be a dead end (library-chat-handoff.ts:68-74).

steps.what_happens: The person paints on a canvas; strokes are drawn at the image's native size.
On pointer release the canvas exports a PNG mask (black with the painted area cut out).
Source and mask are read as base64 and sent with operation inpaint.
Server resolves bytes, checks the upload hashes and structure, then checks the mask.
The provider receives the mask and source in a multipart edit call and returns the image.
Result stored and shown as a new version; the earlier image stays in version history.

data.where_stored: Inline in the request; the job stores a mask hash (and an asset id if the mask was a stored asset) (managed-image-generation.ts:769-785)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The mask is passed only to the openai adapter's edit endpoint (image-generation-provider.ts:500-505). Models on other image APIs are refused for any edit (managed-image-generation.ts:685-697).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Mask counts inside the 9 MB per-image cap (managed-media.ts:80-84). Reservation happens only after the mask passes (managed-image-generation.ts:653-757). Mobile refuses a mask larger than the cap (ImageAreaEditor.tsx:151-156).

features.summary: A generation option that asks the model for an image on a see-through background, returned as a PNG. Web has a 'Transparent' pill in image mode, mobile has a 'Transparent background' row, the CLI has --transparent. It is not a separate background-removal tool, and the code never inspects the result's transparency.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends transparent_background true so the provider is asked for a transparent PNG (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-generation-provider.ts:484, 544).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants background removal and alpha preservation (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/045-image-editor.md S45.15, S45.33). The code implements this as a request option, not as a removal tool.
purpose.who_uses_it: People making logos, icons, stickers and cut-outs.
problems_solved: Getting a subject without a backdrop for slides and design work.
use_cases: Generate a logo on transparent.
Attach a product photo and ask for the product alone on transparent.
CLI: draw an icon with --transparent.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web): the pill button 'Transparent' with tooltip 'Return the image on a transparent background', shown in image mode when the selected model can edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6439-6453).
Mobile: Add to chat sheet, row 'Transparent background' with hint 'Return the image without a background', shown in image mode for an editing model (AddToChatSheet.tsx:1034-1045).
CLI: 'agi image --transparent' (value needs an equals sign: --transparent=false turns a saved default off) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1127-1130).
Chrome and VS Code: not available.
prerequisites: Image mode, an edit-capable model on web and mobile, a plan with image generation.

Selectable row on mobile.

Send.
Download or share the PNG.
feedback_and_outputs: The toggle shows pressed state.
Result is a stored image; download uses the image's real type for the file extension (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:86-100).
settings: Mobile keeps the choice in the chat view store (AddToChatSheet.tsx:222-223).
CLI: --save-defaults and --clear-defaults (lib.rs:1143).

working: Web composer sends transparent only when the model can edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3763-3768) and passes it through the request options (imageGenerationOptions.ts:177-182; useMediaGeneration.ts:513).
Server accepts transparent_background (managed-media.ts:109) and puts it in the job plan (managed-image-generation.ts:776).
The openai adapter sends background transparent for edits and background transparent plus PNG output for new images (image-generation-provider.ts:484, 544).
Mobile applies the option when the model is edit-capable (resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:86-95) and remembers it for retry (runImageGenerationTurn.ts:174-178).
CLI passes transparent_background to the same route (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7790; apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs:1270).
incomplete: No code checks that the returned picture really has transparency; the PNG alpha check (pngHasAlpha) validates masks only (edit-mask.ts:30-40).
The web revision panel (New version) never sends transparency: buildEdit and handleRegenerateImageInPlace pass no flag (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:449-466; WebChatPage.tsx:3410-3414).
The brief marks mobile missing but a toggle exists.
The edit call sets background transparent but not an explicit PNG output format, unlike the generation call (image-generation-provider.ts:484 vs 544); effect: unknown.

Server does not check that the model is an editing model: it stores the flag from the request (managed-image-generation.ts:776) and the google adapter does not read it (image-generation-provider.ts:869-876).
disconnected_or_disabled: The pill and row are hidden for models that cannot edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6439; AddToChatSheet.tsx:1034).
not_available: Removing the background of an existing photo as a dedicated tool: not built; only the edit path with the option.
Chrome: not available. CLI: only on new images, not on an existing picture (no source option in apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs).

established.statement: User removes the background and gets the subject on a transparent background.
A transparent image keeps its transparency through editing, storage and download.
The option is shown only for models that can edit.

acceptance_criteria: With an editing model, Transparent sends transparent_background true; with a non-editing model the control is absent.
A generation with Transparent returns a PNG whose alpha channel has transparent pixels (check file bytes).
Stored and downloaded copies keep the alpha channel and the .png extension.
A retry replays the same transparent setting (mobile retry memory keeps it).
The panel New version keeps or loses transparency as decided and documented.
inferred: Stored bytes are written as returned by the provider with no re-encode [inferred from image-job-executor.ts:352-380], so alpha should survive; no test proves it.
proposed: [proposed] Add a post-generation alpha check and tell the person if the result has none.
[proposed] Send transparency from the panel when the source image has alpha.
[proposed] A dedicated 'Remove background' action on an existing picture.

features.summary: On web, the revision panel's Aspect ratio button pads the picture to a new ratio and asks the model to draw the new border, so the scene extends. If the model cannot edit, it regenerates from the prompt. Mobile's 'Another shape' always makes a new image from the same description. CLI and Chrome: none.

purpose.what_it_does: Extends a picture past its edges or changes its shape. Web builds a bigger canvas with the picture centred and a mask that covers only the new border, then sends operation outpaint (apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts:240-298).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants outpainting and reframing of an existing image (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/045-image-editor.md S45.16, S45.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who need the same scene in another shape (banner, story, square).
problems_solved: Cropping loses content; this adds content instead.
Re-asking for a new picture changes the scene.
use_cases: Turn a square picture into 16:9 for a slide.
Make a landscape picture portrait for a story.
On mobile, ask for the same description in another shape.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web): 'Revise this image' panel, the top button with aria-label 'Aspect ratio' and a menu of ratios (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:603-690).
Mobile: 'Change this image' sheet, section 'Another shape', buttons 'Make it <shape>' (ImageChangeSheet.tsx:222-243).
CLI: 'agi image --aspect' for new images only (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1115-1117). Chrome: not available.
prerequisites: A generated image with a recorded prompt (mobile hides shapes without a prompt, ImageChangeSheet.tsx:51-52).
Web: an editing model for the true extend; otherwise a regeneration.
Plan with image generation.
screens_and_controls: Web ratio menu lists only ratios the model supports (imageGenerationOptions.ts:73-106).
Mobile note: 'Makes a new image in that shape from the same description.' (ImageChangeSheet.tsx:22).
journey: Open the panel on the image.
Press Aspect ratio and pick a ratio.
Web: if the new ratio is within 1 percent of the current one, only the setting changes.
Otherwise the browser pads the picture and marks the new border as the area to draw.
Wait; the card updates and the previous image is kept as an earlier version.
feedback_and_outputs: Role status 'Generating a new version of this image', then 'The new version of this image is ready'.
Error line: 'This browser cannot prepare the image for reframing.' or 'Could not prepare this image for reframing. Try again.' (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:481-491).
Model that cannot edit: hint 'Describing a change generates a new image from the updated description. The image above is not modified.' (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:733).
settings: Ratio list depends on the image API of the model (imageGenerationOptions.ts:73-106).

working: Web reframe: pad, mask the border and send outpaint when the model can edit and the ratio is not Auto (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:471-499; imageGenerationOptions.ts:257-298).
Same ratio within 1 percent only sets the label (imageGenerationOptions.ts:240; ImageGenerationCard.tsx:478-481).
Unsupported browser (no createImageBitmap or no canvas context) returns a clear message (imageGenerationOptions.ts:258, 281-285).
Non-editing models regenerate from the prompt and the original is not changed (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:728-734; handleAspectChange falls through to runRevision without an edit).
Schema allows a mask for outpaint (managed-media.ts:146-150).
Mobile 'Another shape' sends a plain generation with the saved prompt and the new ratio, replayable on Retry (wholeImageEdit.ts:46-56).
incomplete: Web only pads, never crops: a ratio narrower than the current one adds top and bottom space (imageGenerationOptions.ts:268-274).
Always centres the picture; no control for where it sits.
Picking Auto regenerates from the prompt rather than editing (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:475).
disconnected_or_disabled: The composer deliberately does not offer outpaint because it cannot author a canvas and mask (ChatComposerNew.tsx:275-281).
Ratio button disabled while generating or retry-blocked (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:631-640).
not_available: Mobile true outpaint: not available; 'Another shape' is a new image (ImageChangeSheet.tsx:22).
CLI and Chrome: not available. Desktop: only via hosted web.

established.statement: The user extends an image beyond its borders and the new area is generated to match.
The user changes the framing or aspect ratio of an existing image and gets the same scene reframed.
A ratio within 1 percent of the current shape does nothing new.
A model that cannot edit regenerates from the prompt and does not change the original.

acceptance_criteria: On web, choosing 16:9 on a square image sends operation outpaint with a source canvas wider than the original and a mask.
The mask is opaque over the original area and transparent over the border (check the PNG).
Choosing the current ratio sends nothing and updates the label.
On a non-editing model, choosing a ratio makes a new image and the earlier image stays in version history.
If the browser cannot decode the image, the stated message shows and nothing is sent.
On mobile, 'Make it <shape>' creates a new image with the saved prompt and the new ratio; Retry replays it.
inferred: The mask built here is opaque on the original area and transparent on the new border only if it follows the rule that painted equals transparent; the code fills the original area black on a transparent canvas, which fits that rule [inferred from imageGenerationOptions.ts:287-293 and edit-mask.ts:92].
proposed: [proposed] Let the person place the picture on the canvas (left, centre, right).
[proposed] Offer a real extend on mobile using the same canvas and mask method.
[proposed] Offer a crop when the ratio is narrower.

steps.what_happens: Person picks a ratio in the panel.
Browser fetches the displayed image, decodes it, draws it centred on a larger canvas and draws the mask for the border.
Both canvases are encoded as PNG base64 and sent as source and mask with operation outpaint.
Server runs the same checks as F045-01 and F045-03 and calls the provider edit endpoint.
Provider returns the extended image; the card shows it and appends the old image to versions.
Mobile reshape sends a plain generation with the same prompt and the new ratio.

features.summary: In image edit, the first attached picture is the one that is changed. Up to three more pictures can be added as guides for subject, layout or style. Works on Web (and the Electron desktop, which shows web) and Mobile, only on models that accept edits. Combining images and pose or depth guidance are not built. CLI and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person attach extra pictures next to the picture being edited so the result follows them. The contract allows one source image plus up to three reference images, four images in total (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:86). References are only valid for the 'edit' operation (managed-media.ts:136).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief asks that a person can supply a reference image and the result is composed from it, with subject, layout or style carried over (S45.22, doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/045-image-editor.md). Both leading assistants take several input images, so the product follows [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: People on a paid plan with image creation who edit a photo on Web or Mobile and want another picture to steer the result.
problems_solved: A text prompt alone cannot describe a specific face, object or style; a picture can.
Without references the person must re-describe the look in words each time.
use_cases: Edit a product photo and attach a style picture so the new image matches it.
Attach a second photo of a person and ask for the first photo's scene with that person.
On the phone, pick up to four photos from the library, the first is edited and the rest guide it.

where_to_find_it: Web (and Desktop through the hosted web app): chat composer in image mode. Attach several images. The first is the picture to edit, the rest are guides (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:3777). The operation menu shows 'Edit', 'Variation' and 'Mask edit' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:283-285); references travel only with 'Edit'.

Mobile: the 'Add to chat' sheet in image mode shows the hint 'Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:994). The Images screen has a paperclip labelled 'Attach photos' next to the 'Describe an image' field (apps/mobile/src/features/image/ImagesScreen.tsx:423,455).
CLI: not available. Chrome extension: not available. VS Code: not applicable (brief).
prerequisites: Signed in with an account whose plan includes image generation (canUseImages and the image_generation capability) (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1067; apps/mobile/src/features/image/imageCreationAvailability.ts:17).
An image model whose catalog entry supports edits; the web asks the media availability endpoint for supports_edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1370).
Cloud mode. Mobile blocks with 'requires_cloud' when not in Cloud mode (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:268 area, block code list at :19-29).
Network connection (mobile block code 'offline').
screens_and_controls: Web composer: image mode toggle, attach button, operation menu (aria-label 'What to do with the attached image'), 'Transparent' toggle (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6364-6450).
Web: when a model cannot edit, the notice reads 'This image model cannot edit an attached picture. Choose a model that supports editing, or remove the attachment.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3757).

Mobile Images screen: paperclip 'Attach photos', thumbnail strip with remove, one-line note 'Using <model>, which can work with photos.' when the model was switched (apps/mobile/src/features/image/useImageReferences.ts:67-70).
Mobile: paperclip states ready, full, unavailable (useImageReferences.ts:34).
journey: Open image mode (Web composer or Mobile Add to chat / Images screen).
Attach the picture to edit first, then up to three guide pictures.
Type what to change.
Send. Web: refuses with a notice when more than three guides are attached ('Attach up to 4 images: the first is edited and the others guide it.') (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3778-3783).

The files are read after the composer clears; guide pictures are shrunk to at most 1024 px on the long side and re-encoded as JPEG on the web (apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts:216-243). On mobile a guide is sent as is when it fits, else shrunk to 2048 px and compressed (apps/mobile/src/features/image/services/imageReference.ts:7-8,66).
A new image card appears in the chat when the job finishes.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: local notices in the composer for too many images, unreadable image ('That image could not be read. Attach it again and retry.') or a model that cannot edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3757,3811).

Mobile: messages 'You can add up to 4 photos.', 'Each photo can be added once.', 'Could not open Photos. Please try again.' (useImageReferences.ts:30-32); alerts 'Reference image is too large' and 'This image model cannot use a reference image' (resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:151-158).
Output: one generated image card; the edited source picture is kept as an attachment on the mobile user turn (runImageGenerationTurn.ts:253-266).
settings: Image model choice (web image model menu; mobile model row in Add to chat).
Aspect ratio and the 'Transparent' toggle apply to the same request.
No setting turns references off separately.

working: Web composer builds the edit with source plus up to three guide pictures and sends them as reference_images (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3777-3805; apps/web/lib/hooks/useMediaGeneration.ts:358-362).
The server schema caps references at three and allows them only for 'edit' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:86,104-108,136-141).

The server resolves each reference, hash-checks it against a denylist, checks image structure, and refuses the request before any charge (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:555-640).
The OpenAI edit call sends the source plus references as the 'image[]' form field (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-generation-provider.ts:485-498).

Retry of a failed job can re-supply references (apps/web/app/api/media/image/retry/route.ts:43-47,124-133) and the executor checks a hash over source and references so a retry cannot swap images (image-job-executor.ts:282; image-generation-provider.ts:838-844).

Mobile enforces the same limit, size, image-only and model-support rules before sending (resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:190-232) and sends guides as reference_images (runImageGenerationTurn.ts:317-318).
Mobile keeps up to three failed edit requests in memory for retry (runImageGenerationTurn.ts:154-176).
incomplete: The web edit panel on a finished image card builds an edit with source and mask only; it never attaches guide pictures (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:450-466).
The web does not check the guide count when attaching, only when sending (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3778) [inferred from the absence of an earlier check; not exhaustively searched].

The provider adds every reference to the form as image/png named reference-N.png although the web re-encodes guides to JPEG (image-generation-provider.ts:485-498; imageGenerationOptions.ts:241). Effect on the provider is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: The Tauri desktop client's cloud image call sends text-only requests (apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:464-471); no reference path exists there. Tauri is retained internal code (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
not_available: Multi-image combination (S45.23) and pose, depth or edge guidance (S45.24): no code path found (brief).
CLI: image generation in apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs has no source or reference option found by search.
Chrome extension: nothing found. VS Code: not applicable.
Models whose image API is not 'openai' cannot take references; the edit API list contains only 'openai' (managed-media.ts:62).

established.statement: The user supplies a reference image and the result is composed from it (subject, layout or style carried over). Web, Desktop and Mobile done; CLI and Chrome missing.
The user combines several images into one result. Missing on every app.
The user guides pose or structure with a reference (pose, depth, edges). Missing on every app.
If a provider does not support vision, image input must not be accepted for that model.
Unsupported capabilities are visible: file and image controls respond to the selected model's capability.

acceptance_criteria: Attach one source and three guide pictures in image mode with an edit-capable model on Web: the request is sent and one image returns.
Attach one source and four guide pictures on Web: nothing is sent and the notice 'Attach up to 4 images: the first is edited and the others guide it.' shows.
On Mobile, a fifth photo cannot be added: the message 'You can add up to 4 photos.' shows.
Choose a model that cannot edit and attach a picture: the send is refused with a message naming the problem and nothing is charged.
Set operation to Variation or Mask edit: guides are not sent (reference_images only with edit).
A guide larger than the size limit is refused on Mobile with 'Reference image is too large'.
An API call with reference_images and operation other than edit returns a validation error.
inferred: The extra guides are not stored as message attachments; only the source picture is kept on the mobile user turn [inferred from runImageGenerationTurn.ts:253-266].
The first attachment is the edit source because the code takes attachments[0] (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3759 region and 1376).
proposed: [proposed] Let the card's edit panel attach guide pictures too.
[proposed] Show the 'first is edited, the rest guide it' hint on Web at attach time, as Mobile does.
[proposed] Send each guide with its real file type to the provider.

steps.what_happens: Person attaches source and guide pictures in the composer or phone sheet; limits and model support are checked.
Pictures are read and shrunk (web 1024 px JPEG; mobile 2048 px when needed) and base64-encoded.
Client posts the edit with reference_images to the managed image route.
Server runs gates, prompt moderation, upload hash and structure checks, edit-model check, usage reservation, and creates a durable job.
Executor sends source and references to the image provider's edit API.
Result image is stored and its URL returned; the chat shows the card.

access_and_usage.local_mode: Not available. Image generation runs in Cloud only: mobile returns 'requires_cloud' outside Cloud mode (resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:268 area) and web uses the managed route. Own-key mode: no path found.

features.summary: When a person revises a generated image, the chat card keeps the earlier picture in a list and shows a pager with 'Previous version' and 'Next version'. The original upload is kept on the message. Before/after slider, a version list view, and undo or redo are not built. Web has the pager; Mobile only reads and shows versions.

purpose.what_it_does: Each time a new version of an image is made from an existing card, the previous image URL, prompt, aspect ratio and model are appended to the message's imageVersions, and the card shows 1 / N with arrows (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:3466-3485; ImageGenerationCard.tsx:1132-1152).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants editing to keep the original next to the result instead of overwriting it (S45.31) and wants earlier versions to be visible and openable (S45.29).
purpose.who_uses_it: People iterating on a generated image on Web, Desktop (hosted web) and Mobile.
problems_solved: A revision would otherwise replace the picture and lose the earlier one.
The person cannot compare or return to an earlier take.
use_cases: Ask for a brighter version, dislike it, step back to the earlier one.
Reframe an image and still open the first picture.
On the phone, open a chat from the web and page through its versions.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): image card in the chat. Hover shows 'New version' (pencil) and share; below the card is a group 'Image versions' with buttons 'Previous version' and 'Next version' and a label such as '1 / 3' (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:1036,1132-1152).

Mobile: generated image in a chat shows a toolbar 'Image versions' with 'Previous version' and 'Next version' and the label 'N of M' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/GeneratedImage.tsx:156-196; imageVersions.ts:48).
CLI, Chrome: not available. VS Code: not applicable.
prerequisites: A generated image message with at least one earlier version.
To make versions on web: the card must offer 'New version' (needs onRegenerate) (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:1034,1318).
screens_and_controls: 'New version' button opens the panel 'Revise this image' with aspect ratio menu, optional mask, and a text field 'Describe a change to generate a new version...' (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:603,862).
Pager buttons, disabled at the ends.
'Download' and 'Copy image' act on the version shown (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:948,1058).
No before/after slider, no undo, no redo.
journey: Open a chat that has a generated image.
Click 'New version', describe the change, send.
A new image replaces the card's main picture; the old one goes into imageVersions.
Use 'Previous version' to see the older picture and its prompt; 'Next version' to return to the latest.
Revising while an older version is on screen edits that older version (test name: 'edits the version on screen, not the latest one').
feedback_and_outputs: Live region announces 'The new version of this image is ready' (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:435).
Errors from a failed revision show in the panel ('Could not generate a new image. Try again.') (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:437-441).
The pager label shows the position and total.
settings: None specific. Aspect ratio and model used per version are stored with it.

working: Web appends the previous image URL, prompt, aspect and model to metadata.imageVersions when a new version finishes (WebChatPage.tsx:3466-3485), then saves the message (persistImageGenerationAssistantMessage, imageGenerationPersistence.ts:96-130).
Web card computes the version count and shows the older picture, its prompt, aspect and model (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:1284-1320).
The pager resets to the latest when a new image arrives (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:1236-1239).

Mobile validates and bounds imageVersions (50 entries, URL 2048 chars) and shows the same pager (apps/mobile/src/features/image/imageVersions.ts:7-45; GeneratedImage.tsx:114-196; MessageBubble.tsx:2542).
Preserve original on mobile: the source photo of an edit is attached to the user turn (runImageGenerationTurn.ts:253-266).
Web: the edit panel takes the version on screen as the source of the next edit (ImageGenerationCard.test.tsx:457 name).
incomplete: Mobile has no code that writes imageVersions; it only reads them (search of apps/mobile found read-only use).
Web stores versions per message, but the first uploaded source picture of a composer edit is not obviously kept as a message attachment on web; not established (unknown).
MessageMetadata type in apps/web/features/chat/types/message-metadata.ts does not list imageVersions, while the store type does (web-chat-store.ts:464); effect unknown.

features.summary: A signed-in person on a paid plan writes what a clip should show, picks a video model, aspect, quality and length, and sends it. The AGI Cloud server checks the choices against the model's catalog contract, reserves credits and starts a durable job at an outside video provider. Built on web (and so the public desktop); Chrome is prompt-only; mobile is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a text prompt (and, on web, optional input images, see F046-06) into a generated video clip. The person chooses the video model, the aspect ratio, the quality (resolution) and the length. The server only accepts a combination the chosen model declares in the catalog, and refuses anything else with a validation error rather than changing it silently.
purpose.why_it_exists: Video is a paid media capability of the AGI Subscription (Ultra and Enterprise plans). The founder decision records that video is generated in chat and kept in the Library, with no separate video studio (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:132-133). The model-agnostic catalog means the picker is built from data, not from a fixed list of models.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid-plan users on web (and the Electron desktop, which shows the hosted web app), plus Chrome side-panel users in a prompt-only form. Mobile users once the v1 flag is switched on.
problems_solved: A person can make a clip from words without leaving the chat.
Unsupported model/size/length combinations are refused before any money is reserved or any provider is called.
The cost, plan, workspace-policy and safety checks run in one server route, so every app gets the same rules.
use_cases: A marketer on web picks a model, 9:16, 720p, 6 seconds and types a product teaser prompt.
A user on the Chrome side panel chooses Create a video from the attach menu and types a one-line scene.
A user whose workspace blocks a model is refused with a workspace-policy error, not a silent model swap.

journey: 1. Open the '+' menu and choose 'Create video'. The composer enters video mode and turns image mode off (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2659-2730, 1122).
2. The composer waits for media availability; if no video model is 'enabled' it shows a notice instead of entering the mode (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2685-2692).

3. Pick a model from the 'Video model' menu. The aspect, quality and length menus rebuild from that model's catalog contract; a stored choice the model does not support falls back to the first option the model offers (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1421-1443).
4. Type the prompt and press send. The composer refuses an empty prompt, attached non-image files, or a model that is not 'enabled' with a notice (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3817-3862).

5. The composer sends the derived model, aspect, resolution and duration to the page's video handler (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3869-3893), which adds your prompt and an assistant placeholder to the chat and starts the job (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:3904-4066).
6. The server validates and starts the job (see execution flow). Progress, stop and the finished clip are covered by F046-03 and F046-05.
