Server errors shown to the person: validation messages such as '<model> does not support <n>-second output.' (route.ts:455-457), '<model> does not support <res> output at <aspect>.' (route.ts:460-462), plan errors 'Video generation is available on <plans> plans. Upgrade your plan and I can create that video for you.' (route.ts:986), 'No active subscription found. Please subscribe to use video generation.' (route.ts:945).
On success the server answers with a task id, status 'queued', provider, model and an estimated duration in seconds (route.ts:1287-1295). The chat shows the placeholder (F046-03).
settings: Account setting that limits media to models that do not train on inputs: a chosen model that may train is refused with code model_may_train; with no model chosen the server picks one that does not train (route.ts:1159-1176).
Workspace model policy and spend limit can refuse the request (route.ts:917-936, 1181-1187).
No video-specific user setting for audio: the web client never sends generate_audio, so the server uses the model default (route.ts:1207-1208).

working: Web: video mode, model/aspect/quality/length menus, send path, and the full server route exist and are connected (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1116-6931; WebChatPage.tsx:3904-4066; route.ts:873-1314). Existing tests cover the route and the composer input path (see verification).

Server contract checks: duration 2 to 30 whole seconds, resolution one of 480p/720p/1080p/4k, aspect one of six ratios, prompt 1 to 2000 characters, strict schema (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:31-47, 193-217). Defaults: 4 seconds, 720p (managed-media.ts:196-197) and 16:9 (route.ts:1206). The web composer always sends explicit derived values, so defaults only matter to clients that send a bare prompt (Chrome, Tauri desktop).
The server rejects a duration, size tuple or audio mode absent from the model's catalog entry before billing or provider contact (route.ts:446-481; test media-video-generate.test.ts:627).

Chrome side panel: prompt-only video turn is wired from the attach menu to POST /api/media/video/generate with body {prompt} (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:109-126; side_panel.ts:8779-8793, 6288-6312).
Internal Tauri desktop: prompt and optional duration only (apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:600-617).
incomplete: Chrome has no model, aspect, resolution or length controls: it relies on server defaults (4 s, 720p, 16:9 and the catalog's video slot model) (videoGenerationClient.ts:126; route.ts:381-412). Whether the default tuple is valid for the slot model in production is unknown.
The server accepts n (1 to 4 candidates, each its own paid job) (managed-media.ts:160, 205-210; route.ts:1044, 1262-1285) but no client read sends it.
No frame-rate, style preset, template or storyboard control exists (brief S46.09, S46.15, S46.16, S46.18-24 are outside this feature).
The brief's code anchors are stale: for example the web picker is at ChatComposerNew.tsx:6850-6931, not 5081.
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile: the whole flow (sheet row, pickers, send, progress) is built but switched off by FEATURES.videoGen=false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:28. The docs agree that mobile video UI stays paid-only/unreleased (doc: docs/product/definition.md:347-349).

Runway: the route still contains a Runway adapter, but isVideoProviderReleaseEnabled returns true only for google and openrouter, so a Runway model is refused at route.ts:1189-1193 (apps/web/lib/server/video-provider-release-policy.ts:17).

Catalog: three Google video entries carry a deprecation date of 2026-10-22, already past; the project register says the routing slots still name them (audit/registers/known-flaws.md row VIDEO-VEO-SLOTS-SHUTDOWN-2026-10-22; doc: docs/product/definition.md:352-357). Whether a live executable video model exists in production is unknown.
not_available: CLI and VS Code extension: no video generation code (grep of apps/cli and apps/extension-vscode found only plan comparison text). The server also refuses a CLI idempotency surface (route.ts:1055).
Local mode and own-key (BYOK) video: no code path found; the route is Managed Cloud only (route.ts:1055-1060).

established.statement: A user writes a prompt in a video mode and gets a generated clip back (S46.01).
The user picks which video model generates the clip (S46.05), chooses the duration (S46.06), the aspect ratio (S46.07) and the resolution, and gets that resolution (S46.08).
Video is generated in chat and kept in the Library; there is no separate video studio.
Camera-motion, scene, dialogue and generated-audio controls (S46.10-13) are declined; generation is by prompt.

Video generation is paid-plan included (Ultra, Enterprise). A separate limited offer allows eligible managed-chat accounts up to 5 video requests per user per UTC day when inventory and admission permit; mobile video UI stays paid-only.
Documentation availability stays separate from account and route availability: video depends on a provider route, not on the model alone.

acceptance_criteria: On web with an entitled account, 'Create video' opens video mode, and the aspect, quality and length menus list only values present in the chosen model's catalog output sizes.
Switching model to one that lacks the current aspect or quality changes the shown value to that model's first supported option, and the request sends the shown value.
POST /api/media/video/generate with a duration, resolution/aspect pair or audio mode the model does not declare returns a validation error and creates no job and no credit reservation.
A prompt of 2001 characters is refused by the schema; 2000 is accepted.
An account on a plan without video receives 403 with code plan_upgrade_required (or subscription_required with no subscription) and no job is created.
With no admitted video model, the composer does not enter video mode and shows a notice; the server returns a service-unavailable error for a request with no live configured model.
Turning on video mode turns off image mode, and the reverse.
inferred: [inferred] A Chrome prompt-only request depends on the default 4 s, 720p, 16:9 tuple being valid for the slot model; if it is not, every Chrome video fails with a validation error.
[inferred] Because the web client never sends generate_audio, audio-capable models always generate with audio and the cost estimate assumes audio (credit-estimates.ts:106 vs route.ts:1207-1208).
proposed: [proposed] Show the Chrome side panel's chosen defaults, or add the same four menus, so the person knows the length and shape they get.
[proposed] Add a guard test that the default tuple (4 s, 720p, 16:9) is valid for the model in the video_generation slot.
[proposed] Decide whether the unused n (candidates) field stays in the contract or gets a control.

steps.what_happens: Person opens 'Create video', picks model and options; the composer derives the supported tuple from the bundled model catalog.
Composer reads model admission from the server to decide which models are 'enabled'.
Send: the page saves the prompt and an assistant placeholder to the chat transcript, then posts the request with an Idempotency-Key built from the placeholder id.
The server runs CSRF, rate limit ('video-generation'), age gate, managed-compute kill switch, workspace policy, spend limit, subscription, plan and feature-flag checks.
The server parses the strict schema, checks the idempotency key, replays an earlier matching job if one exists, and runs the platform prompt moderation (422 content_policy_violation on refusal).
The server resolves the model, applies the no-training rule, workspace model policy and provider release policy, then validates duration, size tuple and audio against the model contract.

The server computes the cost from the catalog, checks the monthly video-seconds allowance and that video storage is configured, then for each candidate acquires admission, reserves credits (1 hour lease), starts a durable workflow owner and inserts the job row.
The server submits the clip to the outside provider (Google interactions API, OpenRouter, or Runway when released) and records the provider task id.
The server answers with the job id and status 'queued'. Polling, reconciliation and delivery are in F046-03 and F046-05.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model comes from the generated model catalog (type 'video', videoGen capability, live, executable: model-catalog.ts:2320-2334). With no model named, the server uses the catalog's video_generation routing slot (route.ts:381-413). Providers: Google (interactions API), OpenRouter, Runway (withheld). Provider keys are server environment variables (route.ts:336-342); values are not recorded here.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account required (getClerkAuthUser, route.ts:889). Adult-eligibility gate 'media-video' (route.ts:890-896). Chrome sends a bearer token from the managed cloud account (videoGenerationClient.ts:96-107).
access_and_usage.permissions: CSRF token, rate limit bucket 'video-generation', workspace policy gate, workspace spend limit and workspace model policy are checked (route.ts:879-936, 1181-1187). Workspace client allow-list does not apply because video resolves to an api or unknown surface (audit/registers/known-flaws.md row WEB-SURFACE-ALLOWLIST-UNKNOWN-01).
access_and_usage.subscription: Active subscription plus plan in the video_generation list: Ultra (max_15x) and Enterprise only (billing-catalog.ts:357; route.ts:941-1001). Free users: a separate limited offer (up to 5 video requests per UTC day) exists on web (doc: docs/product/definition.md:342-349); its code path (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3686-3706, 3838-3840 sends it through chat with a model override) was not read in depth.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Monthly video-seconds allowance per plan (tier-unit-quota-service.ts:57, 96-103, 165-168) checked for duration times candidates (route.ts:1238-1256). Credits reserved from the catalog cost (route.ts:485-521, 1442-1453). One admission slot per user at a time, else 409 video_generation_admission_busy (route.ts:1412-1432).
access_and_usage.flags: Capability canUseVideoGeneration (route.ts:1003-1013); managed-compute kill switch (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:73-85); mobile FEATURES.videoGen=false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:28).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Only catalog models of type video with the videoGen capability that are live and carry a duration list or per-second price (model-catalog.ts:2320-2334). Duration, resolution, aspect and audio must match the model's output sizes (route.ts:446-481). Models that cannot keep inputs out of training are refused when the account opts out (route.ts:1159-1176).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: google and openrouter are released; runway is withheld until a charged-moderation outcome exists (video-provider-release-policy.ts:5-17). Runway prompts are capped at 1,000 characters (route.ts:533, 1209-1211). Google video requires audio (route.ts:472-474).
access_and_usage.local_mode: No video in Local mode. Mobile blocks it with 'Video generation uses AGI Cloud' and the text 'Local Mode runs entirely on-device.' (resolveMobileVideoGenerationRequest.ts:65-68, 107). No Local or own-key video path was found on web, Chrome or desktop; the route is Managed Cloud only (route.ts:1055-1060).

features.summary: Before sending a video, the web composer shows 'About <credits>' next to the controls, computed from the model catalog price for the chosen model, shape and length, and turns warning-coloured when it exceeds the credits available. purpose.why_it_exists: Video is expensive and metered by credits. The person should see the likely cost, and be told a failed video costs nothing, before committing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid-plan users choosing video options on web (and the public desktop), and mobile users when video is released.

Uncertainty about whether a failure is charged.

steps.what_happens: The composer computes the credit estimate from the bundled catalog for the shown model, resolution, aspect and duration.
The composer compares it with spendable credits from the usage summary, which it fetches from the server.
On send the server recomputes the cost in cents, checks the monthly seconds allowance and reserves credits.
On delivery the reconciler settles the reservation; on failure it releases it.

features.summary: While a clip is made, the chat shows a placeholder with elapsed time and, when the provider reports it, a percentage. Stop generating asks the server to cancel. For Google and OpenRouter the provider cannot stop the clip, so cancel only means the result is not delivered or charged. The job runs on the server whether or not the page stays open.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows that a durable server-side video job is running, polls its status about every 5 seconds, and lets the person ask to cancel. The job keeps running on our servers if the person leaves; they can resume checking later.
purpose.why_it_exists: A clip takes a minute or more. People need feedback, a way to back out, and confidence they are not charged for a clip they stopped or that failed.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone generating a video on web (and the public desktop), mobile when released, and Chrome (progress only).
problems_solved: Not knowing whether the job is alive.
Paying for a clip nobody wanted.
Losing the result when the tab is closed.
use_cases: Watch the percentage climb on web.
Press Stop generating after realising the prompt was wrong.
Return to a chat after an hour and press Resume checking.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: the assistant message shows 'Creating your video' (with ' with <model>' when known) and a dot-field frame sized to the aspect ratio (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:35-38, 204-222).

Mobile chat (when released): card 'Generating video…' / 'Queued with the provider…' with a thin bar and 'Stop generating' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/VideoGenProgress.tsx:23-30, 118-176).
Mobile library: 'Generations' section listing in-flight and failed jobs with 'Open chat', 'Try again' and 'Cancel' actions (apps/mobile/src/features/library/MediaJobsSection.tsx:20-26, 146-186).
Web library: the shared library host wires a cancel action for video jobs to /api/media/video/cancel (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:244-252).

Chrome side panel: text 'Creating your video. This usually takes a minute or two.' or 'Creating your video, N% done.' and later 'Your video is still being made. Open this chat again later to see it.' No stop control (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json spVideoCreating*, spVideoStillRunning).
prerequisites: A started job with a task id; the Stop button only appears once a task id exists (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:257).
Signed in as the owner of the job; the server checks ownership.
screens_and_controls: Web: elapsed clock ('Elapsed' read by screen readers), a percentage pill with role='progressbar' (aria-label 'Video progress', 0 to 100) only when the server reports progress (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:244-256), a 'Stop generating' button at the top right that reads 'Stopping…' while sending and disappears once accepted (257-272).
Web, after the 5 minute watch window: panel 'Your video is still being generated' with 'Resume checking' (MessageBubble.tsx:3300-3338).
Web, failure panel 'Video generation ended' (MessageBubble.tsx:3351).

Mobile: VideoGenProgress with a determinate bar only when progress is a number, hint 'This usually takes a minute or two. You can keep using the app.', button 'Stop generating' (aria 'Stop generating this video'), error 'Could not stop this generation: <reason>' (VideoGenProgress.tsx:123-174).
journey: 1. Send a video (F046-01). The placeholder appears with the elapsed clock.
2. The page polls status every 5 seconds (useMediaGeneration.ts:94-95, 657-659).
3. When the server reports a percentage it appears (and the message metadata stores videoProgress).
4. To stop, press 'Stop generating'. The button reads 'Stopping…'.
5. The server records the cancel and answers with a message; the page shows that message under the frame and hides the button (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:287-310).
6. If the request fails, an alert-role note appears and the button comes back (300-314).
7. If nothing finishes in 5 minutes the page stops watching and shows 'Resume checking'; the job continues on the server (WebChatPage.tsx:3850-3870; useMediaGeneration.ts:691-700).
8. On completion the placeholder is replaced by the player (F046-05); on failure by the failure panel (F046-04).
feedback_and_outputs: Cancel messages from the server: 'Cancelled. This provider cannot stop a video it has started, so the result will not be delivered and you will not be charged for it.' (cancel/route.ts:57); for Runway acknowledgements: 'Runway acknowledged the task-management request...' (cancel route:59-60); for a terminal job: 'This video job is already terminal and cannot be cancelled.' (cancel route:62).
Final status text in the chat for a cancelled job: 'Video generation was cancelled, so the result was not delivered or charged.' (video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:109-110).
Mobile after stop: content from the server message or 'Video generation stopped.'; status label 'Video generation stopped' (chatMessageStore.ts:1682-1687; VideoGenProgress.tsx:30).
settings: None. Respect for reduced motion: the dot field paints one still frame under prefers-reduced-motion (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:118-146).

working: Web: durable job, 5 s polling, progress percentage, resume after the watch window, and a Stop button wired to POST /api/media/video/cancel (useMediaGeneration.ts:639-704; MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:287-314; MessageBubble.tsx:3273-3338). Existing tests cover the placeholder, the cancel post and the failure note (see verification).

Server status route reconciles the job on each request and returns status, progress, video_url and error (apps/web/app/api/media/video/status/route.ts:44-125). A durable workflow keeps reconciling without a client (apps/web/lib/workflows/video-generation-workflow.ts).
Server cancel route: validates task_id, returns the terminal state for a finished job, otherwise records the request and tries the reconciler once (cancel/route.ts:87-112).
Mobile (built, off): polling and stop (videogen.ts:145-175, 124-126; chatMessageStore.ts:1637-1695), plus library cancel (libraryClient.ts:184-187).
Chrome: 5 s polling with 3 consecutive failure tolerance and progress text; no stop (side_panel.ts:6134-6197).
incomplete: For google and openrouter, which are the only released providers, Stop cannot stop the provider: the job is marked cancel-requested, the reconciler then fails it as 'cancelled, not delivered or charged' (video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:497-503). The provider may still render the clip. Only Runway has a provider stop (reconciliation-service.ts:440-490), and Runway is withheld (video-provider-release-policy.ts:17).

Mobile times out its own watch at 5 minutes and shows a generic failure while the server job may still complete and charge (videogen.ts:170-175; runVideoGenerationTurn.ts:176-181); a Retry then starts a second paid job [inferred].
The web 'progress' is a percentage pill, not a bar.
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile progress, stop and library actions are built but unreachable while FEATURES.videoGen=false, except the library Generations section, which lists video jobs from the server whatever the flag (MediaJobsSection.tsx; libraryClient.ts:176-190) [inferred].
Runway stop code path is dormant because Runway is not admitted.
not_available: Chrome: no stop control, no cancel call (videoGenerationClient.ts exposes only start and status).
CLI, VS Code: no video.

established.statement: The user sees progress while the video is generated (S46.26).
The user cancels a video in progress and the job stops (S46.28).
A generation queue view (S46.25) is declined.
A cancelled or failed video is not delivered and not charged.
A progress indicator must not fake motion for an unknown wait (determinate bar only when the provider reports a number).

acceptance_criteria: After sending, a placeholder with an elapsed clock appears within a second and the status poll runs about every 5 seconds.
When the status response includes progress, a percentage between 0 and 100 is shown and values outside the range are clamped.
Pressing 'Stop generating' posts the task id to /api/media/video/cancel and shows the server's message; the button text is 'Stopping…' during the request.
If the cancel request fails, an alert-role message is shown and the button is usable again.
Cancelling a finished job returns its current state and does not change it.
After a cancel on a google or openrouter job, no clip is delivered and no charge remains.
Closing the tab and reopening the chat shows the job still running and 'Resume checking' continues observation.
Chrome shows progress text and, after 5 minutes, the 'still being made' note.
inferred: [inferred] Because only Runway can be stopped at the provider and Runway is withheld, the user-visible promise 'the job stops' is false for every released provider; the promise that holds is 'not delivered, not charged'.
[inferred] The platform may still pay the provider for a cancelled clip; who bears that cost is not recorded in the files read.
proposed: [proposed] Reword Stop to say the clip will be discarded, not stopped, for providers without a stop call.
[proposed] Mobile should, after 5 minutes, show 'still being made' and offer Resume, like web, instead of a failure.
[proposed] Add a Stop to the Chrome progress text or document that Chrome cannot stop.

steps.what_happens: After the start response the page binds the task id to the assistant message and starts watching.
Each poll calls GET /api/media/video/status; the server claims and reconciles the job against the provider and returns the public state.
The reconciler asks the outside provider for the task state, downloads and re-hosts the clip, marks it AI-generated and settles billing.
A durable workflow also reconciles with no client present, and the OpenRouter webhook nudges early reconciliation.
Stop: the page posts {task_id} with a CSRF header; the server records cancel_requested, runs one reconcile and answers 200 if terminal or 202 otherwise.

For a non-Runway job the next reconcile fails the job as cancelled, not delivered, and settles it uncharged; for Runway one provider stop request is attempted (an outside call) and the state verified.
After 5 minutes the page stops watching and keeps the task id so the person can resume.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The provider is chosen at start (F046-01). Progress values come from the provider via the reconciler when it reports them; Google and OpenRouter are polled, OpenRouter also sends webhooks.

access_and_usage.account: Signed in; status and cancel check job ownership and return a forbidden or not-found error otherwise (status/route.ts:62-71; cancel/route.ts:91-93).
access_and_usage.permissions: Cancel needs a CSRF token and the rate-limit bucket 'video-status' (cancel/route.ts:80-83). The status route does not require CSRF (GET).

features.summary: When a video fails, the person can start a new generation from the same prompt. On web the button reads 'Try video again' and reuses the stored model, shape and length; reference images are reused only while the page stays open. Mobile re-sends '/video <prompt>' with the current settings. Chrome re-runs the prompt. Mobile is off in v1.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers a one-press new attempt after a failed clip. The retry is a brand new job through the same generate route, so plan, budget and policy checks run again.
purpose.why_it_exists: Provider failures and refusals happen. People should not retype the prompt and options, and a failed clip must be safe to retry without double charging.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone whose video failed on web, Chrome or mobile (when released).
problems_solved: Retyping long prompts.
Losing the chosen shape and length.
Unsafe replay of an unknown-outcome job.
use_cases: A provider timeout fails the clip; press 'Try video again'.
A first-frame clip fails; retry works if the page was not reloaded.
After Stop on web, retry the same prompt.

established.statement: The user retries a failed video job with the same settings (S46.29).
A retry starts a new durable job through the same route so all checks run again; an old unknown-outcome attempt must not be replayed.
An action that spends money or cannot be undone names its consequence; the retry is a new paid job.
Mobile: Retry is offered on a failed card; a refused prompt should not offer a retry that cannot pass.

acceptance_criteria: A failed web video shows 'Try video again' only when videoRetryable is true.
Pressing it starts a new job with the same model, aspect, resolution and length as the failed one and a new task id.
After a page reload, retry of a first-frame or reference-image video does not start and explains why.
A job that ended in an unknown outcome shows the 'cannot be replayed safely' text with no retry button after reload.
The retry request runs the plan and spend checks again (a plan downgrade makes it fail with plan_upgrade_required).
On mobile (flag on), Retry reuses the failed attempt's model and shape, or the screen states which settings will be used.
No video job appears with a 'Try again' action in any library.
inferred: [inferred] The web client sets videoRetryable true for any 'failed' status it sees, but the server maps outcome_unknown to failed (video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:75-81) while the transcript marks it not retryable (video-generation-transcript.ts:47); until the transcript syncs, an unknown-outcome job may show a retry button, risking a second paid clip.
proposed: [proposed] Carry the original settings in the mobile retry, or store them on the message.
[proposed] Distinguish unknown-outcome from failed in the public status so the client never offers retry for it.
[proposed] Remove the image-retry call for video jobs in library hosts, or add a video-aware retry.

The provider is called as in F046-01.

features.summary: Finished clips are stored as the person's own files. They play in the chat and in the Library 'Videos' tab, can be downloaded, and on mobile can be saved or sent to another app through the share sheet. The file route streams video with range support and a 256 MB cap. There is no share on web. Chrome plays and offers file actions.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person find, watch, save and (on mobile) pass on a finished clip. The server serves the stored bytes only to the owner, in ranges so the player can scrub.
purpose.why_it_exists: The founder decision keeps video in the chat and the Library rather than a separate studio (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:132-133). A clip must outlive the chat message and be usable outside the product.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who generates a clip, on web, Chrome, and mobile when released.
problems_solved: Losing a clip when the chat scrolls away.
Not being able to save a clip to a device.
Mixing videos with images in one list.
use_cases: Open Library, choose Videos, play an old clip.
Download the clip from the chat.
On a phone, press Save and send it by message.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: the finished message shows 'Your video is ready.' with a player (aria-label 'Generated video') and a round download button (aria-label 'Download video') at the top right (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3393-3470).

Web Library page (route /chat/library, apps/web/app/chat/library/page.tsx): tab 'Videos' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:91-96, 111); opening a clip plays it in a video element with test id library-video-player (LibraryView.tsx:1293-1300).

Mobile chat (when released): card with 'Play' overlay and a 'Save' button (accessibility label 'Save video', hint 'Downloads the video and opens the share sheet') (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/GeneratedVideo.tsx:105-123, 205-235).
Mobile Library: filter 'Videos' (apps/mobile/src/features/library/index.tsx:904-906), tap to play (486-505), item menu 'Share' (644) and selection share (686-690).
Chrome side panel: an inline <video controls> with file actions (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/generatedFiles.ts:341-392; actions built at 274-).
prerequisites: A completed job with a stored asset; signed in as the owner.
Mobile: network to fetch the clip and a device with a share sheet (shareFile throws 'Sharing is not available on this device', services/fileCreation.ts:355-357).
screens_and_controls: Web in-chat player with native controls (play, pause, scrub, volume, fullscreen).
If the video cannot load: 'Video failed to load' with 'Retry' (up to 2 times) and a 'Download video' link (MessageBubble.tsx:389, 3398-3425).
Library tabs: All, Images, Videos, Documents, Artifacts, Uploads, Generated files (LibraryView.tsx:91-99).
Mobile VideoPlayerModal: full-screen player with save and report controls (VideoPlayerModal.tsx:15-60).
journey: 1. When the job completes the placeholder is replaced by the player (web) or card (mobile).
2. Press play. Web streams from /api/files/<id> with range requests.
3. Press the download button or link to save the file; or open Library > Videos for older clips.
4. Mobile: press 'Save' to download the file and open the share sheet to save to the device or send to another app.
5. Library: delete and restore follow the library's recovery rules (not video specific).
feedback_and_outputs: A playable clip; the file is marked as AI-generated in the stored file and response headers (video-job-reconciliation-service.test.ts:270, 302; status/route.ts:88-114).
Errors: 'Video failed to load' (web), 'The video could not play. Retry, or Save to open it in another app.' (mobile GeneratedVideo.tsx:195), 'Could not save the video' alert (mobile).
settings: Plan download allowance does not apply to the owner's own generated, AI-marked video (apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:472-479; apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:246).

working: Web: in-chat player and download link, Library 'Videos' tab with kind=video query and a library video player, served from the file route (MessageBubble.tsx:3393-3470; LibraryView.tsx:95, 111, 1293).

File route for video: 256 MB cap, requires stored byte size, supports a single byte range and answers 416 for a bad range, verifies the streamed length against the asset record, then streams (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:46, 224-293).
Missing bytes return 404 'Video bytes are not available' (route.ts:260, 276); a size mismatch returns an internal error 'Stored video bytes did not match the authenticated asset.' (route.ts:283-286).
Library list: the 'kind' filter returns videos (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts, handleListLibrary at 148; test route.test.ts:163-176).

Mobile: play through a local file prepared from the download, Save through the share sheet, library Videos filter and Share (GeneratedVideo.tsx:62-96; fileCreation.ts:348-368, 593-620; library/index.tsx:445-456, 486-505).
Chrome: video result with object URL lease, loading and failure text (generatedFiles.ts:341-392).
incomplete: Web has no share for a video: no share control found in the chat bubble, and the library's shareArtifact host action is typed for artifacts (LibraryView.tsx:296, 664, 711-720); whether it applies to videos is unknown. Brief S46.33 says web share is missing.

The web library download reads the file into the page for videos (large-file browser download is only for uploads other than video) (LibraryView.tsx:259-263, 559-592) [inferred risk for clips up to 256 MB].
The library storage breakdown counts documents and images only; video is in neither bucket (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:117-130).
A 'thumbnail' for videos in the library grid shows a Play glyph when none exists (LibraryView.tsx:1536-1537).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile chat card for new clips is hidden with the video flag; the mobile Library Videos filter and play are not behind the flag in the lines read (library/index.tsx:904-906) [inferred].
not_available: Web and Electron desktop share of a video.
Add video to a Project (S46.34) is declined (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:144).
Remix, extend and segment regeneration (S46.35-37) are not present.

established.statement: The user browses all completed clips together in a gallery (S46.30), plays, pauses and scrubs a finished clip (S46.31), downloads it (S46.32) and shares it with someone (S46.33).
Video is generated in chat and kept in the Library.
A stored video is served only when its stored bytes match the signed-in owner's asset record.
AI-generated media is marked as such and keeps provenance.
Deleting library items goes to a recovery window; permanent removal is an explicit user action.

acceptance_criteria: A completed web video plays with native controls and can be scrubbed (range request returns 206).
The download button saves a playable file.
Library > Videos lists generated videos and no images; All lists both.
A request for another user's video asset is refused.
A stored video whose bytes are gone returns 404 'Video bytes are not available' and the chat shows 'Video failed to load' with a Download link.
A video above 256 MB is refused with a payload-too-large response.
On mobile (flag on), Save downloads the clip and opens the share sheet; if sharing is unavailable an error is shown.
Downloading your own generated video does not reduce the monthly file-download allowance.
inferred: [inferred] 'Share' for web would be a link or file hand-off; the product has not decided (the founder decision declines external image sharing, S44.31, and is silent on video share).
[inferred] A 30 s 4k clip may exceed 256 MB; the cap is not tied to the model limits.
proposed: [proposed] Record a decision on web video share (parity with Claude and ChatGPT should be checked against current pages).
[proposed] Use a browser-native download for videos to avoid reading them into memory.
[proposed] Count video bytes in the library storage breakdown.

aliases: Make a video from the attached image
features.summary: On web, a person attaches one image as the first frame, or several as references, and the server sends them to a video model that accepts images (Google and OpenRouter families only). The server checks type, size, a known-bad hash list and the model's image limit. Video-to-video is not built. Mobile, Chrome and CLI do not send images.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person start a clip from a picture ('the clip opens on this image') or guide its look with up to four reference pictures.
purpose.why_it_exists: Image-to-video is a common way to control a clip and is part of the area brief (S46.02, S46.04). Video-to-video (S46.03) is in the brief but has no code.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid web users (and the public desktop) making clips from existing pictures.
problems_solved: Describing a look in words alone.
Animating a still image.
Keeping a character or product consistent across a clip.
use_cases: Attach a product photo, choose 'First frame', and describe the motion.
Attach three style pictures and let them act as references.
Attach an image while in a chat and use the 'Video' chip to enter video mode with the image kept.

where_to_find_it: Web composer: attach a PNG, JPEG or WebP image, then use the 'Video' chip (aria 'Make a video from the attached image' or '...images') or enter 'Create video' first (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2750-2756, 5796-5815).

In video mode with one image: a menu (aria 'How the attached image is used') with 'First frame' (hint 'The video opens on this image') and 'Reference image' (hint 'The image guides how the video looks'); with several images it shows a 'Reference images' label (ChatComposerNew.tsx:604-607, 6482-6545).
Other apps: no control (mobile request builder has no image fields: runVideoGenerationTurn.ts:132-146; Chrome refuses attachments in video mode: side_panel.ts:8779-8784).
prerequisites: Video mode on; a video model whose admission is 'enabled' and which accepts images (limit above zero) (video-input-images.ts:25-31).
Images must be PNG, JPEG or WebP (video-input-images.ts:15-23).
Same plan and sign-in rules as F046-01.
screens_and_controls: Attachment row with the staged images; a hint 'Video takes up to N PNG, JPEG or WebP images.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5228-5230).
A link-style button 'Use <model label>' when the picked model cannot take images but another can (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5242-5248).
The input-use menu (above).
journey: 1. Attach image(s) in the composer.
2. Choose the 'Video' chip, or open 'Create video' and attach there.
3. For one image choose First frame (default) or Reference image; for several images they are references (video-input-images.ts:33-35).
4. Describe the clip in words (a prompt is required; with only an image the composer says 'Describe the video you want to make.').
5. Send. The page reads the images as base64 and sends them in the request (video-input-images.ts:37-50; useMediaGeneration.ts:29-36).
6. The server validates and sends the images to the provider (F046-01 flow).
feedback_and_outputs: Composer notices: 'Video generation works from your prompt only. Attached files are not sent to the video model...' for a model with no image input (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2226-2233); 'Video takes PNG, JPEG or WebP images only...' (2240); 'Video takes up to N PNG, JPEG or WebP images, so only X of Y were attached.' (2247).

Server errors: '<model> cannot take input images. Choose a video model that can, or send the prompt alone.' (route.ts:795-797); '<model> takes at most N input images.' (800); 'An input image could not be read. Attach it again and retry.' with code invalid_input_image and status 422 (813-818); 'Input images must be PNG, JPEG or WebP.' (857); refusal with content_policy_violation for a denylisted image (836-841).
settings: The account no-training setting still applies to the chosen model (route.ts:1159-1176).

working: Web: first-frame and reference image input is built and connected end to end: composer UI, base64 reading, request fields, route checks and provider mapping. The brief's 'missing' status for S46.02 and S46.04 on web is out of date (ChatComposerNew.tsx:604-607, 6482-6545; route.ts:779-871; tests listed below).
Contract: first_frame_image or reference_images (not both), reference list 1 to 4 (managed-media.ts:205-232).

Per-model limit: only providers 'google' and 'openrouter' take images, the catalog entry must list the image modality and a maxImagesPerRequest of at least 1, and the limit is capped at 4 (managed-media.ts:160-190).
Server safety: image bytes are resolved for the caller, checked against a hash denylist, then structure-checked; a match is recorded as a moderation event and refused (route.ts:821-861).

Provider mapping: Google receives image parts before the text with a task of image_to_video or reference_to_video (route.ts:589-613); OpenRouter receives input images through submitOpenRouterVideo (route.ts:729-737).
incomplete: Chrome refuses attachments in video mode and its request is prompt-only (side_panel.ts:8779-8784; videoGenerationClient.ts:126).
Retry of an image video works only while the page stays open (F046-04).

Only two catalog video entries declare image input today (read from the generated catalog file packages/contracts/types/src/models.json, not line cited); which of them is live in production is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile: the shared request type allows the fields (videogen.ts:13) but no mobile code sets them; the mobile video flow is also off.
Runway: no image input (limit 0 for runway) and the provider is withheld (managed-media.ts:168-181; video-provider-release-policy.ts:17).
not_available: Video-to-video (S46.03): the request schema is strict and has no video input field (managed-media.ts:193-217), and no client sends a video.
Per-shot references, saved characters and style slots (S46.17, S46.24) do not exist.
CLI, VS Code: no video.

established.statement: The user supplies an image as the first frame or source of a video (S46.02).
The user supplies a video as input to generate a new video (S46.03).
The user fills several reference slots (images, characters, styles) for one video (S46.04).
Uploaded media is refused when it matches the known-bad hash list or is malformed, and the refusal is recorded.
Send first_frame_image or reference_images, never both; images are limited to the model's declared maximum and to four.
Input images leave the device to our server and then to the outside provider; this must be consented and trust-boundary correct (Local content never silently goes to a cloud route).

acceptance_criteria: Attaching one PNG and choosing 'First frame' sends first_frame_image and no reference_images.
Attaching two or more images sends reference_images and no first_frame_image.
A model with no image input shows 'Video generation works from your prompt only...' and the send is refused with attachments.
A GIF or PDF attachment is refused with the PNG, JPEG or WebP message.
An image above the model limit is refused client-side with the count message and server-side with 'takes at most N input images.'
An image matching the denylist returns 422 content_policy_violation and records a moderation event.
A request carrying both fields returns a validation error and starts nothing.
After a reload, retrying a first-frame video does not silently drop the image.
inferred: [inferred] Because the image goes to an outside provider, a consent step like mobile's cloud-send consent is expected for any future mobile or Chrome input path.
[inferred] The brief's S46.02/S46.04 'missing' status should read 'built on web, absent elsewhere'.
proposed: [proposed] Update the brief and the surface matrix to reflect the web build.
[proposed] Decide whether video-to-video is in scope; the founder decision log does not mention S46.02-04.
[proposed] Add first-frame input to Chrome and mobile through the same request fields.

steps.what_happens: Person attaches images; the composer filters to PNG, JPEG and WebP and to the model's limit.
On send, the images are read to base64 (large files downscaled by readReferenceImageAsBase64) and placed in the request as b64_json.
The server checks the model's image limit, resolves bytes, checks the hash denylist and image structure, and rebuilds data URLs.
The images are sent to the outside provider (Google as image parts with an image_to_video or reference_to_video task; OpenRouter through its video API).
The page keeps the images in memory for a possible retry.

aliases: Voice or music reference for a clip
features.summary: Video-generation studio does not let a person pick a frame rate or supply reference audio on any app. The generate request has no field for either. The only audio control the server accepts is a yes/no generate_audio flag, and no client sends it. Both items are missing everywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person choose a clip's frame rate (where a video model supports it) and attach reference audio (a voice or music track) that guides the clip's sound. Today neither exists. The server accepts only prompt, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, a generate_audio flag, provider, model, candidate count and image inputs (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:193-217).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists both as parts of a complete video studio: S46.09 (frame rate where the model supports it) and S46.14 (reference audio where supported) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md). Competitor guidance tells engineers to inspect audio behaviour and references in video workflows (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.17, item 132).
purpose.who_uses_it: People making short clips in the Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome video modes who want smoother or cinematic motion, or a specific voice or soundtrack. CLI and VS Code have no video mode, so they do not apply (brief status n/a).
problems_solved: Today: none, because the feature is not built.
If built: a person could match a clip's motion rate to their project and keep a consistent voice or music across clips.
use_cases: Pick 24 or 30 frames per second for a social clip (not possible today).
Attach a narration voice sample so the generated characters speak in that voice (not possible today).
Attach a music track as the mood reference for a clip (not possible today).

where_to_find_it: Not available on Web, Desktop, Mobile or Chrome. The Web video controls are the video model menu, 'Select video aspect ratio', 'Select video quality' and 'Select video length', with no frame-rate or audio control (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6561, :6614, :6668, :6857).

Mobile 'Create video' sheet offers 'Video model' and aspect, resolution and duration pickers, with no frame-rate or audio control found (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:943, :966).
CLI and VS Code: no video mode (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md).
prerequisites: Not applicable: nothing to use. Video generation in general needs a signed-in account on a plan that includes video generation (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1001-1012, :1102-1115).
screens_and_controls: No frame-rate control and no audio-upload control exist. A search of apps and packages for frame-rate and reference-audio names found no matches in TypeScript or TSX sources.
journey: A person opens video mode and writes a prompt.
They can set model, aspect ratio, quality and length, but no frame rate or audio file.
They send. The request carries no frame rate or audio reference.
feedback_and_outputs: No related feedback exists. The clip comes back at whatever frame rate the provider chooses; the app never states one [inferred from the absent field].
settings: None. generate_audio is a request field the server accepts but the Web client's request type omits it (apps/web/features/media/services/media-api-service.ts:41-51).

working: The server decides audio on its own: generate_audio defaults to the model's supportsAudio flag, or true for the google provider (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1207-1208).
The server refuses audio when the model does not support it and refuses audio-off for the google provider (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:469-474).
Generated audio is passed to OpenRouter as generate_audio (apps/web/lib/services/openrouter-video-provider-service.ts:147).
incomplete: The model catalog describes video models with durations, output sizes, audio support and seed support only; there is no frame-rate field (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:213-219).
disconnected_or_disabled: generate_audio exists in the shared request schema (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:199) but no app UI sends it (media-api-service.ts:41-51; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:126; apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:610-613).
not_available: Frame-rate selector: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
Reference-audio input: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
Both: CLI and VS Code (no video mode).

established.statement: A person picks the frame rate of the clip where the model supports it.
A person supplies reference audio (voice or music) for the clip where supported.
Advertised video options must produce real decodable media, and unsupported configurations must show an honest disabled state.

acceptance_criteria: When a video model declares supported frame rates, the composer shows a frame-rate control listing only those rates; models that declare none show no control.
The generate request carries the chosen frame rate and the server rejects a rate the model does not list, in the same way it rejects an unsupported duration (route.ts:446-481 pattern).
A model that accepts reference audio shows an audio attach control; a model that does not shows it disabled with a reason.
Reference audio is validated for type and size before upload and is covered by the same content-safety checks as prompts and images.
The cost estimate (VideoCostEstimate) reflects any price change caused by the chosen options.
Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome offer the same control or an honest disabled state; none shows a dead control.
inferred: A frame-rate field would need to be added to the catalog model description first, because the server validates duration and size against the catalog (route.ts:446-481) [inferred].
Reference audio would need a new uploaded-file type, since reference images today are image-only (managed-media.ts:209-216) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add optional frame_rates and supports_reference_audio to the video metadata in the model catalog, edit the curation file and regenerate, and read them in the composer.
[proposed] Keep generate_audio as the single audio on/off switch and add a separate reference-audio input only for models that declare it.

steps.what_happens: The person writes a prompt and sets model, aspect ratio, quality and length in the video composer; no frame-rate or audio file step exists.
The client posts prompt, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, model and optional images to the Cloud route.

The server validates the body against the shared schema (unknown fields are rejected because the schema is strict), then resolves audio, checks model limits, billing allowance and starts a durable job.
The job calls the video provider (Runway, Google or OpenRouter) with the chosen model; frame rate and audio reference are never sent.

problems_solved: Today: none, not built.
If built: removes the need to write style words by hand and gives a starting point for a blank prompt.
use_cases: Pick 'cinematic' before generating (not possible today).
Start from a product-ad template (not possible today).
Reuse a saved look across several clips (not possible today).

where_to_find_it: Not available for video on Web, Desktop, Mobile or Chrome.

For images only: the Web composer maps IMAGE_STYLE_PRESETS to a menu (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6344) and the features page describes it (apps/web/app/features/images/page.tsx:100).

features.summary: Video-generation studio has no saved characters. A person cannot pick a stored character or reference to appear in a clip. The nearest feature is uploaded reference images, which exist on the Web composer only for models that accept images. No character store was found on any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person pick a saved character or reference (a face, a mascot, a product) and have it appear consistently in a video. Not built. Per-clip uploaded reference images are a related, separate feature that does exist on Web (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:209-216).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists character or reference selection (S46.17) and several reference slots (S46.04) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: People making several clips with the same subject on Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome.
problems_solved: Today: a person must upload the reference image again for each clip on Web, and cannot at all on Mobile, Desktop or Chrome.
If built: keeps the same subject across clips without re-uploading.
use_cases: Reuse a brand mascot across a series of clips (not possible today).
Pick a saved person photo as the lead of a clip (not possible today).
Attach a product image as a reference for an ad (possible on Web as an upload only, for models that take images).

where_to_find_it: Saved characters: not available on any app.

Web uploaded references: attach an image in video mode when the selected video model takes images (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1569-1590). Exact visible label for the attach control: unknown, not read.

Mobile, Desktop, Chrome: no image input found in their video request code (apps/mobile/src/features/video/services/videogen.ts:13; apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:610-613; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:126).
prerequisites: Signed-in account on a plan with video generation (route.ts:1102-1115).

For uploaded references on Web: a video model that declares image input; the limit is the model's declared maximum, capped at 4 (managed-media.ts:161, :181-190). Only google and openrouter adapters carry images (managed-media.ts:168).
screens_and_controls: Web: image attach in video mode; the composer closes the attach rows when the model cannot read an image (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1577-1582) and flags a conflict (line 1584).
No character picker or character library exists.
journey: Person opens Web video mode and chooses a model that takes images.
They attach up to the model's limit of images; one image is sent as first frame, several as references (apps/web/lib/hooks/useMediaGeneration.ts:30-37).
They send. First frame and references cannot be combined (managed-media.ts:219-231).
The clip returns.
feedback_and_outputs: If the model cannot take images the attach rows are closed; if the images are unusable the composer reports an attachment conflict (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1580-1585). Server refusals come back as 422 with a code and the parameter name (route.ts:765-777).
settings: None for characters. Input limit comes from the model catalog imageInput.maxImagesPerRequest (managed-media.ts:186-190).

working: Web sends first_frame_image or reference_images for models whose catalog entry allows images (useMediaGeneration.ts:30-37; managed-media.ts:181-190).
Server resolves, inspects and moderates the input images before billing (route.ts:779-871; imports inspectImageBytes, matchDenylistedUpload at route.ts:20-25).
incomplete: Image input exists on Web only; Mobile, Desktop and Chrome requests carry no image (see paths above).
The brief marks image-to-video and reference slots missing on all apps (S46.02, S46.04), which disagrees with the Web code; code wins (doc: AGENTS.md section 2).
disconnected_or_disabled: Promotional video models are given an input limit of 0 (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1569).
not_available: Saved character store and picker: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
Reference images: Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
All video input: CLI and VS Code.

established.statement: A person selects a saved character or reference to appear in the video.

acceptance_criteria: A saved character can be created from an image, named, listed and deleted by the person; deleting asks first and names the consequence.

Characters sync across a person's apps on the same account.

Uploaded or saved reference images pass the same safety checks (upload inspection and denylist) before any credit is reserved.

inferred: The existing reference_images field could carry a saved character's image bytes without a new server field, if the client resolves the character first [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Store characters as owner-scoped media records in the existing files and library storage rather than a new table family.
[proposed] Port the Web image-input control to the Mobile sheet using the same catalog limit function.

incomplete: Candidate generation (n up to 4) makes parallel alternatives, not an ordered sequence (managed-media.ts:203-207).

established.statement: A person builds a storyboard of several shots for one video.
Each shot is an editable card.
A person reorders shots.
A person duplicates a shot.
A person deletes a shot.
A person sets a duration per shot.
A person attaches references per shot.
Deleting is a user-initiated action that asks first and names what is lost.

acceptance_criteria: A person can add, edit, duplicate, delete and reorder shot cards before generating.
Each shot has its own prompt, duration chosen from the model's allowed durations, and references limited by the model's image limit.
A cost estimate covers the total of all shots before sending.
Generating a storyboard creates one job per shot with its own reservation, and the results are shown in order.
A failed shot can be retried alone without paying again for finished shots.
Deleting a shot with content asks first and can be undone or names what is lost.
The same flow works on Web, Desktop and Mobile, or shows an honest disabled state.
inferred: A per-shot design fits the existing durable job model, which already creates one job per candidate with its own idempotency key (route.ts:1140-1160) [inferred].
Joining shots into one file would need a new server step; no join step exists in the code read [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Create storyboard as a parent record with ordered child jobs, so retry, cancel and refund stay per shot.
[proposed] Reuse the library to hold finished shots and provide an in-product sequence playback first, before building a join step.

If built: keep what works in a clip and change only the rest.
use_cases: Extend a 6-second clip by 4 seconds (not possible today).

features.summary: Six brief items for the video-generation studio are marked not applicable on every app: camera-motion, scene text, dialogue, a generated-audio switch, a job queue view and save to Project. This page records what the code does for each, so every brief item has a home. No dedicated control exists for any of them.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a home to brief items the owner marked not applicable: S46.10 camera-motion instructions, S46.11 scene and action instructions, S46.12 dialogue instructions, S46.13 generated-audio option, S46.25 generation queue and S46.34 save to Project (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md).
purpose.why_it_exists: Every brief item must be listed so none is lost, and the reason it does not apply can be checked.
purpose.who_uses_it: Engineers and testers reading the video-studio scope; not an end-user feature.
problems_solved: Prevents a reader from treating these items as forgotten.
Shows where the behaviour is covered by the prompt, a flag or another feature.
use_cases: Check why there is no camera-motion control: motion is described in the prompt.
Check how audio is chosen: the server picks it.
Check there is no queue screen: jobs run server-side.

where_to_find_it: Scene, action, camera motion and dialogue: typed into the single video prompt box (prompt up to 2000 characters, packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:195).
Audio: no control on any app; the server decides (route.ts:1207-1208).

Queue: no queue screen; progress shows inside the chat message (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/VideoGenProgress.tsx).

Save to Project: no video-specific action found; Library item menu has an add-to-project action gated by accepted attachment types (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1844-1845).
prerequisites: Signed-in account on a plan with video generation (route.ts:1102-1115).
screens_and_controls: Single prompt box and the model, aspect, quality and length menus (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6561-6857). No camera, dialogue, audio or queue control.
journey: Person writes the scene, action, camera motion and dialogue as prose in the prompt.
They send; progress appears in the message.
The clip appears with play and download.
feedback_and_outputs: Progress display and a finished clip; credit estimate shown before sending (VideoCostEstimate.tsx:24-45).
settings: None for these items.

working: The prompt carries scene, action, camera and dialogue text as free text [inferred from a single prompt field].

The server picks audio: request value, else the model's supportsAudio, else true for google (route.ts:1207-1208); audio on a model without support is refused (route.ts:469-471); audio-off on google is refused (route.ts:472-474).

Server-side concurrency: one admission per user at a time, otherwise 409 video_generation_admission_busy (route.ts:1414-1432). Jobs are durable rows with statuses queued, processing, completed, failed (media-api-service.ts:62-64).
incomplete: generate_audio is accepted by the shared schema (managed-media.ts:199) but the Web, Desktop, Chrome and Mobile requests were not seen to send it (media-api-service.ts:41-51; cloudApi.ts:610-613; videoGenerationClient.ts:126).
disconnected_or_disabled: Library 'add to project' is shown only for accepted attachment types (LibraryView.tsx:1844); the accepted list in packages/contracts/types/src/chat.ts:97-159 has no video entry found, so a clip is probably not accepted [inferred].

features.summary: Trimming would let a person cut the start or end off a finished generated video and save the result as a new version. No app has it. No trim control, route, table or library exists. Today a person can only create a clip from a prompt and cannot change its length afterwards. Plan rules are undefined. (brief S47.01)

purpose.what_it_does: Intended: remove unwanted seconds from the start or end of a generated clip and keep the original. In the code today, nothing does this. The only video code creates a clip from a prompt (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:880-1030).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists it as an expected capability (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/047-video-editing-and-media-continuity.md, S47.01). The founder decisions record that video editing is not built because neither leading product documents one (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:310). The owner has not decided to build it [inferred from the same document].
purpose.who_uses_it: Intended: a signed-in person who has generated a clip on a plan that includes video. Today nobody can use it. Video creation needs the Ultra or Enterprise plan (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357).
problems_solved: A generated clip is a fixed length chosen before generation (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:449-470), so a person who wants a shorter clip must pay for a new generation.
A person cannot drop a bad first or last second without regenerating.
use_cases: Cut the last two seconds of a clip where the subject drifts.
Remove a slow start so the clip opens on the action.
Save a shortened copy while keeping the full clip in the Library.

where_to_find_it: Web: not present. No trim control exists in apps/web (search for trim, ffmpeg and caption terms in apps and packages found no video editing code).
Desktop (public Electron build shows the hosted web app, so it follows web): not present (doc: AGENTS.md section 5; brief status missing).
Desktop Tauri build: not present (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/media.rs:242-252 builds a prompt-only request).
Mobile: not present. Video creation is switched off in v1 (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:28).
Chrome extension: not present. Video mode takes words only (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:8779-8784).
CLI and VS Code: not applicable per brief.
prerequisites: A completed generated clip.
Account sign-in and a plan with video generation (billing-catalog.ts:357).
Unknown: plan rules for editing are not defined anywhere.
screens_and_controls: None exist. Brief draft: a timeline with start and end handles, or start and end time fields, a preview, and a save button. [proposed]
journey: Open a finished clip [proposed].
Drag the start or end handle or type times [proposed].
Preview the trimmed result [proposed].
Save as a new version, original kept [proposed].
feedback_and_outputs: Today: after generation the person sees the clip in the chat or Library with no edit options (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx).
Intended: progress while the trimmed copy is made, an error naming that the trim did not save, the new version listed. [proposed]
settings: None found in the code.

working: Creating a clip from a prompt works on web and is the base a trim would extend (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:880-1030).
Finished clips are stored as media assets and linked from video jobs (apps/web/db/neon/0036_media_assets.sql:7-24; apps/web/db/neon/0105_durable_video_generation_jobs.sql:74-130).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile video creation is switched off by the video flag, so no clip can exist there to trim (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:28).
not_available: Trimming on web, desktop, mobile and the Chrome extension: no code found (brief S47.01 status missing; repository search for trim and video-processing terms found nothing).
No video processing library or server step exists: no ffmpeg reference in apps, packages, crates or services (searched).

inferred: A trim needs a server or device video-processing step that does not exist today [inferred from the absence of video processing code].
Local mode could do trimming on the device because it needs no model [inferred].
proposed: Decide first whether trimming is wanted, since the founder decision defers editing.

features.summary: Joining would combine several clips into one video; extending would make a new shot that continues from the last frame of an earlier one. Neither exists in any app. The only video code creates one clip from a prompt, with an optional first-frame image on web. Plan limits are undefined.

purpose.what_it_does: Intended: play chosen clips in order as one video, and continue a scene with a new shot that starts where the previous one ended. Today nothing does this.
purpose.why_it_exists: Each generated clip is short; the allowed durations come from the model catalog (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:449-470). Longer stories need several shots. The brief lists join, extend and continuity (S47.09, S47.02, S47.07). Founder decisions say video editing is not built (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:310).
purpose.who_uses_it: Intended: signed-in people on a plan with video (Ultra or Enterprise, packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357). Nobody can use it today.
problems_solved: Clips cannot be longer than one generation.
A second shot does not know what the first looked like unless the person re-describes it.
use_cases: Join three shots into one short film.
Extend a scene with what happens next.
Continue a shot from the final picture of the previous one.

where_to_find_it: Web, desktop (Electron shows web), mobile, Chrome: not present (brief S47.09, S47.02, S47.07 missing; searches found no join, extend or last-frame code).
CLI and VS Code: not applicable per brief.
Closest existing control on web: First frame in the video composer, an image the clip opens on (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:605).
prerequisites: Two or more finished clips for joining; one finished clip for extending.
Signed in, plan with video.

Or choose Extend on a clip and describe what happens next [proposed].
Watch progress, then get a new clip with sources untouched [proposed].
feedback_and_outputs: Today: none for these actions.
Intended: progress, a result that plays in the order shown, an error naming the failed step. [proposed]
settings: None found in the code.

Add a catalog flag per video model for continuation support, so the app can say when it is unsupported.

features.summary: On web, a person can guide a new video with one first-frame image or up to a model-set number of reference images. That works only on models whose catalog entry takes images. Last frame, and linking one character reference across several clips, do not exist. Other apps do not send images. The brief calls this missing everywhere.

purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web users on a plan with video (Ultra or Enterprise), with a video model that takes images.
problems_solved: A text prompt alone cannot pin the exact starting picture.
A person cannot easily keep a character's look steady.
use_cases: Animate a product photo as the first frame.
Attach two reference photos of a character to guide the look.
Retry a failed image-guided video after re-attaching the images.

where_to_find_it: Web: video mode in the composer; attach images; choose First frame or Reference image in the menu labelled Attached image use (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:605-606, 6500-6530). A Video chip with the label Make a video from the attached image appears when images are attached (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5800-5812).

Desktop Electron: shows the hosted web app, so same as web [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5]. Desktop Tauri build: no images sent (apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:610-613; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/media.rs:242-252).

features.summary: Lets a person choose which frame of a generated video clip, or which uploaded picture, stands for the clip wherever it is listed. It is not built on any app. Only a generated poster field exists in the mobile and web clients, and the server never fills it. The Library draws small pictures for images only.

purpose.what_it_does: Planned: a person picks a frame (Use as thumbnail) or uploads a picture (Set cover) to represent a generated video clip in chat, the Library and shared lists. Today the only related code is a poster slot in the video players and a server thumbnail for Library images.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists S47.15 and S47.16 so a clip is recognisable in a grid. The product guidance asks that media management keep thumbnails and provenance (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:417 item 134). Both leaders' media lists show a picture per item [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: People who generate videos with AGI Workforce on a plan that allows video, and later look for them in the chat or the Library. Cloud mode only, because video generation is a managed Cloud feature (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:958).
problems_solved: A video tile in the Library is a bare Play glyph, so clips look alike (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1536).
A video in chat shows a black first frame until played because no poster is supplied by the server (apps/web/lib/services/video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:75).
use_cases: After generating three similar clips, pick the best frame of one so it is easy to find in the Library.
Upload a branded cover image for a clip before sharing it.
See a poster image on a finished clip in the mobile chat before pressing play.

where_to_find_it: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome extension: no picker and no menu item 'Use as thumbnail' or 'Set cover' exists in the code (brief status S47.15 and S47.16 are missing on all four apps; searched apps/web, apps/mobile/src, apps/desktop/src, apps/extension/src for thumbnail, none is a picker).
CLI and VS Code extension: not applicable (brief status n/a).

Existing related display only: the web chat player (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3438) and the Library tile grid (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1490).
prerequisites: Signed-in account on a plan that includes video generation: the plan list is max_15x and enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357).
A finished video clip. Cloud mode, because the generate route is a managed Cloud route (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:938-990).
screens_and_controls: Not built. Proposed labels from the brief: 'Use as thumbnail' (scrub to a frame) and 'Set cover' (choose an image file) [proposed].

Built and unrelated to choice: the video element's poster attribute (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3446), and the Library tile that shows a Play icon for a video (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1536).
journey: Planned: open a finished clip.
Planned: scrub to a frame and choose 'Use as thumbnail', or choose 'Set cover' and pick an image.
Planned: the chosen picture shows on every list that shows the clip.
Today instead: generate a video, the player appears with the browser's own first frame, and the Library tile shows a Play icon.
feedback_and_outputs: Today: no thumbnail feedback. The chat shows 'Your video is ready.' with the player and a download link (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3419-3458).

If the video file fails to load the chat shows 'Video failed to load' with a Retry button (up to two retries) and 'Download video' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:389,3402-3425).
settings: None found in the code.

working: Web chat player takes a poster from message metadata thumbnailUrl (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3446) and the web page copies result.thumbnailUrl into the message when present (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:3818).

The Library list adds thumbnail_uri for those items (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:76; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/library.ts:69).
incomplete: The status route's response type has thumbnail_url (apps/web/app/api/media/video/status/route.ts:33) but the object it returns is built by publicVideoJobStatus, whose type and body have no thumbnail field (apps/web/lib/services/video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:63-110). The brief's statement that the status response 'already returns' one is true of the declared type only.
The Library thumbnail covers images only: hasLibraryThumbnail rejects any non-picture type, so a video row gets none (apps/web/lib/server/library-thumbnail.ts:26-38).

not_available: Thumbnail picker, cover upload, storage for a chosen thumbnail and any API to set it: not available on web, desktop, mobile or Chrome (brief S47.15, S47.16 status missing; no column for it in media_assets, apps/web/db/neon/0036_media_assets.sql:9-25).

steps.what_happens: Person asks for a video in chat; the client posts the request with an Idempotency-Key to the video generate route.
The server checks plan access, runs prompt moderation, creates a durable job and sends the work to a video provider.
The provider renders the clip; the server stores it as a media_assets row and links it to the job.
The client polls status every 5 seconds up to 5 minutes and receives video_url (no thumbnail today).
The player shows the clip; poster is set only if a thumbnailUrl exists on the message.
For Library images only, the browser asks the thumbnail route, which reads the stored bytes and returns a WebP.
