features.summary: Planned: compare a clip before and after a change, see the parent clip of a derived clip, and restore an older version. For video it is not built on any app. The server can record versions and parent links for generated files, but nothing reads them, and no video editing exists to create them. Text artifacts have their own version history.

purpose.what_it_does: Planned: a clip with a changed version can be opened in Compare (side by side or slider), Details shows its parent clip, and Versions lists older ones to restore. Today only the storing half exists on the server, for generated files in general.
purpose.why_it_exists: Briefs S47.17 to S47.19 ask for it. The guidance says never overwrite the wrong original and distinguish edits, copies, exports, new versions and rollback (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:329).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who revise generated clips and need to find where a clip came from or go back. Video editing itself is missing (briefs S47.01 to S47.05), so there is no derived clip yet.
problems_solved: A republished file overwrote the earlier one so history was lost (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:6-11).
After the chat scrolls away nobody can tell which upload an export came from (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:11-14).
use_cases: Compare a restyled clip against the original.
See that clip B was made from clip A.
Go back to the first version after a bad revision.

where_to_find_it: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome extension: no Compare, Details or Versions control for clips exists (brief S47.17-S47.19 missing on those four; CLI and VS Code n/a).

Different, built: text artifacts have 'Version history' with 'Restore version N' on web (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx:109,171), in the shared chat panel (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx) and in the mobile sheet 'Version history' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactVersionHistorySheet.tsx:58). These are not for video.
prerequisites: A clip with at least two versions or a parent. No feature creates them for video today (briefs S47.01-S47.05 missing).
Cloud mode; video generation needs plan max_15x or enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357).
screens_and_controls: Not built for video. Proposed: Compare, Details, Versions [proposed from the brief's wording].

Library item actions today: Download, Add to chat, Add to Work, Open chat, Remix, Add to project, Share link (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1795-1850); none shows versions or parent.
journey: Planned: open a clip with changes, choose Compare.
Planned: open Details to see the parent clip.
Planned: open Versions, choose an older one, restore it as a new version.
Today: a regenerated clip is a separate Library row with no link to the first.
feedback_and_outputs: Planned empty state: a clip with no changes has one version and no comparison.
Planned failure: a missing version shows as unavailable, not blank (brief).
Today: nothing.
settings: None found in the code.

working: Server stores a version number and parent for a generated file: persistGeneratedFile bumps version and sets parent_version_id when given supersedesFileId, and writes a file_lineage edge when given parentFileId (apps/web/lib/server/generated-file-persist.ts:56-125,296-318).

The migration file is listed in the applied-checksums file (scripts/config/applied-migration-checksums.json:258), account erasure lists file_lineage (apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:178), deletion policy covers it (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:247) and the data export describes it (apps/web/app/api/user/export/route.ts:2485).
Text artifacts: published versions can be read and restored through a route (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/versions/[version]/route.ts:1-45).
incomplete: The 0257 header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:4) while the checksums file lists it and server code writes to its tables. The code and config outrank the comment (doc: AGENTS.md section 2), but whether production applied it is unknown.
No production caller passes supersedesFileId or parentFileId: only tests do (searched apps/web; matches only in apps/web/lib/server/generated-file-persist.test.ts:440,473).

The version and lineage helpers exist in the shared type model (packages/contracts/types/src/file-model.ts:32-104) but the Library item contract has no version or parent field (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/library.ts:62-81).
disconnected_or_disabled: Storage side (version, parent_version_id, file_lineage) is written by code but no route or screen reads it back for files or videos (searched apps/web/app/api/library and files routes; no read).
not_available: Compare, lineage display and version list for video on web, desktop, mobile, Chrome (brief missing).
Any video editing that would create a derived clip (briefs S47.01-S47.05 missing; founder decision: video editing not built, doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:310).

established.statement: Compare shows a clip before and after a change.
User sees which clip a derived clip came from.
User browses earlier versions of a clip.
Distinguish source edits, copies, exported derivatives, new versions, conflicts and rollback; never overwrite the wrong original.
Video editing is not built; image and video edit controls are declined.

acceptance_criteria: Compare shows two versions side by side or with a slider.
Details shows exactly one parent link for a derived clip, and none for an original.
Restoring an older version never deletes any version.
A clip with one version shows no comparison and a plain empty state.
A missing version shows as unavailable, not blank.
A person cannot read lineage of another account's clips.
inferred: Without video editing the only derived clips are regenerations, so lineage for video needs a caller that passes the parent id [inferred from generated-file-persist.ts and the missing S47.01-S47.05].

History must be append-only; the draft makes published_artifact_versions append-only with no update policy (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:73-76) [inferred as the model to follow].
proposed: Add version and parent fields to the Library item contract and a details route.
Record a lineage edge whenever a video is regenerated from an earlier clip.

features.summary: Planned: a person makes a reusable avatar or cameo of themselves, gives explicit consent, sets who may reuse it, and can revoke it. None of this exists. The only related code is a moderation rule that refuses requests to impersonate real people, and a Local-free rule is not relevant. No consent or likeness storage exists.

purpose.what_it_does: Planned: Likeness settings lets a person create a cameo from a recording or upload, read consent text and tick a box, choose who may reuse it, and revoke it. Revoke stops new use and says which past clips keep the old copy.
purpose.why_it_exists: Briefs S47.21 to S47.24. The guidance says media safety must enforce consent (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:418 item 136). Putting a real person in video without consent is a safety and legal risk.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who want to appear in generated video, and others who might be asked to allow reuse of their likeness.
problems_solved: Today a person has no consent-based way to appear in a video; reference pictures are checked only for known-bad content and by prompt text rules.
Nobody can withdraw a likeness once used, because none is stored.
use_cases: Record a short clip once and reuse it in many videos.
Let a teammate use my cameo but not the public.
Revoke my cameo after leaving a company.

where_to_find_it: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome extension: no Likeness settings, Create cameo, consent box or Revoke exists (brief S47.21-S47.24 missing; searched apps and packages for cameo, likeness, remix: only moderation and Library hits).
CLI and VS Code: not applicable.
prerequisites: Planned: signed-in adult account. Adult-only rule exists: all surfaces are 18 and over with a server-held decision (project memory, not a code citation); exact code location unknown.
Cloud mode; plan limits not defined.
screens_and_controls: Not built. Planned labels from the brief: Likeness settings, Create cameo, consent box, who may reuse it, Revoke [proposed].
Related built control: reference or first-frame picture upload in the web composer for a video (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/video-input-images.ts:14-40).

Planned: set who may reuse it.

Today: a prompt that asks to impersonate a real person is refused with HTTP 422 and code content_policy_violation (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1137-1155).
settings: None found in the code.

working: Text rule 'likeness.impersonation-request' blocks prompts like deepfake, face swap, voice clone or likeness of a real person unless an exemption word appears (consent, with permission, my own face, fictional, parody and others) (apps/web/lib/moderation/text-classifier.ts:161-165,268-273).
Rule 'likeness.photoreal-depiction' covers photoreal depictions of real people with the same exemptions (apps/web/lib/moderation/text-classifier.ts:276-281).

Managed video runs prompt moderation before billing (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1135-1160) and checks input pictures against a hash denylist and structure rules (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:787-860).
Output moderation lists 'likeness' as a category (apps/web/lib/moderation/output-moderation.ts:65-69).
incomplete: The exemption is by words in the prompt, such as 'consent' or 'myself'. A person can claim consent by typing the word; no consent is recorded [inferred from the regex at apps/web/lib/moderation/text-classifier.ts:164].

Searched apps, packages, crates and docs for cameo and likeness; no feature code. No table for it in the migration list (searched apps/web/db/neon file names).

features.summary: A person starts a spoken conversation bound to one chat. On web and desktop the live voice session needs a Cloud model, a signed-in account and a plan that allows voice. On mobile it is live in Cloud mode and turn based on the device otherwise. The CLI only offers push-to-talk dictation.

purpose.what_it_does: Opens a voice conversation tied to a chat. If the chat already has earlier turns, the server loads up to 24 of them as context, so the person continues the same conversation by voice. If the chat is new, a chat is created first. If another device left a session open for the same chat, web offers to continue with that session's voice, language and pace.
purpose.why_it_exists: The leading assistants let a person talk instead of type and then carry on in the same chat. The product requirements say live voice must be separate from dictation and say plainly when it is unavailable (docs/product/requirements.md:996-1004; docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:399-408).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web, desktop and mobile who want hands-free talk; CLI users who want to dictate instead of type.
problems_solved: Typing is slow or impossible while walking, driving or cooking.
A spoken exchange would otherwise be lost; here it lands in the chat history and can be reopened.
People need a clear, non-broken answer when voice is not allowed on their plan or mode.
use_cases: Open an existing chat on web, press the round voice button, and keep talking about the same topic.
On the mobile new-chat screen press the voice button and a new chat called 'Voice chat' is created and opened in live voice.
Reopen last week's chat and start voice again so the assistant has the earlier turns as context.
In the CLI type /voice, hold SPACE and dictate a prompt.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (the Desktop app shows the hosted web app): in the chat composer, when the text field is empty, a round button labelled 'Start voice mode' replaces Send (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/VoiceEntryButton.tsx:9; apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6955). Both the new-chat landing view and an open chat render it (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7672, 7800).

Mobile: the round composer button with accessibility label 'Start voice mode' and hint 'Opens hands-free voice conversation' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2278-2294); a long press on the dictation button also opens it (ChatInput.tsx:2255); the slash command '/voice' (ChatInput.tsx:1563, 1576); the setting 'Start with Voice' opens voice on launch (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx:399; apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1128). Settings > Voice has a row 'Open Voice Companion' (settings/voice/index.tsx:515) for the on-device companion screen.
CLI: the slash command /voice with an optional language, or the --voice-lang flag for the default language (apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:296-306; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:354).

VS Code and Chrome extension: no live voice entry found; both only have speech-to-text dictation files (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/dictation.ts; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/dictation-language.ts).
prerequisites: Web/Desktop: a signed-in account, a Cloud model selected (not a model on this device, not a chat that holds Local turns), the 'canUseVoice' capability, microphone permission, and a browser with WebRTC (WebChatPage.tsx:5906-5910; ChatComposerNew.tsx:6955; live-voice-session.ts:444-452).
Adults only: the server applies an adult-eligibility gate named 'voice-live' (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:181-188).
Mobile live voice: Cloud mode, signed in, the native WebRTC module present, and an https server (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-44).

CLI: a build with the 'voice' feature (macOS and Windows release builds only), a working microphone, and a transcription backend (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:77-105; .github/workflows/release-cli.yml:268-279).
screens_and_controls: Web: voice surface in the composer slot with a round orb, call timer, composer row (plus button, text field, mic button, 'End voice session'), header label 'Voice' with a 'Voice settings' gear (VoiceModeSurface.tsx; VoiceComposer.tsx:9-16; VoiceHeaderLabel.tsx:12-15).
Web rejoin dialog titled 'This chat already has an open voice session' with buttons 'Continue that session' and 'Use my settings' (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:57-62, 446).

Mobile live: LiveVoiceBar with orb, status line, mic, 'End live voice', 'Switch to text for this chat' (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:704, 726, 746). First use shows an onboarding sheet then a voice picker sheet (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1721-1745).
Mobile on-device fallback: VoiceInlineBar in the chat, and the full screen voice companion (apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx).
CLI: terminal text prompts '[SPACE to record, ESC to exit]' (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:176-190).
journey: 1. The person taps 'Start voice mode' (web) or the mobile voice button.

2. Web: the voice session status moves to 'entering' (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-session-store.ts:219-222). If the chat is not a Cloud chat the surface shows an unavailable message and 'Continue in text' (use-voice-session.ts:826-834; VoiceModeSurface.tsx:339-352).

3. Web with an existing chat: the app asks the server whether the chat already has an open voice session (GET /api/voice/live/sessions/active) and, if so, shows the rejoin dialog; otherwise it starts (use-voice-session.ts:844-866).
4. If there is no chat yet a new one is created and the address is replaced with it (WebChatPage.tsx:6695-6722).
5. The browser asks for the microphone, builds a WebRTC offer and posts it with the chosen voice, language, pace, reasoning and the chat id (live-voice-session.ts:480-545).

6. The server checks account, plan and budget, loads earlier turns, and asks the voice provider to open the session; the app applies the answer and shows 'Listening' (route.ts:181-731; live-voice-session.ts:1003-1010).
7. Mobile does the same through LiveVoiceSession.start; on a new chat it first creates a chat titled 'Voice chat' and opens it with voice=live (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1090-1093).
8. To resume, open an older chat and start voice again; its earlier turns are loaded as context (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/live-voice-context.ts:22-27, 95-131).
feedback_and_outputs: Web connecting state is announced as 'Connecting to voice' (voice-announcements.ts:4-12).

Web microphone refusal: 'Microphone access was denied. Allow the microphone to use voice mode.' and the app retries by itself once the browser permission is granted (live-voice-session.ts:61-77; use-voice-session.ts:880-905).

Web no plan access: 'Voice needs usage your plan doesn't include. Upgrade to talk with voice, or continue in text.' with Upgrade and Continue in text buttons (voice-session-budget.ts:40-44; VoiceModeSurface.tsx:314-336).

Mobile reasons shown when live is unavailable: 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' and 'Sign in to use live voice; this chat stays turn based.' (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-19).
CLI prints which backend transcribes, then 'Press SPACE to talk, ESC to exit voice mode.' (voice.rs:105-176).
settings: Web voice settings are remembered in the browser under the store name agi-web-voice-session (voice-session-store.ts:28, 206-212).
Mobile: 'Voice Input', 'Auto-listen', 'Start with Voice', 'Speech language', 'Voice' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx:387-422).
CLI: --voice-lang and the /voice language argument (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:354, 5950-5955).

working: Web/Desktop: entry button, rejoin check, chat creation, WebRTC start and server session creation are all connected (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6955; use-voice-session.ts:539-720; route.ts:731).
Server refuses with 400 voice_conversation_required when no chat id is sent (route.ts:255-262).
Server loads up to 24 earlier turns, 700 characters each, plus project, personalization and memory context into the session instructions (live-voice-context.ts:22-27, 95-131; route.ts:494-506).

Server closes any older open voice session for the same chat as 'superseded' and settles it (route.ts:642-665). 'Continue that session' starts a new session with the old settings; it does not reattach (use-voice-session.ts:868-883).
A chat created only for voice is deleted again if the session fails to start (use-voice-session.ts:690-700).
Mobile live start from an open chat and from the new-chat tab, with onboarding, capability check and fallback to on-device turn-based voice (chat/[id].tsx:1697-1745; (tabs)/chat.tsx:1071-1112).
Desktop (Electron) grants only audio media to the trusted cloud origin, so the web voice code can use the microphone there (apps/desktop/electron/permissionPolicy.ts:49-58).
CLI /voice runs push-to-talk dictation and sends the confirmed text to the agent session (voice.rs:75-300).
incomplete: CLI: there is no live conversation; the brief marks start, resume and new voice as done for CLI, but the code is record, transcribe, confirm, send as text (voice.rs:1-12, 176-300). Resuming an earlier CLI voice conversation is not implemented as a voice feature; whether earlier turns of the REPL session count as context is [inferred] from the session object being reused (voice.rs:261-272).

The 20 second timeout covers only the server's call to the voice provider (route.ts:128, 563); the client has its own 10 second ICE wait (live-voice-session.ts:43) but no overall start timeout was found.
The brief's line references are out of date (for example route.ts:254-262 is now 255-262 and the 20 second constant is route.ts:128).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web/Desktop: when the chat model is a model on this device, or the chat holds Local turns, or the model is not a managed route, the voice entry button is not rendered because onEnterVoiceMode is undefined (WebChatPage.tsx:5906-5910, 7672, 7800; test: WebChatPage.local-model-and-voice.test.tsx:464).
Mobile: Local mode never starts the live session; it uses turn-based on-device voice instead (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-25).
CLI voice is compiled out on Linux release builds; the stand-in returns an error naming the missing feature (release-cli.yml:268-279; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:83-105).
not_available: VS Code extension and Chrome extension: no live voice found; only dictation files exist (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/dictation.ts; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/dictation-language.ts).
Own-key live voice on web: not offered; the server only uses a server-held key and a managed provider (route.ts:189-198, 235).

established.statement: From an open existing chat, a control starts a voice conversation bound to that chat.
A control starts a brand-new voice conversation and a new chat is created for it.
The user can reopen a previous voice conversation and continue it by voice with its earlier turns as context.
Live voice and dictation are different things; if live voice is not available the app says so without broken controls.
Voice controls include microphone, mute, stop, captions, device selection, voice choice and understandable connection state; audio must not escalate to the cloud without required consent.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to BYOK or managed cloud.

acceptance_criteria: On web with a Cloud model and an empty text field, 'Start voice mode' is visible; with a model on this device it is absent.
Starting from a chat with earlier messages produces a session whose first reply shows awareness of those messages.
Starting from the new-chat screen creates exactly one chat, and a failed start leaves no empty chat behind on web.
A request without a conversation id is refused with code voice_conversation_required.
Refusing the microphone shows the microphone message, creates no charge, and retries after permission is granted.
A plan without voice shows the not-in-plan message with Upgrade and Continue in text.
Starting voice twice for the same chat on two devices leaves one open session; the first is closed as superseded.
On mobile in Local mode the voice button opens the on-device turn-based voice and says live voice runs in Cloud.
inferred: The CLI voice mode should not be described as a live conversation until a live path exists [inferred from voice.rs:1-12].
The web rejoin dialog should say it starts a new session with the same settings, because the old session is closed [inferred from route.ts:642-665 and use-voice-session.ts:868-883].
proposed: [proposed] Offer voice on web/desktop for own-key chats only through an explicit, labelled fork with consent, as AGENTS.md section 6 requires.
[proposed] Add an overall client start timeout with a clear 'could not connect' message.
[proposed] Mark the CLI row as 'push-to-talk dictation' in the surface matrix instead of 'live'.

steps.what_happens: Person presses 'Start voice mode'; the voice store moves to 'entering'.
App checks for an already open session for this chat.
Browser asks for the microphone and creates the WebRTC offer.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, adult gate, managed-compute, organization policy, spend limit, model policy, entitlement, capability flag and plan voice allowance.
Server reserves one minute of usage (paid plans) or grants one minute of the monthly free allowance (Free).
Server loads earlier turns, project, personalization and memory, then calls the voice provider to open a session with a delegated reasoning backend.
Server closes older sessions for the chat as superseded, stores a voice_sessions row and returns session id, SDP answer, settings, tool list and a 60 second ceiling.
Browser applies the answer; audio flows directly between browser and provider; 'session.started' makes the app show Listening.
Mobile Local mode instead runs on-device speech recognition, the chosen reply model, and on-device speech output.

data.what: voice_sessions row (user, chat, provider session id, surface, voice, language, pace, active tools, last turn id, status, times)
data.synced: Readable from any device through the active-session endpoint
data.retained_or_deleted: Closed with a reason when the call ends or is superseded; deletion policy unknown

data.where_stored: chat history on our servers (web posts each final turn with skipLlm); mobile chat store
data.retained_or_deleted: Follows chat retention; not a separate audio recording (WebChatPage.tsx:6739-6785; chatMessageStore.ts:1161-1200)

data.where_stored: Not stored by this code; streamed to the voice provider

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The live voice model comes from the voice_live routing slot and must be a live, priced model on a managed provider (route.ts:189-198, 253-262). A second, plan-dependent backend model handles reasoning and tools (route.ts:318-323). The server key is read from an environment variable named OPENAI_API_KEY (route.ts:235), so the provider is most likely provider:openai [inferred]. Model identifiers are deliberately not recorded here. See SYS-model-catalog-and-routing.

access_and_usage.account: Web/Desktop and mobile live voice need a signed-in account (route.ts:178; liveVoiceAvailability.ts:19). Mobile on-device voice and the CLI local binary need no account [inferred from voice.rs:105-140 and liveVoiceAvailability.ts:21-25].
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone permission. Adults only gate 'voice-live' (route.ts:181-188). Organization policy, model policy and spend limit gates (route.ts:199-231). Tool approval policy is applied to what voice tools may do (route.ts:507-515). Mobile asks for cloud-send consent before starting (liveVoiceSession.ts:269; test live-voice-session.test.ts:256).
access_and_usage.subscription: Capability canUseVoice is withdrawn when the plan policy has allowVoice false (apps/web/lib/services/capability-handshake-service.ts:118) and checked again on the server (route.ts:300-316). Free plan has a monthly voice allowance set by voiceMinutesPerMonth (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1255-1256); paid plans fund voice from their usage budget (route.ts:341-372).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: One minute blocks (LIVE_VOICE_BLOCK_SECONDS) reserved at start and extended while the call runs; lease 10 minutes (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-billing.ts:20-28). Rate limit key 'voice-live-session' (route.ts:176). Earlier-turn context capped at 24 turns, 6000 characters (live-voice-context.ts:22-24).
access_and_usage.flags: Feature flag capability 'canUseVoice' evaluated per user, workspace, plan and surface (route.ts:300-307). Mobile 'Start with Voice' and 'Voice Input' settings (settings/voice/index.tsx:387-399).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs a live, priced voice model in the voice_live slot and a live backend model for the plan; otherwise the route throws or returns 503 live_voice_unpriced (route.ts:189-198, 266-280).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Managed providers only; a server key is required, else 503 live_voice_not_configured (route.ts:192-197, 232-246). If the model may train on inputs and the user opted out of training, or the chat carries Google user data, voice is refused with 403 model_may_train (route.ts:322-341).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web/Desktop: voice entry is not offered for Local chats or models on this device (WebChatPage.tsx:5906-5910). features.summary: Spoken turns from a voice call are written into the same chat as typed turns. Web has an optional 'Captions' panel showing the last four lines, and an orb tap that fades the transcript. Mobile shows captions in its live bar and has a separate full-screen on-device voice screen. The CLI prints what it heard.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns what the person and the assistant say into text in the chat, shows it live as optional captions, and offers a focused view where the transcript is hidden but the call keeps running.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to see what was heard, check mistakes, and find the conversation later. A voice call that leaves no text is hard to trust or reuse.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone on a voice call; people who cannot hear well; people in noisy or silent places.
problems_solved: Misheard words can be seen and corrected by typing.
The call is kept with the chat so it can be reopened and continued by typing.
A clean full focus view for people who want only the orb.
use_cases: Turn on Captions on web to read what the assistant says while listening to it.
After a call, open the chat and read the spoken turns in the message list.
Tap the orb to hide the transcript during a call, tap again to bring it back.
On mobile, open the voice companion to read the on-device transcript and report a response.

features.summary: A round orb and status text show whether the assistant is connecting, listening, speaking, muted or working on a task, and the orb moves with the microphone or reply level. Web also announces state changes to screen readers. Mobile shows the same states in its live bar and companion screen.

purpose.what_it_does: Tells the person what the call is doing right now and follows the sound level so they can see they are heard.
purpose.why_it_exists: In a spoken call there is no screen text to wait on; a clear state avoids talking over a busy assistant or wondering whether the microphone works.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone on a voice call, including screen reader users and people who prefer less motion.
problems_solved: Is it listening me or thinking?
Is a tool still running or did it stall?
Is my microphone muted?
use_cases: Watch the orb change from listening to speaking when the assistant answers.
See 'Working on your request' with a Stop the task button while a tool runs.
Hear 'Assistant is speaking' announced by a screen reader.
On mobile see 'Speaking, talk any time to interrupt'.

where_to_find_it: Web/Desktop: the orb in the voice surface above the composer row (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:290-300, 562-568), the call timer, and the agent status line (574-610).
Mobile live: LiveVoiceBar status text, orb, glow and waveform (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:164-181; components VoiceOrb.tsx, VoiceStateGlow.tsx, Waveform.tsx).
Mobile companion: orb with phase label and sublabel (voice.tsx:75-100).
CLI: a 'REC' line with a level meter while recording and spinners 'Transcribing...' and 'Thinking...' (voice.rs:766, 846, 203, 261).
prerequisites: A running call. Indicators need no setting.
screens_and_controls: Orb states: idle, listening, thinking, speaking, muted with labels '', 'Listening', 'Thinking', 'Speaking', 'Muted' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice/voice-session-machine.ts:232-238).
Web shows thinking when the backend is busy while the state is listening (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceOrb.tsx:26-29).

Web agent status shows the tool label or 'Working on your request', a spinner, and a 'Stop the task' button with hint 'Stops the running action and keeps the call open.' (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:40-45, 574-610).
Web slow tool: the label plus 'is taking longer than usual' and an alert icon (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:44, 215-221).

Companion strings: 'Tap to speak', 'Listening...', 'Thinking...', 'Speaking...' and sublabels 'Speech stays on this device', 'Speak naturally', 'AI is responding', 'Sending to AGI Cloud' or 'Answering on this device' (voice.tsx:75-100).
journey: 1. Call connects; the orb shows connecting then listening.
2. The person speaks; the level moves the orb.
3. The assistant works on a request; the orb shows thinking and an agent status line appears.
4. The assistant speaks; the orb shows speaking and follows the reply audio level.
5. A screen reader hears each state change in a polite region.
feedback_and_outputs: Announcements: 'Connecting to voice', 'Listening', 'Transcribing what you said', 'Sending your turn', 'Working on your request', 'Assistant is speaking', 'Microphone muted', 'An action is waiting for your approval on screen' (voice-announcements.ts:4-12).

working: Web: the controller maps session status plus backendBusy to an orb state; speaking is detected from reply audio level at or above 0.03 held 350 ms, sampled every 50 ms (live-voice-session.ts:48-51, 918-972).
The orb level source returns the larger of microphone and reply level, and the microphone level is 0 while muted (live-voice-session.ts:436-438, 940-950).
Announcements for each status, muted, thinking and approval pending (voice-announcements.ts:23-46).

steps.what_happens: Browser analysers read the microphone and the reply audio every 50 ms.
A reply level of 0.03 or more marks the assistant as speaking and keeps that for 350 ms.
Delegation events from the provider mark the backend busy and name the running tool.
The reducer and store turn these into a status; the orb and the live region render it.
Mobile derives its status from session callbacks and the interruption flag.

features.summary: During a call the person can mute the microphone, end the call, or pause it, and the call keeps listening without a button each turn. Pausing on web and mobile closes the live connection and resuming opens a new one. The CLI can only end its loop with Escape and has no hands-free mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the basic call controls: mute without hanging up, end the call and settle its usage, pause so nothing is used, and an always-listening mode.
purpose.why_it_exists: A call must be controllable and must stop costing minutes when the person stops talking.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone on a voice call.
problems_solved: Cough or side talk should not reach the assistant.
Leaving the call must stop billing and release the microphone.
Hands-free use needs no per-turn press.
use_cases: Press the microphone button to mute while a colleague talks.
Press Escape or the X button to end the call.
Choose 'Pause call' to step away without using minutes, then 'Resume'.
On mobile switch between hands-free and push-to-talk on the companion screen.

prerequisites: A started call (F048-01).
screens_and_controls: Web paused state: hint 'Paused. The call is closed and nothing is being used. Resume to pick up this conversation.' with a Resume button (testid voice-resume) (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:63-64, 361-372).

journey: 1. Mute: press the microphone button; the app disables the audio track and tells the provider to mute; the orb shows Muted.
2. Unmute reverses it.
3. Pause: the app ends the live connection, records the paused flag and shows the paused hint.
4. Resume: the app opens a new live session with the current settings.
5. End: the app asks the provider to close, waits up to 3 seconds, posts the usage seconds to the close endpoint, and the server settles the usage.
6. Hands-free: with no button needed the provider detects when the person stops talking and replies, turn after turn.
feedback_and_outputs: Microphone button shows pressed state with the device name in its tooltip (VoiceComposer.tsx:41-48; test VoiceComposer.test.tsx:41).

working: Mute: web disables microphone tracks and sends session.input_audio.mute or unmute; a mute chosen while connecting is replayed after the session starts (live-voice-session.ts:772-787, 1003-1010).

The server accepts these browser events on the data channel: mute, unmute, instructions append, thinking append, commentary append, response item create, response create and session close; session.update is excluded (route.ts:138-147, 559).

End: close() cancels backend work, stops tracks, sends session.close and waits up to 3 s, then settle posts seconds, reason, last turn and backend usage to the close endpoint (live-voice-session.ts:789-815, 591-600; close/route.ts:63-175).
Pause on web: pause() sets the flag, ends the live session with reason 'paused' and mutes; resume() starts a new session (use-voice-session.ts:940-959).
Mobile pause: LiveVoiceComposer sets the session inactive while paused so the live session is closed, and resumes by starting again (LiveVoiceComposer.tsx:25-43).

Hands-free on web and mobile live: there is no per-turn control in the live path; the provider session is open-microphone until muted [inferred from live-voice-session.ts: no commit or press events are sent].
Mobile companion: hands-free restarts listening after each reply when Auto-listen is on (useVoiceConversation.ts:299-310, 352).
Web ends the call on page hide and mobile ends it when the app goes to the background (use-voice-session.ts:926-927; useLiveVoiceSession.ts:480-486).
incomplete: Pause does not keep the connection; it closes it and a new session is created on resume, which reserves a new minute block (use-voice-session.ts:942-959; route.ts:373-400). The brief's 'should keep the call' is therefore only met at the conversation level.
CLI: Escape is the only exit; brief says end is done and hands-free missing, which matches (voice.rs:563-580).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web 'Pause call' is hidden once the call is in error or already paused (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:641-643).
not_available: CLI: mute, pause, hands-free.
VS Code and Chrome: no call.
Lock-screen or background control (brief S48.34, S48.35 missing).

established.statement: The user can mute and unmute the microphone without ending the conversation.
A control ends the conversation, closing the session and settling its usage.
The user can pause the whole conversation (mic and assistant) and resume it later without ending it.
A hands-free mode keeps listening across turns without a button press per turn.
Meter actual voice usage and disclose limits.

acceptance_criteria: Mute stops the assistant from hearing, keeps the call open, and the orb shows Muted.
A mute chosen before the call connects is still muted when it starts.
End closes the session; the voice_sessions row is closed and the billed seconds are returned.
Pause shows the paused hint, the call timer stops, and no new minutes are reserved until resume.
Resume starts listening again in the same chat with earlier turns as context.
After 3 or more turns the person never had to press anything on hands-free.
Closing the browser tab ends the session and settles usage within the lease.
inferred: Pause should say plainly that the call is closed (it does) and resume opens a new session that can be refused by a spent allowance [inferred from route.ts:373-418].
proposed: [proposed] Show remaining voice allowance at resume so a pause is not a surprise refusal.
[proposed] Offer a hands-free mode in the CLI only after a live path exists.

steps.what_happens: Mute disables the local audio track and sends a mute event on the data channel.
Provider stops hearing the microphone.
End: the browser sends session.close, then posts the usage report to the close endpoint.
The server reads the canonical record, closes it and settles billed seconds against the reservation or free allowance.
While a call runs the browser asks for the next minute block 15 s before the ceiling; if refused the call ends with the notice.
A tab that vanished is swept and settled by the server on the next start or active-session read.

aliases: Stop the task and keep talking
features.summary: Mobile's on-device voice companion has hold-to-talk. Web live voice has no push-to-talk. Interrupting is a provider-side behaviour on live calls: mobile shows a 'Go ahead' state when the person talks over the reply, web has no equivalent. Stopping the running task is separate from ending the call on web and mobile. The CLI has hold-to-record dictation.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person record only while a control is held, interrupt the assistant by speaking or tapping, and stop a running task without hanging up.
purpose.why_it_exists: Noisy places need push-to-talk. Natural conversation needs interruption. A wrong or long task needs a stop that does not end the call.
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users in noisy places; anyone who changes their mind mid-answer; CLI users dictating.
problems_solved: Background noise sending false turns.
Having to wait for a long reply to finish.
Having to hang up to cancel a tool run.
use_cases: On the mobile companion, hold the orb, speak, release to send.
Say 'wait' over the reply on mobile live voice and see 'Go ahead'.
Press 'Stop the task' on web to cancel a running action but keep talking.
In the CLI, hold SPACE to record and press Enter to stop.

where_to_find_it: Mobile push-to-talk: Settings > Voice, mode 'Push to talk' ('Hold the orb to speak, release to send.') and the hand icon on the companion screen labelled 'Switch to push-to-talk mode' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx:45-60; apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx:653-672). Default is off (apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:132).
Mobile live bar: 'Stop the task and keep talking' (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:674).
Web: 'Stop the task' button in the agent status row (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:595-607) and 'Do not send that' on the pending-utterance chip (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:39-40, 385-399).
CLI: SPACE to record, Enter or release to stop, Escape to cancel (voice.rs:735-765).
prerequisites: A call or the companion screen; for push-to-talk the 'Push to talk' mode must be on (mobile).
screens_and_controls: Companion orb: onPress, onPressIn, onPressOut (voice.tsx:CompanionOrb at 118-142; useVoiceConversation.ts:299-330).
Phase text in push-to-talk: 'Hold to talk' when idle and 'Release to send' while listening (voice.tsx:82-92).
journey: Push-to-talk (mobile companion): 1. turn the mode on. 2. press and hold the orb; if the assistant is speaking, its speech stops. 3. speak. 4. release; the audio is transcribed on the device and sent as a turn. 5. the reply is spoken.
Interrupt on live voice (mobile): 1. the assistant speaks. 2. the person talks. 3. the app sees user words arriving while the assistant is speaking and shows 'Go ahead'.
Stop the task (web, mobile live): 1. a tool runs and the status row appears. 2. press 'Stop the task'. 3. pending work is ended, the live model is told the task stopped, and the call stays open.
feedback_and_outputs: Web stop-task hint 'Stops the running action and keeps the call open.' (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:44-45).
Mobile companion label 'Voice paused when AGI left the foreground.' if the app leaves the screen (useVoiceConversation.ts:370-395).
CLI prints '(recording too short, skipped)' under 300 ms and '(max recording time 120s reached)' (voice.rs:~196, 735-740).
settings: Mobile voicePushToTalk (settingsStore.ts:132); Auto-listen is forced off when push-to-talk is on (useVoiceConversation.ts:~395).
CLI --voice-lang.

working: Mobile companion push-to-talk: press in starts capture (and stops any speech first), press out stops and processes (useVoiceConversation.ts:312-330; test VoiceConversationPtt.test.tsx:268).
Mobile companion tap-to-interrupt: tapping the orb while the assistant speaks stops the speech and starts listening (useVoiceConversation.ts:299-310).

Mobile live: user transcript arriving while the assistant is speaking sets interrupted and clears speaking (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:726-731; test live-voice-session.test.ts:303; label LiveVoiceBar.tsx:177-178).

Cancel the task without ending the call: web cancelBackendWork ends pending delegations, cancels function tools and appends an instruction that the user stopped the task (live-voice-session.ts:58-59, 1187-1200; use-voice-session.ts:974-977). Mobile exposes the same through onStopTask (LiveVoiceComposer.tsx:62).
Web 'Do not send that' cancels a pending utterance before it is sent (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:385-399; reducer event cancelUtterance in voice-session-machine.ts).
CLI hold-to-record dictation with a 300 ms minimum and 120 s maximum (voice.rs:35-47, 735-765).
incomplete: Web barge-in: the reducer has a bargeIn event and advanceBargeIn helper, but no web code calls them (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice/voice-session-machine.ts:156, 301; searched apps/web and packages/ui). Whether the provider stops the reply itself when the person talks is unknown.

Provider cannot cancel a Responses delegation; only closing the session cancels queued backend work, so 'Stop the task' ends the tools this app runs and tells the model to drop the result (live-voice-session.ts:1181-1186).
No control stops only the spoken audio on web; mute only stops the microphone.
disconnected_or_disabled: Push-to-talk is off by default on mobile (settingsStore.ts:132).

The desktop Tauri code has bargeInEnabled and bargeInSensitivity settings defaulting to off, but the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (apps/desktop/src/stores/settings/voice.ts:36, 59; AGENTS.md section 5).

steps.what_happens: Mobile companion: hold starts on-device speech recognition capture.
Release stops capture; text is produced on the device and sent as a normal chat message to the selected model (local or Cloud).
The reply is spoken by the device voice.
Live interrupt: provider streams the user's transcript while it is speaking; the app marks interruption.
Stop the task: the app cancels its own tool calls and sends an instruction event so the live model drops the result.
CLI: records audio with cpal, encodes a WAV, transcribes via the chosen backend, shows text, sends on Enter.

features.summary: The person picks the assistant's voice, spoken language, pace and, on web, voice reasoning. The choices travel to the server when a call starts; language and pace can change mid-call, a voice change waits for the next call. The web 'Play sample' button is hidden because the sample list is empty; mobile can preview device voices.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets people choose how the assistant sounds and which language it speaks and listens in, and hear a voice before choosing.
purpose.why_it_exists: Leading assistants offer several voices and languages; people need one they understand and like.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using voice, and people who speak languages other than English.
problems_solved: Wrong language heard or spoken.
Voice too fast or too slow.
Not knowing what a voice sounds like before picking it.
use_cases: Open 'Voice settings' on web and move to the next voice.
Set Language to a specific language instead of Auto-detect.
Set Speaking pace to Slower.
On mobile choose a voice in the picker sheet or preview a system voice in Voice & Language.

where_to_find_it: Web/Desktop: gear button labelled 'Voice settings' in the header while voice is on (VoiceHeaderLabel.tsx:12-35; testid voice-settings-trigger) opens a dialog titled 'Voice settings' (VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:40-45, 350).

Mobile: a bottom sheet voice picker (VoicePickerSheet.tsx) shown at first voice use and from the live bar 'Voice settings' button (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:325); Settings > Voice rows 'Speech language' and 'Voice' (settings/voice/index.tsx:416-422); the 'Voice & Language' screen with 'Voice mode' and 'Speaking style' sections (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice-language/index.tsx:104-130).
CLI: --voice-lang and /voice <lang> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:354, 5950-5955); supported languages are a fixed list of 20 codes (apps/cli/src/voice_languages.rs:8-29).
prerequisites: Web: voice session active to open the dialog (VoiceHeaderLabel only renders when voice is active, WebChatPage.tsx:7339).
screens_and_controls: Web dialog rows: voice carousel with 'Previous voice' and 'Next voice' and dots (13 voices); 'Voice reasoning' Instant or Thinking; 'Language' Auto-detect plus the app's supported languages; 'Speaking pace' Slower 0.75x, Normal 1x, Faster 1.25x, Fastest 1.5x; 'Chat intelligence' only when the Auto model is in use (VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:40-75, 282-283, 360-404).
Thinking option hint: 'Thinks longer on harder questions. Paid plans, from your next voice session' (VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:59-65).
Web audio output picker inside the dialog (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:652).
Web 'Play sample' button under the carousel, rendered only when a sample exists (VoiceSampleButton.tsx:58-61, 98-119).
Mobile 'Play sample' button and per-voice 'Preview <name>' buttons (VoicePickerSheet.tsx:70-110; voice-language/index.tsx:30-60).
journey: 1. During a call open 'Voice settings'.
2. Move through voices with the arrows or dots; a sample button appears if a sample exists.
3. Pick a language; pick a pace.
4. Language and pace are sent to the running call at once; the voice change applies from the next call.
5. Choices are remembered in the browser for the next call.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: the dialog says the voice, reasoning, language and pace can be chosen; with 'Chat intelligence' it adds the intelligence for typed replies (VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:42-44).
Web sample error text: 'The sample could not play. Try again later.' (VoiceSampleButton.tsx:70-76).
Mobile preview sentence: 'This is how AGI will sound.' (useVoicePreview.ts:9).
settings: Web store agi-web-voice-session persists voice, language, pace and reasoning (voice-session-store.ts:28, 206-212).
Mobile: liveVoice (the live voice id) and system voice, speed, pitch, speech language per Local or Cloud mode (settingsStore.ts:53; speechSettings.ts:15-56).

working: Server validates the voice and falls back to the default when invalid; trims the language or stores null; clamps pace to 0.5 to 2 (route.ts:264-267, 148-160; voice-session-store.ts:35-41).
The voice goes into the provider session audio output; language and pace go into the instructions (route.ts:520-530; live-voices.ts in packages/contracts/types/src:38-48).
Web updateSettings sends an instructions-append event and PATCHes the session settings; a voice change waits for the next session (live-voice-session.ts:673-707; settings/route.ts:20-90).
The settings are stored in the voice_sessions row and echoed in the create response (route.ts:723; settings/route.ts:84-93).
Web reasoning level is chosen by the user within what the plan allows (route.ts:337-340 via resolveLiveVoiceReasoning).
Mobile live start sends the chosen live voice id and the two-letter language (useLiveVoiceSession.ts:~300; liveVoiceSession.ts:345-350).
Mobile preview of system voices plays on the device through the speech owner (voice-language/index.tsx:199-290; test VoiceLanguagePreview.test.tsx:96).
CLI validates the language against its fixed list (voice.rs:84-97; voice_languages.rs).
incomplete: Voice preview from the sample manifest is empty, so 'Play sample' never shows on web and desktop, and mobile reads the same manifest (apps/web/public/voice-samples/manifest.json:1-3; VoiceSampleButton.tsx:61; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceSamples.ts:20-27). The generator script exists at scripts/generate-voice-samples.mjs and needs a server key run by the owner.

Language is applied as a text instruction to the model, not as a separate recognition setting, on web (live-voices.ts:38-41; live-voice-session.ts:681-690), and mobile sends only the first part of the language tag (useLiveVoiceSession.ts:~302).
disconnected_or_disabled: 'Chat intelligence' row appears only for the Auto model and eligible plans (WebChatPage.tsx:6838-6846).
Web 'Thinking' reasoning is for paid plans only per its hint; the exact enforcement is in resolveLiveVoiceReasoning, not opened [see unknowns].
not_available: Changing the voice mid-call on web: not possible by design of the provider (live-voice-session.ts:664-672).
VS Code and Chrome: none.

established.statement: The user picks the assistant voice, and the chosen voice is the one the conversation speaks with.
The user can hear a sample of a voice before choosing it.
The user can choose the spoken language, and it is applied to recognition.
Provide voice choice among the voice controls.
General settings must include voice and voice speed.

acceptance_criteria: The voice chosen before the call is the voice heard; an invalid voice id falls back to the default.
A language chosen mid-call changes the assistant's spoken language from the next turn.
A pace change is heard and recorded on the session row.
With an empty manifest no 'Play sample' button is shown and nothing errors.
With a populated manifest 'Play sample' plays and 'Stop' stops it.
Mobile system voice preview does not change the saved voice.
CLI rejects an unsupported language with the list.
inferred: The brief's 'applied to recognition' should be restated as 'applied by instruction to the model' unless a provider setting is found [inferred from live-voices.ts:38-41].
proposed: [proposed] Run the sample generator and commit the files, then add a test that the manifest is non-empty.
[proposed] Allow a voice change without losing the call by offering a quick restart.
[proposed] Show on mobile live voice the same pace choice as web.

steps.what_happens: The person chooses voice, language, pace; the store saves them in the browser.
At call start the browser posts voice, language, pace and reasoning to the server.
The server checks the voice id, normalises language and clamps pace, then builds the provider instructions with language and pace and sets the audio voice.
The provider speaks with that voice.
Mid-call language or pace: the browser sends an instruction event and PATCHes the record.
Preview: the page fetches the sample manifest and plays a file if one is listed.
Mobile device voices are previewed by the operating system speech engine.

data.where_stored: browser local storage (web); mobile settings stores; voice_sessions row for the running call
data.synced: Row is readable by other devices; local choices are not synced

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The voice is a feature of the voice_live slot's session; names are a fixed list of 13 voices in the shared contracts package (packages/contracts/types/src/live-voices.ts:7-21). Reasoning applies to the backend model by plan. Sample files are generated with a server key by a script and never at runtime. No model identifiers recorded here.

access_and_usage.account: Web needs a signed-in session to call the settings endpoint. Mobile on-device voice choice needs no account.
access_and_usage.permissions: CSRF and rate limit on the settings endpoint (settings/route.ts:23-32).
access_and_usage.subscription: Voice choice and language are open to any plan that can use voice; the 'Thinking' reasoning level is for paid plans per its on-screen hint (VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:62-65).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Pace bounds 0.5 to 2 with 0.05 steps (voice-session-store.ts:31-41). Voice id max 64 characters, language 2 to 32 characters (route.ts:150-153).
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for voice or language choice.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Only the 13 listed voices are accepted; others fall back to the default (route.ts:264; settings/route.ts:50-56 returns 400).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Voice list is fixed by the contracts package, tied to what the managed provider offers [inferred].
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web: no voice in Local. Mobile Local mode: the voice is a system voice with speed and pitch chosen on the device, and the speech language is stored per Local or Cloud mode (speechSettings.ts:15-56; voice-language/index.tsx:199-290). CLI: language only.

features.summary: Lets a person choose where the assistant's voice plays. On web and the public Desktop (which shows the web app) it is an 'Audio output' menu inside Voice settings. On iPhone it is an 'Audio route' sheet (Automatic, Speaker, Bluetooth, Headset). Live voice always records from the default microphone; a microphone choice exists only for dictation.

purpose.what_it_does: Controls which speaker or headset plays live voice replies (web, Desktop, iPhone) and records which microphone is in use. A web Settings > Voice page also has a 'Microphone' choice, but the code uses it for dictation only, not for live voice (apps/web/features/settings/sections/VoiceSection.tsx:125-168; apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:480-482).
purpose.why_it_exists: People use headsets, Bluetooth speakers and several microphones. A voice call that cannot be rerouted forces them to change the whole system output. The brief lists input choice, output choice and speaker/Bluetooth routing as separate items (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/048-voice-conversation-interface.md S48.18-S48.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone on web, Desktop or iPhone who starts a live voice conversation and has more than one audio device.
problems_solved: Voice plays through the wrong speaker.
On iPhone, voice plays out loud when a headset is wanted, or the reverse.
The person cannot tell which microphone the call is using (the mute button tooltip names it on web).
use_cases: On web, switch the reply voice from laptop speakers to a USB headset during a call.
On iPhone, force the call to the loud speaker, or prefer a paired Bluetooth headset.
On web, check which microphone the call opened by hovering the mute button.
In Settings > Voice, pick the microphone that dictation records from.

where_to_find_it: Web and public Desktop: start voice with the 'Start voice mode' button in the chat composer (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/VoiceEntryButton.tsx:9), tap the gear named 'Voice settings' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceHeaderLabel.tsx:10-27), then use the 'Audio output' control at the bottom of the dialog (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:407; apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:10-15).
Web and Desktop dictation microphone: Settings > Voice > 'Microphone', described 'Used for dictation' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/VoiceSection.tsx:136-150).

iPhone: the route button in the live voice bar, accessibility label 'Audio route, <name>' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:54; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:721).
Android: no route control (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/audioRoute.ts:59-61).
CLI: no device control; the default input device is used (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:528-533, 623-629).
prerequisites: Web output menu: a signed-in Cloud chat where voice is allowed, a browser that can set the audio sink, and at least two output devices (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:24-28, 103).
Device names show only after the browser has granted some audio access; before that an entry reads 'Audio output' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:30-33, 51-53).
iPhone: a Cloud chat with live voice available (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:21-27).
screens_and_controls: Web: menu button 'Audio output, <device>' (data-testid voice-audio-route-trigger) opening a radio menu 'Audio output device'; first entry shows 'System default' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:109-127, 130-134).
Web: mute button titled 'Turn off microphone, <microphone name>' so the active microphone is visible (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceComposer.tsx:54-55).

iPhone: sheet titled 'AUDIO ROUTE' with Automatic, Speaker, Bluetooth, Headset and a hint under each (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:114, 130-163; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/audioRoute.ts:12-24).
journey: 1. Start a live voice conversation (web: 'Start voice mode'; iPhone: live voice from the chat).
2. Open the output control (web: gear 'Voice settings', then 'Audio output'; iPhone: route button).
3. Pick a device or route.

4. Web: the browser is asked to move the reply audio element to that device and the menu closes (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:87-100). iPhone: the choice is saved and applied to the audio session (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:34-42).
5. Keep talking; replies play on the new device.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: the trigger label changes to the chosen device and a check mark shows in the menu (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:125, 141, 155).

Web: if the browser refuses the switch nothing is shown and the old route stays (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:92-95; test: apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.test.tsx:73).

iPhone: if the route cannot be applied, the sheet stays open with a polite message 'Could not switch audio to <route>. This call may use a different output.' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/audioRoute.ts:73-75; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:116-129). At call start an unapplied saved route shows the same notice (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:314-317).
settings: Web/Desktop: Settings > Voice > 'Microphone' (device id kept in the persisted voice input store, dictation only) (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:280-282, 438-441).
iPhone: saved audio route preference, default 'auto' (apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:58, 136, 157, 183).

working: Web output switching through the browser's audio-sink call on the live reply element, with keyboard menu support and a menu that disappears when fewer than two outputs exist (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:34-103).
Web device list refreshes on the browser's device-change event (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:61-65).
Web microphone name shown on the mute button (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:748, 839; apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:612-614).
Web Settings > Voice microphone choice is stored and used by dictation (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:280-282).
iPhone route sheet and call-start application of the saved route (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/audioRoute.ts:37-71; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:314-317).
Public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it carries the same web picker (doc: AGENTS.md section 5) [inferred for Electron audio-sink support].
incomplete: Live voice microphone choice: the live session asks the browser for the default microphone only (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:480-482); iPhone asks for default audio (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:298).

Web output choice is held in component state and not saved (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:79) [inferred: no store write]; each session builds a new reply audio element (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:489) and nothing re-applies the choice [inferred], so after a reconnect or pause/resume the menu may still show the old device while audio plays on the default.
Web refusal of a switch is silent (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:92-95).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web Settings > Voice 'Microphone' is not read by the live voice session; it feeds only dictation (apps/web/features/settings/sections/VoiceSection.tsx:139; apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:480-482).
not_available: Microphone choice for live voice on web, Desktop, iPhone and CLI.
Android route switching: the picker returns nothing off iOS (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/audioRoute.ts:59-61).
CLI output device: voice mode only records and prints text; it plays no audio (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:75-300).
VS Code and Chrome extension: no live voice.

established.statement: The user can choose which microphone voice uses.
The user can choose which speaker voice plays through.
On devices with a speaker and Bluetooth the user can route audio between speaker, earpiece/headset and Bluetooth.
Voice must have recoverable states for absent microphone and permission denial, and exit must release capture and playback.

acceptance_criteria: On web with two or more outputs and a browser that supports setting the audio sink, the Voice settings dialog shows an 'Audio output' control; choosing a device moves the reply audio to it and marks it.
With one output, or a browser that cannot switch, no output control is shown.
If the browser refuses a switch the previously selected device stays marked.
On iPhone the route sheet lists Automatic, Speaker, Bluetooth, Headset; choosing one is saved and applied, and an unappliable route shows the 'Could not switch audio' message.
On Android and CLI no route control appears.
Live voice starts on the microphone the person chose (currently fails: default microphone only).
inferred: The output choice should survive reconnect and pause/resume inside one call [inferred from the new audio element at apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:489].
A refused switch should tell the person, as iPhone does [inferred from apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/AudioRoutePicker.tsx:116-129].
proposed: [proposed] Pass the Settings > Voice microphone id to the live session's microphone request and show a microphone control next to 'Audio output'.
[proposed] Re-apply the chosen sink whenever a new session creates its reply element.
[proposed] Show a one-line notice when the browser refuses an output switch.

steps.what_happens: Web: the browser lists audio outputs and the person picks one.
Web: the reply audio element, fed by the realtime connection's remote track, is told to play on the chosen device.

Live voice asks the browser for the default microphone with echo cancellation, noise suppression and gain control, and streams it to the voice provider over a realtime connection set up through our server.
The provider session is created by our server with a provider key; audio then flows between the browser and the provider.
iPhone: the chosen route becomes an iOS audio-session category with options and is applied through the speech-recognition module.
Dictation (not live voice) asks for the saved microphone as an ideal device id.

features.summary: Lets a person leave live voice and keep going in the same chat by typing. On web the voice screen also has a typed field that sends a normal text turn while the call stays open. iPhone has 'Type instead' to leave the call. In the CLI, spoken text can be edited before sending, and Esc returns to the same typed session.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a way to move between speaking and typing without losing the conversation. Voice turns are saved as messages in the same chat as typed ones, so ending a call leaves a normal chat to continue (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6739-6790).
purpose.why_it_exists: Voice fails or is unwelcome at times: noisy rooms, limits reached, no microphone, sensitive text. The brief requires that unfinished work can continue in text (S48.38). The brief calls typing during voice and transcript editing not applicable, but the code has both on web and the CLI.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop users in a voice call, iPhone users in a live call, CLI users in /voice.
problems_solved: A usage limit or error ends the call but the task is not finished.
Names, numbers and code are hard to speak.
A wrong transcript is sent to the assistant (CLI lets the person fix it first).
use_cases: Ask something by voice, then type a precise follow-up in the voice screen on web.
Hit the voice limit, press 'Continue in text', and keep the same chat.
On iPhone tap 'Type instead' to bring up the keyboard in the same chat.
In the CLI press 'e' to edit the transcribed sentence, then Enter to send.

steps.what_happens: Web: Enter in the voice field calls submitTyped, which marks the state as streaming and calls the chat send path.
The typed message goes through the normal chat pipeline on our servers to the chat's model.
Each final spoken turn is added to the list and saved to the conversation without a model call.
Leaving voice closes the realtime connection, then records the session close and its usage.
iPhone: 'Type instead' hides the bar; the effect cleanup closes the call and settles it.
CLI: audio is recorded locally, then transcribed by the signed-in AGI account, the OpenAI transcription API, or a local whisper binary; the text is sent to the agent session like typed text.
CLI Local privacy mode blocks cloud transcription unless AGIWORKFORCE_VOICE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Spoken turns on web use the realtime voice model (managed OpenAI route) for speech and a plan-based backend model for delegated work (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:311-318). A typed turn uses the chat's selected model, or the 'Chat intelligence' choice set in Voice settings (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:45). CLI transcription uses AGI managed, OpenAI Whisper API with OPENAI_API_KEY, or a local whisper binary (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-6).

access_and_usage.account: Web and iPhone live voice need sign-in (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:19). CLI managed transcription needs 'agi login'; other backends need a key or binary (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:127-143).
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone permission. CLI asks for agreement before recording and states where audio goes (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:379-420).
access_and_usage.subscription: Typing in a call has no rule of its own. Opening voice needs allowVoice on the plan (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:311).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Voice minutes are metered per call (see F048-10). Typing and the typed model turn follow normal chat limits, not voice minutes [inferred]. The CLI records at most 120 seconds and ignores clips under 300 ms (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:36-41).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Live voice on web is blocked for chats on a local model or non-managed provider; those chats keep the text composer (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907-5911).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Live voice is managed OpenAI only. CLI transcription may use OpenAI, AGI managed or local whisper.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web: no voice entry in a Local chat; typing continues as normal. iPhone: 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-18). CLI Local privacy mode: cloud transcription is refused unless AGIWORKFORCE_VOICE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1; a local whisper binary works with no egress (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:62-72, 481-483).

features.summary: While a live voice call is running, the screen shows what tools the assistant is using and what they returned, asks for approval on screen before sensitive actions, and links to files a tool made. Approval is by tapping Allow or Deny, never by speaking. Tool text is cut to 32,000 characters before the voice model reads it.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the live voice assistant run tools (web fetch, code, Office files, connector tools, AGI Work tasks) and keeps the person informed and in control through on-screen status, results, approvals and a Stop the task button.
purpose.why_it_exists: Spoken conversation hides what the assistant is doing. Sensitive actions need explicit consent that a spoken 'yes' cannot give safely, so the prompt tells the model a spoken yes does not approve (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts:437-445).

steps.what_happens: The realtime voice model decides to call a function tool; the browser receives the call over the data channel.
The bridge posts the call to our tool route.
Our server checks CSRF, sign-in, rate limit and the session, then applies the approval gate and tool permissions.
If approval is needed the server returns approval_required; the screen shows the card and the model is told to say it waits for approval.
Tap Allow or Deny; the browser resends the call with the decision.
The tool runs (web fetch with egress guard and site rules, code sandbox, Office file creation, connector tools) and output is cut to 32,000 characters.
Output goes back over the data channel and the model speaks the result.
Opening a file: web link in a new tab; Desktop detached window; iPhone download then share sheet.
