features.summary: When the live voice link drops, the app shows 'Reconnecting, attempt N of 3' and retries with growing delays; if that fails it shows an error with 'Try again'. When voice minutes run out it ends the call with a clear limit notice and, on web, 'Upgrade' and 'Continue in text'. Minutes are reserved one minute at a time.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps a call alive through short network drops and stops it cleanly when the plan's voice time or budget is gone, telling the person what happened and what to do next.
purpose.why_it_exists: Networks drop; realtime voice costs money per minute. The product must not silently overspend, keep charging a dead call, or leave the person with a broken screen (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-billing.ts:15-28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone using live voice on web, Desktop and iPhone; the plan decides when the limit is reached.
problems_solved: A flaky network ends the call for good.
A provider outage re-reserving minutes on every drop (the retry budget is bounded).
Unclear 'it stopped' with no reason or reset time.
A dead call still counting against usage.
use_cases: Walk between rooms, lose Wi-Fi briefly, and the call resumes by itself.
A Free account uses up its monthly 10 minutes mid-call and sees the limit with an upgrade choice.
A paid account hits a rolling 5-hour limit and sees when it resets.
Close the laptop; the server closes the stale session after the lease.

where_to_find_it: Web and public Desktop: notice row above the orb in the voice screen (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:303-361).

iPhone: status line 'Reconnecting live voice...' and an error box with 'Try again' and 'Type a message instead' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:173, 378-420); a limit that ends the call appears as a notice line above the inline voice bar (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1771-1777, 2814).
prerequisites: A live voice call in progress or starting.
screens_and_controls: Web: status text 'Reconnecting, attempt <n> of <max>' (data-testid voice-reconnecting).
Web error after retries: message and 'Try again' (voice-error).
Web limit: message, 'Upgrade' (opens the plan dialog) and 'Continue in text' (voice-usage-limit, voice-usage-upgrade).
Web pause: 'Paused. The call is closed and nothing is being used. Resume to pick up this conversation.' with 'Resume' (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:62-65, 362-376).
iPhone: no Upgrade control in the voice bar; text only.
journey: Drop: 1. The link breaks. 2. The call is settled as 'connection_lost' and a retry is scheduled after 1 second, then 2, then 4 (max 8) (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:165-168, 241-254, 665-678). 3. The row shows the attempt count. 4. A new session opens; if it stays up 30 seconds the attempt count resets (269-279). 5. After 3 failed attempts the row reads 'The voice connection could not be restored.' with 'Try again'.
Limit at start: 1. Start voice. 2. Server refuses; the row shows the server's sentence (with reset time for known limits) plus Upgrade and Continue in text.

Limit mid-call: 1. About 15 seconds before the reserved minute ends the app asks for the next minute (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:60, 394-427). 2. If refused, the call ends at the ceiling with the limit row.
feedback_and_outputs: Limit text examples: '5-hour limit reached. <reset>.', 'Weekly limit reached. <reset>.', 'Monthly limit reached. <reset>.' (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:259-269); fallback 'Voice ran out of included minutes on this plan, so the session ended. Nothing was lost from the conversation.' (line 71-72); plan without voice: "Voice needs usage your plan doesn't include. Upgrade to talk with voice, or continue in text." (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/voice-session-budget.ts:40-44).
Toast when closing fails: 'This voice session did not close cleanly, so it may keep counting toward your voice usage for a few more minutes.' (use-voice-session.ts:309-312).
settings: None for reconnect. Limits come from the plan (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47-51).

working: Web reconnect with bounded attempts, backoff, immediate retry on the browser 'online' event, and manual retry after the budget is spent (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:165-168, 241-279, 928-929; VoiceModeSurface.tsx:303-313, 346-361).
Server detection of lost connections: keepalive every 15 seconds, 60 second timeout, 5 second disconnect grace (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:45-47, 856, 878).
Web block extension: second block requested 15 seconds before the ceiling, retried every 10 seconds on server errors, call ended when refused (use-voice-session.ts:60-62, 394-427).

Server: one-minute blocks, 10 minute lease, free monthly allowance with grants and settlement, paid plans reserve against the usage budget (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-billing.ts:20, 28; apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:178-235, 242-269; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:346-413).
Limit errors carry reset time (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:271-275; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/voice-session-budget.ts:184-198).
Abandoned sessions are settled when the same user starts voice again and by a cron job (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:398-403; apps/web/app/api/cron/recover-reservations/route.ts:12).

iPhone has the same 3 attempt reconnect, the same extension timing, and shows the server sentence at start refusal (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:66-72, 261-294, 400-428; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:158-168, 842-863).
incomplete: iPhone reads only the message and code of a refusal, not the reset time (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:158-168) [inferred: web reads resets_at at apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:279-283].
iPhone voice bar has no Upgrade control (rg found no 'Upgrade' in apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx).
iPhone has no network-online trigger for an immediate retry in the code read (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found.
not_available: CLI and VS Code/Chrome: no live voice session to reconnect or meter (CLI uses push-to-talk transcription).

Background reconnect: web ends the call on page hide and iPhone ends it on background (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:926; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:486-490).

established.statement: When the connection drops, a reconnecting state is shown and the session reconnects or says it could not.
When voice usage is exhausted the user sees a clear usage-limit notice in voice.
Voice draws on the same usage budget as chat, one minute at a time, settling at what it used.
Voice must have recoverable states for permission denial, absent microphone and exit.

acceptance_criteria: Cutting the network mid-call shows 'Reconnecting, attempt 1 of 3' within about a second and the call resumes when the network returns.
After three failed attempts the row shows 'The voice connection could not be restored.' and 'Try again'.
A Free account with 10 minutes used in the month is refused at start with a limit notice that includes the reset date and offers Upgrade and Continue in text on web.
A call crossing a minute boundary asks for the next minute; when refused the call ends with the limit row and no more usage is recorded.
Closing the tab or ending the call settles usage; an unsettled session stops counting after the lease and one block.
A microphone refusal does not trigger reconnect attempts.
inferred: iPhone should show the reset time like web [inferred from web behaviour].
iPhone should link to plans from the limit notice if the platform allows [inferred; store rules for mobile were not read].
proposed: [proposed] Add an online-event retry on iPhone.
[proposed] Give the iPhone limit notice the same wording with reset time.

steps.what_happens: Start: the browser builds a realtime offer and posts it with voice, language and conversation to our server.
The server checks sign-in, subscription access, capability flag, plan allows voice, model training rules.
Free plan: grant the first minute from the monthly allowance. Paid plans: check budget and tier unit allowance and reserve the first minute.
The server asks the voice provider to create the session and returns the answer and settlement ceiling.
The browser extends the call one minute at a time before the ceiling.
On drop the browser settles with reason connection_lost and retries.
On end the browser posts close with seconds used; the server settles to usage, never above what was granted.
A lost browser leaves a lease; after 10 minutes the session counts as ended and its reservation is settled by the next start or a cron job.

steps.what_happens: A file is chosen; the browser reads it, downsizes a photo to JPEG, or reads a PDF as base64.
Size is checked against the connection's maximum message (at most 256 KB).
The item is sent over the realtime data channel to the voice provider session, which hands it to its backend model that can read images and files.
The live model is quietly told a file arrived so it refers questions to the backend.
Tool image: our tool route stores a file and returns its /api/files address; the screen loads it.
On page hide the web call is closed and settled; on iPhone background the call ends.

features.summary: On web, a person who has paired a browser to their computer can speak a task into the 'Your computer' page or the Code composer using a 'Start voice input' button. This is dictation: speech becomes text, which is then sent to the computer as a task. It is not live conversation. iPhone has no such control.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a spoken sentence into text for a task that Desktop on another computer runs, so the person can steer a coding or computer task without typing (apps/web/features/remote-dispatch/components/RemoteComputerPage.tsx:283-299).
purpose.why_it_exists: Coding and computer tasks are long to type; voice makes quick direction possible from a browser. The brief lists steering a remote coding session by voice (S48.40).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in web user who has Desktop running on a linked computer, or who uses the Code composer with a Cloud session.

steps.what_happens: The browser records microphone audio in the voice input store.
The recording is posted to our transcription route, which checks sign-in, the dictation switch and, on Free, the monthly voice allowance.
The route passes the audio to OpenAI's transcription service and returns text; our servers keep no audio.
The text lands in the task box (insert) or is sent at once (send).
The task is wrapped in a signed envelope and sent over the relay to the paired computer.
Desktop on the computer runs the task with the folders, apps and browser allowed there.
Status returns over the same relay to the task list.

aliases: Dictate with AGI Cloud (VS Code button label)
features.summary: Lets a person speak a message into the composer instead of typing it. The speech becomes text in the message box, ready to edit, or is sent at once on web, desktop and phone. Web, desktop, CLI and VS Code upload the audio to AGI Cloud. The phone transcribes on the device. Chrome uses the browser's speech service.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns one spoken recording into text that lands in the message field (web, desktop, phone, Chrome, VS Code, and CLI /dictate) or is sent as a message (web send button, phone send, CLI /voice after confirmation). It is dictation, a single recording turned into text. It is not the live two-way voice conversation (see F049-05). (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-dictation.ts:189; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1381; apps/cli/src/voice.rs:310)
purpose.why_it_exists: Speaking is faster than typing and helps on phones and for people who cannot type easily. The project requirements ask for a mic control, a separate dictation versus live voice, and edit-before-send. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:912-920; doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1001-1003)
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on web, desktop, phone, CLI, Chrome or VS Code who prefers to talk. Free-plan users get a monthly voice allowance on the cloud path. (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47)
problems_solved: Typing long messages on a phone or in a terminal is slow.
A mis-heard dictation can be fixed before it is sent because the text lands in the editable field.
Local-only users on phone get dictation with no upload and no payment.
use_cases: Web user clicks the mic, speaks a paragraph, clicks stop, edits two words, presses send.
Phone user holds the mic, speaks, releases, and the text is added to the draft.
CLI user types /dictate, holds SPACE, speaks, and the text is placed in the composer without sending.
VS Code user clicks the sidebar mic, records in a browser tab, and the text returns to the draft.

journey: Person clicks or taps the mic (or uses the shortcut / slash command).
The app checks it is allowed (setting on, kill switch off, cloud destination on web; phone Voice setting and on-device support).
The app asks for microphone permission if needed. Phone shows the intro sheet on first use.
Recording starts. Web and desktop draw a waveform; phone shows a pulsing ring and live transcript; CLI shows REC, a level meter and elapsed seconds.
Person stops: web stop square (insert) or send/Enter (send); phone tap again or release hold; CLI release SPACE or ENTER; Chrome click again; VS Code 'Stop and transcribe'.
A 'Transcribing' state shows on web and desktop. Phone shows processing. CLI shows a 'Transcribing...' spinner.

Text is added after the existing message with a single space and the field is focused (web: ChatComposerNew.tsx:2023-2036; phone: ChatInput.tsx:166-171, 608-617). CLI /voice shows the text and waits for ENTER/e/r/ESC.
Person edits and sends, or the send path sends it.

CLI: '(no speech detected)', 'Transcription failed: ...' (voice.rs:208-225).
Web usage refusals: 'This month's voice minutes are used up. Type instead.' etc. (voice-input-store.ts:125-130).

The brief marks S49.28 desktop missing, so the brief is out of date (apps/desktop/electron/__tests__/dictationElsewhere.test.ts exists).

CLI: three backends (AGI account, user's OpenAI key, local whisper program), recording notice that must be agreed, 120 second cap, minimum 300 ms, confirmation step (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:37-40, 379-415, 968-1010).
Chrome: browser SpeechRecognition appended to composer, microphone notice, permission pre-check (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/voice.ts:136-283).

VS Code: capture in a local browser page, upload to managed endpoint, result posted to the draft (ChatStateManager.ts:5730-5810; dictationClient.ts:12-43). The brief says missing; the code and tests exist, so the brief is out of date (apps/extension-vscode/src/__tests__/dictationClient.test.ts). The matrix doc says VS Code cannot record audio (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:328), which the browser-page design works around.
incomplete: Interim text while speaking: not required (brief S49.04 n/a; doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:128). Only phone shows it (ChatInput.tsx:1976); Chrome sets interimResults false (voice.ts:206); web, CLI, VS Code show none.

Undo of inserted text: unverified in every app (brief S49.30). Web appends through appendComposerMessage (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2023); whether the browser undo stack keeps it was not established. CLI records composer undo (tui_app.rs:7527-7531).

Phone filler-word cleanup removes words such as 'like' and 'actually' and replaces the draft when the transcript starts with a command-like phrase (packages/platform/utils/src/voice.ts:11-44; ChatInput.tsx:166-171). Whether this is wanted is not documented.
disconnected_or_disabled: CLI voice code is compiled out by default; builds without the voice feature report that audio capture is unavailable (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:77-100; apps/cli/Cargo.toml:126-132). The release workflow adds it for some targets (.github/workflows/release-cli.yml:240-278).
Web kill switch 'dictation' can close the feature server-side and per version (use-dictation.ts:44-52; apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:18-26).
Old Tauri desktop code (apps/desktop/src) has its own voice hooks; not examined (unknown).
not_available: Web and desktop: no dictation with a Local model or own-key model selected (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2055-2060).
VS Code: not available in untrusted, remote, or local-model sessions (ChatStateManager.ts:5710-5722).
Phone: no cloud transcription path in dictation; unsupported Android below API 33 hides the mic (VoiceInputButton.tsx:91-92; voiceInput.ts:291).

established.statement: A microphone control in the composer turns speech into text in the message field.
The transcript lands in the message field where the user can edit it before sending.
While dictating, interim text should appear before the recording ends, but the brief marks this n/a everywhere and the founder decisions say ChatGPT and Claude have no interim dictation text.
When dictation ends, the final transcript is produced and delivered.
Text inserted by dictation can be undone with the normal undo action (unverified).
Dictation is separate from live voice. Mobile mic requests native permission, text is editable, user can cancel or send, and voice privacy says whether audio is local or cloud.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to own-key or managed cloud.

acceptance_criteria: On web with a cloud model selected and microphone allowed, click mic, speak, click stop: text appears at the end of the message field, cursor in field, nothing sent.
On web, click send (or Enter) while recording: the transcript is added and the message is sent.
On web with a Local or own-key model selected, the mic gives the message 'Cloud dictation is unavailable for this destination. Type instead.' and no audio is recorded or uploaded.
On phone, with airplane mode on and the language model installed, dictation still produces text.
On CLI /dictate, the text is placed in the composer and is not sent until ENTER.
With the dictation kill switch closed, web refuses to record and shows the reason.
A silent recording shows an empty-result message, not an inserted blank.
inferred: The phone text should also be editable before sending when stopped with stop rather than send [inferred from ChatInputDictation test 'delegates stop as review and inserts without sending' (apps/mobile/__tests__/ChatInputDictation.test.tsx)].
Chrome audio goes to the browser vendor's speech service, but whether it is on-device was not established in code [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Verify undo (S49.30) with a test in each composer and record the result.
[proposed] Show a visible provider label on web when audio is uploaded to AGI Cloud, matching the phone and CLI notices.
[proposed] Update the brief rows for VS Code and desktop dictation elsewhere.

steps.what_happens: Web/desktop: click mic; useDictation checks the setting, the kill switch and the destination, then asks the store to record with MediaRecorder (100 ms slices).
On stop, the whole clip is sent as multipart (file, model from the voice_transcription routing slot, optional two-letter language) to /api/voice/transcribe.

Server checks region, CSRF, rate limit, sign-in or key, age gate, organization and spend policy, size, type, content scan, privacy setting, plan and quota, then reserves usage (or a free-allowance grant).
Server forwards the audio to the speech provider with a 60 second timeout; the audio is not stored.
Server settles usage and cost and returns the provider JSON; the client trims the text and appends it to the composer.
Phone: native recognizer is started with on-device required, partial text streams to the composer, final text returned on stop.

CLI: cpal records 16 kHz mono, writes a WAV in a private folder, sends it to the chosen backend (AGI account endpoint, OpenAI Whisper with the user's key, or local whisper program), then deletes the folder.
Chrome: browser SpeechRecognition produces text; where the browser processes audio is decided by the browser.
VS Code: the extension serves a one-time local page, the user records in the browser, the extension uploads the audio with the account token to the managed endpoint.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Web, desktop, VS Code and CLI managed use the catalog routing slot 'voice_transcription', resolved by getRoutingSlotModel; the server requires it to be a live speech-to-text model from the openai provider, else it throws (route.ts:487-504). A client-requested model is honored only if it is a live openai speech-to-text catalog entry (route.ts:517-527). The server key is a server environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY (name only) (route.ts:725). The CLI own-key path posts to OpenAI directly with the user's OPENAI_API_KEY (voice.rs:1089-1100). Phone uses the operating system recognizer. No other provider is wired for dictation.

access_and_usage.account: Web, desktop, VS Code and CLI managed backend need sign-in (route.ts:297; ChatStateManager.ts:5762). Phone on-device dictation: none found in the code requiring sign-in. CLI own-key and local backends: no AGI sign-in needed (voice.rs:427-441). Chrome: none found.
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone permission everywhere. Phone also speech recognition access (VoiceInputButton.tsx reportError 'Voice input needs microphone and speech access'). Desktop only grants audio media permission to the trusted cloud origin (apps/desktop/electron/permissionPolicy.ts:43-53). CLI and Chrome show a recording notice before first use (voice.rs:379-415; voice.ts:76-100). Age gate: adults only for session users (route.ts:307-316).
access_and_usage.subscription: Free plan has a monthly voice allowance of 10 minutes (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47-58; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1256). Paid plans use assertTierUnitAllowance for voice_minutes and a usage reservation (route.ts:594-620). CLI also checks the canUseVoice capability before managed transcription (voice.rs:978-986; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:282). Web hides nothing behind a plan; the code comment says voice input remains capability-neutral (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6937).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit 'audio-transcription' (route.ts:294). Upload cap 25 MB, types listed in route.ts:399-411. Seconds estimated from file size (route.ts:560-570 area). Phone 60 s (voiceInput.ts:68). CLI 120 s with a 300 ms minimum (voice.rs:37-40). VS Code 120 s and 3 MB (apps/extension-vscode/src/protocol/dictationLimits.ts:1-3). features.summary: Controls to end, throw away or redo a dictation. Web keeps a failed recording in memory so Try again re-sends it. The CLI offers R to retry. The phone cancels with X and re-records on failure. Pause, resume and a timer are not built for dictation, except a whole-seconds counter in the CLI.

purpose.what_it_does: Stops a recording and gets its text, discards it without inserting anything, retries a failed transcription, and shows how long a recording has run. (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:385-436; apps/cli/src/voice.rs:357-377, 762-771)
purpose.why_it_exists: A long dictation should not be lost because the network blinked, and a person must be able to back out. The brief requires retry (S49.06), discard (S49.07), pause and resume (S49.18) and a duration display (S49.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone dictating, especially long or noisy recordings.
problems_solved: Losing a long recording after a temporary error.
Accidental recordings inserting junk text.
Not knowing how long recording has run (CLI only).

Web: user presses Escape to discard.
CLI: transcription fails; user presses R to retry the same recording.
Phone: user taps X to cancel.

CLI: '[R to retry this recording, any other key to drop it]' after an error; ESC to discard after the text is shown; REC line with elapsed seconds (voice.rs:357-377, 762-771).
Chrome: no discard or retry control found (voice.ts:252-270); this follows decision D-2026-09-28-23 listing retry of a failed dictation as outside the side panel's scope.
VS Code: 'Cancel' on the recorder page and a cancelDictation message (dictationPage.ts:91; ChatStateManager.ts:1648-1650).

features.summary: Turns a whole recording or audio file into text in one request. Web, desktop, CLI and VS Code use it after you stop recording. Developers can call the API with an audio file. The phone has an on-device file transcriber. No app screen lets a person upload an existing audio file.

purpose.what_it_does: Accepts one complete audio file, checks it, bills it against the person's plan, sends it to the speech provider and returns the text. (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:273-858)
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S49.09 requires batch transcription; S49.08 requires audio-file upload. It is the one cloud path shared by dictation and developer use.
purpose.who_uses_it: The web, desktop, CLI and VS Code dictation flows; developers holding an API key with the inference:write scope; the phone's voice screen for on-device file transcription.
problems_solved: One consistent, quota-checked transcription path.
Files that fail content checks are refused before provider spend.
use_cases: Developer posts a recording with a file field and optional language and gets JSON with text.
Web dictation uploads a recorded blob.
CLI uploads a WAV from a push-to-talk session.
Phone transcribes a recorded voice note on the device.

where_to_find_it: Developers: POST /api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions with a Bearer token or API key (route.ts:297).

prerequisites: Sign-in or an API key with the inference:write scope; adult-eligibility for session users; plan or free allowance remaining.

working: Full server pipeline: region block, CSRF, rate limit 'audio-transcription', auth, project spend limits for API keys, age gate for sessions, managed compute gates, organization and model policy, workspace budget (route.ts:273-360, 533-545).
Validation: 25 MB cap, MIME allow-list (mpeg, mp3, mp4, m4a, wav, webm, ogg, flac variants), magic-byte check, content scan (route.ts:398-500).
Billing: reservation per request for paid plans; monthly free allowance grant and settle for the free plan; refund on provider failure (route.ts:594-720).
Provider call with 60 s timeout to the openai provider; usage settlement from provider token usage or an estimate (route.ts:722-850).
Dictation wrapper checks the 'dictation' kill switch first (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:18-29).

steps.what_happens: Client posts multipart audio to the endpoint.
Server runs region, CSRF, rate limit, auth, age or project spend, managed and policy gates.
Server reads the form, checks size, type, magic bytes and content scan.
Server resolves the catalog speech model, privacy check, builds provider form (file, model, language).
Server reserves usage or free-allowance seconds before spending.
Server calls the provider with the platform key and waits up to 60 seconds.
Server settles cost and returns the provider JSON.

features.summary: A spoken, two-way conversation with the assistant. The client opens a live session on the server, streams audio over a peer connection and reads transcript updates as words are spoken. Web, desktop and phone have it. The CLI, Chrome and VS Code do not.

purpose.what_it_does: Streams the person's speech to a live voice provider through a session created by the server, and shows input and output transcript text as it arrives; the assistant answers by voice. (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:488-540, 996-1020; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:533-565)
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S49.10 asks for streaming transcription with text during speech. Requirements say live voice is separate from dictation. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:918, 1003)
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people with a plan that allows voice, or Free users within the monthly allowance.
problems_solved: Hands-free conversation.
Natural interruption of the assistant while it speaks.
use_cases: Web user clicks 'Start voice mode', talks, sees the live transcript, ends the session.
Phone user starts live voice and pauses the call.
User types a message during voice mode, which is sent as a normal turn.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop: 'Start voice mode' button in the composer when the field is empty and the capability allows (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/VoiceEntryButton.tsx:9; ChatComposerNew.tsx:6951-6955).

Phone: live voice bar with pause, mute and call time (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:231-232).
prerequisites: Signed in; plan allows voice (getTierPolicy(plan).allowVoice) or Free allowance remains; capability canUseVoice not closed (route.ts:299-322); microphone permission; on phone a first-use disclosure sheet (VoiceOnboardingSheet.tsx VOICE_DISCLOSURE).
screens_and_controls: Web: mute toggle (Space when the field is empty), type field with Enter to send, round close control or Escape to end (VoiceComposer.test.tsx cases).

Phone: status text such as 'Connecting live voice...', 'Listening', 'Muted, tap the mic to talk', 'Speaking, talk any time to interrupt', 'Reconnecting live voice...', 'Live voice stopped' (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:166-182).
journey: Person starts voice mode.
The client asks the microphone, builds a peer connection, and posts its offer to /api/voice/live/sessions.
Server checks entitlement, voice budget or free allowance, builds instructions and tools, calls the live provider, and returns the answer and session id.
Audio streams; transcript delta events update the screen.
Person talks, types, mutes or ends; the client closes the session through the close endpoint, which settles usage.
feedback_and_outputs: Live transcript text and status label; error states with plain messages from describeLiveSessionFailure (route.ts:92).
settings: Web Settings > Voice: voice carousel, live voice language picker and reasoning level (VoiceSection.tsx:93-100 area).

Sub-routes: active, [sessionId]/close, extend, settings, tools (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/).
Web client: peer connection, data channel, keepalive 15 s, disconnect grace 5 s, transcript deltas (live-voice-session.ts:41-55, 488-540, 996-1020).
Phone client: same server contract through liveVoiceSession.ts (LIVE_VOICE_SESSION_PATH use at line 343), pause and elapsed timer (LiveVoiceBar.tsx).
Desktop shows the web app so it shares the web client.

not_available: CLI, Chrome and VS Code: no streaming dictation (brief S49.10; CLI voice.rs is batch).

purpose.what_it_does: Would take a long recording of a meeting and turn it into a transcript, a summary, a list of action items, a list of decisions and a follow-up email draft, then link all of it to a project. None of this exists as a product feature in any of the six apps. [inferred from the brief marking S49.16 and S49.20 to S49.24 missing in every app] (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/049-dictation-transcription-and-recording.md)

established.statement: The user can record a meeting and get it transcribed.
A recorded meeting produces a summary.
Action items are extracted from a recording transcript.
Decisions made are summarised from a recording transcript.
A follow-up email draft is generated from a recording.
A recording and its transcript can be associated with a project.

acceptance_criteria: A person can start and stop a recording longer than the current 60 to 120 second clip limits on at least web, desktop and mobile, with a visible elapsed time.
The finished recording produces a transcript without the person pasting audio anywhere.
A summary, a list of action items, a list of decisions and an email draft are produced from the transcript and shown together.
The person can attach the result to a project and find it again from that project.
A notice says what is recorded and where it goes before capture starts.
The feature obeys the same subscription, quota and Local, own key and Cloud rules as other voice features, and a refusal says why.
inferred: Meeting length audio will exceed the 25 MB upload cap of the transcription endpoint at common bitrates, so recording must be split into chunks or compressed. [inferred from route.ts:398]
Because transcription is metered against voice minutes for paid plans, a long meeting needs a clear quota message. [inferred from route.ts:594-596]
proposed: Record in chunks on the device and transcribe each chunk, then run summary steps on the joined text. [proposed]
Reuse the existing project template for meeting notes as the destination for the summary. [proposed]
Offer an on-device transcription path on phone and desktop so Local mode works without any subscription. [proposed]

features.summary: People can save a chat, including dictated messages, as a file and delete chats. Dictated text is ordinary message text. Audio is not kept, so there is no audio download and no separate recording retention setting, except the command line's temporary folder cleared after an hour.

purpose.what_it_does: Exports a conversation to a file (web: markdown, PDF, Word, HTML or JSON; phone: PDF, text or markdown; command line: markdown or JSON; VS Code: markdown) and lets people delete a chat. Dictated words are saved as normal messages, so they travel with the chat. Original audio is not stored, so audio download does not exist.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires transcript export, audio download and retention and deletion controls for recordings and transcripts (S49.25 to S49.27).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who dictates into chats and wants a copy of the text, or wants dictated content removed.
problems_solved: Keeping a copy of a conversation outside the app
Removing a conversation that holds dictated text
Knowing that no raw audio is retained by the web dictation route
use_cases: Export a dictated chat as a Word file on web
Share a chat as a PDF from the phone
Export a CLI session as JSON with /export
Delete a chat that contains private dictated text

features.summary: Before the first capture, some apps tell the person what is recorded and where it goes. Phone shows an introduction sheet with a Continue button. Chrome shows a note with Continue and Not now. Command line asks for ENTER or ESC. VS Code's capture page shows a sentence. Web and desktop show no notice in the code I opened.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a short disclosure before microphone capture so a person knows if audio stays on the device or goes to a server or provider, and lets them continue or cancel.
purpose.why_it_exists: S49.17 requires a notice of what is recorded and where it goes, with agreement, before audio is captured. AGENTS.md section 6 requires explicit consent for moves across trust boundaries.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using dictation for the first time in an app.
problems_solved: Surprise that speech leaves the device
No record of agreement to record
Different destinations (account, own key, local program) look the same without a notice
use_cases: First tap on the phone microphone shows the introduction sheet
First microphone click in Chrome side panel shows the note
First /voice in the CLI shows the agreement line
VS Code user sees the sentence on the browser capture page

established.statement: Before audio is captured, the user sees a notice of what is recorded and where it goes, and must agree.
Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route Local audio to BYOK or cloud.
The CLI notice must name the destination.

In the CLI, the first /voice shows the destination and ENTER agrees; ESC cancels and no recording is made.
In the CLI, changing the destination (for example from a key to a managed account) asks again.
On web and desktop, a notice or an accepted decision exists before first capture (currently fails).
VS Code's capture page states the destination before recording.

aliases: Dictate into the app you are using
features.summary: On the Mac desktop app, when switched on, the dictation shortcut opens a small floating bar over the app in front. You speak, press the shortcut again, and the text is typed into that app. It never types into password prompts, and falls back to the clipboard with a notice. Off by default; macOS only.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person dictate text into any app, not just the product window, using the global dictation shortcut.
purpose.why_it_exists: S49.28 requires a global desktop shortcut that dictates into the focused application. Competing assistants offer system-wide dictation.
purpose.who_uses_it: Mac desktop users who write in other apps such as mail, notes or editors.
problems_solved: Having to dictate in the product window and copy text across
Typing by hand in other apps
use_cases: Dictate an email body into the mail app
Dictate a note into a notes app
Dictate a message into a chat app

where_to_find_it: Desktop settings, row 'Dictate into the app you are using' with a switch (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:57, 380-386). The row is only offered when the host reports the preference, which main.ts does on macOS only (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1989-1991).

Shortcut: 'Dictation' shortcut, default Alt+Shift+V, choices include CommandOrControl+Alt+V and CommandOrControl+Alt+D (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:166; apps/desktop/electron/garnishCore.ts:91). Spec table lists the default (doc: docs/specs/desktop-global-voice/spec.md).
Web, phone, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: not applicable.
prerequisites: Desktop app on macOS (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseService.ts:226-232).
The setting switched on and confirmed in the native dialog (main.ts:2078-2089, 2251-2258).
macOS Accessibility access for the app (computerUseService.ts:331-338).

Signed in and dictation switched on in Settings > Voice, otherwise the bar says 'Dictation is off. Turn it on in Settings > Voice, then press the shortcut again.' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DictationBar.tsx:15-17).
Microphone permission; the desktop grants audio-only requests from the trusted app origin (permissionPolicy.ts:60-70).
screens_and_controls: Native confirmation 'Dictate into other apps?' with buttons Cancel and 'Type into other apps' (main.ts:2081-2089).
Floating bar, 440 by 72, bottom centre, always on top, never takes focus (apps/desktop/electron/dictationBar.ts:11, 62, 90).
Bar shows the dictation strip with stop, send, cancel and retry controls (DictationBar.tsx:70-90).
journey: Turn on the switch and confirm; allow Accessibility when macOS asks.
Click into a text field in another app.
Press the dictation shortcut; the bar opens and recording starts.
Speak.
Press the shortcut again; recording stops and the transcript is made.
The text is typed into the app that was in front.
feedback_and_outputs: Typed text appears in the other app.
If it cannot be typed, a notification 'Dictation copied' says 'Paste it where you want it.' with the reason (apps/desktop/electron/dictationElsewhere.ts:101-105).
Bar notices: 'What you said could not be typed.' on failure (DictationBar.tsx:18).
settings: dictateIntoFocusedApp, default false (apps/desktop/electron/garnishCore.ts:575).
Dictation shortcut in the tray Shortcuts submenu (doc: docs/specs/desktop-global-voice/spec.md).
Settings > Voice dictation switch and language (apps/web/features/settings/sections/VoiceSection.tsx:113-121, 184-189).

working: A press with the setting on and another app in front opens the bar there; a second press stops it (apps/desktop/electron/dictationElsewhere.ts:116-127).
With the setting off, or AGI Desktop in front, or the front app unreadable, the press dictates into the desktop app as before (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1921-1930; dictationElsewhere.ts:113-114).

Text cleaning: line breaks become spaces, invisible and direction characters are removed, empty text or text over 10,000 characters is refused (dictationElsewhere.ts:61-71; packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:443).
Sessions longer than 10 minutes end on the next press, and a finish after that copies instead of typing (dictationElsewhere.ts:45, 118-121, 149-151).
Never types into password or keychain windows, secure input fields, a changed front app or the product itself; it copies instead (dictationElsewhere.ts:17-27, 153-163).
If typing fails it copies and notifies (dictationElsewhere.ts:165-170).
Only the bar window can hand back text, via a bridge present only in that window (apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts:182-191; main.ts:586-594).
Turning the setting off closes any bar and cancels pending work (main.ts:2257; dictationElsewhere.ts:173-176).
incomplete: macOS only: other platforms never get the setting and typing needs the macOS helper (computerUseService.ts:226-232).
Product documents still say system dictation is unbuilt, so they are stale (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:667-674; audit/registers/known-flaws.md:235).
disconnected_or_disabled: Off by default (garnishCore.ts:575).
The retained Tauri dictation module is separate; the spec says its system dictation availability is false (doc: docs/specs/desktop-global-voice/spec.md).
not_available: Windows and Linux: not available.
Phone and Chrome extension: not applicable (brief marks missing).

established.statement: A global desktop shortcut dictates into whatever application is focused, not only the product window.
System-wide dictation is a separate native subsystem, not a composer-only microphone.
Turning it on needs a confirmation from native code, not a page.

acceptance_criteria: With the setting off, pressing the dictation shortcut over another app does not open the bar.
With the setting on, pressing it over a text field in another app opens the bar without taking focus; pressing again types the transcript there.
A transcript containing line breaks is typed as one line.
Pressing the shortcut over a macOS password prompt does not type; the text is copied and a notification explains.
If the user switches to another app before the second press, nothing is typed into the new app; the text is copied.
After 10 minutes the dictation is not typed; it is copied.
Turning the setting off while a bar is open closes it and types nothing.
inferred: The bar needs the hosted app to load, so it fails offline [inferred from dictationBar.ts:100 loading CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN].
Transcription for this path runs through the web transcription route, so it needs sign-in and is metered like web dictation. [inferred from DictationBar.tsx using useDictation]
proposed: Update the product contract and flaw register to match the code. [proposed]
Add a Local on-device transcription option so the bar works without a subscription. [proposed]
Add a Windows typing helper if Windows is in scope. [proposed]

steps.what_happens: Global shortcut fires; main checks the setting and asks the macOS helper for the front app.
Bar window opens over the display under the pointer and loads the hosted page.
The page records audio and uploads it for transcription.
The server checks flags, age gate, policy, quota or free allowance, then forwards audio to the provider and settles usage.
The provider returns text.
The page hands the text to the shell, which cleans it, re-reads the front app, and types it or copies it.

features.summary: Read aloud plays an assistant reply as speech. Web and mobile use the AGI server voice when signed in to Cloud and fall back to the device voice. Chrome extension, internal Tauri desktop and Local mode use the device voice. CLI and VS Code have none. The brief wrongly lists Chrome as missing.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns the text of one assistant reply into sound. It cleans the text, picks a voice engine, plays it, and lets the person stop it. Web and mobile can use a managed server voice (OpenAI-style speech endpoint behind /api/voice/speech) or the voice built into the browser, phone or operating system. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:411-511; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceOutput.ts:124-157)
purpose.why_it_exists: People listen to answers while walking, cooking, driving or when reading is hard. The product guidance lists read aloud as a standard message action next to copy, retry and feedback. (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:400-410; doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:286)
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in or local user of Web, the public Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile, and the Chrome extension side panel. Internal Tauri desktop users also have it.
problems_solved: Reading long answers on a small screen or while hands and eyes are busy.
Accessibility for people who prefer to listen.
Hearing a reply without copying it into another speech tool.
use_cases: On Web, a person opens the More message actions menu on a reply and chooses Read message aloud.
On Mobile in Cloud mode, a person taps Read aloud under an answer while commuting and hears the server voice.
In the Chrome side panel, a person clicks the speaker button on an answer to hear it in the browser's own voice.
On a phone in Local mode, a person hears the answer in the phone's installed voice with no account call.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: the 'More message actions' button (three dots) on an assistant reply opens a menu with a checkbox item 'Read message aloud', which becomes 'Stop reading message' while playing (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3926-3991). The draft said hover or focus then click; the code puts it inside this menu.

Web Code surface: a 'Read aloud' button with a speaker icon in the reply action row, 'Stop reading' while playing (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeTranscript.tsx:260-282; apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:204-205).

Also Settings > Voice 'Speak Assistant Replies' (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/VoiceSettings.tsx:674-720).
Mobile chat: a 'Read aloud' action button under an assistant reply, 'Stop reading aloud' while playing (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:3167-3174).

Chrome extension side panel: a speaker button in the reply action row with title 'Read aloud' / 'Stop reading aloud' (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:519-525, 627-629; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:4485-4490).
CLI and VS Code: no read-aloud control; no speech code found (apps/cli/src/voice.rs is voice input only: apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-9).
prerequisites: Web server voice: a signed-in session, an adult-eligibility pass, managed compute switched on, quota left. Without a session the web uses the browser voice (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:433-437; apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:76-91).

journey: 1. Person receives a finished assistant reply (the Chrome and web controls show only on non-error, non-streaming replies: bubbles.ts:622-628).
2. Person opens the action (Web: More message actions > Read message aloud; Mobile and Chrome: tap or click the speaker).
3. The app cleans the text (web and Tauri strip Markdown; mobile removes citation markers only).
4. The app picks an engine: server voice or device voice.
5. Audio plays; the control changes to Stop.
6. Person lets it finish or taps Stop; playing another reply stops the first.

Control state flips to Stop while speaking (web: isReadingAloud; mobile: isSpeaking; Chrome: aria-pressed).
Failure shows the toast 'Read aloud could not play. Try again.' on web and mobile.
Disabled control with a reason when blocked (web policy, mobile owner/voice checks).
settings: Web: Settings > General rows 'Backup read-aloud voice' and 'Read-aloud speed' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx:308-312). See F050-02.
Mobile: Settings > Voice (speed, pitch, voice, speech language). See F050-02.

Desktop Tauri: Settings > Voice 'Speak Assistant Replies' and Voice Persona (VoiceSettings.tsx:674-762).

working: Web: reply text is cleaned (fenced code replaced by 'code block omitted.', inline code, headings, bold, quotes, links, images, rules removed) (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:116-139).
Web: signed-in speech is requested per chunk from POST /api/voice/speech, decoded and played with the Web Audio API; chunks are 3,800 characters (useTTS.ts:11, 27-39, 460-494).
Web: if the first server chunk fails to fetch or decode, the browser's device voice speaks the whole reply; a later chunk failure shows the toast and stops (useTTS.ts:466-472).
Web: starting another reply retires the previous operation; asking for the same text again toggles it off (useTTS.ts:262, 426-430).

Web server route: CSRF, rate limit 30/min fail-closed, adult gate, kill switch, schema (1-4000 chars, optional voice and speed 0.25-4), privacy check, org model policy, idempotency key, entitlement and workspace access, usage reservation, provider call with 60 s timeout, usage settlement (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:48-247; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:404-408).
Web: Local and own-key replies get a disabled control with 'Read-aloud is unavailable for this reply’s privacy mode.' (apps/web/lib/read-aloud-policy.ts:4-5, 16-26; ChatMessageList.tsx:860).

Web Code surface: managed sessions can read aloud; local/own-key sessions show the privacy reason; unverified sessions show the unverified reason (read-aloud-policy.ts:40-45; LocalSessionPanel.tsx:1375).

Mobile Cloud: text goes in 3,800-character chunks to the same /api/voice/speech route, each saved to a temporary cache file, played, then deleted; the next chunk is prefetched (serverSpeech.ts:10-11, 46-63, 65-116, 149-175).
Mobile: server failure falls back to the device voice for the unfinished chunks (voiceOutput.ts:139-148).
Mobile Local: only the device voice (expo-speech) is used; a Local owner cannot request the server voice (voiceOutput.ts:102-105; tts.ts:83-103).
Mobile: citation markers are removed from the spoken text when the answer shows sources (MessageBubble.tsx:2024).
Chrome: device voice only, with saved voice and rate; one reply at a time (apps/extension/src/features/read-aloud/index.ts:41-65; bubbles.ts:536-565).
Internal Tauri desktop: strips Markdown, then speaks through the native engine (configured provider or downloaded Piper voice), else the webview voice (apps/desktop/src/hooks/useTTS.ts:39-46, 52-98).
incomplete: Mobile does not strip Markdown before speaking; it passes message.content (minus citation markers) to speech (MessageBubble.tsx:2024). Whether the device voice reads symbols aloud is unknown.
Chrome extension does not strip Markdown; it speaks the copy text of the message (bubbles.ts:625-628). What copyText holds is unknown.
Web 'isSupported' is true whenever a window exists, even if the browser has no speech synthesis, because the server voice does not need it (useTTS.ts:222).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web speech route accepts a 'voice' field, but the web client never sends it, so the server default voice is always used (route.ts:54, 122; useTTS.ts:58).
Mobile server speech sends only text and speed; the person's chosen voice, pitch and language do not reach the server voice (serverSpeech.ts:46-51).
not_available: CLI: no speech output (apps/cli/src/voice.rs is input only: apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-9).
VS Code extension: no speech code found in apps/extension-vscode (grep of src found nothing).

Chrome extension is listed as missing in the brief and ledger but exists in code (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/050-audio-overviews-speech-generation-and-music.md S50.01; apps/extension/src/features/read-aloud/index.ts).
No separate API app and no public API for speech beyond the web route.

established.statement: An assistant reply can be played aloud as speech.
Read aloud is a standard message action alongside copy, edit, retry, branch, feedback.
Verify read aloud as a message action against the leaders and keep read aloud distinct from dictation and live conversation.
Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local chat to cloud.
Speech is a managed side call that must respect the person's privacy setting and workspace policy.

acceptance_criteria: A finished assistant reply on Web, Mobile and Chrome side panel shows a read-aloud control; CLI and VS Code show none.
Activating it plays speech; activating again (or the Stop state) stops it within one interaction.
Starting a second reply stops the first on the same surface.
Fenced code in a reply is not read aloud on Web (the phrase 'code block omitted.' is spoken instead).
On Web, a reply stamped Local or own-key has a disabled control showing the privacy reason, and no request to /api/voice/speech is made.
On Mobile in Local mode no call to /api/voice/speech is made; in Cloud mode the call is made and a failure falls back to the device voice.
A playback failure shows 'Read aloud could not play. Try again.' on Web and Mobile.
Empty or whitespace-only text speaks nothing.
inferred: The same Local-mode rule should hold on every app: device voice is free of any subscription and needs no server (follows the product rule that local inference is free). Web currently blocks even the device voice for Local replies [inferred from read-aloud-policy.ts:16-26].
Read aloud text cleaning should be the same on every app [inferred: Web and Tauri strip Markdown; Mobile and Chrome do not].
proposed: [proposed] Share one text-cleaning function across Web, Tauri, Mobile and Chrome so all remove Markdown the same way.
[proposed] Allow device-voice read aloud for Local and own-key replies on Web, because no text leaves the device on that path.
[proposed] Add the read-aloud control to CLI (system speech command) only if the product decides it is wanted.

steps.what_happens: Web: person chooses Read message aloud; the list re-reads the current message and refuses a Local or own-key one.
Web: the hook strips Markdown and checks for a session; with no session or deviceVoice it uses the browser voice.
Web: for each 3,800-character chunk the browser posts text and speed to /api/voice/speech with an Idempotency-Key.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, age gate, kill switch, schema, privacy setting, org policy, then reserves usage against the plan.
Server sends the text to the OpenAI speech endpoint and receives mp3 audio.
Server settles usage and returns the audio with no-store caching.
Browser decodes and plays the audio; on first-chunk failure the browser voice speaks instead.
Mobile Cloud: the owner sends chunks to the same route, writes each mp3 to the cache folder, plays it with expo-audio and deletes it.
Mobile Local, or Cloud after a server failure: expo-speech speaks 500-character chunks in the phone's engine.
Chrome: the side panel loads saved settings from chrome.storage.local and calls the browser's speechSynthesis.
Tauri desktop: asks the capability probe, then speaks with the configured provider, or a downloaded Piper voice, else the webview voice.
steps.evidence: apps/desktop/src/hooks/useTTS.ts:39-81; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/voice.rs:775-821. A configured ElevenLabs or OpenAI provider calls an outside service with a stored key (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/features/speech/tts.rs:22-27, 682-688); where the key comes from in the Tauri build is unknown.

data.retained_or_deleted: Provider retention unknown. Response uses Cache-Control no-store (route.ts:160, 245).

data.what: Usage record for the speech call (operation speech, estimated tokens from characters, cost)
data.where_stored: Managed usage request records via managed-usage-request-service
data.retained_or_deleted: Retention unknown; table name not opened (unknown).

data.retained_or_deleted: Deleted when playback ends or is stopped (serverSpeech.ts:66-88).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The web route needs a live text-to-speech model from the OpenAI provider, resolved from the voice_speech routing slot; it throws if the slot is not a live OpenAI speech model (route.ts:102-105; packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json:919-921). Speech is not model agnostic or provider agnostic today: one provider is hard-required in the route. The reply's own chat model plays no part. Device voices come from the browser, phone or OS. Desktop Tauri supports System, ElevenLabs, OpenAI and Piper (tts.rs:22-27).

access_and_usage.account: Web server voice needs a signed-in account; without a session the web uses the browser voice (useTTS.ts:433-437; route.ts:76). Mobile server voice needs a Cloud account; Local needs none (voiceOutput.ts:102-105). Chrome and Tauri device voice need no account.
access_and_usage.permissions: Adult-eligibility gate on the route (route.ts:78-84); workspace policy and spend limit (managed-compute-access.ts:100-176); organization model policy (route.ts:114-120); the person's privacy setting that blocks providers that may train on content (route.ts:106-113). Mobile requires no microphone permission for playback [inferred].
access_and_usage.subscription: Free and no-plan accounts pass the subscription check; paid accounts need an active status (apps/web/lib/services/managed-compute-access.ts:68-75, 80-98). Quota is applied at usage reservation (route.ts:156-166). The settings note says the AGI voice 'uses a few credits per reply' (GeneralSection.tsx:853-856). The mapping to a named plan is unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Text 1-4,000 characters per request; speed 0.25-4; 30 requests per minute per user, fail closed (route.ts:48-56; rate-limit.ts:404-408). Cost is estimated from characters (4 characters per input token, 1.5 output tokens per character) (route.ts:49-50, 123-132). Free-plan numeric limits: unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: Environment kill switch AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA; when off the route returns 403 public_launch_blocked (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40, 55-91).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: The route requires a live OpenAI text-to-speech model from the voice_speech slot (route.ts:102-105). Any chat model's replies can be read except those tagged Local or own-key on web.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: OpenAI only for the server voice (route.ts:103). Providers that may train on content are refused when the person's privacy setting says so (route.ts:106-113). Own-key (BYOK) replies are blocked on web (read-aloud-policy.ts:19-22). Desktop Tauri can use ElevenLabs or OpenAI with a configured key (tts.rs:22-27).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local: device voice only, no server call, no account, no subscription (voiceOutput.ts:102-105; server-read-aloud tests name this). Web Local replies: the control is disabled and shows the privacy reason, even though a device voice exists (read-aloud-policy.ts:16-26). Chrome: always the device voice. Tauri desktop: downloaded Piper voice runs offline (local_tts.rs:1-5).

429 gives 'Read aloud is busy right now. Try again in a moment.'; 5xx gives 'The speech provider is unavailable. Try again shortly.' The web client discards these texts and treats any non-OK response as failure, so the person sees the fallback or the generic toast.
Stop retires the operation, stops the audio source or utterance, and ignores late callbacks.
Server aborts the provider call after 60 s; mobile aborts after 60 s.
Web server fetch fails and falls back to the device voice (works offline if the voice is local); mobile Cloud likewise falls back. Chrome and Local work offline [inferred].
Web retires playing audio on an identity change; mobile stops Cloud speech on account epoch change and dims the button with 'account changed'.
An unlock() primes the synthesizer silently; if the audio context cannot resume the device voice is used.
Control is dimmed with 'No speech voice is installed on this device.' iOS does not probe.
Web menu uses checkbox semantics; mobile and Chrome set labels and aria-pressed. Screen-reader behaviour while speech plays: not handled in the code or not found.

features.summary: Settings that shape how read aloud sounds. Web has a device-voice picker and three speeds. Mobile has speed, pitch, voice and speech language. Chrome has a voice picker and five speeds. Tauri desktop has voice personas. The server voice on web cannot be picked, and on mobile it ignores the voice, pitch and language.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person pick the voice and the speed of read aloud, and on mobile the pitch and language. The settings are saved on the device and read each time speech starts. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:355, 442; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/speechSettings.ts:48-56)
purpose.why_it_exists: People differ in how fast they listen and in which language they hear. The brief requires voice, language and rate choice where the engine supports it. Voices differ per device, so the choice is stored per device. (S50.02, S50.03 Should; doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:425)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using read aloud on Web, Mobile, Chrome or Tauri desktop.
problems_solved: A default voice too fast, too slow or in the wrong language.
A voice that is not installed on a new machine silently being ignored.
Hearing a preview before choosing.
use_cases: A web user sets Read-aloud speed to Slow and the next reply plays slower.
A phone user sets Speed to 1.25x and a French speech language.
A Chrome user picks a specific browser voice and presses Preview.
A desktop user picks the Calm persona so read aloud sounds slower and softer.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > General, row 'Backup read-aloud voice' (a dropdown with 'Browser default' and installed voices, plus a Preview/Stop button) and row 'Read-aloud speed' with buttons Slow, Normal, Fast (apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx:733-768, 808-858). The row is titled 'Backup' because it applies only when the device voice speaks.

Mobile: Settings > Voice has rows 'Speech language' and 'Voice' and two sliders 'Speed' and 'Pitch' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx:415-460). The 'Voice' row opens the 'Voice & Language' screen with 'Speaking style' and a 'System default' voice row and a preview button per voice (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice-language/index.tsx:150-200, 296-330).

Chrome: Options page, row 'Read aloud' with Voice and Speed selects (0.75x to 2x) and Preview (apps/extension/src/features/options/read-aloud-row.ts:28-66; apps/extension/src/features/read-aloud/index.ts:3).

Tauri desktop: Settings > Voice, 'Voice Persona' (friendly, calm, energetic, storyteller, technical, professional) and 'Piper TTS Voices' downloads (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/VoiceSettings.tsx:754-762, 849-897; apps/desktop/src/features/settings/voicePersonaParams.ts:7-22).
CLI and VS Code: none.

established.statement: The user can choose the voice and language used for spoken playback.

steps.what_happens: Person changes a setting; the app writes it to a local store (web localStorage, mobile persisted store, chrome.storage.local).
At the next read aloud the app reads the setting at call time.
Web sends the speed number to /api/voice/speech; the provider applies it.
Mobile Cloud sends only rate to the server; the device voice receives voice, rate, pitch, language.
The speech provider applies the speed in its own synthesis.

features.summary: A way to save generated speech as an audio file. It is intentionally not built on any app. The founders declined it to match Claude, which offers no download of spoken replies. Mobile writes a temporary file only to play it and deletes it afterwards.

purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists it for parity checking. The decision record declined it because Claude offers no download of spoken replies. (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:250-258)
purpose.who_uses_it: No one. Marked not applicable on all apps.
problems_solved: Would have let people share or archive spoken replies; the product chose not to.

features.summary: A guided builder where an owner would name a phone or web voice bot, give it a role, instructions, a speaking voice and call goals, then save a draft. Not built on any app. Only a text-agent builder (Agents page) and a personal live-voice mode exist as neighbours.

purpose.what_it_does: Intended: lets an owner create a configurable voice agent (a phone or web voice bot) step by step, with a name, a role, editable system instructions, a chosen speaking voice and goals a call should reach (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl: rows S51.01 to S51.04 and S51.07). Today nothing of this exists for voice agents (audit/missing/051-voice-agent-builder-and-telephony-extensions.md).

The ledger says builders of this kind ship as hosted dashboards (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl: S51.01 cli note).
purpose.who_uses_it: Intended users are account owners on Web, Desktop and Mobile who want a bot that answers calls or speaks on a website. CLI, VS Code and Chrome are marked not applicable (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl: S51.01 cells).
problems_solved: No way today to define a persona and instructions for a voice bot that others (callers) talk to.

The existing live voice mode is a personal assistant session for the signed-in user, not a configurable bot [inferred from apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:149, whose request has no agent, name or instruction field].

A support lead writes instructions and a goal such as 'book an appointment' for a web voice bot.
A team copies the text-agent configuration idea (name, instructions) to a spoken agent [proposed].

established.statement: A voice agent can transfer a live call to a human (warm or cold transfer).

acceptance_criteria: An owner can set one or more human targets and a transfer mode per agent.
On a cold transfer the caller is connected without an introduction.
On a warm transfer the human hears a summary before the caller joins.
If nobody answers, the agent returns to the caller and offers voicemail or callback.
The transfer and its outcome are recorded with the call.
Transfers need explicit owner consent for each target.

proposed: [proposed] Limit targets to a verified list and rate-limit transfers per hour.

features.summary: A planned feature that would let an owner get or connect a phone number or SIP trunk and route inbound calls to a chosen voice agent by rules. Nothing is built on any app or in the API. The only telephony-related code is a Twilio chat connector with no calling feature behind it.

purpose.what_it_does: Would give a voice agent a way to be reached by phone: buy or provision a number, connect a number the owner already has, connect a SIP trunk or endpoint (an internet phone line), and choose by rules which agent answers an inbound call. Today it does nothing; all four brief items are missing on web, desktop, mobile and the API (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl:1672-1675).
purpose.why_it_exists: A phone voice agent is useless without a number that callers can dial. The brief lists these four items as the entry point of the telephony part of the voice-agent builder (data/area-briefs/051-voice-agent-builder-and-telephony-extensions.md S51.12-S51.15). The audit overview says telephony and a voice-agent builder are not built (audit/overview.md:161).
purpose.who_uses_it: Business owners and admins who would run a voice agent that answers calls. Not the CLI, VS Code or Chrome apps: the ledger marks them n/a because they hold no telephony or voice-agent code (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl:1672).
problems_solved: Callers cannot reach an agent by phone because no number exists for it [inferred].
Owners with an existing business number cannot keep it when moving to an AGI voice agent [inferred].
Several agents and numbers need rules that decide which agent answers [inferred].
use_cases: An owner buys a local number and points it at a front-desk agent [proposed].
A company keeps its existing number and connects it through a SIP trunk to a support agent [proposed].
Calls to a sales number go to a sales agent and calls to a support number go to a support agent [proposed].

established.statement: Owners can buy or provision a phone number for a voice agent.
Owners can connect an existing phone number (bring your own number) to a voice agent.
Owners can connect a SIP trunk or SIP endpoint to route calls to a voice agent.
Inbound calls to a number are routed to a chosen voice agent using routing rules.
Connector copy must describe what the connector does in chat, not telephony.

acceptance_criteria: A signed-in owner can reach a screen to buy or provision a number for a named voice agent on web (and the same flow appears in the desktop app).
An owner can add an existing number and must prove ownership before it is routed.
An owner can connect a SIP trunk or endpoint and see a connection status.
A rule can send an inbound call to a chosen agent, and a test call reaches that agent.
A call that matches no rule gets defined behaviour (voicemail, a message or a hangup), set by the product.
Numbers and routes are refused for accounts whose plan or entitlement does not include voice agents.
The Twilio connector copy no longer promises voice calls unless calling exists.
inferred: Number and SIP setup needs a telephone carrier, which is an outside service, so it cannot run in Local mode on the device [inferred from how phone numbers work; no code to confirm].
Because Local, own key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries (AGENTS.md section 6), a number routed to a cloud-hosted agent must show that it is a Cloud feature [inferred].
proposed: Own numbers through one carrier abstraction in a shared package, so apps never keep a private copy of carrier data (AGENTS.md section 3) [proposed].
Define the no-match fallback and the ownership-verification step before building the UI, since the brief leaves them unspecified [proposed].
Change the Twilio connector summary to say what it does in chat until calling ships [proposed].

aliases: S51.16 Outbound calling, only where offered and authorized
features.summary: A planned feature that would let a voice agent place phone calls, only where the product offers it and the owner is authorised. It is not built on web, desktop, mobile or the API. The Twilio chat connector advertises voice calls, but no calling code exists.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a voice agent start a phone call to a person, for example a reminder or a follow-up, under authorisation and consent rules. Today nothing places a call (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl:1676).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists outbound calling as a part of the voice-agent builder, limited to where it is offered and authorised (S51.16 in data/area-briefs/051-voice-agent-builder-and-telephony-extensions.md). The 'only where offered and authorised' wording points at legal and consent limits on automated calls [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: Business owners who run a voice agent and are allowed to call out. Not the CLI, VS Code or Chrome apps (ledger n/a).
problems_solved: Agents can only answer calls, never start them [inferred].
Follow-ups and reminders need a person to dial by hand [inferred].
use_cases: An appointment agent calls a client to confirm a booking [proposed].
A collections or survey agent calls a list of consenting contacts [proposed].
A support agent calls back a customer who left a voicemail [proposed].

where_to_find_it: Web: not present (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl:1676).
Desktop: not present. Desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile: not present.
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not applicable.
prerequisites: None can be met today.
Intended [proposed]: a voice agent, an authorised caller number (see F051-07), consent for each contact, and an entitlement.
screens_and_controls: No screen or control exists in the code.
Intended [proposed]: a Call button or campaign on a voice agent, a list of authorised numbers, and a stop control.
journey: Today: not possible.

Intended [proposed]: 1 pick an agent; 2 pick an authorised number to call from; 3 enter who to call; 4 the product checks authorisation and calling limits; 5 the call starts; 6 the result lands in call records (F051-09).
feedback_and_outputs: Nothing today.
Intended [proposed]: call status (ringing, connected, failed), a refusal message when authorisation or consent is missing.
settings: none found in the code.

working: The Twilio connector card says 'SMS, WhatsApp messages, and voice calls' (apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts:659).
incomplete: That card is the only mention of calls and the audit found it contradicted by behaviour (audit/doc-corrections/contradictions-register.md:80-86).

established.statement: A voice agent can place authorized outbound phone calls, only where offered.
Connector copy must not claim voice calls while no telephony exists.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; a placed call cannot be undone.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to BYOK or managed cloud.

acceptance_criteria: An outbound call can only start from a number the owner is authorised to use.
A call to a contact without recorded consent is refused with a plain message.
The owner confirms a call with a prompt naming the cost and effect before it starts.
Calling limits per owner and per contact apply and are configuration, not constants (AGENTS.md section 8).
Each outbound call appears in call records with an outcome (F051-09).
Outbound calling is hidden or refused where the product does not offer it (plan, region or app).
Minutes used are metered to the subscription system (F051-10).
inferred: Authorisation, consent and calling-time rules vary by country and need legal review before launch [inferred; no document in docs/compliance was found for calls].
Because a call goes through a carrier, it cannot be a Local-only feature [inferred].
proposed: Require a consent record per contact and an owner confirmation before every campaign [proposed].
Start with single test calls to the owner's own verified number [proposed].

established.statement: Voice-agent configurations are versioned so earlier versions can be inspected.
A voice-agent version can be published live and rolled back to a previous version.
The migration chain is append-only; add the next numbered file rather than editing an applied one.
Restore of a custom agent version asks for confirmation naming the effect.

acceptance_criteria: Every publish of a voice agent creates a new numbered version that cannot be edited.
The owner can list versions with time, author and note.
Publishing a version makes it the one new calls use.
Rolling back makes an earlier version live again and records who did it.
A publish with no changes is refused with a clear message.
Two simultaneous publishes cannot create the same number.
Calls already in progress finish on the version they started with, or the behaviour is documented (the brief does not say).
inferred: The custom-agent flow is the closest owned pattern, and AGENTS.md section 3 says to search for the canonical owner before building a second one [inferred]; a voice agent version table could reuse its shape.
Voice versions must hold the number, routing and voice choice as well as instructions, otherwise rollback is partial [inferred].
proposed: Add a one-step 'Roll back to this version' that sets the live version directly [proposed].
Decide the in-progress call rule before building: finish on the old version [proposed].
Record the reason note for each publish, as custom agents do (max 300 characters per 0370_user_agents.sql:99) [proposed].

features.summary: The list of a person's custom assistants, called Agents in the product. Web and mobile show a Cloud list with Edit and Chat. The CLI lists agent files on disk with show, delete and rename. The Tauri desktop settings list agent files. The brief says web, desktop and mobile are missing; the code says otherwise.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows every custom assistant a person can use in one place and lets them open, edit, chat with or remove each. On web and mobile the list comes from the managed cloud API and splits into the person's own agents and agents shared with them. In the CLI and the Tauri desktop settings the list is the set of agent Markdown files on the device.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S52.01 says a user sees their custom assistants in one place and can open, edit or remove each (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/052-custom-assistant-builder.md). Without a list a person cannot find or reuse what they built.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and mobile: signed-in people on Cloud, including teammates who were shared an agent. CLI and Tauri desktop: developers who keep agent files on their machine.
problems_solved: Finding an assistant built earlier without searching chat history.
Telling owned agents from agents someone shared (apps/web/features/agents/components/AgentsPage.tsx:154-155).
Seeing at a glance whether an agent is a draft, shared, paused or retired (apps/web/features/agents/lib/agent-display.ts:14-31).
Removing an assistant that is no longer wanted.
use_cases: A person opens Agents on web, sees 'Your agents' and 'Shared with you', and presses Chat on a row to start a conversation that runs as that agent.
A mobile user opens Agents, filters by segment and starts a chat with a built-in agent from the 'By' catalog group.
A developer types /agents in the CLI to see project and global agent files, then /agents show <name> for detail.
A developer deletes an old agent file with /agents delete <name> --yes.

steps.what_happens: Web page requests GET /api/custom-agents with a bearer token.
The route applies the chat-conversation rate limit (60 per minute), opens a user-scoped database connection and lists rows the person owns plus rows of other people in the same workspace.
For a teammate's agent the service returns only the last published copy; an agent never published is dropped from that person's list.
The browser validates the response against the shared schema and draws the sections.
CLI /agents reads Markdown files from the global and trusted-project agent folders and prints the list; nothing leaves the device.
Tauri desktop settings call list_custom_agents, which reads the two .claude/agents folders.

Server checks ownership with requireOwnedAgent (custom-agent-service.ts:321). Row-level security policies exist on user_agents (0370_user_agents.sql:170-186).

features.summary: Making a new custom assistant and changing its fields. Web and mobile use a form that saves a draft through the Cloud API. The Tauri desktop settings write an agent file. The CLI writes a template, asks the session model to draft one from words, or edits one field at a time.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person create an assistant and edit its fields: name, description, icon, colour, instructions, output examples, starters, preferred model, reasoning effort, web search, code execution, image generation, connectors, skills, website rules and limits on web and mobile; name, description, model, tools and prompt in Tauri desktop; description, model, colour, tools, disallowed tools, skills, max turns, budget, permission mode and prompt in the CLI.
purpose.why_it_exists: S52.02 says a user can create a custom assistant from the product; S52.04 says a user can edit its fields in a form or editor (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/052-custom-assistant-builder.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and mobile: any signed-in person. CLI and Tauri desktop: developers.
