steps.what_happens: The person fills the form; the browser keeps the draft in React state and compares it with the saved copy.
Save sends POST or PATCH with a CSRF header and bearer token.
The route checks CSRF, rate limit and user scope, parses the body against the shared schema, then runs createAgent or updateAgentDraft.
The service normalises website rules, validates the model against the catalog, aligns effort, and writes the row.
The saved agent is returned and shown; the saved copy is a draft until published.
CLI create from words sends the text to the session's own model and provider, parses the JSON reply, and writes an agent file.

features.summary: Intended: build an assistant by chatting with a builder, try it in a preview that uses unsaved changes, and test each tool. None of these exist in the code read. The nearest things are a one-shot model draft in the CLI and a web Chat button that is disabled while edits are unsaved.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person describe an assistant in chat so the builder fills the fields, try the assistant before saving, and run a single tool to see its result. Today none of this is built; this page records what is missing and what stands in for it.
purpose.why_it_exists: S52.03, S52.05 and S52.24 require a guided conversational builder, a live test pane that reflects unsaved changes, and tool testing with the result shown (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/052-custom-assistant-builder.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who build assistants and are not sure of the right wording or tools.
problems_solved: Blank-form paralysis when writing instructions.
Saving, chatting, finding a flaw and editing again in a long loop.
Not knowing whether a tool or connector works before sharing the assistant.
use_cases: Describe a support assistant in chat and see the fields fill.
Type a test message to the half-edited assistant and read the answer before saving.
Press 'test' on a web-search or connector tool and read what it returns.

While configuring, the user can try it in a preview or test chat that reflects unsaved changes.
A builder can test an assistant's tools or actions and see the result.

A builder chat fills at least name, description and instructions and shows them in the form before saving.
The preview answers using the unsaved instructions, not the saved ones.
The preview does not count against the saved agent's daily turn limit unless that is stated [proposed].
A tool test shows the tool result or the error text.
Local mode builders send nothing to Cloud [proposed, from the trust-boundary rule in AGENTS.md section 6].

[proposed] Add a Test button per connector or skill selection row.

features.summary: Lets a person decide what a custom assistant (called an agent in the product) may use: a preferred model, reasoning effort, web search, code execution, image generation, connectors and skills. Web and mobile store these as saved switches the server enforces in Cloud chats. The CLI and desktop file editors use tool lists in an agent file.

purpose.what_it_does: Each agent carries a small set of capability choices. On Web and Mobile they are fields on the agent (model, effort, webSearch, codeExecution, imageGeneration, connectorIds, skillNames, allowed and blocked websites) saved in our database and applied to every Cloud chat or scheduled run that uses the agent (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/agents.ts:89-111; apps/web/lib/agents/agent-turn-config.ts:193-216). In the CLI the same idea is a markdown agent file with model, tools, disallowedTools, skills and mcpServers lines (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:1429-1560).
purpose.why_it_exists: A builder wants one assistant that is narrower than a general chat: cheaper model, no web, no code, only some connectors. The product brief asks for model preference, tool selection, web search, code execution, media generation and connector selection as separate switches (brief S52.16 to S52.21). The migration that created agents says people could only paste the same instructions into every chat before (apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:1-9).
purpose.who_uses_it: A builder (an individual or a workspace member) who creates an agent. Teammates who chat with a shared agent feel the effect but cannot change it (apps/web/lib/services/custom-agent-service.ts:321-331).
problems_solved: Stops an agent from using web search, code or image tools its builder does not want it to use.
Lets a builder pin a model and a reasoning level so an agent behaves the same way in every chat.
Limits which connectors and skills a shared agent can reach, so a teammate's connected accounts are not opened to an agent that should not use them.
use_cases: A support-reply agent with web search off and only the helpdesk connector ticked.
A research agent that pins a strong model and a high reasoning level and may only read three named websites.
A drafting agent with code execution and image generation switched off to keep answers plain text.
In the CLI, a reviewer agent file that allows only read tools and a turn limit.

established.statement: An assistant can pin a preferred model that is used when it runs.
An assistant's configuration chooses which tools it may use.
Web search can be turned on or off per assistant.
Code execution can be turned on or off per assistant.
Image or media generation can be turned on or off per assistant.
The configuration selects which connectors the assistant can use.
Model-agnostic and provider-agnostic: model ids resolve through the generated catalog, never a literal in a consumer.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud; Cloud agents run only in Cloud.
Documentation availability of web search, code execution and image generation is separate from route availability; they depend on a provider route or an AGI harness.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, create an agent with Web search off; in a chat with it, the model gets no web search or web fetch tool, and the same chat on a normal conversation still has them.
On Web, pin a model on an agent and open a chat on Auto: the turn runs on the pinned model. Pick a different model in the chat: the chat model wins.
Ticking one connector under 'Connectors and skills' limits tools to that connector; unticking all gives an agent with no connector tools (after connectors are released).
PATCH with an unknown model id answers a validation error 'Pick a model from the list.' and saves nothing.
CLI: /agents set <name> tools "read_file" then --agent <name>; only that tool is offered, and if a command-line allowlist is given the result is the overlap only.
CLI: an agent file with permissionMode looser than the session leaves the session mode unchanged and prints a notice.
CLI: a subagent invoked by the model keeps the parent's model and permission mode even if the agent file names others.
inferred: The same switches should exist on every app that lets a person build an agent; today VS Code and Chrome have none [inferred from the area brief and AGENTS.md section 5].
A pinned model the owner's plan cannot use should be refused or flagged when saving, not only at chat time [inferred from the plan-aware model list in schedule-models.ts:17-41].
Image generation should be switchable in CLI and desktop files to match Web and Mobile [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Share one tool vocabulary between web switches and CLI tool names, so an agent exported from one app keeps its limits in the other.
[proposed] Add an effort control and website lists to Mobile so Mobile agents are not behind Web.
[proposed] Reject a pinned model the builder's plan lacks at save time with a clear message.

steps.what_happens: Web or Mobile sends the form values to POST /api/custom-agents or PATCH /api/custom-agents/[id]; the server checks CSRF, the rate limit and the user's session.
The server validates the model against the catalog, rounds the effort, sorts lists and writes the row in user_agents under the user's row-level rules.
On a chat turn the conversation's agent id is read, the owner's working copy or a teammate's published copy is chosen, and paused, retired or over-limit agents are refused before any model call.

The request is edited: web search, web fetch and code execution forced off if the agent says so; the model replaced by the agent's model only when the chat is on Auto or empty; the agent's system prompt added.
Tool lists for the turn are built: connectors and skills outside the agent's list are dropped and image tools removed when the agent has them off.
The provider call runs on whichever provider and model the router picked for the (possibly pinned) model.
CLI: the agent file is read from disk, its fields are applied to the session and the model switch is attempted locally; tool filtering runs in the CLI process.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The agent stores only a model id or an Auto id, never a provider. Routing to a provider happens later in the chat route (SYS-model-catalog-and-routing, SYS-inference-providers). The CLI switches model through its own catalog and local-model scan (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1114-1134).

access_and_usage.account: Web and Mobile need a signed-in account; Mobile also needs Cloud mode (useCloudFeatureAccess.ts:30-35). CLI and desktop file editing need no account.
access_and_usage.permissions: Only the owner edits an agent (requireOwnedAgent, custom-agent-service.ts:321-331); a teammate sees a read-only form (AgentEditorPage.tsx:184, 416-420). In the CLI only agents in the project or global agents folders can be edited by /agents set (agents.rs:1129-1145).
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan gate was found on creating or editing an agent in the routes (apps/web/app/api/custom-agents/route.ts). Image generation inside a chat is limited to Pro, Max, Max 15x, Team, Team Premium and Enterprise plans (billing-catalog.ts:356; request-processor.ts:6336). Which plan tiers may run web search and code execution inside an agent chat was not traced: unknown. A per-agent monthly credit cap exists (agent-turn-config.ts:91-100).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Connector and skill lists hold at most 200 entries each (agents.ts:24, 33); website lists hold at most 32 (agents.ts:30 constant AGENT_WEB_DOMAINS_MAX); daily message cap up to 10,000 and monthly credit cap up to 100,000,000 (agents.ts:20-21). Turns and credits are counted by the server before a turn (agent-turn-config.ts:81-100). CLI: maxTurns and maxBudgetUsd cap a session (agents.rs:57-65, 1117-1127).
access_and_usage.flags: Connector release state 'coming_soon' hides the connectors picker (connector-release.ts:14). No flag found for the other switches.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: A pinned model must exist in the catalog; effort levels are limited to what the model offers and a model without levels hides the effort control (agents.ts:58-80; AgentConfigForm.tsx:523). Whether a model supports tools is checked in the chat route (request-processor.ts:6334, resolvedModelCaps) and is not an agent rule.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None stored on the agent. A pinned model is routed by the normal router, so provider access rules of SYS-inference-providers apply [inferred].
access_and_usage.local_mode: The Web and Mobile agent switches are Cloud only: Mobile Local mode shows a gate 'Agents run in AGI Cloud; switching won't upload your local chats.' (AgentEditorScreen.tsx:79-90). The CLI and desktop file agents run on the device and can pin a local model; the CLI refuses a model switch that would cross a privacy boundary (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1135-1145). Local inference itself needs no subscription [doc: product context]; whether CLI sign-in is needed for local agent files: unknown.

features.summary: A planned way to turn an API description such as OpenAPI into actions an assistant can call, with sign-in settings for those calls. Nothing implements it in any app. The nearest existing pieces are MCP servers in the CLI agent file and the connector directory, which is currently hidden as coming soon.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a builder paste or upload an API schema, have the product list the operations as callable actions on one assistant, and store how calls sign in (API key or OAuth). Not built.
purpose.why_it_exists: The area brief lists custom-action schema (S52.22) and authentication configuration for actions (S52.23) as parts of a complete assistant builder, matching how other assistant products let builders attach their own APIs (brief S52.22, S52.23).
purpose.who_uses_it: Builders who own or use an API that no connector covers, for example an internal tool.
problems_solved: Reaching a private or niche API without waiting for a first-party connector.
Keeping the API key or OAuth setup with the assistant rather than pasting keys into instructions.
use_cases: A support lead links an internal ticket API and the assistant files tickets.
A finance assistant calls a company reporting API with an API key.
A developer imports an OpenAPI file for a staging service to test calls.

established.statement: A builder can define custom actions from an API schema (for example OpenAPI) that the assistant can call.
A builder can configure authentication (API key or OAuth) for an assistant's custom actions.
Reusable plugins combine instructions with apps and tools; Custom GPTs and the GPT Store are a migration source, not AGI's enduring target architecture.

OpenAI announced a custom-GPT retirement and plugin migration; this is a migration notice, so investigate reusable instructions, tools, sharing and migration rather than freezing an old GPT-builder design.
Secrets are never committed and security fails closed; Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud stay separate trust boundaries.
No mock production paths or dead controls.

acceptance_criteria: A builder can add an API description and see the list of operations it produced.
Each action can be switched on or off for the assistant.
An API key or OAuth connection is stored without showing the secret again, and is used only for that action.
A call to the action from a chat shows what was sent and the result.
A teammate who runs a shared assistant uses the builder's saved sign-in only if the builder allowed it, and never sees the key.
Egress goes through the product's host-owned policy.
inferred: Because the product direction treats the GPT builder as a migration source, actions are likely to map onto MCP servers or connectors rather than a separate schema runtime [inferred from definition.md:183].
Credentials need a server-side secret store; the agent table has none [inferred from 0370_user_agents.sql].
proposed: [proposed] Build actions on the existing connector and MCP layer: import a schema into a workspace-owned connector, then select it in the agent's connector list.
[proposed] Keep credentials in the connector credential store and show only 'connected' status in the builder.
[proposed] Add an action test button before publish.

features.summary: A builder edits an agent as a working draft, then publishes it to freeze a numbered version that shared people run. The builder can browse past versions and restore one back into the draft. Web and Mobile have this against our servers. The CLI and desktop have only a single file, with no versions.

purpose.what_it_does: The agent's row in user_agents is the working copy, saved in place. Publish copies it into user_agent_versions as the next number and points published_version at it. Teammates run the published copy; the owner's own chats run the draft. Restore copies an old version's settings into the draft without publishing (apps/web/lib/services/custom-agent-service.ts:146-149, 449-551).
purpose.why_it_exists: Builders need to try changes without breaking an assistant others rely on, and to roll back a bad edit (brief S52.27 to S52.30; migration comment 'Publishing freezes the copy into user_agent_versions' at apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:11-17).
purpose.who_uses_it: The owner of an agent. Teammates are affected only through what is published.
problems_solved: Edits do not reach teammates until published.
Mistakes can be undone from the history.
Each publish carries a short note on what changed.
use_cases: Tweak instructions, chat with the draft yourself, then publish when happy.
Publish a new version for the team with the note 'tighter tone'.
Restore version 2 after version 3 behaved badly, check it, then publish again.
Notice 'Unpublished changes' on the list and decide to publish.

established.statement: A builder can save an assistant as a draft without publishing it.
A builder can publish an assistant so others (or they) can use the published version.
An assistant keeps a version history the builder can browse.
A builder can revert an assistant to an earlier published version.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and the question names the consequence; restore uses the shared confirm surface.
Migrations are append-only; version rows are never edited by the app.

acceptance_criteria: Save draft with a change: the saved agent shows 'Unpublished changes' only after it has been published once.
Publish with no changes: refused with 'There are no changes to publish.' and no new version appears.
Publish twice with edits between: versions 1 and 2 exist, version 2 is marked Published.
A teammate chatting with the agent uses the published version, not the draft.
Restore version 1 after publishing version 2: the form shows version 1's settings, the live version stays 2 until you publish.
A note longer than 300 characters is refused by the server.
A retired agent cannot publish or restore.
inferred: Every surface that lets a person edit an agent should let them publish and restore, or say that it cannot [inferred].
Restore should work even if the pinned model has left the catalog, by clearing the model with a notice [inferred from the failure path at service:214].
Local file agents on CLI and desktop could use git history as their version history, which the product does not state [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show a diff between a version and the draft before Restore.
[proposed] Offer 'Chat with draft' using unsaved edits as a preview pane.
[proposed] Let the owner see which version each teammate chat used.

steps.what_happens: The person edits the form in the browser or app; the draft is held in memory with a dirty flag and an unsaved-changes guard.
Save sends PATCH; the server updates the owner's row only (where id and user_id match).

Publish sends POST with the note; inside one transaction the server compares the draft to the published copy, picks max(version)+1, inserts the version with the config JSON, and sets published_version.
Version list reads user_agent_versions for the owner; Restore reads one version's JSON, parses it against the schema, and runs the draft update.
A teammate's chat loads the row with the joined published config and runs that copy.

features.summary: Controls who may chat with an agent: only the owner, named workspace members, or everyone in the workspace. Sharing needs a workspace and a published version. Web and Mobile support it against our servers. A public directory does not exist. CLI agents are private by file location.

established.statement: An assistant can be kept private to its creator.
A builder can share an assistant with named people.
A builder can make an assistant available to everyone in their workspace.
A builder can list an assistant in a public directory others can browse.
Workspace and role rules decide who may read a resource; sharing a Local item to another boundary needs consent.
Custom GPTs and the GPT Store are a migration source, not the enduring target architecture, so a public store is not assumed.

acceptance_criteria: A new agent is private: another workspace member does not see it in 'Shared with you'.
Sharing before publishing is refused with 'Publish the agent before you share it.'
A personal-space agent cannot be shared and the panel says so.
'Specific people' with nobody ticked is refused.
After sharing with person A only, person B cannot read or chat with the agent (route and database both refuse).
After 'Everyone in the workspace', every member sees it; after 'Only you', they no longer do.
A recipient cannot edit, publish, share, transfer or delete.
Retiring the agent removes it from recipients.
inferred: Sharing should extend to every app that can run an agent; VS Code and Chrome do not list agents today [inferred].
The 100-person cap and member listing should page for larger workspaces [inferred].
A public directory, if wanted, needs review, reporting and a separate visibility value; none exists [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add paging and search to the people picker.
[proposed] Decide on public listing in a decision record before building, given the product direction on GPT stores.
[proposed] Show the owner who currently has access in the list row.

features.summary: Lets an owner export an agent as a Markdown file, import one, hand it to another workspace member, pause it, retire it or delete it. Web and Mobile have these against our servers. There is no duplicate button, no deprecation notice and no replacement link. Export and import drop most settings.

purpose.what_it_does: Export downloads a Claude Code style agent file. Import turns such a file into a new draft. Transfer hands ownership to a workspace member. Pause stops new chats until resumed; retire stops them and hides the agent from recipients but keeps history; delete removes it (apps/web/lib/agents/agent-markdown.ts:84-172; custom-agent-service.ts:418-447, 602-618).
purpose.why_it_exists: Builders move agents between products and people, and need a safe way to stop one without losing history (brief S52.38 to S52.41; migration comment about retired keeping the agent and history read-only, 0370_user_agents.sql:20-22).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners. Recipients feel pause and retire.

steps.what_happens: Export: the server reads the agent, picks the viewer's copy (owner draft or recipient's published), builds Markdown and returns it as a download.
Import: the browser reads the file text and posts it; the server parses frontmatter, rejects bad files, creates a private draft in the current workspace.
Status change: owner posts the new status; the server updates status and timestamp; later chats and routines check status first.
Transfer: the server checks ownership then calls the database function that checks workspace membership and moves the row and files.
Delete: the server removes the row; foreign keys cascade versions, access and files and null the agent id on conversations and schedules.
CLI and desktop file actions read or write Markdown files on disk.

features.summary: Shows the skills an account can use, each with a name and a description. Web and Desktop list them in Settings under Skills, with an installed view and a whole-catalogue view. Mobile has a Skills screen (Cloud mode only). The CLI and VS Code list skill files found on the device and synced from the account.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists built-in AGI skills, the person's own (personal) skills, plugin skills and, on the CLI, project and user folder skills. Each row shows the skill name and its description. The default web list is what the account has switched on; the whole catalogue also includes skills the account switched off (apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:141-153).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person cannot use a skill they cannot find. The list is where a skill is discovered, opened, switched on or off, and chosen for a chat. Project requirements ask for user, project and marketplace/plugin skills (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, section 'Connectors, MCP, Plugins, And Skills').
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on Web, Desktop (hosted web app) or Mobile (Cloud mode); developers on the CLI and in VS Code.
problems_solved: Finding which skills exist and what each one does
Seeing which skills are on for the account
Telling built-in skills from your own and from plugin skills
use_cases: A person opens Settings > Skills on the web to see the built-in skills and searches for a PDF skill.
A mobile user in Cloud mode opens Skills, searches 'report' and sees which matching skills are installed.
A developer runs /skills in the CLI to see the skills the agent will be offered.
A developer opens the Skills quick pick in VS Code to see which workspace skills are on.

Mobile: route /(app)/skills, header 'Skills' with a 'Cloud' badge (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillsScreen.tsx:132-177, apps/mobile/app/(app)/skills/index.tsx); opened from the composer (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1048).
CLI: '/skills' prints the list; '/skills-toggle' opens the on/off overlay (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6198-6212, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6540-6556).

VS Code: 'Skills' item in the surface menu and the '/skills' entry, both run command agi-workforce.showSkills, which opens a quick pick titled 'Skills' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/surfaceMenu.ts:38, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:220-226).

established.statement: A user can browse a catalogue of available skills, including ones not yet installed, and open any of them (S53.01).
A user can see the list of skills installed or active for them (S53.02).
Each skill shows its name and a description of what it does (S53.07).
Skills requirements include user skills, project skills and marketplace/plugin skills.
Install, create, enable, invoke, disable and uninstall must affect the next turn and survive reload; failures are explained without claiming installation.
Skills stay available in Free chat.

acceptance_criteria: Web Settings > Skills lists built-in skills each with name and description, and the status filter separates installed from not installed.
A skill the account switched off still appears in the whole catalogue but not in the default list or the composer picker (apps/web/app/api/skills/__tests__/skill-catalog-param.test.ts:204-216).
A draft skill shows a draft label and has no Install action.
Mobile in Cloud mode shows the list; in Local mode it shows the gate with no network request.
Searching mobile with no matches shows 'No matching Skills' and 'Clear search' restores the list.
CLI /skills lists the skills the agent is offered, and a skill turned off in /skills-toggle no longer appears.
inferred: [inferred] 'Installed' on the web means 'not switched off': a never-toggled built-in skill counts as installed (apps/web/lib/services/skill-catalog-service.ts:150-158).
[inferred] The brief's 'not yet installed' therefore covers only skills the account switched off, since built-in skills are on by default.
proposed: [proposed] Give the CLI and VS Code a read-only view of the account catalogue so a developer can see skills not yet synced.
[proposed] Use one wording for drafts across web, mobile and CLI.
[proposed] Add a mobile empty message that points a person with no installed skills to Install.

steps.what_happens: Web: opening Settings > Skills requests GET /api/skills?catalog=all and GET /api/skills/installs together, and shows a spinner meanwhile.

The server applies a rate limit, finds the signed-in account, checks whether the workspace allows plugins, loads the bundled skill catalogue (cached 60 seconds) and reads the account's install overrides.

The server adds the account's personal skills, plugin-directory skills, each skill's origin and measured install totals, validates the answer against the shared schema and replies; a bad shape clears the catalogue cache.
The client maps entries to cards with installed state, filters and sort, and renders the list.
Mobile makes the same requests with the signed-in session, only in Cloud mode.
CLI reads skill folders on disk; when signed in to Managed Cloud it downloads the account's skills into an account-skills folder at most every 10 minutes and lists them too.
VS Code asks the local CLI runtime for skills/list and shows the answer.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider takes part in listing skills. The list does not depend on which model is chosen.

access_and_usage.account: Web, Desktop and Mobile need a signed-in account; the signed-out /skills page shows only a public list of built-in skills (apps/web/app/skills/page.tsx:41-49). CLI and VS Code local skills need no account.
access_and_usage.permissions: A workspace admin can switch the Skills feature off, which closes the capability canUseSkills and replaces the settings pane with a notice (apps/web/lib/services/capability-handshake-service.ts:183; apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx:243-258). When the workspace disallows plugins, plugin skills are not listed (apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:146-152).
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan check found in the list route. The platform capability canUseSkills is true for the web, desktop and mobile rows (packages/contracts/types/src/capabilities.ts:55, 88, 121). Project doc says Skills remain available in Free chat (doc: docs/product/definition.md:383). The CLI refuses its skill list when the cached capability document denies canUseSkills (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:144-149). Rows for the CLI, VS Code and Chrome capability: unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 300 catalogue reads per minute per the skills-catalog-read bucket, not fail-closed (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:311-317). No usage metering for listing found.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING (server, default on) affects canAuthorSkills; FEATURES.skills (mobile, true) (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:20).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable to listing; none found in the code.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode: the Skills screen shows the gate and loads nothing (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillsScreen.tsx:639-640, 785-790). CLI: local skill files work with no account; account skills are synced only for Managed Cloud (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:652-683). Desktop local mode: unknown, because the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

states_and_edge_cases.behaviour: Section shows a spinner; a newer request replaces an older one so a slow earlier answer is ignored.
Shows the skills failure copy with a retry action; the previous list stays.
A catalogue load failure raises SkillCatalogUnavailableError and the route answers 500 'Failed to load skills'; a bad response shape clears the cache.
Chat treats skills as withheld; only plugin-owned skills stay.
'No managed Skills yet' or, when searching, 'No matching Skills' with 'Clear search'.
Keeps the list and shows 'Refresh failed' with Retry; first-load failure shows 'Could not load Skills' and 'Try again'.
Results from a previous account are dropped by an account epoch check.
The list reloads when the screen regains focus.
not handled in the code beyond the retry controls above and the abort signal on mobile loads.
Rows have an accessibility label with name and source, a status label per skill and alert role on errors.

scenarios.name: Web default versus whole catalogue
steps: Sign in on the web.
Switch off a built-in skill from its detail view.
Open Settings > Skills and use the Status filter.
Open the composer slash menu.
scenarios.expected: The skill shows as not installed in the catalogue and is absent from the composer slash menu.

scenarios.name: Mobile Local mode gate
steps: Open the mobile app in Local mode.
Open Skills.
scenarios.expected: The gate 'Skills are available in AGI Cloud' shows and no skills request is made.

scenarios.name: Mobile search with no match
steps: Switch to Cloud mode and open Skills.
Type a word that matches nothing.
scenarios.expected: 'No matching Skills' appears with a 'Clear search' button that restores the list.

scenarios.name: CLI toggle
steps: Run /skills and note a skill.
Run /skills-toggle, switch it off with Space, press Enter.
Run /skills again.
scenarios.expected: The skill is gone from the list and present again after switching it back on.

scenarios.name: Workspace closes Skills
steps: Have a workspace admin switch the Skills feature off.
Open Settings > Skills as a member.
scenarios.expected: A notice replaces the list.

features.summary: Opens one skill and shows its description, its instruction file and bundled files, where it came from, the tools and connectors it needs, and whether each connector is connected. Web and Desktop have a full view; Mobile has a smaller detail screen. CLI and VS Code show name, description and missing requirements only.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what a skill is before and while it is used: instruction text, file tree, source, date added, version, license, needed tools and needed connectors with a Connected or Connect control.
purpose.why_it_exists: A skill is a set of instructions the model follows. People need to read it, see what it can touch, and fix a missing connection before relying on it. The access line states that a skill gets no access of its own (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:137-138).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone choosing, checking or editing a skill; admins checking where a skill came from.
problems_solved: Not knowing what a skill will do
Not knowing which tools or connectors a skill needs
Not knowing who supplied a skill
use_cases: A person opens a built-in skill, reads SKILL.md and sees it needs a connector that is not connected, then presses Connect.
A person checks that a plugin skill shows 'Part of a plugin' as its source.
A person opens a bundled script in the file tree and copies its contents.
A mobile user opens Details on a skill and reads its Needs section.

features.summary: Lets a person pick one skill for a message (slash menu, plus menu, mention, mobile Use in chat, Chrome Skills menu, CLI slash command) or lets the assistant load a matching skill itself. The server checks the name, the model's tool support and the skill's needs, then the model loads the skill text through a skill tool.

purpose.what_it_does: Gets a skill's instructions into one chat turn, either because the person chose it or because its description matches the request. Skill text is loaded on demand, not pasted into every prompt.
purpose.why_it_exists: Skills only help when they are used at the right moment without crowding the prompt. Manual pick gives control; automatic matching saves effort.
purpose.who_uses_it: Chat users on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile, Chrome and API callers; developers on the CLI and in VS Code.
problems_solved: Repeating the same instructions every chat

Prompt size growth from listing every skill in full

steps.what_happens: The person picks a skill; the client stores its name for one send.
The chat request carries skill_name (1 to 200 characters, no slashes or control characters).
The server loads the account's selectable catalogue (built-in switched on, plugin-directory, personal), filters by agent rules, refuses a model without tool support, and refuses an unknown name.
The server adds a system message listing skills with the pick marked, offers the skill tool and forces it as the first call.
The server checks the skill's needed tools and connectors against the tools offered this turn and refuses with 422 if some are missing.
With no pick and a tool-capable model on web, desktop, mobile or Chrome, the server adds matching skills (when the workspace allows skills) and offers the skill tool without forcing it.

The model calls the skill tool; the server finds the skill (built-in, plugin-directory or personal), returns the text wrapped as untrusted guidance, and stages scripts in the code sandbox if code execution is on.
CLI: the skill text is read from disk and added to the turn; the model runs on the user's chosen route.

data.what: Skill text loaded during a turn

Up to 4 MB staged per turn; later turns must load the skill again (skill-staging.ts note text)

Which provider answers is chosen by the normal routing, not by skills. The CLI sends the skill text to whichever route the session uses (Local, own key or Managed Cloud).

features.summary: Lets a person switch a built-in skill on or off without deleting it. Web and Desktop use Install, Uninstall and an 'Enable skill' switch; Mobile has Install, Uninstall and a 'Turned on' switch; the CLI uses /skills-toggle; VS Code uses Turn on and Turn off. Web and mobile save the choice on the account; the CLI saves it on the device.

purpose.what_it_does: Controls which skills the assistant can use. Switching off hides a built-in skill from the composer and from the model; the skill stays in the catalogue so it can be switched on again.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want fewer skills in the way, or want to try a skill, without losing or re-creating it.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on web, desktop (hosted web) and mobile; CLI and VS Code developers.
problems_solved: Too many skills offered in chat
Wanting to disable a skill without deleting it
Controlling which skills a project may load (CLI consent)
use_cases: A person turns off a skill that keeps matching the wrong requests.
A mobile user taps Install on a skill they had switched off.
A developer disables a global skill in /skills-toggle.
A developer in VS Code turns off a skill for all folders.

steps.what_happens: The person flips a switch; the client sends POST /api/skills/installs with the name, or DELETE /api/skills/installs/{name}, with a CSRF token on web.
The server checks CSRF, the rate limit, and (install only) the workspace Skills feature gate; finds the skill in the catalogue; refuses unknown (404), plugin-owned (409) and draft (409) skills.
The server locks the account's settings row, writes the true or false override in one transaction, records an audit event and returns the new installed list.
The client clears its catalogue cache, announces a catalogue change and reloads the section.
The next chat turn reads the overrides and offers only skills not switched off.
CLI: the overlay writes the disabled list file on the device.

features.summary: Lets a person write their own skill (name, description, instructions), change it and delete it. On web and Desktop an editor does this; on Mobile a New skill sheet does; on the CLI and in VS Code a skill is a SKILL.md file in a folder. Web and mobile save the skill to the account only.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a skill the person wrote so only they can use it. The server records it with origin 'personal' and the time it was added, and offers it in chat before built-in skills.
purpose.why_it_exists: People repeat the same instructions; a skill turns them into a reusable, named step. Requirements ask for user skills (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, section 19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person; developers keeping skills as files.
problems_solved: Retyping the same instructions
Sharing instructions across chats
Keeping instructions private to one account
use_cases: A person writes a 'weekly-report' skill on web and picks it from the slash menu.
A mobile user starts a copy of a built-in skill with 'Use as a template' and edits it.
A developer runs the VS Code 'Create a skill' command and edits the template file.
A person deletes a skill they no longer need.

established.statement: A user can own personal skills that only they have and that they created or added (S53.03).
A user can write and edit a skill's instructions in an editor in the product (S53.09).
The server stores the skill for that account only with origin personal and the time added; a built-in name is refused with a conflict message.
Skills requirements include user skills and project skills.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names what is lost.

acceptance_criteria: Creating 'weekly-report' on web shows it in Settings > Skills as 'Created by you' and in the slash menu under 'Your skills'.
Creating a name that a built-in skill uses returns 409.
Creating the same name twice returns 409 'You already have a skill named'.
Saving a name with capital letters is refused with the name message.
Editing the instructions changes what the model loads on the next turn.

steps.what_happens: The person fills the editor and saves; the client sends POST /api/skills (create) or PUT /api/skills/{name} (edit) with a CSRF token.
The server checks CSRF and the rate limit, requires authoring to be on, finds the account, and (create) checks the workspace Skills feature.
The body is parsed with a strict schema, a built-in name is refused, text is validated and scanned, then inserted into user_skills.
An audit event 'skill_installed' (source authored) is recorded and the summary is returned with 201.
The client closes the editor, clears its list and announces a catalogue change so the lists reload.
Delete: DELETE removes the row where user and name match, files cascade, an audit event 'skill_uninstalled' is recorded.
CLI and VS Code: a SKILL.md file is written to disk; no server call.

steps.what_happens: The client checks the file against the payload limit and posts it as a multipart form (field 'file') with a CSRF token on web or the session on mobile.
The server checks CSRF, the rate limit, authoring and the workspace Skills feature.
The bytes are inspected by the upload scanner, then a zip is detected by its first four bytes; a zip is opened and must hold exactly one SKILL.md directly inside one folder named like the skill.
Text companion files are read; non-text ones are listed as omitted. Frontmatter is parsed and only allowed keys pass.
The package is scanned; blocked content is refused, review-level content needs an acknowledgement hash sent back by the client.
The skill row and its file rows are inserted in one transaction; a duplicate name returns 409.
The client reloads the list and shows the result.
CLI import copies files on disk and validates the copy.
Export: the client opens the download URL; the server streams the file bytes with attachment headers.

features.summary: A skill can ship extra text files (references, templates, scripts) beside SKILL.md. On the web, desktop (hosted web), mobile and Chrome paths, the cloud chat loop lists them, reads them on request and copies them into a code sandbox so scripts can run. In the CLI and VS Code the files stay in the skill folder on disk.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps a skill's whole folder, not just SKILL.md. The model sees a file list when it loads a skill, can read any listed text file, and can run bundled scripts: in the cloud code sandbox on web/desktop/mobile, or through the model's own file and shell tools on the CLI and VS Code.
purpose.why_it_exists: A skill that is only instructions loses the templates, references and scripts it needs. The migration that stores skill files says Claude and ChatGPT keep a skill's folder whole and run its scripts in a code sandbox (apps/web/db/neon/0318_user_skill_files.sql:1-12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Skill authors who upload a zip or folder, and anyone who installs a skill from the catalog, a plugin repository, a workspace, or the CLI skills folder.
problems_solved: A skill folder uploaded as a zip no longer loses its references and scripts (apps/web/db/neon/0318_user_skill_files.sql:5-9).
The model reads long reference material only when the skill points at it, so the base prompt stays small (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:23-27 description of action=read).
Scripts can run without the user installing anything, inside the cloud sandbox (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:80-96).
use_cases: Upload a zip of a skill folder with a references/ folder and a scripts/ folder; ask a question; the model loads the skill, reads a reference and runs a script.
Install a plugin from a repository whose skills carry templates; the model reads them on demand.
CLI: put scripts/ next to SKILL.md in ~/.agiworkforce/skills/<name>; the loaded skill tells the model where the folder is.
Turn code execution off; load a skill with scripts; the model is told the scripts cannot run here.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): Settings, Skills directory, button 'Upload a skill' (accepts .zip, .skill or SKILL.md) (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:408-415); the skill detail view shows a file tree and a file viewer with a 'Download file' button for non-text files (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/SkillFileViewer.tsx:180-195, packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:251).

Mobile: skill detail screen, section 'Files' with the text 'The instructions and the reference files and scripts bundled with them.'; tapping a text file previews it (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillDetailScreen.tsx:317-360).

CLI: skill folder under ~/.agiworkforce/skills/<name>/ or <project>/.agiworkforce/skills/<name>/; commands '/skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder>' and '/skills remove <name>' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6169-6186).

VS Code: command-palette skill manager 'Skills' with items 'Create a skill' and 'Install a skill' ('Copy a skill folder, the one that holds SKILL.md, into your skills') (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:220-247).
Chrome: no screen; the side panel only lets the person pick a skill by name (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/skillsClient.ts:30-48).
prerequisites: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome: signed in; skill authoring is on unless the server switch AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING is '0' (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts:6-13); the workspace policy must allow the 'skills' feature (apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:215-221).
Running scripts in the cloud: code execution must be offered in that chat turn (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:87).
CLI and VS Code: a skill folder on disk; project skills also need the person's consent (see F053-08).
screens_and_controls: Upload a skill dialog (UploadFileDialog) with a trust notice (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryPanel.tsx:1060-1076).
Skill detail: file tree, rendered/raw toggle, copy, 'Download file' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/SkillFileViewer.tsx:163-215).

Upload result lines: '/<skill name>' and, when files were left out, 'Left out a file that is not text: <files>. Skills can bundle text files such as references and scripts.' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:311-326).
Mobile 'Files' list, with 'no preview' for non-text files (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillDetailScreen.tsx:322-335).
journey: 1. Author zips the skill folder as <skill-name>/SKILL.md plus other files and chooses 'Upload a skill' (apps/web/app/api/skills/skill-upload-rules.ts:5-18).

2. The server checks the zip, reads text companions (binary or empty ones are left out and named), scans every file for unsafe content, and stores a personal skill plus one row per file (apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:84-139, apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-service.ts:261-293).
3. In chat the skill is picked by the person or offered by relevance; the model calls the skill tool with action=load (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1047-1102).
4. The result lists up to 50 files with sizes; the model calls action=read with an exact path for the ones it needs (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:252-265, 454-486).

5. If any listed file looks like a script, the loaded result gets a skill_sandbox note: either 'code execution is off ... turning on code execution lets the skill run its scripts' or the sandbox folder where files will be copied (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:26-27, 72-96).

6. The first time the model runs code in that turn the files are copied to <workspace>/.skills/<skill name>/ and the model runs a script from there (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:4900-4930).
feedback_and_outputs: Upload success title 'Skill added' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:306).

Read failures shown to the model: 'No file at <path> in this skill. Load the skill again for its file list.', '<path> is not text and cannot be read.', '<path> is too large to read.' (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:445-452).
Result too big: the model gets 'Skill output exceeded the safe response limit and was not returned.' (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:238-251).
Skipped files named in the sandbox note: 'These files were not copied because they are not text or are too large: ...' (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:72-78).
settings: Server switch AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING (name only; '0' turns authoring off) (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts:6).

Per-chat code execution setting (Run code); on mobile it is switched on automatically for a skill that requires the code-run tool when the plan allows it (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/skillRequirements.ts:21-39).
Enable/disable of a skill: web directory toggle, CLI '/skills-toggle' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4520).

working: Cloud skill tool with list, load and read actions, file inventory capped at 50 entries and default output cap of 100000 bytes (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:4-5, 454-486).

Reading files from five stores: built-in catalog (apps/web/lib/services/skill-catalog-service.ts:473-484), the person's personal skill files (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-service.ts:334-392), stored plugin entries, workspace plugins, community submissions and GitHub repositories (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/skill-companions.ts:99-219).

Per-file limits: at most 200 listed files and 512 KiB per file (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:137-138); non-UTF-8 or NUL-containing files are 'binary' (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/skill-companions.ts:55-63).

Zip upload keeps text companions, names the others in omittedFiles, and refuses a zip with more than 200 files (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/archive.ts:300-338, 651-673; apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:222-258).

Sandbox staging: files recognised as scripts (a scripts/ folder or py, js, mjs, cjs, ts, sh, bash, rb, pl, r) trigger copying of up to 100 files and 4 MiB of text to the sandbox; unsafe paths, binary and oversize files are skipped and named (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:8-11, 38-78).
Copy is deferred until the sandbox exists and is flushed right after attachments are staged (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:4900-4930).
If code execution is not offered the model gets an explicit note instead of a failed run (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:26-27, 87).
Uploaded files are scanned; a blocking finding refuses the save, a review finding needs an acknowledgement hash (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-service.ts:122-150).

CLI: a skill folder is hashed as a whole (SKILL.md plus scripts/references/assets), and the loaded result tells the model the package directory so relative paths resolve there (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:884-908, 1202-1232).
CLI import copies a skill folder (max 500 files, skipping links and dotfiles) into the global skills folder (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:1496-1588).
CLI signed in: account skills are synced to disk with up to 64 files of at most 1,000,000 bytes each (apps/cli/src/cloud/skills.rs:14-15, 130-165).

VS Code lists, enables, installs from a folder and removes skills by calling the CLI runtime (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/cliCapabilities.ts:10-14; apps/cli/src/app_server/surfaces.rs:996-1005).
Mobile detail screen lists files and previews text ones through the same /api/skills/<name>/files routes (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/service.ts:152-185).
incomplete: CLI has no read action: invoke_skill_tool accepts only list and load ('Unsupported skill action ... Expected list or load') (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:1459-1463). Files are read by the model's own tools [inferred].
Files cannot be added, replaced or removed after a personal skill is created: the update statement changes only name, description and body (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-service.ts:295-318).

The sandbox note says files 'are copied' before the copy happens, and a failed copy is only logged ('some skill files could not be copied into the sandbox') (apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:72-78, 98-118).

A file between roughly 100 KB and 512 KiB can be stored and listed but a read returns the 'exceeded the safe response limit' error because the output cap is 100000 bytes (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:138; packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:238-251) [inferred from both limits].
The inventory shows 50 files while up to 200 are readable; files beyond 50 appear only as '<omitted count>' with no names (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:252-265).
disconnected_or_disabled: Skill authoring and personal-skill file storage switch off with AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING=0; list, find and create then return nothing or 404 (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-service.ts:160-176).
The implicit skill offer is skipped for the vscode, cli and api surfaces of the cloud chat route (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1073-1090).
apps/desktop/src (retained Tauri code) has SkillsPluginsSettings.tsx; whether it handles bundled files was not checked (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/SkillsPluginsSettings.tsx).
not_available: Mobile: no mobile-side reading or sandbox of bundled files; the brief marks S53.10 and S53.11 missing, and the code agrees that all file work is server-side (brief: S53.10, S53.11). Mobile only shows the file list and turns on code execution for skills that require it.
Chrome: no file list, reader or sandbox control (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/skillsClient.ts).
Local mode on every app: the bundle reader and sandbox live in the cloud chat route; no on-device sandbox for skill scripts was found [inferred from absence in apps/mobile and apps/extension].

established.statement: A skill can bundle reference files that the model reads when the skill runs.
A skill can bundle scripts that run when the skill is used.
Reference files are listed (up to 50 entries) and read on request; a skill tool result is capped at 100000 bytes by default.
A skill with scripts is copied into the sandbox when code first runs in a turn; if code execution is off the model is told.
Files that are not text or are too large are skipped and named in the note.
Claude and ChatGPT keep a skill folder whole (SKILL.md plus references, assets and scripts), read while the skill runs and executed in the code sandbox; the product follows them.

acceptance_criteria: Upload a zip <name>/SKILL.md + references/a.md + scripts/run.py: the skill is created and its detail view lists both files.
Upload a zip that also holds a PNG: the result says a file that is not text was left out and names it; the skill still works.
In a chat with code execution on, load the skill and ask for the script to run: the result carries a skill_sandbox note with the .skills/<name> path, and a run from that path finds run.py.
In a chat with code execution off, load the same skill: the result carries the note that scripts cannot run and the model tells the person so.
A read of a path not in the list returns the 'No file at ... Load the skill again' error; a read of a binary file returns 'is not text and cannot be read'.
A skill with 60 files shows 50 entries and an 'omitted count=10' line.
CLI: a skill with scripts/ in its folder shows the package directory in the loaded result, and changing a script changes the tree hash.
inferred: A staged-copy failure should be reported to the model instead of claiming the copy happened [inferred from skill-staging.ts:72-78 vs 98-118].
The read-size limit and the output cap should agree so a listed file is always readable [inferred].
Mobile and Chrome should be able to show bundle contents and script needs the same way the web does [inferred from brief status 'missing'].
proposed: [proposed] Let a person add, replace and remove files on an existing personal skill.
[proposed] Report files skipped in staging, and failed writes, to the model in the same note.
[proposed] Give the CLI skill tool a read action with package-contained paths, as the cloud tool has.

steps.what_happens: Person uploads a zip; the browser posts multipart form data to POST /api/skills.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, workspace policy for the 'skills' feature, scans the upload for unsafe content, reads the zip and parses SKILL.md.
Server stores the skill row and one file row per text companion in one database transaction; writes an audit event 'skill_installed'.
In a chat turn the cloud route adds the skill tool; the model asks to load the skill; the server returns the instructions plus the file inventory.
The model reads files with action=read; the server reads from the database, a stored plugin entry, or a repository over HTTPS (raw file fetch with a timeout).
Repository-hosted skill files are listed from a GitHub tree and fetched from the repository host.
Script files are queued; when the model first runs code the files are written into the code sandbox under .skills/<name>; scripts run there.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The skill tool is offered only to models that can call tools; the implicit offer checks toolsCapable and the sandbox needs a model with code execution capability and permission (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1082-1090, 5925-5937). Any model family that meets those checks can use it; no provider-specific code was found in the skill files path. In the CLI the instructions go to whichever model the person configured.

access_and_usage.account: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome: signed in (the routes use user-scoped database access: apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:141-146). CLI and VS Code: skills on disk need no account; account skills sync only when signed in (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:222-232).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace policy for the 'skills' feature can refuse creating a skill (apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:215-221). Workspace plugin policy can hide plugin and directory skills (apps/web/app/api/skills/route.ts:146-160). Skill-file content is always treated as untrusted reference guidance (packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:267-278).
access_and_usage.subscription: The skills capability is true for the web, desktop and mobile rows (packages/contracts/types/src/capabilities.ts:55, 88, 121). The CLI hides skills when the cached capability document denies canUseSkills, for example 'on your plan' (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:144-148; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:376-392). Plan-specific rules for bundled files: none found in the code. Running scripts needs cloud code execution, and mobile needs the tier flag codeExecutionAvailable plus canUseCloudExecution (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/skillRequirements.ts:26-36).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 200 files and 512 KiB per file, 50 files shown, 100000-byte tool output, 100 files and 4 MiB staged (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:137-138; packages/tools/skills/src/tool.ts:4-5; apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts:10-11). The cloud sandbox is metered as hosted code execution (apps/web/lib/e2b/compute-metering.ts, apps/web/lib/e2b/hosted-code-execution.ts); exact plan amounts: unknown. No metering was found for reading files.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING (server switch); mobile FEATURES.skills and FEATURES.codeExecution (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:20, 34).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs a tool-calling model; running scripts needs a model with code-execution capability (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:5925-5937). Whether specific models are excluded: unknown.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: The free-trial route refuses code execution when the trial capabilities do not include it (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4383). Other provider restrictions: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile and Desktop on-device models: the bundle reader and sandbox are part of the cloud chat route, so scripts do not run on-device; whether a Local chat can use a skill's files at all: unknown. CLI: everything is on the device; no sign-in or payment is needed for skills on disk, and a missing capability cache lets skills load (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:376-380).

features.summary: A skill can belong to one project folder (CLI and VS Code, loaded only after the person allows it) or be shared with a workspace (web: an admin publishes a personal skill as a workspace plugin that members can add, or that an admin can require). Web, desktop and mobile have no per-project skill scope.

purpose.what_it_does: CLI and VS Code: loads skills from <project>/.agiworkforce/skills only after the person allows that exact set. Web: lets a workspace admin share a personal skill with the workspace through the workspace plugin system.
purpose.why_it_exists: Repository skills are instructions written by whoever writes the repository, so they must not reach the model unasked (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:285-292). Teams also want one skill every member can use (apps/web/app/api/skills/[name]/workspace/route.ts:35-44).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers working in a shared repository; workspace admins who want to give a team a skill.
problems_solved: A cloned repository cannot silently add instructions to the model.
A team no longer has to ask each member to upload the same skill.
A project can override a global skill of the same name, because project skills load first (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:155-160).
use_cases: CLI: commit .agiworkforce/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md; the first run in the repo asks 'Load them?'; the answer is remembered until a skill changes.
VS Code: 'New skill' then 'This project'; then 'Allow this folder’s project skills'.
Web admin: edit a personal skill and press 'Share with workspace'; members then add it from Skills.
Web admin: publish a skill as 'required' or 'installed by default' through workspace plugin settings.

where_to_find_it: CLI: folder .agiworkforce/skills in the project; prompt on terminal; '/skills-toggle' to turn skills off; project file .agiworkforce/disabled-skills.json (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:111-125; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4520).

VS Code: command-palette Skills manager; 'Create a skill' opens a quick pick titled '<product>, New skill' with 'Personal' and 'This project'; item '$(shield) Allow this folder’s project skills' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/skillAuthoring.ts:33-50; capabilityManagement.ts:250-254).
Web and Desktop: Settings, Skills, skill editor (edit mode) shows the section 'Share with your workspace' for workspace admins (apps/web/features/skills/components/SkillEditorDialog.tsx:264-304).
Mobile, Chrome: no project or workspace scope control found.
prerequisites: CLI: project folder trusted for its disabled list (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:111-114); a terminal to answer the prompt, or consent given through VS Code (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:445-448).

VS Code: a trusted workspace, otherwise the item reads 'Open a trusted workspace to reach the AGI CLI.' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/cliCapabilities.ts:5-6); AGI CLI at the minimum supported version.
Web share: signed in, personal skill saved (no unsaved changes), workspace permission policy.manage (apps/web/app/api/skills/[name]/workspace/route.ts:15-33).
screens_and_controls: CLI consent question: 'This project supplies N skill(s) of its own that would load on every run in <path>: <names>. Load them? You are asked again when one changes.' (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:459-466).

VS Code rows show scope text and ', not allowed yet' until allowed; a 'Review skill file' button opens the file for review before allowing (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:257-303).

Web editor: confirm dialog 'Share <name> with your workspace?' with button 'Share with workspace'; success text 'Shared. Members can add it from Skills now.' (apps/web/features/skills/components/SkillEditorDialog.tsx:264-304).
journey: CLI: 1. Put SKILL.md in .agiworkforce/skills/<name>. 2. Run the CLI in the project. 3. Answer the question. 4. The skills load; the answer is stored against that exact set. 5. Edit or add a skill: asked again.

VS Code: 1. Skills manager, 'Create a skill', choose 'This project', give a name and 'When should AGI use this skill?'. 2. The SKILL.md opens for editing. 3. Choose 'Allow this folder’s project skills'. 4. Skills load in sessions for that workspace.
Web: 1. Edit a personal skill. 2. 'Share with workspace', confirm. 3. Members see it under workspace plugins and add it, unless the admin changes its install preference.
feedback_and_outputs: Declined sets are not asked again in the same run (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:289-290, 449-457).
VS Code error toasts use the CLI's refusal reason (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:79-85).
Web share errors show the server message or 'Could not share this skill with the workspace.' (apps/web/features/skills/hooks/useSkillsSettingsAdapter.tsx:22, 113-134).
settings: CLI: ~/.agiworkforce/project-skills-consent.json (config folder) and ~/.agiworkforce/disabled-skills.json; project .agiworkforce/disabled-skills.json (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:95-125, 285).
VS Code: environment AGIWORKFORCE_HOME to relocate the personal skills folder (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/skillAuthoring.ts:9-15).
Web: workspace plugin install preference values required, installed_by_default, available, not_available (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/plugin-packages.ts:14-19).

working: CLI loads project skills first, then user, account, plugin and project-plugin skills; a project skill wins a name clash because the first entry wins (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:155-190, 1252-1275).
Consent is kept in the user's config folder as a digest of file paths, content hashes, package hashes and hidden or linked package members; any change asks again (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:329-424).
With no terminal the project skills do not load, and the app-server reports the gate read-only (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:445-448, 482-496).
Project skill files are read only as regular files inside the project (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:798-806).
CLI and VS Code can grant and revoke consent (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:529-562; apps/cli/src/app_server/surfaces.rs:153-170).
VS Code 'New skill' writes <folder>/.agiworkforce/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and refuses to overwrite (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/skillAuthoring.ts:31-88).

Web: POST /api/skills/{name}/workspace publishes a personal skill with its files as a workspace plugin, needs policy.manage, writes an audit event (apps/web/app/api/skills/[name]/workspace/route.ts:22-61).

Web: workspace plugin skills reach members who have the plugin enabled (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/installed-skills.ts:115-144), with their files (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/skill-companions.ts:111-122).
incomplete: The share button publishes with preference 'available' only; making it required or installed by default is done elsewhere in workspace plugin settings (apps/web/app/api/skills/[name]/workspace/route.ts:41; apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/plugins/route.ts:118-140).
No UI that calls the share endpoint was found outside the web skill editor (searched apps and packages).
Project-level disabled list is read only for trusted projects (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:111-114).
disconnected_or_disabled: The generated surface matrix says VS Code is 'absent' for skills, but the extension has a skills manager; the matrix is older than the code (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:368 vs apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:220).
not_available: Web, Desktop, Mobile project scope: no skill is tied to a project; skill sources 'project' and 'workspace' exist in the contract but no web project-skill authoring was found (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/skills.ts:10-17; brief S53.04).
Chrome: no scope control (brief S53.04, S53.05).
Mobile: no share or scope control found; it only labels sources 'Project' and 'Workspace' (apps/mobile/src/features/skills/SkillsScreen.tsx:46-47).
CLI and VS Code: no organisation skills or sharing (brief S53.05, S53.25).

established.statement: Skills can be scoped to a project so they load only in that project.
An organization can provide skills that all its members get.
A user can share a skill with their organization.
Project skills load only after the project is consented (CLI) or allowed once (VS Code).
Developer extension discovery is folder-aware; CLI and VS Code show the same inventory for the same trusted workspace; compatibility never authorises changing another tool's files.

acceptance_criteria: CLI: a project with one skill and no recorded consent asks once on a terminal and loads nothing if declined.
CLI: after a yes, adding a new skill file or editing one asks again.
CLI: a project skill named like a global skill is the one the model sees.
VS Code: a created project skill shows 'not allowed yet' until 'Allow this folder’s project skills' is chosen.
Web: a non-admin does not see the 'Share with your workspace' section; an admin does and, after confirming, members see the skill under workspace plugins.
Web: sharing a skill with unsaved edits is blocked (button disabled while dirty).
A skill with files keeps its files when shared.
inferred: Web, Desktop and Mobile project scope is wanted because the brief lists S53.04 as 'Should' for every app; the code shows none [inferred].

Organisation skill delivery for members should be visible in the skill directory with the workspace as source [inferred from origin kind 'workspace' in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/skills.ts:28-35].
proposed: [proposed] Attach a skill to a web Project so it loads only in chats of that project.
[proposed] Offer 'required for everyone' directly from the share confirmation.
[proposed] Show the consent digest change reason (which skill changed) in the CLI prompt.

steps.what_happens: CLI starts, reads the project .agiworkforce/skills folder (regular files inside the project only) and the config-folder consent file.
CLI hashes the project skill set and compares with the stored digest; on mismatch it asks on the terminal.
VS Code asks the CLI runtime for the list, shows the digest, and sends consent with the digest it showed; the CLI refuses if the set changed meanwhile.
Web admin presses Share; the browser posts to /api/skills/{name}/workspace.
Server checks permission policy.manage, reads the personal skill and its files, scans, publishes the workspace plugin in the database and records an audit event.
Members' skill lists and chat turns include the workspace plugin's skills when the plugin is enabled for them.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Scope does not depend on a model. Project skill text is sent to whichever model the CLI or VS Code session uses, only after consent. Workspace skills are loaded by the cloud chat loop for any tool-calling model.

access_and_usage.account: CLI project scope needs no account. Web sharing needs a signed-in admin of a workspace (apps/web/app/api/skills/[name]/workspace/route.ts:25-33).
access_and_usage.permissions: CLI: user consent plus project trust for the disabled list. VS Code: workspace trust and CLI version. Web: permission policy.manage (apps/web/app/api/skills/[name]/workspace/route.ts:15, 31-33).
access_and_usage.subscription: The CLI hides all skills when the cached capability document denies canUseSkills (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:144-148). Whether workspace plugins need a specific plan: none found in the code read.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Same file limits as F053-07 for shared skills. Number of workspace plugins: unknown. No metering found for scope features.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING must not be '0' for a personal skill to exist to share (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts:6).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: No model rule found for scope.
access_and_usage.local_mode: CLI project scope is entirely local: no sign-in or payment needed, and skills load with local or own-key models. Web workspace sharing is cloud only. Desktop and Mobile local inference: no project scope exists.

features.summary: Not built. A skill cannot declare the inputs it takes, the outputs it makes, or the apps it works on. No app reads such fields, and the web upload refuses unknown frontmatter keys. The nearest existing fields are required tools, required connectors and an unused argument-hint.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a skill state inputs a person or model fills in, outputs it should produce, and the surfaces it works on, so apps could show or check them.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S53.12, S53.13 and S53.16 list these as required behaviour for every app; none is built.
purpose.who_uses_it: Skill authors and people choosing a skill; nobody can use it today.
problems_solved: Today a person cannot tell from the skill which apps it works on or what it needs besides tools and connectors; only required tools and connectors are shown (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/SkillDetailView.tsx:64-120).

established.statement: A skill can call or build on other skills as part of its workflow.
A user can choose which version of a skill to use.
The product notifies users when an installed skill has an update.
A user can duplicate a skill (e.g. a built-in one) and customize the copy.

acceptance_criteria: A skill body that names another skill leads the model to load that skill by exact name (today: model can call the tool again; no declared dependency).
Version shows in detail on web, desktop and mobile only when declared.
A user can choose among versions and the chosen one is the one loaded.
An installed skill with a newer version shows an update notice.
'Use as a template' keeps the files of the source skill.
Duplicating a built-in skill on web gives an editable personal copy.

features.summary: Partly built. On the desktop app, 'Record a skill' takes a screenshot every few seconds (macOS and Windows), then attaches chosen screenshots to a chat so the model drafts a skill. No voice, no replay settings. Save-as-skill turns finished chat work into a skill draft. The CLI auto-writes skills from repeated tool use.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person teach a skill by showing the screen: the desktop records screenshots with consent, the person picks frames, and the chat drafts a skill from them. A separate 'turn this chat into a skill' prompt and a CLI pattern learner also create skills without hand-writing.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S53.27 to S53.30 ask for creation by demonstration, screen and voice teaching, replay configuration and generation from examples.
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users with a skill-capable account; any chat user for save-as-skill; CLI users after repeated sessions.
problems_solved: Writing a skill from scratch is slow; screenshots give the model the steps.
Finished work in a chat can become a reusable skill (apps/web/features/skills/components/save-as-skill.ts:8-15).
use_cases: On the desktop app: record a task in another app, stop, choose screenshots, 'Draft a skill', describe the goal, send.
Web chat: ask 'Turn the work we just finished in this chat into a reusable skill' and save the draft card.
CLI: after the same tool pattern appears in 3 or more sessions a skill file is written to ~/.agiworkforce/skills/learned/.

established.statement: A user can create a skill by recording a demonstration of the task.
A user can teach a skill by showing the screen and narrating with voice.
A recorded skill has configurable replay settings.
A user can create a skill from examples or a template, with the product generating the skill.
Recording needs explicit consent; clicks, typing and audio are not recorded; screenshots stay on the device until saved or discarded.

acceptance_criteria: In the desktop app, 'Record a skill' shows the consent text before anything is captured; Cancel or Escape captures nothing.
Recording stops by itself after 10 minutes or 200 screenshots and says why.
Frames taken while a password field is active are skipped and counted.
Discarding asks first and names the screenshot count.
'Draft a skill' attaches no more screenshots than the plan allows and selects skill-creator.
In a browser, and for an account that cannot author skills, the row is absent.
A stopped recording not saved or discarded is dropped after 15 minutes.
inferred: Replay (S53.29) implies stored steps, which the screenshot-only recording does not produce [inferred].
Voice teaching needs microphone consent and the voice system [inferred from SYS-voice-and-media].
proposed: [proposed] Add narration as a second channel with its own consent.
[proposed] Offer the recorder on Windows and macOS CLI-free surfaces only after the brief is corrected.
[proposed] Make the CLI learner use real success.

steps.what_happens: Page asks the Electron host to start capture with the consent revision; the host shows its own prompt.
The host takes JPEG screenshots every 3 seconds, skips while secure input is active, and keeps them in memory until saved or discarded.
Person chooses frames; the page turns them into files and attaches them to the chat composer.
On send, attachments go to the cloud chat; the model (with the skill-creator skill) drafts a skill; the person saves it.
CLI: after a successful turn, tool counts are compared with recent sessions and a SKILL.md is written under the config folder.

data.retained_or_deleted: An unsaved stopped recording is deleted after 15 minutes; discard deletes immediately (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/skill-capture.ts:44; SkillRecorder.tsx:95-97).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The skill is drafted by whichever model the cloud chat route serves for that turn; the draft needs a model that accepts images and calls the draft tool. Which models qualify: unknown. The CLI learner uses no model call (apps/cli/src/skill_learner.rs:5-6).

access_and_usage.account: The recorder row needs a signed-in account that can author skills (apps/web/features/skill-recorder/hooks/use-skill-recorder-entry.ts:20-34). The CLI learner needs none.
access_and_usage.permissions: macOS Screen Recording permission; the host consent prompt; the recorder never records clicks, typing or audio (SkillRecorder.tsx:55). Egress and attachment rules for the chat apply on send.
access_and_usage.subscription: Screenshots chosen are limited by the plan's attachment allowance per message (apps/web/features/skill-recorder/components/SkillRecorder.tsx:25-28, getPlanMaxAttachmentsPerMessage). Plan names and numbers: read from the types package, not restated here. Skill authoring capability comes from the catalog (canAuthorSkills).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 10 minutes, 200 screenshots, 1280 px width, 15 minutes retention (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/skill-capture.ts:38-45); the drafting chat turn is metered like any chat turn.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING (authoring on/off); host feature detection for 'skill_capture_*' commands, which an older host answers with unknown-command (apps/web/features/skill-recorder/lib/skill-capture-client.ts:57-59).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Image input and tool calling needed for the draft turn; specific models: unknown.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: The free-trial route refuses image input when trial capabilities exclude vision (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4383-4390).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Recording itself is on-device and needs no payment. Drafting the skill sends screenshots to the cloud chat; a Local (on-device model) draft path was not found, so Local-only recording-to-skill is not available [inferred].
