features.summary: One place to shape what the assistant can do: Skills, Connectors and Plugins. On web and the public Desktop it is the 'Customize' group in Settings. Mobile has a Customize screen. The CLI has plugin commands and a /plugin overlay. VS Code has separate Plugins and Skills pickers. Chrome has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Gathers the three ways to extend the assistant (skills, connectors, plugins) under one name. On web it is a nav group of the settings modal whose Plugins panel is the shared directory panel (packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts:374-386; packages/ui/ui/src/settings-modal/SettingsModal.tsx:2198-2256). Old /chat/customize links redirect into it (apps/web/app/chat/customize/page.tsx:17-23).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S54.01 says one Customize destination should gather skills, connectors and plugins. The product requirements list plugins, skills and connectors together as one extensibility area (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who wants to add skills, connect apps or install plugins. Developers use the CLI and VS Code equivalents. Workspace members see their workspace's plugins in the same tab.
problems_solved: People do not need to know three different places for skills, connectors and plugins.
Old shared links still land on the right section instead of an error page.
A workspace administrator can switch skills or plugins off and the tab says so instead of showing a broken list.
use_cases: A web user opens Settings, then Customize, then Plugins to install a plugin.
A phone user taps Customize and sees a Plugins row with a count of added plugins.
A developer runs 'agi plugin list' or opens /plugin in the terminal to see what is installed.
A VS Code user runs the 'Code: Show Plugins' command to turn a plugin off.

Old link: /chat/customize?section=skills|connectors|plugins redirects to /settings/<section> (apps/web/app/chat/customize/page.tsx:5-23).
Desktop (public, Electron): the same hosted web app, so the same Settings (doc: AGENTS.md section 5; apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:17).

Mobile: the 'Customize' screen lists 'Plugins', 'Skills' (when the skills flag is on), 'Connectors' and 'Agents' (apps/mobile/src/features/customize/CustomizeScreen.tsx:41-77; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:20).

(apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2340), 'agi connectors' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1275), and the /plugin, /plugins, /marketplace, /market slash command that opens a tabbed overlay (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6292; apps/cli/src/command_registry.rs:576); /skills (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6198).

established.statement: One Customize destination gathers skills, connectors and plugins.
A Plugins section lists available and installed plugins.
A Skills section sits beside plugins in the customization area.
A Connectors section sits in the customization area.
Old Customize links must still reach the right section; the chat route redirects to settings; only skills, connectors and plugins are accepted and anything else opens General.
Plugins requirements: install, enable or disable, update, uninstall, namespacing, marketplace and source controls, included MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents and prompts.

Install, enable, update, disable and uninstall of skills and plugins affect the next turn and survive reload; failed source fetches and revoked workspace permissions are explained without claiming installation.

acceptance_criteria: Web: Settings shows a Customize group with Skills, Connectors, Plugins and each opens its panel.
Visiting /chat/customize?section=plugins lands on /settings/plugins; ?section=bogus and no section land on /settings/general.
With the workspace plugins switch off, the Plugins tab shows the denial reason and no list.

CLI: 'agi plugin list' prints each installed plugin with enabled or disabled state and signature.
Chrome extension offers no Customize screen (expected absent).

features.summary: Browse and search the plugin catalogue. The server merges built-in packs with a daily-refreshed copy of an outside public directory and the official marketplace repository. People filter by source, works-with, category and publisher, and page through results. Web and Desktop use it. Mobile has its own screen. CLI searches only the account's own marketplaces.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists plugins from the catalogue with search text, source tabs (Built in, Partners, Marketplace), works-with and category filters, a publisher filter reached from a plugin's page, and paging (apps/web/app/api/plugins/route.ts:30-42; apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:1108-1150).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S54.05, S54.08 and S54.09: a user can browse a public plugin marketplace, search and filter it, and browse role or use-case categories. Product requirements ask for marketplace and source controls (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on web or the public Desktop, and phone users in Cloud mode. Developers use the CLI for account marketplaces and VS Code for the account marketplace picker.
problems_solved: Finding a plugin without knowing its name.
Seeing only plugins that work on this surface (works-with filter).
Keeping a long list usable by paging and category shelves.
use_cases: Search 'calendar' and install the top matching plugin.
Filter by category to browse plugins for one job.
On the phone, scan the Popular shelf and category shelves.
In the CLI, search the plugins of marketplaces added to the account.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Customize, Plugins (packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts:378). Search box placeholder 'Search plugins' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:58-62).
Mobile: Customize, Plugins; bottom search bar 'Search plugins' (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:845-851).
CLI: 'agi marketplace browse', 'agi marketplace search <query>', 'agi marketplace show <plugin>@<marketplace>' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2340-2380, 7552-7632).
VS Code: 'Code: Browse AGI Cloud Marketplace' with a search box 'Search plugins by name, description, or source' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/accountMarketplace.ts:104).
Chrome: not available.
prerequisites: Signed in on web, Desktop, mobile and VS Code. Catalogue reads need only the public API on web (GET /api/plugins is public, apps/web/app/api/plugins/route.ts:50-56) but the settings tab is behind sign-in.
Mobile: Cloud mode (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:658).
CLI: an account; the account's plan must not deny canUseMarketplace (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7553-7558).
screens_and_controls: Web: search field with Clear button, source tabs All, Built in, Partners, Marketplace and one tab per marketplace the user added, 'Works with' filter (Web, CLI, Cowork), 'Category' filter, count label such as '120 plugins' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryToolbar.tsx:84-140; apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:93-98, 150-154, 119).
Web: sort control is hidden because plugins offer one sort (name) (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:149; packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryToolbar.tsx:222).
Web: the 'verified' and 'status' filters exist on the server but have no control in the UI (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:219-232).

Mobile: chips All, Built in, Partners, Marketplace, Popular, Name; a second row 'Every category' plus one chip per category; sections Updates available, Popular, Recommended for you, category shelves, All plugins; 'Show more' button (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:76-86, 704-840).
VS Code: quick pick list of marketplace entries plus 'Manage marketplace sources' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/accountMarketplace.ts:83-102).
journey: Open the Plugins tab; the first page loads (100 per page on web).
Type in the search box; after 250 ms the list reloads.
Choose a source tab or filters; the list reloads with the new request.
Scroll down; near the bottom the next page loads automatically (a 'Load more' label exists too).
Click a plugin to open its detail (F054-06).
feedback_and_outputs: Web error: 'The plugin catalog is unavailable right now.' when the directory request fails and nothing else can be shown (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:243).
Mobile empty: 'No matching plugins' with 'Try a different name, category or source.', or 'No plugins yet' (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:770-775).
Mobile load error banner with retry; refresh by pulling down (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:701-702).
settings: No user setting. Page size and limits are constants (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:182; apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:68-70).

working: GET /api/plugins validates search (trim, 1-200 chars), verified, worksWith, source, category (max 100), publisher (max 200), status, sort (installs or name), limit (1-100), cursor (digits only, max 7), offset (0-10000); a bad value returns 400 INVALID_QUERY (apps/web/app/api/plugins/route.ts:22-72).

Results are filtered, sorted (default most installs, then name) and ranked by eight search rules from exact name to marketplace name; the page comes back with total, nextCursor and stats (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/query.ts:67-156).
The catalogue is built-in packs from the registry plus a snapshot of external entries, merged (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/catalog.ts:11-37).

The snapshot is refreshed by a daily cron that reads the outside public directory and the official marketplace repository (vercel.json:158-159; apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/ingest.ts:146; apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:1-17).
Rate limit 'model-catalog' 120 per minute per IP, fail-open; response cached 60 s with 300 s stale-while-revalidate (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:459-463; apps/web/app/api/plugins/route.ts:55, 83).

Web client: debounced search (250 ms), IntersectionObserver paging, source, works-with, category and publisher filters (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:386; packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryPanel.tsx:269; apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:219-254).

Web: a 'popular' group of up to 6 verified, installable, not-yet-installed plugins ranked by installs (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:1222-1239; apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:118).
Mobile: search, source, sort and category chips, category shelves, Show more with cursor (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:304-460, 704-840).
CLI: search and browse over entries of the marketplaces added to the account (apps/cli/src/cloud/marketplaces.rs:145-153; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7552-7632).
VS Code: pick-and-install over the account marketplace entries (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/accountMarketplace.ts:83-170).
incomplete: The web client always sends sort=name and limit=100 and never sends offset or verified (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:219-254), so those server options are unused by web.

Sort order differs by surface: server default is installs, web sends name, mobile defaults to installs (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/query.ts:116; apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginsScreen.tsx:310).
CLI search covers only account marketplaces, not the built-in or public catalogue (apps/cli/src/cloud/marketplaces.rs:145-153); the brief marks CLI public marketplace unverified.
Categories come from the catalogue entries' own category text, lower-cased; there is no editorial role or use-case taxonomy (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/query.ts:48-65).
disconnected_or_disabled: None found for browse on web.
not_available: Mobile has no works-with filter or publisher filter control; it passes publisher only from the detail screen (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginDetailScreen.tsx:101).
VS Code and CLI have no category or works-with filter.
Chrome: nothing.

established.statement: A user can browse a public plugin marketplace and install from it.
A user can search the plugin catalogue and filter the results.
Plugins are grouped into role or use-case categories a user can browse.
Search text is trimmed and capped (200 characters); the server rejects bad filter values with 400 INVALID_QUERY.
Page size is capped by the server at 100 (default 50).
Requests are rate limited.
Marketplace and source controls are a plugin requirement.
Discovery, packaging, compatibility and trustworthy publishers should be explicit for plugins.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/plugins?limit=101 returns 400 INVALID_QUERY; limit=100 returns at most 100 entries.
GET /api/plugins?search=<201 characters> returns 400; a 200-character search succeeds.
Searching an exact plugin name returns it first; a name prefix next; description matches last.
If the response has nextCursor, requesting with cursor returns the following entries with no repeats.
On web, typing in the search box reloads the list once, about 250 ms after the last key.
Source tab Partners shows only partner entries; Marketplace only marketplace entries; Built in only built-in packs.
With the catalogue failing, the tab shows 'The plugin catalog is unavailable right now.' and a retry.
More than 120 requests a minute from one IP get a rate-limit response.
inferred: [inferred] Because GET /api/plugins sets a public cache header and is not user-scoped, the list never contains user-specific data.
[inferred] A tester can count total entries from stats.totalPlugins in the response.
proposed: [proposed] Offer the name and installs sort in the web toolbar since the server supports both.
[proposed] Expose a verified-only filter in the UI.
[proposed] Let CLI search include the built-in and public catalogue.

steps.what_happens: Person types or picks a filter; the panel waits 250 ms then asks the adapter to query.
Adapter fetches built-in and partner pages, installs, user marketplaces, workspace and community plugins, and the marketplace page.
GET /api/plugins checks the rate limit, validates parameters, loads built-in rows from the database and the snapshot from cache, merges, filters, ranks, pages.
Once a day the cron refreshes the snapshot from the outside public directory and the official marketplace GitHub repository, then inspects plugin sources on GitHub.
Scrolling near the end triggers the next page using nextCursor.
CLI search lists the account's marketplaces and entries, then matches name or description on the device.

data.retained_or_deleted: snapshot 7 days, sync state 30 days, inspections 30 days TTL (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:122-126)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider is used for browse, search or filtering. Ranking is rule based (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/query.ts:67-101). access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: IP rate limit 120 per minute, fail-open (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:459-463); mobile and CLI paging limits come from the server. No usage metering against the AGI Subscription was found for browsing.
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for browse on web; mobile pluginMarketplaceAdmin does not affect browse.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model dependent. none found in the code.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code; the catalogue is not tied to a model provider.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web has no Local mode. Public Desktop is Cloud by construction. Mobile in Local mode shows a gate and sends no plugin request. CLI plugin commands over local folders work offline; marketplace browse and search need our servers.

features.summary: A person adds a public GitHub repository that holds a plugin marketplace manifest. The server fetches and checks it, scans it, saves it as a source on the account and lists its plugins, which can then be installed on every surface. Web, Desktop, CLI and VS Code can add; mobile can only list sources because the add form is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Registers a GitHub repository as a personal plugin marketplace, caches the plugins it lists and lets the person refresh or remove it (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/route.ts:39-95; apps/web/lib/services/plugin-marketplace-service.ts:839-907).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S54.07: a user can add a git repository as a plugin marketplace and install plugins listed in it. The migration says it adds a self-serve path beyond the curated catalogue (apps/web/db/neon/0159_plugin_marketplace_sources.sql:3-20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers, teams and publishers who host their own plugin list; also people following a publisher's instructions to add their marketplace.
problems_solved: Installing a plugin that is not in the built-in or public catalogue.
Sharing a set of plugins by publishing one repository.
Keeping the server's outbound fetch to a known host (github.com only).
use_cases: Add a publisher's marketplace from the web Plugins tab and install one plugin.
Run 'agi marketplace add owner/repo' then 'agi marketplace get plugin@marketplace'.
In VS Code choose 'Add GitHub source' in the marketplace picker.
Refresh a marketplace after the repository changed.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Customize, Plugins, 'Add marketplace' action; dialog title 'Add marketplace' with 'Add from a repository', fields 'Repository url' and 'Branch or tag (optional)', button 'Sync marketplace' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:226-236). Added sources become tabs next to Marketplace, removable and refreshable (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:1108-1124).
CLI: 'agi marketplace add <owner/repo or URL> [--ref <tag>] [--name <name>]', 'agi marketplace sources', 'agi marketplace remove <id>' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2340-2362).
VS Code: 'Code: Browse AGI Cloud Marketplace', then 'Manage marketplace sources', then 'Add GitHub source' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/accountMarketplaceSources.ts:115).

Mobile: Plugins screen title menu, then 'Sources' shows sources; the 'Add a marketplace' form exists but is hidden because FEATURES.pluginMarketplaceAdmin is false (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginSourcesScreen.tsx:267; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:32).
Chrome: not available.
prerequisites: Signed in with an AGI account.
A public github.com repository with a marketplace manifest.
Mobile: Cloud mode.
screens_and_controls: Web dialog: Repository url, Branch or tag (optional), Sync marketplace, Cancel. No name field in the dialog; the API accepts an optional name (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/AddMarketplaceDialog.tsx:73; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/plugin-marketplaces.ts:172-178).
CLI: arguments repository_url, --ref, --name; prints 'Added <name> to your account (<n> plugins).' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2758-2778).
VS Code: input boxes 'Public GitHub repository URL' and 'Branch, tag, or commit' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/accountMarketplaceSources.ts:23-40).
Mobile sources screen: lists each source with status, a Sync again button, Remove marketplace, entries with Install or Remove (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginSourcesScreen.tsx:309-410).
journey: Open the add control and enter the repository address (and optional branch).
The surface sends it to the server, which checks it is a public GitHub address, fetches the manifest, validates and scans it.
On success the source appears with its plugin count and the plugins show in the list under that source.
Pick a plugin and install it (F054-06 shows what it includes).
Later use refresh to re-read the repository, or remove to forget it.
feedback_and_outputs: Web failure copy: 'That marketplace could not be synced.' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:244); validation issues are returned as a list.

Server errors: 422 MARKETPLACE_MANIFEST_INVALID with issues, 502 MARKETPLACE_UNREACHABLE, 400 INVALID_MARKETPLACE_SOURCE 'Provide a public GitHub repository URL.' for a malformed body (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/route.ts:46-90).
CLI success line with plugin count; CLI errors pass the server message (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2758-2778).
settings: Optional ref (branch, tag) and optional name when adding. Sources whose name begins 'agi:installed:' are internal shadow sources and are hidden from the list (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/route.ts:34; apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/constants.ts:48-54).

working: POST /api/plugins/marketplaces: CSRF check, rate limit 20 per minute per user (fail-closed), strict body (repositoryUrl up to 2000 characters, ref and name up to 200), audit event 'plugin_marketplace_changed' (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/route.ts:39-76; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:519-523; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/plugin-marketplaces.ts:172-178).

Service: only public github.com URLs (else 'Only public github.com repository URLs are supported.' as a 422), fetch manifest, check connectors against the known connector catalogue, scan, refuse if the scan blocks, upsert the source by canonical URL, replace entries, write dependency declarations, review permission changes in one transaction (apps/web/lib/services/plugin-marketplace-service.ts:839-897, 598-611).

Refresh and remove endpoints exist (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/[id]/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/[id]/refresh) with route tests (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/__tests__/route.test.ts:198-250).
Web adapter addMarketplace, refreshMarketplace, removeMarketplace (apps/web/features/directory/hooks/useDirectoryAdapter.ts:1544, 1906, 1922).
CLI add, sources, remove, browse, show, get (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7499-7617); owner/repo shorthand is converted to a URL by marketplace_repository_url (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2765-2766).
VS Code add, refresh and remove source (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/accountMarketplaceSources.ts:55-105).
incomplete: The brief says the web route 'accepts only a public GitHub address and anything else is refused with a message'. In code a non-GitHub address passes the body check and is refused later as a 422 with the message 'Only public github.com repository URLs are supported.'; only an empty or oversize body gets the 400 (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/route.ts:46-56; apps/web/lib/services/plugin-marketplace-service.ts:844-849).
Web dialog does not offer the optional name field that the API and CLI accept (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:226-236).
No limit on the number of sources per user was found (none found in the code I read).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile 'Add a marketplace' and 'Submit to directory' are switched off by FEATURES.pluginMarketplaceAdmin = false (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginSourcesScreen.tsx:267, 364; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:32).
not_available: Chrome extension: no marketplace code.

Non-GitHub hosts, private repositories and local paths cannot be registered as account marketplaces (the CLI 'marketplace install' from a local path or git URL is a different, on-device install, apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2392-2405).

established.statement: A user can add a git repository as a plugin marketplace and install plugins listed in it.
The web route accepts only a public GitHub repository address and refuses anything else with a message.
A manifest that does not validate is refused with the list of issues.
Each add writes an audit event.
Server fetches only from a fixed known host and pins the manifest by content hash.
Marketplace and source controls are part of the plugin requirements; source revocation must be clear.
Plugin content must be treated as untrusted and reviewed.

acceptance_criteria: Adding https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> with a valid manifest returns 201 and a source with entry count.
Adding https://example.com/x returns 422 with 'Only public github.com repository URLs are supported.'.
A manifest naming an unknown connector returns 422 MARKETPLACE_MANIFEST_INVALID listing that plugin and connector.
A repository that cannot be fetched returns 502 MARKETPLACE_UNREACHABLE.
A request without a CSRF token does not create a source.
After a successful add, an audit event of type plugin_marketplace_changed exists for the user.
Adding the same repository twice updates the same source rather than creating a second.
Removing the source removes its tab and plugins from the list.
inferred: [inferred] Adding a repository does not install anything; installs are a separate action that is checked against workspace policy (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplace-installations/route.ts:148).
[inferred] Because the table has row level security keyed to user, one person's sources are invisible to others (apps/web/db/neon/0159_plugin_marketplace_sources.sql:42-54).
proposed: [proposed] Add the optional name field to the web dialog.
[proposed] Return 400 with the GitHub message for a non-GitHub address so clients can tell it apart from a bad manifest.
[proposed] Enable the mobile add form after review, or remove the hidden code (doc: AGENTS.md section 9 forbids dead controls).

steps.what_happens: Person enters the repository address; the surface posts it with a CSRF token (web) or account token (CLI, VS Code, mobile).
The server checks CSRF, rate limit and the body shape.
The server checks it is a github.com repository and fetches the marketplace manifest from GitHub.
The server validates the manifest against the connector catalogue, scans its text and refuses if blocked.
In one transaction the source is inserted or updated, entries are replaced, dependency declarations are written and permission changes are reviewed.
An audit event is recorded and the source summary is returned with 201.

aliases: Required / Installed by default / Available to install / Not available
features.summary: A workspace administrator uploads plugins or single skills to a private list for the workspace and sets each one to Required, Installed by default, Available to install or Not available, for everyone or for groups. Members see their allowed plugins on web and mobile. Approval requests for blocked plugins do not exist. There is no per-member assignment.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores plugins published by a workspace and resolves, for each member, which are required, on by default, available or hidden. Admins manage this on the workspace Plugins page; members see the result in their Plugins tab group 'From <workspace>' (apps/web/lib/services/organization-plugin-service.ts:214-470; apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspacePlugins.tsx:33-55; apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:35-43).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S54.06 (private organization marketplace) and S54.30 (assign plugins to an organization, its groups or members). The migration says Claude lets an owner set each plugin to required, installed by default, available or not available and override it per group (apps/web/db/neon/0327_organization_plugin_group_settings.sql:3-12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace administrators with the policy.manage permission, and workspace members who receive the plugins.
problems_solved: A company shares its own skills and plugins without publishing them.
Administrators decide who gets what, by default or by group.
A required plugin cannot be turned off by a member.
use_cases: An admin uploads a plugin zip and leaves it 'Available to install'.
An admin marks a plugin 'Required' for everyone, so it stays on.
An admin sets a plugin 'Installed by default' for the Engineering group only.
A member opens Plugins and sees 'From <workspace>' plugins with a note.

where_to_find_it: Admin: web route /workspace/plugins, nav label 'Plugins' with hint 'Plugins this workspace publishes, and who gets them' (apps/web/app/workspace/plugins/page.tsx:10-17; apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx:108-110). Page title 'Plugins', description 'Choose whether each plugin is required, installed, available or hidden.'
Member (web and Desktop): Settings, Customize, Plugins, group 'From <workspace name>' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:35-43).
Member (mobile): Plugins, then 'Sources', section 'From <workspace>' with the preference and version (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginSourcesScreen.tsx:215-262).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not available.
prerequisites: A workspace (organization) the person belongs to and that is the active workspace.
Admin actions need the workspace permission policy.manage (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/plugins/route.ts:36, 70-74).
Members need plugins not switched off for the workspace.
screens_and_controls: Admin page: list 'Workspace plugins' with a per-plugin selector 'Setting for <plugin>' (Required, Installed by default, Available to install, Not available), group overrides 'Group settings for <plugin>' with 'Group to set <plugin> for' and 'Setting for that group', Retire (confirm title 'Retire <plugin>?', button 'Retire for everyone', 'Keep it published'), and 'Publish a plugin or a skill' with button 'Upload a plugin or skill' (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspacePlugins.tsx:33-55, 240-300, 391-396, 545-580).

Member: toggles to install and turn on or off, with notes 'Your workspace requires this plugin, so it stays on with all its skills.' and 'Your workspace offers this plugin to its members.' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:27-31).
journey: Admin opens /workspace/plugins and uploads a zip (a plugin, or a zip with one SKILL.md).
The server scans the files; findings that need review ask the admin to acknowledge before publishing.
The plugin appears with default setting 'Available to install' (a single skill defaults to 'Installed by default').
Admin changes the setting or sets group overrides.
Members open Plugins and see or receive the plugin as set; required plugins are on and locked.
Admin can retire a plugin for everyone.
feedback_and_outputs: Admin: 'Scanning and publishing…' with a spinner; caution list of scan findings with acknowledge and cancel; error alert 'That change could not be saved.' (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspacePlugins.tsx:425-435, 570-600).

Admin refusal: 'Your workspace role does not allow publishing plugins to this workspace.' or '... changing this workspace’s plugins.' (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/plugins/route.ts:72, 120).
Publishing a plugin that declares dependencies is refused with a message telling the admin to publish the dependencies too (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/plugins/route.ts:37-38, 81-84).
settings: Per plugin: install preference (required, installed_by_default, available, not_available) and status (published or retired). Per group: install preference override. A member in several groups gets the most permissive of their groups' settings in the order required, installed by default, available, not available (apps/web/db/neon/0327_organization_plugin_group_settings.sql:6-11).
Separate workspace allow and block lists of plugin keys can refuse installs (packages/client/client-runtime/src/connectors/policy.ts:105-128).

working: Admin API: GET list, POST publish zip, PATCH change setting or status, each with CSRF, rate limits and permission check; POST and PATCH write an 'admin_policy_changed' audit event (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/plugins/route.ts:46-150).
Service: publish with scan acknowledgement, replace files, update status or preference, replace group settings in a transaction (apps/web/lib/services/organization-plugin-service.ts:214-350).

Member API: GET /api/plugins/organization lists the plugins the member may see with their resolved preference (apps/web/app/api/plugins/organization/route.ts:15-40; apps/web/lib/services/organization-plugin-service.ts:384-407).
A required plugin cannot be turned off by the member (apps/web/lib/services/organization-plugin-service.ts:418-421).

Install gate refuses a plugin that the workspace blocks or does not approve, with 403 PLUGIN_NOT_PERMITTED (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/install-gate.ts:21-52; packages/client/client-runtime/src/connectors/policy.ts:105-128; apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/install-responses.ts:44-52).

Tables organization_plugins, organization_plugin_files, organization_plugin_members, organization_plugin_group_settings and a member-preference SQL function (apps/web/db/neon/0326_organization_plugins.sql:33; apps/web/db/neon/0327_organization_plugin_group_settings.sql:29, 63).
Mobile lists the workspace's plugins with install and turn-on states (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginSourcesScreen.tsx:215-262; apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/sourcesService.ts:23-38).
incomplete: The brief and first draft say assignment can target named members. The code supports workspace-wide and group settings only; the member's own install or enable state is the member's choice (apps/web/lib/services/organization-plugin-service.ts:306-350, 408-470). No per-member assignment was found.

Whether plugin groups come from directory (SCIM) groups or managed groups is stated in the migration (apps/web/db/neon/0327_organization_plugin_group_settings.sql:14-18); the admin UI for creating groups was not traced.
Workspace plugins cannot declare dependencies (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/plugins/route.ts:37-38).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile admin features (add marketplace, submit) are flag-off, but the member list of workspace plugins is on (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginSourcesScreen.tsx:215, 267).
not_available: Approval request: a member cannot ask an admin to approve a blocked plugin. No code, route or table for it was found in plugin, directory, organization-plugin or mobile plugin code (searched). Missing on all six apps (S54.31).
Admin management on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: none found.
The public Desktop shows the web page, so admin management is available there as the web page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5); no separate desktop code.

established.statement: An organization has a private marketplace of plugins for its members.
An admin can assign plugins to an organization, its groups or members.
established.source: S54.30 (brief); code supports organization and groups only

established.statement: A member can request admin approval to install a blocked plugin.
Organization plugins are stored per organization with files, members and group settings.
A member is refused when organization policy blocks a plugin.
Security review of plugins should include organization approval requirements, and sharing should be private, project, organization or public with clear ownership and revocation.
Revoked workspace permissions are explained without claiming installation.

acceptance_criteria: An admin with policy.manage can upload a zip and see the plugin listed as 'Available to install'; a member without the permission gets the refusal text.
Setting a plugin to Required makes it on for every member and a member's attempt to turn it off is refused with the 403 text.
Setting a plugin Not available hides it from members.
A group override replaces the workspace setting for members of that group.
A member in two groups gets the most permissive setting.
Publishing a zip with dependencies is refused.
Installing a plugin that the workspace policy blocks returns 403 PLUGIN_NOT_PERMITTED with the administrator message.
Each publish and change records an audit event.
inferred: [inferred] 'Installation approval request' needs a new request record, an admin queue and a notification; none exist.
[inferred] Per-member assignment can be approximated by creating a one-person group.
proposed: [proposed] Add a 'Request access' button on a blocked plugin that creates a request visible to admins.
[proposed] Show admins which members have each plugin on.
[proposed] Add per-member overrides if product wants the brief's 'named members'.

features.summary: Editorial 'featured' plugins do not exist. Instead, derived suggestions exist on some apps: web and Desktop group up to six popular plugins, mobile shows Popular and 'Recommended for you' (plugins that use connectors you already connected), and the CLI has 'agi marketplace recommend' that matches the current project. Categories are covered in F054-02.

purpose.what_it_does: Highlights plugins without the user searching. Web and Desktop mark the top installed verified plugins as popular; mobile adds a rule-based 'Recommended for you' shelf; the CLI suggests marketplace plugins that fit the folder's language, tools and packages (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts:1222-1239; apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/pluginsModel.ts:138-179; apps/cli/src/cloud/marketplaces.rs:156-200).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S54.10 (featured plugins) and S54.11 (recommended plugins). The brief marks both missing on all six apps; code shows derived popular and recommended features on three apps, but no featured flag for plugins.
purpose.who_uses_it: New users who do not know what to install; developers wanting project-fit suggestions.
problems_solved: Choosing a first plugin.
Finding plugins that fit connectors already connected.
Finding plugins that fit the project in the current folder.

A phone user sees 'Recommended for you' because they connected a calendar connector.

features.summary: Before and after a plugin is installed, the product shows what the plugin asks for, its security-scan verdict and which surfaces it fits. The server refuses unscanned, blocked or badly signed packages, and holds a plugin whose update asks for new permissions. Missing plugin dependencies are installed automatically; the 'Needs attention' list fixes missing skills and connectors.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a person the facts needed to decide on a plugin (permissions it declares, scan verdict with findings, which surfaces it works on, what it depends on) and enforces safety rules on the server: signed and scanned packages only, no silent permission growth, dependency checks. Web and Desktop (hosted web app) show the facts on the plugin detail page (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/PluginDetailView.tsx:296,307,1066,1068). Mobile shows them in its own screens (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginDetailScreen.tsx:453,459). The CLI enforces compatibility and signing rules in the terminal (apps/cli/src/features/plugins/plugins.rs:539,1285).
purpose.why_it_exists: A plugin can add skills, hooks and servers that run with the user's access. The brief asks that a user see permissions, scan result, compatibility and dependency problems before trusting a plugin (brief: S54.19, S54.32, S54.33, S54.34). docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:462 lists plugin review and dependency risk as a security-operations topic (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person installing or updating a plugin on web, desktop, mobile or CLI; org admins who rely on the gates; support staff reading scan records.
problems_solved: Installing a plugin without knowing what access it declares.
A plugin that grows its permissions in an update and runs unreviewed.
Installing a package nobody scanned or signed.
Installing a plugin on a surface that cannot run it.
A plugin that stops working because a plugin it needs is off, missing or suspended.
use_cases: A user on web opens a plugin, reads the Permissions and Security scan sections, then installs.
A user updates a built-in pack to a version that asks for a new permission and must confirm it first.
A CLI user with plugins.require_signed set is refused an unsigned plugin.
A mobile user sees 'Not available on mobile' for a plugin that only runs on Desktop and CLI.

established.statement: Before and after installing, a user sees the permissions a plugin requires (S54.19).
A user can see a plugin's security-scan result (S54.32).
The product warns when a plugin is not compatible with this surface or version (S54.33).
When a plugin's dependency is missing, the product offers to fix it (S54.34).
Plugin requirements include install, enable/disable, update, uninstall, namespacing and marketplace/source controls.
Show which skill or plugin is active, what it can access and how a user can intervene.

acceptance_criteria: On web, a plugin with declared permissions shows each one under 'Permissions' before and after install.
A plugin version with no recorded scan cannot be installed; the message says it has not been scanned.
A plugin whose scan verdict is 'block' cannot be installed on web or mobile (mobile Install button is disabled).
Applying an update whose version adds a permission fails unless that permission is acknowledged in the request.
Installing a plugin with an unmet plugin dependency installs the dependency first and reports its name.
Turning on a plugin whose dependency is off returns an error naming the dependency and the problem.
CLI install of a plugin with an excluded engines.agiworkforce range fails and leaves no files; with plugins.require_signed true an unsigned plugin is refused without --unsafe-allow-unsigned.
inferred: [inferred] The 'repair' in S54.34 should cover plugin-on-plugin dependencies, not only skills and connectors, because the brief says 'dependency'.
[inferred] Every surface that can install a plugin should show scan and permissions, because VS Code and CLI installs run code on the device.
proposed: [proposed] Add a 'Turn on <dependency>' repair button for an unmet dependency on web and mobile.
[proposed] Scan or label as unscanned every directory (GitHub) plugin before install, and say so in the install dialog.
[proposed] Show scan verdict and permissions in the VS Code and CLI install flow.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the plugin detail page; the browser loads the entry, then fetches scan and versions for it.
Server finds the content hash for the plugin (marketplace entry hash, or registry version digest) and reads the stored scan record.
Person presses Install; the server applies the workspace feature gate for plugins and the per-plugin org policy before anything is written.
Server plans dependencies, refuses unreadable or conflicting ones, checks policy for each dependency.
Server verifies hash, signature (Ed25519 against trusted keys) and scan verdict, then compares declared permissions with the approved set; growth holds the install for review.
Install writes the rows (dependencies first) and an audit event per plugin.
CLI install runs entirely on the device: clone or copy, signature policy, sha256 pin, compatibility check; the only network use is git and remote server sign-in.

features.summary: Install a plugin for your account (web, desktop, mobile), or into a folder on your device (CLI, VS Code). Install turns the plugin on and installs its dependencies first, unless org policy refuses. Per-plugin settings choose which skills are on; bundled connections are signed in through the connector path or 'agi plugin login'.

purpose.what_it_does: Adds a plugin to a person's account or device, records it as turned on, installs the plugins it depends on, saves per-plugin settings and helps the person sign in to the connections the plugin bundles.
purpose.why_it_exists: Installing is the step that makes a plugin's skills, agents and connectors usable in chats (brief: S54.21-S54.23; doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 19 lists Install and included MCP servers).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in users on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile; CLI and VS Code users with a local runtime; org admins who set install policy.
problems_solved: Getting a ready-made set of skills and connectors without building them.
Needing one plugin that depends on another.
Org control over which plugins members may install.
Signing in to a plugin's remote servers.
use_cases: Install a built-in pack on web and see 'Also installed: ...' for its dependencies.
Install a public directory plugin that bundles an MCP server and sign in to it as a connector.
Run agi plugin install <git-url> --ref <tag> on a laptop.
Switch off one skill of an installed plugin on the plugin page.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Customize > Plugins > a plugin > button 'Install' (becomes 'Installed') (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/PluginDetailView.tsx:1006-1015 via primaryLabel; constants.ts:120-122).

steps.what_happens: Person presses Install; the browser sends POST with a CSRF token.
Server rate-limits, validates the id, applies workspace gate and per-plugin policy.
Server plans dependencies, refuses if a dependency is blocked by policy, installs dependencies then the plugin in order.
For directory plugins the server fetches the plugin files from the public source (an outside service), stores a shadow entry and installation, and registers bundled remote MCP servers as connectors.
Server returns 201; the browser refreshes installs and the skill catalog.
Person signs in to a connector through the connector flow (OAuth start or credentials form).

CLI install clones or copies, checks signature or hash, validates the manifest, installs dependencies from the registry, prompts for settings, all on the device; login stores tokens in the OS credential store.

features.summary: Turn an installed plugin off and on, move it to a newer or older published version, stay on a chosen version, or remove it. On web and mobile, turning off or removing a plugin that others need asks to include them. Updates that add permissions need the person to approve them first. The CLI uses git commits and tags.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person keep a plugin without using it, move it between published versions, hold it on one version, and delete it, with checks on dependents, permissions and version status.
purpose.why_it_exists: People need control after install: pause a plugin, take a fix, avoid a bad release, or clean up (brief: S54.24-S54.26, S54.29; doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 19 lists Enable/disable, Update, Uninstall).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in users on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile; CLI users; VS Code users; platform admins whose suspend and rollback actions move installs.
problems_solved: A plugin interfering with chats but worth keeping.
A new version asking for more access than before.
A withdrawn or suspended version still installed.
Breaking another plugin by removing one it needs.
use_cases: Turn a plugin off on web with the 'Enabled' switch.
Press 'Update to 1.2.0' and read the new permissions in the dialog.
Pick an older published version and press 'Switch version'.
Run agi plugin install <git-url> --ref v1.0 so 'agi plugin update' leaves it alone.

Server rate-limits, then for turn on checks unmet dependencies and pending permission review; for turn off lists dependents.

Browser refreshes the installs and the skill catalog.
CLI update runs git pull --ff-only in the plugin folder (a network call to the git host), then checks the signature; on failure puts the previous commit back.

features.summary: On web and desktop (hosted web), 'Customize' makes your own editable copy of an installed, turned-on plugin's skills, then turns the original off. 'Edit plugin' changes the copy. In chat, asking to build a plugin or skill can show a draft card with a Save button. Copy and edit are the only fork path found.

purpose.what_it_does: Copies the skills and companion files of an installed plugin into a new personal plugin named '<name> (custom)', installs and enables it, turns the original off, and opens the editor. Also lets a person create a plugin by form or by asking in chat.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to change a plugin's skills without losing the original (brief: S54.27, S54.28, S54.35). Skill authoring is on by default and can be switched off by a server setting (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts:5-12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web and desktop-hosted users who write or tune skills.
problems_solved: A published plugin is almost right but needs one skill changed.
Writing a plugin from nothing.
Keeping the original available to turn back on.
use_cases: Customize a built-in pack and edit its 'summarize' skill.
Ask the assistant 'build a plugin that drafts release notes' and press 'Save plugin' on the card.
Press 'Edit plugin' on an authored plugin and save changes.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Customize > Plugins > installed plugin > button 'Customize' with hint 'Make your own copy of this plugin and edit its skills.' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/PluginDetailView.tsx:911-940; constants.ts:454-455).
Web: authored plugins show 'Edit plugin'; creation form titled 'Create a plugin' (constants.ts:429,449).
Web chat: a card with 'Save plugin' and 'Save as a skill' buttons after a build request (apps/web/features/chat/components/PluginDraftCard.tsx:29-30).

Mobile: no copy or edit; the card titled 'Customize' only switches skills on or off (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/PluginDetailScreen.tsx:549).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not available. For the CLI this is a recorded decision (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-28-29 lists plugin customize and S54.27 for CLI).

Workspace gates for both 'plugins' and 'skills' pass (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/install-gate.ts:14,26-37).
The plugin has at least one skill (customize.ts:161).

The original is turned off so your chats use your copy; you can turn it back on from its page.' and confirm 'Make my copy' (constants.ts:456-459; DirectoryPanel.tsx:669-686).

established.statement: A user can customize an installed plugin (edit its skills or content) (S54.27).
A user can fork a plugin into their own editable copy (S54.28).
The product helps a user build a plugin with an assistant (S54.35).
The CLI does not offer plugin customize.
Skill authoring is refused when the authoring setting is off.
An agent never destroys user data; the copy leaves the original in place and only turns it off.

acceptance_criteria: Customize on an installed, enabled plugin with skills creates one new installed plugin named '<name> (custom)' and turns the original off.
Pressing Customize again returns the same copy (created false) and creates no second one.
With AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING=0 the customize route returns 404 'Skill authoring is not available.'
A plugin with no skills returns 422 with the message 'This plugin has no skills that can be copied.'
Edit plugin saves changes that appear in chats using the copy.
Asking 'build me a plugin for release notes' on web shows a card with 'Save plugin'; saving installs it on.
The Customize button is absent on a turned-off or authored plugin.
inferred: [inferred] The server should reject a customize request for a plugin that is installed but off, matching the message 'Install and turn on this plugin first'.
[inferred] The fork (S54.28) and customize (S54.27) rows describe one action; the brief lists both with the same code.
proposed: [proposed] Merge S54.27 and S54.28 into one item in the brief.
[proposed] Move the 'installed and on' check into customizePlugin so the API matches its error message.
[proposed] Rename the mobile skill card so it is not also called 'Customize'.

features.summary: A signed-in publisher with a verified email submits their own uploaded or authored plugin for review, sees its status and can withdraw it. Platform admins approve, reject or suspend submissions and publish, deprecate, suspend or roll back registry plugin versions on /admin/plugins. Reporting, analytics and paid procurement do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs two linked processes: (1) community submissions with statuses pending, approved, rejected, withdrawn, suspended; (2) registry version lifecycle with statuses draft, in_review, published, deprecated, suspended and actions publish, deprecate, suspend, rollback. Both are done by platform admins on one admin page.
purpose.why_it_exists: The directory needs human review before community plugins reach everyone, and a way to stop a bad version fast (brief: S54.36, S54.37; doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:462 plugin review and emergency controls; doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:105-108 publisher identity checked in the owner's review).
purpose.who_uses_it: Publishers (any signed-in user with a verified email who has an uploaded or authored plugin) and platform staff listed in the platform-admin setting.
problems_solved: Unreviewed community code reaching all users.
A bad version staying installable.
No way for a publisher to see why a plugin was refused.
Installations pinned to a withdrawn version.
use_cases: Publisher presses 'Submit to the directory' and later sees 'Listed'.
Admin rejects a submission with a reviewer note the publisher reads on the plugin page.
Admin suspends a bad version and every installation running it is switched off.
Admin rolls a plugin back to its previous published version.

established.statement: A publisher can submit a plugin for review and track the review (S54.36).
Platform staff can moderate listings: suspend, deprecate (S54.37).
A user can report a plugin (S54.38); a publisher sees analytics (S54.39); paid plugins can be bought through commercial procurement where offered (S54.40). All three are missing on every app.
Publisher identity is checked in the owner's review of each submission.
Plugin review, incident response and emergency controls belong to security operations.
Version changes follow fixed steps; pending or approved submissions can be withdrawn.

acceptance_criteria: A user without a verified email gets 403 when submitting.
Submitting a plugin whose scan verdict is 'block' is refused with the findings.
A second submission of the same plugin key withdraws the earlier pending one.
Only a pending submission can be approved or rejected; only an approved one can be suspended; other combinations return 409.
Rejecting or suspending needs a note; the publisher sees it as 'Reviewer note'.
Suspending a registry version switches off every installation on it and the response says how many.
A non-admin calling /api/plugins/[id]/lifecycle or the admin submission routes is refused, and /admin/plugins returns not found.
inferred: [inferred] A listing report is needed before public launch because anyone can install an approved community plugin.
[inferred] Publishers need a way to see why a scan blocked or flagged a plugin before submitting.
proposed: [proposed] Add a 'Report' control to the plugin detail view feeding the moderation queue.
[proposed] Add per-plugin install counts for publishers.
[proposed] Show the lifecycle 'submit' action in the admin page, or remove it from the API.

steps.what_happens: Publisher presses Submit; browser posts the entry id and optional category and publisher name.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, verified email and the external-sharing gate.
Server reads the owned entry and files, runs the rule-based scan, refuses 'block', and in one transaction withdraws earlier pending rows and stores the submission and its files.
Admin opens /admin/plugins; the page loads the queue and files through admin routes.
Admin decides; server locks the row, checks the expected status, updates it, and for approve replaces the earlier approved row and moves its installs.
Server writes an audit event and sends a notification to the publisher.
For registry versions, admin actions move the status in plugin_registry_versions, repoint the entry, record a lifecycle event and an audit event; suspend disables installations on that version.

data.what: Submission row with status, scan verdict and findings, reviewer note, reviewer id
data.retained_or_deleted: Rows are kept; withdrawn and rejected stay as history (no delete found)

data.what: Version records and lifecycle events with actor and reason

data.synced: Server side, shown on the user's surfaces

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider takes part. The scan is rule based (packages/client/client-runtime/src/plugins/packageScan.ts). Review is by a human.

access_and_usage.account: Signed in; submission also needs a verified primary email (apps/web/app/api/plugins/submissions/route.ts:49-54). Admin routes need a platform admin.
access_and_usage.permissions: Publisher can only submit and withdraw plugins they own (createSubmission query filters by user and source kind; withdraw filters by user_id). Admin actions need requirePlatformAdmin and the admin-operator rate limit (admin route.ts:66-76; lifecycle/route.ts:108,130).
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code. No plan, entitlement or credit check in the submission or moderation routes.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Submit and withdraw use plugin-installation-write 20 per minute (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:519). Admin routes use the admin-operator limiter. The admin queue lists at most 200 rows (plugin-submission-service.ts:292-303). No metering.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Submission and moderation need our servers and a signed-in account; there is no Local-mode path. The CLI has no submission code.
